News.title: Shocking moment skidding truck is left hanging between two motorway ramps after driver loses control in rain
News.content:
Next

THIS is the moment a truck is left teetering between two motorway ramps after it skidded on a rain-slicked road.

Terrifying footage captures a truck sliding over the gap between an exit ramp and an overpass, leaving the vehicle precariously straddling the void.



Transport officials called the scene a “very unusual sight.”

Miraculously, the driver walked away without a scratch and no other injuries were reported.



The near-miss came around midday in Toledo, Ohio, on Thursday – Thanksgiving Day – as much of the US was ravaged by a rare bomb cyclone.

Thanks to heavy rain in the area, the driver suddenly lost control and skidded across the busy motorway on Interstate 75.



As the lorry slid, its trailer swung out to one side before whipping round at a sharp angle and careening over the overpass.

Emergency crews rushed to the scene and closed the entire right-hand lane near the crash site.



After hours of toiling, heavy-duty tow crews managed to get the lorry back onto the road at around 3.45pm.

A fire and rescue official at the scene said: “The driver unfortunately lost control in the wind and rain, and straddled the two overpasses.

“Luckily, there are no injuries.”

First responders said the lorry was leaking fuel at one point, but it was not carrying any hazardous materials.

Toledo Police have launched an investigation into the crash.



The incident caused major delays along the corridor during Thanksgiving, which is historically one of the busiest travel periods on US highways.

Chaotic weather slammed much of the East Coast and large parts of the Midwest on Thursday.

Over 800,000 people were without power as of Thursday afternoon, with biblical flooding hitting New York, New Jersey and Virginia, sparking dozens of rescues.

Some 400 flights were cancelled and more than 1,700 were delayed as of early the afternoon, according to FlightAware.

All flights from La Guardia Airport were grounded in the afternoon as winds battered the busy terminals.



President Trump announced he would likely send disaster relief funds to those impacted in the brutal Thanksgiving storm.

In New Jersey, the enclave of Stone Harbor was under at least two feet of water.

Footage shows locals wading through torrents of water in Ocean City submerged up to their waists.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Water closed in on houses, and sandbags were piled in front of businesses’ doors as the tide drew in ferociously.

Across the state, emergency crews conducted over 14 rescues and evacuated multiple homes in the area.

News.title: Woman, 21, found stabbed to death in wheelie bin after cop noticed ‘overwhelming putrid smell’, court told
News.content:
GRIM END Woman, 21, found stabbed to death in wheelie bin after cop noticed ‘overwhelming putrid smell’, court told







Next

A YOUNG woman was found stabbed to death in a wheelie bin after a police officer noticed an “overwhelming putrid smell”, a court heard.

Chloe Mitchell was allegedly murdered by Brandon Rainey, who then placed her remains in three refuse sacks across two bins, jurors heard.



The 21-year-old had disappeared in Ballymena, Northern Ireland, in the early hours of 3 June, 2023 – sparking a hunt.

Belfast Crown Court heard one officer was out house-to-house inquiries when he noticed a smell from a wheelie bin.



He said just as he and a colleague were leaving one address, the homeowner apologised for the smell coming from her bin.

The detective sergeant added: “It was only as we left her house I did catch a very strong smell.



“I opened the bin, the bin was full to the brim, and I remember there being quite a lot of maggots, and this overwhelming putrid smell coming from it, and I was really struggling not to throw up.

“There were a lot of flies around the homeowner’s garden and kitchen.”

The officer said he phoned his supervisor to report he suspected there were human remains in the bin.

“I have never smelt anything like that before, it seemed quite obvious to me that that was what it was,” he added.



The court heard he located a second bin which had flies around it, which raised his suspicions around it.

A crime scene investigator who was tasked to look at the bins for body parts also gave evidence.

She took photographs of the wheelie bins, and noted a “significant number of maggots” in one of them, the court heard.



The investigator added: “he bin was quite full and there were a few bags of rubbish nearer the top, so I removed those systematically… until I found a bag within the bin which contained a severed leg, so then I stopped my examination in regards to that bin.”

Turning to the second bin, she said she carried out a similar procedure, and under some bags containing general household rubbish she found more body parts and items of clothing.

The court heard Rainey, 30, accepts he killed Chloe but on the partial defence of diminished responsibility.

His barrister Des Fahy KC said he was previously diagnosed with paranoid schizophrenia and had in the past been prescribed anti-psychotic medication.

Jurors were told Rainey had ordered a number of knives online the month before Chloe’s death.



While officers were carrying out searches after the horror, they allegedly intercepted another knife being delivered to his flat.

The court heard his phone was seized five days after Chloe’s death and showed searches about Jack the Ripper, an article on “how to act possessed” and about “how to conceal a knife”.

A video was also found that showed Rainey threatening to stab a man, saying: “I could kill you stone dead. I’m going to murder you.”

Prosecutor David Russell KC said Chloe was “the victim of a brutal and sustained attack inflicted upon her by the accused using weapons, a knife and a blunt object”.

He added: “The attack and the dismemberment and mutilation of Chloe’s body were intentionally carried out by Brandon Rainey.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

“He displayed a callous cruel disregard for Chloe in life and death and the evidence, we say, when it unfolds before you will convince you that this is a case of murder.”

The trial continues.

News.title: Formula 1 boss & parents in £1.1MILLION court row over ‘road sludge’ stopping them from boating on lake at their mansion
News.content:
WADING IN Formula 1 boss & parents in £1.1MILLION court row over ‘road sludge’ stopping them from boating on lake at their mansion







Next

A FORMULA 1 boss is embroiled in a £1.1million row with council and highways bods after tonnes of road “sludge” ended up in the lake at his manor.

Ollie Oakes, the former head of Alpine F1, and his mother Pamela are suing National Highways and Norfolk County Council over the discharges from nearby roads.



They claim “silt and pollutants” have ruined the lake – known as “the fish pond” – at the idyllic Hopton Manor near Great Yarmouth.



The value of the property has been slashed from £2.2million to just over £1million due to the scourge, experts claim.

Ollie and his relatives claim the sludge has smothered the lily pads on their once beloved lake, stopping them boating on the waters.



They are now demanding more than £1million to cover the cost of cleaning it up.

Billy Oakes, Ollie’s dad and Pamela’s husband, said no one wants to use the lake anymore due to the contamination.

Speaking outside the High Court, he said: “We are now unable to boat on the lake, or let our dogs and pets swim in the lake, or family or guests to fish in the lake.

“When we moved in there were lots of lily pads there, but they’re now completely swamped with reeds.”



He added that around 100 metres of the lake is blighted as a result of the silt, with algae and reeds growing on top of it.



Fighting the case has already cost the family £650,000 in lawyers’ bills.

In a High Court case, Mrs Oakes and the children are suing for trespass and nuisance, blaming the polluted water from surrounding drains for blighting the lake.

Their lawyers claim the silting in the lake is from rainwater containing heavy metals and hydrocarbons running off local roads into the water.

Barrister Clifford Darton KC said: “Put simply, the claimants contend that the defendants must stop discharging polluted surface water into the lake and pay for the costs of clearing up the damage that has been done by these discharges.”



But National Highways and Norfolk County Council are refusing to pay them compensation, claiming they were entitled to discharge surface water into the lake.

They claim much of the silt in the water has been caused by “naturally occurring vegetation”.

Pamela and Billy Oakes moved into the property in 1993, converting a coaching house and stables into a home for them and their four children.

The fish pond was a star feature of the home and was home to pike, roach and lily pads.

The property is now held in the name of Mrs Oakes and the children, who boated on the lake and played beside it when they were youngsters.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

Mr Justice Thompsell is expected to rule on the case at a later date.

News.title: Man in his 30s arrested for ‘manslaughter’ after walker, 53, killed ‘touching live electricity cable’ in field
News.content:
CABLE TRAGEDY Man in his 30s arrested for ‘manslaughter’ after walker, 53, killed ‘touching live electricity cable’ in field







Next

A MAN in his 30s has been arrested on suspicion of manslaughter after a walker was killed by an exposed live electricity cable in a field.

Kevin Walkden, 58, died after coming into contact with the live wire while walking in West Yorkshire on November 22.



Police were called to the scene at 2.26pm that day over concern for his safety and he was pronounced dead at the scene.

Detectives from the Homicide and Major Enquiry Team are probing how the cable became exposed and whether any crimes were committed.



A suspect in his 30s was arrested on suspicion of manslaughter and has been bailed pending further enquiries.

Police stressed there is nothing to suggest Kevin was trying to interfere with, steal or damage the cable.

Officers are continuing to appeal for information about any suspicious activity in the area over the past four to six weeks.

Anyone with information that could help our investigation is asked to contact police via 101 or use the Live Chat facility at www.westyorkshire.police.uk/livechat quoting 13260663472

Information can always be given anonymously via Crimestoppers on 0800 555 111

News.title: How I’m training my daughter, 6, to prepare for WW3 in Britain – if you’re not doing the same, you’re FAILING your kids
News.content:
Next

MUMS across Britain will be used to the daily struggle of getting their kids to pack their school bags.

But one has got her six-year-old daughter drilled to quickly gather something much more sinister – her World War Three emergency kit.





Ana, 42, even gets her girl to practice for lengthy blackouts that could come in the event of a major attack on Britain’s infrastructure.

And she warns that parents should be doing the same training with their children – before it’s too late.

“If your kids aren’t prepared, then you’re setting them up for failure,” says Ana who runs a “Food and Lifestyle prepping” YouTube channel – and doesn’t share her full name out of security concerns.

Her “prepper” lifestyle was kickstarted when Ana was a new mum and struggled to breastfeed her daughter.

When no nearby supermarkets had any formula in stock, she went into total panic mode.

Ana scoured online in a haste, though she was quoted £300 for a small tub.

The experience showed her how quickly an everyday essential could become scarce.

Now, she prepares herself and her family for the worst to ensure they never go without again, from preserving and growing her own food to stockpiling the essentials.





She’s also gone one step further – doing “practice” sessions with her six-year-old daughter so she knows what to do if the lights go out.

Her daughter’s bright drawstring bag, complete with a hot pink walkie-talkie, snacks and cuddly toys, is a heartbreaking reminder of the fraught world Brit kids are being brought up in today.

The Government has urged Britons to stockpile essentials like tinned food, bottled water, and batteries to have to hand in the event of a national emergency.

It’s caused a run on wind-up radios, which will be vital in the event of a major power blackout to listen to emergency broadcasts.

This week, MI5 spy chiefs issued a stark warning to British businesses associated with the Ukraine war effort tell them that their staff could be targeted by Russian espionage.

And the Ministry of Defence confirmed it had written to 100,000 British military veterans in the UK’s Strategic Reserve force as part of war planning efforts.

Ana says that in this climate, it’s vital that families prepare themselves properly – regardless of the fear it may bring.

“The new generations aren’t used to being put out like the older ones”, she explains.



“I don’t care if people think I’m scaring my child.

“In fact, she will be less scared than kids who have never experienced a power cut or practiced one.

“All I’m doing is building her into a more capable person.

“The last thing I want is for my daughter to grow up frightened of the world.

“But, at the same time, I don’t want her growing up completely helpless when something doesn’t go to plan.

“And this is why we need to teach children preparedness, at least in my eyes.

“We teach them how to cross the road, not to talk to strangers and what to do if there’s a fire.

“Nobody really questions that – so why does the idea of teaching them what to do in a power cut – or more serious situation – suddenly become controversial?



“I think we’ve made being prepared sound far more frightening than it needs to be.”

Ana often performs “lights out” evenings as part of her daughter’s training.

This involves switching off the lights and putting screens away to give her daughter a feel for what a power cut might be like.

She gets board games out, uses camping lanterns and tries to make an adventure of it – all while teaching a valuable lesson.

Ana said: “When people hear the word prepper, they often imagine bunkers, gas masks and people preparing for the end of the world.

“But most of us are simply trying to make sure our families can cope when normal life is interrupted.

“And I don’t see why children shouldn’t be part of that, in an age-appropriate way.

“It should start with the little things; imagine you’re six years old and suddenly all the lights go out.



“The television stops working, the Wi-Fi disappears and the house goes dark.

“If you’ve never experienced that before, it could be quite frightening.

“But what if you’ve already had a fun evening with your parents using torches and battery-operated lanterns? What if you know where your little torch lives and that Mum and Dad have everything under control?

“It’s exactly the same situation, but the child has some idea of what to expect.

“There’s no need to talk about cyberattacks, wars or the collapse of the electricity grid.

“You’re simply showing children that life can carry on, even when something stops working.”

Ana believes that the teachings should go farther than inside the home, stretching to lessons in schools and other educational settings.

The European Commission urged schools to incorporate disaster and crisis education, such as how to be self-sufficient for 72 hours.

She also thinks that every parent should get their little ones equipped with their very own emergency bag.

She said: “It doesn’t have to be an expensive survival kit.



“Just a small backpack with a torch, a favourite toy, perhaps a colouring book and a few snacks.

“I asked my daughter to make up her own.

“I can understand why some parents might disagree with me.

“We’re constantly hearing about war, cyberattacks, extreme weather and all sorts of things that can make the world seem quite unsettling.

“Of course parents want to protect their children from that – I do too.

“But I think there’s a big difference between frightening a child about what might happen and calmly teaching them what they can do if something happens.”

Ana also gets her little one to help out with her preparations, such as stock rotation, growing and preserving food and cooking.

The founder of the UK Preppers Club thinks the government’s “Be Ready” campaign “isn’t enough” and that there should be more emphasis on what families need to act on if something goes wrong, rather than what should be on their shopping list.

She added: “Preparedness shouldn’t be something we only think about when there’s a frightening headline on the news.

“It should be part of ordinary family life, just like teaching children to cook or look after themselves.



“I’m not suggesting we turn our children into little survivalists.

“I’m suggesting we give them a few useful skills, some confidence and the reassurance that, even when things go wrong, there are things we can do.

“Because eventually our children will grow up and have to deal with problems without us standing beside them and times then may be much harder than they are now.

“And I’m a believer that helping them become a little more capable and resilient is the least we can do as parents.”

Ana’s daughter said: “I don’t think Mummy is crazy. She’s only getting ready for a power cut or storm.

“I find it exciting playing board games in the dark.”

News.title: Chaotic moment woman accidentally reverses her Range Rover into her neighbour’s house & smashes through the front window
News.content:
Next

THIS is the chaotic moment a woman accidentally reverses her Range Rover into her neighbour’s house, smashing through the front window.

The shocking incident unfolded in Northallerton, North Yorkshire on the morning of November 20.



Doorbell footage shows a Range Rover parked outside a home in the Romanby area of the town at around 8.40am.

A woman can then be seen opening the door to exit the expensive motor when it suddenly starts rolling backwards.



In scenes of carnage and with the driver’s door still open, the woman can be seen half-way out the vehicle, desperately trying to bring it to a stop.

The motor then picks up speed as it reverses across the road before crashing through the railings of a neighbour’s property.



The back end then smashes through the neighbour’s front window.

Debris explodes across the pavement and rains down on top of the Range Rover and scatters across the street.



Images circulating on social media later showed the car cordoned off and still lodged in the front porch of the home.

One user said: “That’s my Mam’s house next door. You quite simply cannot park there.”

A spokesperson for North Yorkshire Police said: “At around 9am on November 20, police in Northallerton were called by the ambulance service to an incident in the Romanby area of the town after a Range Rover collided with a residential property.

“It is believed the vehicle was initially parked before it collided with the nearby home.

“There were no serious injuries reported to the police but the driver was treated at the scene for face and head injuries.



“Structural engineers were called to assess the damage to the property.”.

News.title: Man, 20, found dead in freezer outside his family’s home after ‘parents refused to let him in to escape the cold’
News.content:
Next

A MAN has been found dead inside a freezer outside his family’s home after his parents allegedly refused to let him to escape the cold.

Mohammed Al-Omar, 20, knocked on his parent’s door at around 2am on a bitterly cold night and begged to be let inside – but his father reportedly turned him away.



His parents claimed that the Dutch local authorities had threatened to take away their children if they let their 20-year-old son inside the home.

But on Tuesday morning Mohammed’s younger brother, 15, discovered part of a jacket poking out of an unplugged freezer outside the home.

When he and his mother opened the appliance, they discovered the body of Mohammed who had been lying inside for around two days.



Neighbours called the police to the home in Utrecht, the Netherlands after hearing the mum’s screams upon discovery of her dead son.

His family believe the man had climbed into the unplugged freezer for warmth during a night in which temperatures had plummetted to -4.5C.

His grieving father Abdulkarim said that his son’s final words to him on the night of November 22 were: “Dad, I’m cold, let me in.”

He said: “I will never forget those words.”

Old household appliances are often dumped outside for waste collection – and the unplugged freezer had been left out for around two weeks.



One neighbour said: “You don’t pay much attention to it. But I walked past it a couple of times myself, and that is quite a shock.”

Mohammed travelled to the Netherlands from Syria in 2021 when he was 14 or 15 years old.

His family joined him in the European nation in November 2024 – but his father said that by this time his son had fallen in with “bad friends”.

He said his son struggled with drug addiction and mental health problems, with the city’s authorities confirming that he had been recieving help from a local neighbourhood team.

Abdulkarim said: “He had financial problems and arguments with others as well. We tried everything, but he wasn’t listening to us any more.”



He added: “I came from Syria to bring my children to safety. Sadly I have lost my eldest child here.”

Both parents feared losing their younger children if they let their eldest son into the home.

“They threatened that… they would take all our children away”, said the mum with the dad adding: “I was trapped: if I had let him in, I would have lost all my children.”

The neighbourhood team has confirmed it supported the family, but has not said whether it gave such advice.

In the Netherlands only juvenile courts, not neighbourhood teams, have the power to remove kids from a family home.



Police declared on Thursday that there was no indication of a crime.

But Utrecht Mayor Sharon Dijksma has launched an investigation into what advice the support team gave the family.

She said: “I think it’s very important in a case like this that we find out exactly who had what role, exactly what did and didn’t happen and what advice was given.”

“Losing your child is the worst thing that can happen to parents. It’s a nightmare,” she added.

Mohammed’s family are hoping to bury him in Syria and are raising money for the funeral, transport and possible legal fees over the circumstances of his death.

News.title: UK Christmas fair poster goes viral over rude blunder and people can’t stop laughing – can you spot it?
News.content:
Next

A POSTER for a Christmas fair has gone viral after people couldn’t stop laughing at a rude blunder.

The hilarious mistake has sparked lots of reaction across social media.

In a bid to promote their Christmas Mistletoe Fair this Saturday (November 28), bosses at the Oak and Olive Deli in Southampton, launched a poster campaign on various platforms.



It included colourful images of festive favourites such as hot dogs and mince pies.



There were also mugs of frothy hot chocolate and lightly toasted pretzels.

The poster stated: “Oak & Olive Hythe Mistletoe Fair this Saturday. 10am-4pm.”

However, when it came to the text describing the images, ‘mince pies’ had a typo spelling ‘m***e pies’ – sparking hilarity across social media.



One person wrote: “I’ll er .. I’ll pass.”

Another person posted: “Definitely giving that a swerve.”

A third person posted a meme with the caption: “Pull the plug”, while a fourth person replied with SEVEN laughing emojis.

The poster has now been corrected to remove the blunder – and republished on social media.



In a post on Facebook, the deli seemed to poke fun at their own blunder and said: “Lets try again” followed by the same poster but this time spelling mince pies correctly.

News.title: 'A lonely road': Catherine joins cancer support group in new documentary
News.content:
The Princess of Wales is seen joining a cancer support group in newly-released footage from a forthcoming documentary called Heal.

"I haven't really explored this outside my family walls," Catherine tells a group of people from Shine Cancer Support.

The documentary features her personal thoughts on her illness and recovery.

Catherine has never disclosed what type of cancer she faced, but in March 2024 she revealed that she had a diagnosis of cancer and was receiving chemotherapy.

In January 2025 she said that she was in remission and in the following months began a gradual return to royal duties.

Heal will be shown on BBC iPlayer from 12:00 GMT and BBC One at 18:40 GMT on 29 November. It will also air internationally, including on NBCUniversal in the US on 30 November, Channel 9 in Australia on 1 December and CTV and Noovo in Canada on 7 December

News.title: 'I wouldn't be here today without you': Student's praise for man who stopped Huntingdon train attacker
News.content:
Meeting after the guilty verdicts were delivered, the two train passengers hugged.

Astrid told the Nottingham Forest fan, who had been travelling home from a match: "It's brilliant to meet you... now we will know each other for a long time."

Crean said: "It means the world to me to meet her. Meeting her was the best thing, it was worth waiting for. I'm just so happy."

Astrid, who did not want to use her last name, said Crean was a hero for his actions that day.

"I just owe him everything," she said, before adding: "I wouldn't be here today without you, and to put your life on the line for someone else, a complete stranger, is just complete bravery."

She said Crean had a "split second to make a decision" and she owed him her life because of that.

"So I'd just like to say thank you," she said.

Crean praised her for alerting him to the danger of Williams as she ran past.

"You can be proud of yourself, and your parents will be proud of you," he added.

During the trial, Crean told the court he decided "to try to stop" the attack and "launched himself towards and at" Williams.

Crean and Astrid both faced terrifying moments as Williams rampaged down the train.

Crean said Williams asked, "Do you want to die?" as he stabbed him several times.

Crean then managed to lock himself in a toilet and call 999 telling them what had happened and that he was covered in blood and scared.

He said he remembered seeing Astrid crying with makeup running down her face.

The fashion student said she remembered seeing Crean throw himself at the attacker and put himself between her and Williams so she could escape.

"I was able to shut the door with the rest of the people behind me. If you hadn't been in between us... I have no idea what would have happened if you weren't there, literally in that second."

Astrid had seen an interview with the 62-year-old on the BBC two days after the attack and contacted the BBC to say he was the man on the train who had helped protect her and others.

Only now the trial has finished have they been able to meet.

Crean said he is pleased the jury found Williams guilty of attempting to murder him as he did not believe he should be allowed to get away with the vicious attacks on him and the other passengers.

On Thursday Cambridgeshire police apologised for failings in stopping Williams after another assault the month before the Huntingdon attack.

As well as the train attacks, Williams was found guilty of attempting to murder four other people in separate incidents and will be sentenced at Cambridge Crown Court on 4 and 5 February.

Crean believes more should have been done to prevent these further offences. "I think they should have had him before. He shouldn't have been allowed to go running around like this. And if they'd picked up on it, we'd have had him before."

Having survived the attack, Astrid is running the London marathon for Crimestoppers as part of her efforts to turn around the harrowing situation she found herself in.

She can, she says, because of Stephen Crean's actions. And he has promised to be there for her again: this time on the finish line.

Additional reporting by Rozina Sini

News.title: Watch: Student describes moment passenger 'threw himself' at attacker and saved her life
News.content:
A student who survived the Huntingdon train attack has said one of the passengers who was stabbed "saved her life" when he ran towards attacker Anthony Williams, giving her time to escape.

On Thursday, Williams was found guilty of 14 attempted murders, including trying to kill Stephen Crean.

Astrid told the BBC Stephen's actions had allowed her to reach safety in the buffet car.

The BBC's Lucy Manning spoke to them after the verdicts, as they met for the first time since the attack.

News.title: Met Police ruined my life, says Kenyan man wrongly convicted over attack on UK couple
News.content:
In April 2023, Kenya's High Court quashed Kololo's conviction, because of doubts over the prosecution's evidence. This followed years of work by the legal charity Reprieve and a Kenyan lawyer, Alfred Olaba, who represented him for free.

They were supported by Judith Tebbutt, who believed Kololo was innocent. In an interview with the BBC in 2022, she said he had been scapegoated by Scotland Yard.

"He was not there on the night. He was not part of the group that held me. They've put this man in prison without any real evidence."

More than three years after his release, Kololo says he is still living with the effects of his torture and decade in prison. As we walk the narrow streets of Lamu's old town, his thin frame moves stiffly. He is on edge. "My mind is not good," he says. "I have not recovered."

He remembers being kept in a filthy, bedbug-ridden cell with up to eight other inmates, which he thought he would never leave. Twice he contracted tuberculosis and nearly died.

Kololo is now too frail to do the woodcutting he once relied on to make a living. He tries to grow enough to eat on the land around his home, but erratic rain makes it difficult.

"I have nothing. On the days I get food, I eat, and on the days I don't, I endure."

He lives alone in a mud hut. His wife divorced him after he went to prison, and their children went to live with his mother. They dropped out of school because the family could not pay the fees. Kololo says they were not allowed to visit him in prison. When he was released, they barely remembered him, especially his youngest.

"They were too young. Only now are they starting to regain the memory that 'this is our father who disappeared'," he says. "If it weren't for my mother, my children might have died."

For much of our time together, Kololo is remarkably upbeat. He trusts that his lawyers and God will deliver him justice. But when we talk about the Met, his demeanour shifts.

"I am extremely angry with the police," he says. "I'm also angry with the Kenyan Police. They collaborated to incriminate me. What [Hibberd] said destroyed my entire life and my children's lives."

The Met has not apologised to Kololo or admitted wrongdoing. The force is contesting his compensation claim, which his lawyers say could take years to resolve.

"These people falsely accused me. Do I not deserve something?" he asks.

The Met told the BBC that neither they nor Hibberd wanted to comment on Kololo's claim, but it said: "Our thoughts are with Mr Kololo, Mrs Tebbutt, her family and all those who have been affected by this terrible crime. The Metropolitan Police remains committed to supporting the Kenyan authorities in any way that may be possible, in order to get justice for Mrs Tebbutt and her late husband."

Preetha Gopalan, Reprieve's head of UK litigation, describes the Met's behaviour in Kololo's case as "egregious".

"They've spent 10 years trying to evade accountability in every way possible, now dragging him through the courts," she says. "It's possible for them to do the right thing, but they are unwilling, and so this ordeal continues to haunt Kololo and his family."

"Even if I get a billion shillings, I will never be the same," Kololo says. "But if I get the justice I deserve, I can help my children and take care of myself when I am an old man."

Additional reporting by Ed Habershon

News.title: NHS boss warns of 'horrible spike' in flu as hospital admissions surge
News.content:
Sir Ciaran Devane, chief executive of the NHS Alliance, representing employers, said: "While the flu season is clearly hitting earlier this year and could add to the strain on NHS services heading into another difficult winter, we are yet to see how or when it will peak.

"The NHS has already had to deal with the challenge of heatwaves this summer, so this could pile yet more pressure on already squeezed services."

Suzanna McDonald urged people to get vaccinated, saying thousands of people die from the flu every year.

Flu levels are expected to increase further as Christmas approaches and people start socialising indoors more.

McDonald also called on those who are ill with respiratory symptoms to practise good hand hygiene by washing hands with warm soapy water, cough and sneeze into elbow or into a tissue, and to stay at home in bed and avoid anyone at much higher risk from catching diseases.

Meanwhile, it emerged that just a little over a third of toddlers in England have had a vaccine so far this autumn on the NHS.

Two and three-year-olds can have the vaccine, given as a nasal spray, for free at GP surgeries and some community pharmacies.

But the UKHSA said just 39% of those eligible had taken up the offer.

School age children usually have the vaccine at school, with a catch-up available in pharmacies from 1 December for those who missed it.

McDonald said: "Please don't dismiss the importance of a flu vaccine for your children.

"It will help keep them out of hospital and even save lives."

This time last year an early increase in flu cases caused real concern across the NHS.

The virus was spreading sooner than expected and the fear was that the numbers would continue climbing right through the always challenging Christmas and New Year period.

As it happened the outbreak peaked early and the bleakest predictions did not become reality.

This time hospital admissions with flu patients are a little higher than 12 months ago after another early surge materialised.

Once again, officials do not know when the peak might be reached.

Adding to the challenges is an increase over the last year in patient numbers with a range of illnesses and conditions, partly explained by the ageing population. That means even more pressure on hospitals and their staff.

A bad flu winter could create significant problems.

News.title: 'We have no interest in hearing from Huw Edwards', Downing Street says
News.content:
The prime minister's spokesperson has said broadcasters must "act responsibly" and that "we have no interest in hearing" what Huw Edwards has to say, following a backlash against new interviews with the disgraced former BBC News presenter.

Edwards, who was convicted in 2024 for making indecent images of children, has been interviewed for a Channel 4 documentary plus a podcast by the Observer and Tortoise Media.

"Our thoughts first and foremost will be with the victims of child sexual abuse and exploitation. We have no interest in hearing what he has to say," a Downing Street spokesperson said.

"There are extremely serious crimes and anyone convicted of them must face the consequences of their actions."

The No 10 spokesperson added that broadcasters "are expected to act responsibly and have appropriate regards to their audiences when making decisions".

Pressed on whether the prime minister believed Channel 4 had not acted responsibly, they said: "Channel 4 is editorially independent and decisions about individual programmes and contributors are a matter for them."

During the court case, Edwards admitted three counts of making indecent images of children. That involved having 41 images and videos, which were sent to him on WhatsApp â including some showing a victim aged between seven and nine.

Earlier, Environment Minister Emma Hardy said the plan by Channel 4 made her feel "sick", telling LBC, external it was giving a platform to "someone who is on the Sex Offenders Register".

"That platform doesn't exist for his child victims, does it?... It's not something I could support, and it's definitely not something I'd be watching."

Channel 4 has defended the programme, telling the BBC a "highly experienced director", Patrick Forbes, held Edwards to account with "no questions off limits, revealing his account of what led to his offending and very public downfall".

News.title: 'It's impossible': Spain's young people on housing ahead of Sunday's election
News.content:
Housing has been the biggest issue for voters ahead of Spain's general election on Sunday, with millions of people protesting across the country in recent weeks over a lack of affordable homes.

Final opinion polls suggest the conservative People's Party will receive the most votes and that the right-wing Vox party is set to enter the national government for the first time. It would mean an end to Socialist prime minister Pedro SÃ¡nchez's eight years in power.

Europe correspondent Nick Beake speaks to a young couple from Valencia, who have been kept apart due to high rents in their city.

News.title: Fury cleared to fight Joshua after wife retracts schizophrenia claim
News.content:
Tyson Fury has been medically cleared to fight Anthony Joshua in December after the bout was put in jeopardy by claims of a schizophrenia diagnosis.

Fury, 38, spoke of his mental health struggles in a Netflix documentary which was released on Friday, with his wife, Paris, saying he had been diagnosed with schizophrenia.

But Paris has since retracted that statement, saying he "doesn't have this condition" and Netflix have edited the remarks out of their film.

The British Boxing Board of Control (BBBoC) told BBC Sport: "Tyson Fury has been cleared to box on 11 December."

Fury faces Joshua, 37, in a long overdue all-British heavyweight contest at Cardiff's Principality Stadium in the early hours of 12 December.

Originally, the Netflix documentary featured the Furys recalling his admission to hospital in June 2016 with a suspected heart attack.

Doctors said he had suffered an anxiety attack. He was diagnosed with schizophrenia after he left hospital, according to the film.

The NHS describes schizophrenia as a form of psychosis, and symptoms can include hallucinations, delusions and muddled thoughts and speech.

Under regulation 8.1(b) of the British Boxing Board of Control's 2026 rules and regulations, schizophrenia is among the conditions that "may preclude" a boxer from obtaining a first licence, while for an existing licence holder the board "may take such action as in its absolute discretion as it sees fit".

On Thursday, the BBBoC general secretary Robert Smith told BBC Sport that it was "in the process of dealing with the matter" and that it was "confident he [Tyson Fury] will be absolutely fine".

News.title: Dec Donnelly says I'm a Celebrity tension 'became much bigger deal than it should have'
News.content:
Frostrup apologised during an amicable conversation on Tuesday, and Odudu accepted, explaining it was "triggering" because "it's a strong word to use in casual scenarios, particularly towards black women".

On their podcast, Hanging Out with Ant and Dec, Donnelly said tensions in camp started "surprisingly early".

"From day one cooking was tense and then it obviously came to a head with AJ and Mariella, and it spilled over to breakfast the next morning," he said.

McPartlin added: "You have 12 hungry mouths to feed and you and your sous chef, the other chef, are cooking and everyone is stood around looking at them. The pressure is quite a lot."

Donnelly continued: "When you are there, and so much of your life revolves around that mealtime, it's the only meal of the day you really get that isn't rice and beans.

"There is a lot of pressure and obviously Mariella was feeling that pressure.

"AJ wanted to come in and help and it all came to a head, and maybe because there was so much pressure and because it was so important, Mariella maybe didn't handle it very well around the campfire when she was cooking, and it spilled over into the next day - and it became a much bigger deal than it should have done."

He said the "most important thing" was that "the two ladies were able to sit down and drew a line under it, they were adult enough to sit there, talk it through, and move on together. If more people did that the world would be a much better place".

McPartlin agreed, saying: "If some of our leaders did that, the world would be a better place."

News.title: Police officers discovered Chloe Mitchell's remains in bins, court hears
News.content:
A police officer told Belfast Crown Court on Friday that when he was carrying out house-to-house enquiries in James Street, a resident apologised for a smell coming from her bin.

The officer said as he and a constable walked across an alleyway he noticed a very strong smell and went back to the resident's home and looked in her bin.

He said when he opened the bin it was "full to the brim" and there were maggots and a bad smell which left him struggling not to vomit.

The officer said he then came across another bin which had flies coming out of it.

A crime scene investigator recounted to the court how she had searched two of the bins and found body parts inside them in black bin liners.

Her evidence was followed by evidence from another crime scene investigator who examined the inside of Rainey's flat on 8 June, the day Rainey was arrested.

He told the court he had seized a number of items including a duvet, protein container and tracksuit bottoms which were all stained with suspected blood, as well as a knife in a sheath.

The following day he returned and seized more items including black bags and a roll of masking tape.

News.title: Tube strike ends but more dates set for December
News.content:
The first in a series of 24-hour strikes on the London Underground has ended, with more industrial action planned for December, January and February.

Tube drivers from the Rail, Maritime and Transport (RMT) union walked out at noon on Thursday, with workers ending their action at noon on Friday.

The strike action was the result of a dispute between the union and Transport for London (TfL) over the changing terms and conditions attached to the option of a four or five day week.

On Friday, six Underground lines were suspended or part-suspended, and five others experienced delays. Disruption was forecast to last until 18:00 GMT "as services start to recover".

News.title: UK to pay 'participation' fee to deliver EU deals
News.content:
The UK will pay a "participation fee" to the EU as part of the deals agreed by Andy Burnham, according to legal documents.

The surcharge will go towards the running costs of EU agencies and systems required to deliver two of the agreements unveiled by the prime minister last week.

It will be paid in addition to a contribution towards costs that broadly mirrors how EU members contribute to the bloc's shared budget, the documents show.

The government has sought to contrast the financial costs of the deals against their overall effect on the economy, which it estimates will receive an eventual boost by billions a year due to increased trade.

The government is yet to publish an estimate of overall additional costs, but officials said they expected them to be in the low tens of millions per year and "massively outweighed" by predicted economic gains.

British ministers had already said they were prepared to pay towards administrative costs required to implement deals to re-link the UK to the EU's carbon trading regime, and align Britain with the EU's food standards.

Now, details of how the payments will be calculated have been revealed in treaties to deliver the two agreements, which are meant to take effect during 2028.

Legal text for a third agreement agreed last week, on youth visas for 18 to 31 year olds, is expected to be published in the coming days.

News.title: Rape charge for most 'swiped-right' man on Tinder
News.content:
A man who was once described as "the most swiped-right man on Tinder" is due in court charged with rape following an alleged attack at The Groucho Club in central London.

Stefan-Pierre Tomlin, 36, who in 2017 was said to be the most coveted man on the dating app, is due at Southwark Crown Court on Monday also charged with two counts of assault by penetration.

It follows a Met Police investigation after a woman reported she had been raped inside the private members' club in Soho on 13 November 2024.

Tomlin, of Brentwood, was arrested in Hertfordshire on suspicion of rape in 2024 and charges were authorised in September this year. He appeared at Southend Magistrates' Court on 2 November.

The Met Police said the woman continued to be supported by specialist officers.

Tomlin, who has 454,000 followers on Instagram, describes himself as a pilot, actor and "most right swiped man on Tinder".

The Groucho Club was opened in 1985 as a more relaxed alternative to traditional gentlemen's clubs and has a long association with celebrities.

The venue was temporarily closed in late 2024 after Westminster City Council suspended its licence following a request from the Met Police but reopened a month later.

News.title: Man City owners should be forced to sell, say clubs
News.content:
The independent commission has yet to decide on a sanction that could range from a fine, to a points deduction, the stripping of past titles, or even expulsion from the league.

But speaking on condition of anonymity, one executive claimed they are among a group of clubs who feel that City's punishment will be irrelevant unless the owners are also forced to sell. They added that anything less will make them question why they are funding the regulator through a levy.

In comments that reveal the level of anger felt by other clubs, another source claimed the rule breaches had undermined the league's credibility, and that they would not be able to draw a line under the scandal and move on if the owners were allowed to stay. The club were found guilty of inflating revenues and disguising losses by Â£900m through "sham" commercial arrangements.

Manchester City's owners are Abu Dhabi United Group - a private investment company belonging to United Arab Emirates vice-president and deputy Prime Minister Sheikh Mansour.

The official - who also spoke anonymously - said that clubs had been asked by the Premier League to refrain from publicly revealing their views on sanctions, and let the process run its course, although some are said to have privately made their opinions clear to IFR officials. They acknowledged that some clubs were less opinionated about a punishment.

Other clubs the BBC approached declined to comment, or said they were willing for the independent commission panel and IFR to reach their own conclusions following the publication of the commission's ruling in September.

But the fact that some clubs want the unprecedented sanction of a forced sale will put pressure on Kogan to mete out the harshest penalty possible in what is being seen as a defining test of the watchdog just over a year after it was established.

It also comes amid mounting questions over whether wider UAE trade and investment in UK projects could be impacted by such a move. In September, Prime Minister Andy Burnham was criticised for saying he would be "really concerned" if the scandal led to City's owners selling the club, adding that "they have been such a huge partner in the building of modern Manchester".

When approached, the IFR declined to comment. But Kogan has consistently said that the IFR will not be influenced by any political pressure.

Earlier this week he told a parliamentary committee that the watchdog would not be afraid to investigate City's hierarchy and take action, depending on the outcome of the appeal.

"Forget the name of the club, forget the size of the club, forget the scale of the issue. We cannot simply ignore our statutory duties in relation to a club because it happens to be of a certain size," Kogan said.

"We absolutely will have to take the appropriate action as laid out in the legislation, depending on the circumstances as they come to us, which are the evidence that's been presented and collated by the independent commission of the Premier League and by any judgement that takes place on that evidence through an appeal.

"But in one sense, the evidence has already been judged by those cases having been found guilty, so we will absolutely have the stomach to do so... assuming those circumstances are triggered, if we don't act, what is the purpose of having a football regulator?"

News.title: Five Gladiators will not return for new BBC series
News.content:
Five Gladiators stars will not be returning to the BBC television show for its upcoming series, it is understood.

Athena, Comet, Bionic, Phantom and Cyclone will not be featured when the show returns in 2027.

A spokesperson for the production said the departing cast members "remain part of the wider Gladiators family" and are taking part in the ongoing arena tour, which comes to an end in December.

Gladiators relaunched on the BBC in 2024, having originally been aired on ITV from 1992 until 2000, and then on Sky between 2008 and 2009.

A spokesperson for Gladiators said: "We would like to thank our incredible Superhuman athletes for their contribution to the success and power of the Gladiators TV show.

"While they will not be appearing in Series 4, they remain part of the wider Gladiators family, and you can currently see them across the remaining shows in the UK Gladiator Arena Tour 2026."

Athena, real name Karenjeet Kaur Bains, 30, is a powerlifter and former track and field athlete, while Comet, real name, Ella-Mae Rayner, 31, is a former elite-level gymnast.

Cyclone is 25-year-old Irish powerlifter Lystus Ebosele.

Bionic is the alter ego of 30-year-old body builder Matty Campbell, while Phantom is Toby Olubi, 39, who competed for Team GB in the bobsled at the 2018 Winter Olympics.

The upcoming series is due to introduce the first celebrity Gladiator, former England rugby union international and Celebrity Traitors star Joe Marler, who will use the name Mauler.

In June, the BBC said the series will return in 2027, hosted by father and son duo Bradley and Barney Walsh.

A celebrity special will also be broadcast over Christmas, featuring Big Brother presenter and I'm A Celebrity campmate AJ Odudu, TV presenter Chris Ramsey, social media star George Clarke and comedian Sara Pascoe.

News.title: Beach attacker sentenced to 10 years after victim, 17, loses leg in bank holiday stabbing
News.content:
A man whose unprovoked knife attack on a 17-year-old boy caused the victim to lose his leg has been sentenced to 10 and a half years.

Idris Ahmed, 19, from Riverside in Cardiff, attacked the teenager on Barry Island beach on bank holiday Monday, on 25 May. He previously denied grievous bodily harm with intent, and possessing a knife, but changed his plea to guilty during the trial.

The victim, who cannot be named because of a court order relating to his age, had to have his leg amputated below the knee after the wound became infected.

In a statement read at Newport Crown Court, the victim's mother said she continued to have nightmares, and often ran into her son's room to check on him.

Appearing in the dock wearing a grey top and grey trousers, Ahmed was told by Judge Daniel Williams he would be sentenced to a decade in a young offender insitution, because his "violence" had led to the 17-year-old losing his leg.

"The consequences of your action can only be understood by [the victim] and his family," the judge said.

Angharad Jones, prosecuting, said the victim suffered life-changing injuries after Ahmed attacked him "without warning". She said the victim had acted "as a peacemaker" between the group Ahmed was socialising with and those in his own party after some friction broke out between them.

The victim previously told the jury he had bled heavily and fallen in and out of consciousness immediately after the stabbing.

The 17-year-old fell to the ground immediately after the attack and looked pale, saying: "I am going. I feel myself going", the court previously heard.

He was airlifted to hospital where he underwent four surgeries, but despite several transfusions, doctors noticed that oxygen was not flowing properly to the lower leg.

The jury heard it was determined the teenager needed an amputation of the lower half of his leg.

Following the stabbing, Ahmed fled the scene and discarded the knife close by, an act seen by an eyewitness who later identified him in an identity parade.

He was also captured fleeing the scene by a woman who was taking selfies on the beach with her partner.

Before he threw the knife, Ahmed was heard saying: "I need to dash this."

News.title: Ofcom cancels Arabic news channel’s licence after Houthi leader livestream
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

An Arabic-language news channel has lost its UK broadcasting licence after livestreaming a speech by the Houthi leader Abdul Malik al-Houthi.

Ofcom found that Lualua TV was “not fit and proper” to hold the licence after it broadcast a 45-minute speech by the Houthi leader on its website, which Ofcom found glorified antisemitic hate speech.

The regulator began its investigation in October 2026 after viewing an English translation of the speech by al-Houthi, which it said featured a banner on screen with the statement: “God is Greater. Death to America. Death to Israel. Curse the Jews. Victory to Islam.”

The regulator's report states that he repeatedly characterised the October 7 2023 attack on Israel by Hamas in positive terms.

Referring to the attacks carried out by Hamas, he described them as an “important, great and blessed operation”, a “historical milestone”, a “major leap forward”, and a “successful, powerful, meticulously planned, and expertly executed operation”.

He also expressed support for Hezbollah, a proscribed terrorist group.

Ofcom said it considers that the speech as livestreamed contained material that constituted hate speech and abusive and derogatory treatment towards Jewish people.

open image in gallery The regulator’s decision comes after a 45-minute livestream on the channel’s website of a speech by Abdul Malik al-Houthi ( EPA )

The regulator requested a copy of the livestream from Shell For Media Productions.

It identified differences between the first recording provided to Ofcom and the full version of the livestream, including that the banner had either been removed or obscured.

It stated: “Upon review Ofcom identified significant gaps in the material supplied, including recordings whose durations were substantially shorter than the periods indicated by their filenames and several periods for which no recordings had been provided.”

Ofcom also raised concerns about posts on the channel's social media accounts which it felt encouraged support for “proscribed terrorist organisations”.

The regulator also noted social media posts by the channel which expressed support for Hezbollah leaders.

Lualua TV is primarily focused on Bahrain.

It is available to view in Britain via livestream on its website, and its licence was provided by Shells For Media Productions Limited.

Although Lualua TV did not broadcast on British TV, the removal of its licence means it will not be able to commence broadcasting in the UK under that licence in the future.

It does not prevent the continued livestream of Lualua TV to audiences online.

Cristina Nicolotti Squires, Ofcom's broadcasting and media group director, said: "Freedom of expression is something we guard fiercely in this country, and the bar for action against broadcasters is rightly set very high."

“Following a detailed investigation and taking account of a wide range of evidence, we have concluded that Lualua TV is not fit and proper to hold a UK broadcasting licence, and so have revoked it with immediate effect.”

Shell For Media Productions could not be reached for comment.

News.title: Ex-Iceland goalkeeper Ingvar Jonsson who was part of Euro 2016 squad that stunned England dies aged 37
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Ingvar Jonsson, the former Iceland goalkeeper who was part of the squad that defeated England at the 2016 European Championship, has died at the age of 37.

His former club Víkingur announced his death on Thursday. The team did not provide a cause of death, although Jonsson had reportedly been diagnosed with cancer earlier this year.

In a statement, the Icelandic club said: "It is with great sorrow and deep sadness that we announce that our dear friend and teammate Ingvar Jonsson, goalkeeper for Víkingur, passed away on Wednesday, November 25, in the arms of his loved ones."

They added: "The club and all of Víkingur are thinking of his family and loved ones. We send them our deepest condolences."

Jonsson served as an unused substitute during Euro 2016, when Iceland created one of the greatest shocks in tournament history by knocking England out in the round of 16. The team were later eliminated by France in the quarter-finals.

open image in gallery Iceland stunned England at Euro 2016 (Jonathan Brady/PA) ( PA Wire )

Paying tribute on X, European football’s governing body Uefa wrote: "We extend our deepest condolences to Ingvar’s family, friends and former team-mates. Our thoughts are with them at this difficult time."

Jonsson earned eight international caps for Iceland, having made his first squad back in 2012. He had to wait another two years before making his first appearance for his country in a friendly against Belgium.

His final cap for Iceland came in 2019, but he continued to make the squad through until 2022.

His club career saw him start at Njardvik in his homeland before moving to Norwegian outfit IK Start in 2015. He would go on to play for Sandnes Ulf and Sandefjord prior to leaving Norway in 2018 to join Danish side Viborg.

After two years in Denmark, Jonsson returned to Iceland to play for Vikingur and remained at the club until his passing.

News.title: Manhunt launched after dismembered cat found ritualistically placed in Malibu park
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

A dismembered cat was found at Malibu Bluffs Park, prompting a $10,000 reward offer for information leading to a conviction.

Park visitors reported the discovery, and the Mountains Recreation and Conservation Authority was notified on Nov. 18.

“As described by park visitors, rangers and staff who responded found a dismembered domestic cat, ritualistically placed with candles and other imagery,” the Santa Monica Mountains Conservancy said in a Facebook post on Wednesday.

A view of the Pacific Ocean seen from Malibu Bluffs Park ( City of Malibu )

Rangers recovered evidence at the scene, the MRCA said.

The animal's remains were transferred to the Los Angeles County Department of Animal Care and Control for examination.

The authority is offering $10,000 for information leading to the identification, arrest and conviction of the person or persons responsible for what it called the atrocity.

The reward offer expires on Jan. 31.

A sergeant with the Los Angeles County Sheriff's Department's Malibu/Lost Hills Station confirmed to City News Service on Thursday that the MRCA was handling the investigation.
