News.title: eBay discount codes for November 2026
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Today’s top eBay discount codes and deals

Whether you're after a new gadget or a pre-loved designer bag, eBay is one of the UK's most popular online marketplaces for a reason. With millions of listings from top brands and individual sellers, there is a wide variety to shop, including everyday essentials, fashion, beauty, tech and even one-of-a-kind pieces. Whilst eBay is already known for its competitive pricing, The Independent’s team of deal experts has been hard at work finding the latest eBay discount codes and offers to help you save even more.

eBay Black Friday deals

This Black Friday, eBay is offering up to 80 per cent off selected products across tech, home appliances, fashion, homeware and more. Plus, using the eBay Black Friday discount code above, you can save an extra 20 per cent at checkout.

Some of the standout deals from the 2026 Black Friday sale includes 47 per cent off the Dyson cyclone v10 vacuum, over half price off the De'Longhi coffee machine magnifica evo and 44 per cent off Dr. Martens Polley Mary Jane school shoes – and that’s before applying the extra 20 per cent off code.

How we source eBay promo codes

We work closely with the team at eBay to bring our readers the latest deals and offers. Our team of expert deal hunters is always on the lookout for ways to help you save on your shopping, whether it’s discounted refurbished items or flash sales on brand new products.

All eBay promo codes and offers are manually verified by our in-house team before sharing, and expired offers removed immediately.

Best ways to save at eBay

Daily deals

Ebay’s daily deals section is packed with limited-time discounts and promotions across a range of categories, often with free postage. From security systems and robot vacuums to slippers and heated blankets, there’s no end to what you can find. These deals are hand-picked and usually run for just 24 to 48 hours, so if you spot something you like, don’t hang around. Discounts can go up to 80 per cent, so it’s well worth a scroll through if you’re looking for a bargain.

View the eBay sales page

The sale section has longer-running deals, split into categories for easy navigation. Expect to save anywhere between 15 and 50 per cent on almost all shopping categories, from tech and computing to sofas and household essentials, like laundry detergent and personal care. You can often find eBay voucher codes promoted at the top of the page for extra money off.

Shop eBay’s brand outlet

The outlet is another savvy way to find discounted fashion pieces from top brands. Retailers use this space to sell off refurbished pre-loved items and last-season products, with up to 70 per cent off the RRP. Shops that have their own outlet pages include Seasalt Cornwall, River Island, M&S, Sports Direct, Oliver Bonas and many more. If you’re looking for a specific brand, check out the brand directory to see if it has its own outlet store.

The savings don’t stop at fashion, as you can also shop directly from tech brands and retailers like Dyson, Currys and AO, but take advantage of cheaper pricing compared with their main websites.

Shop pre-loved fashion or refurbished items

Ebay also has a dedicated section of pre-loved fashion and designer pieces. Browse a selection of women’s, men’s or children's clothing and accessories, with many items available for less than £20. You can also save up to 60 per cent with ‘imperfects’, which come directly from brands like Ray-Ban, Sweaty Betty and Burberry. These may have small marks or minor imperfections, meaning they cannot be sold at full retail price.

Choosing certified refurbished products over buying brand new is a smart way to save on high-ticket items tech and appliances. Each item is expertly serviced and cleaned before re-listing, with all accessories included. Plus, there’s a minimum 12-month refurbished guarantee, which covers any defects or issues with functionality. You will receive a separate email from eBay with full details of what’s covered, along with contact details – this will also be included in the package.

You can buy pre-loved items direct from some of our favourite tried-and-tested brands such Dyson, Apple, Eufy, Shark and more, with savings of up to 50 per cent compared with buying brand new.

Buyer information

Ebay money-back guarantee

You can shop on eBay with peace of mind and security, as most purchases from the online marketplace are covered by the eBay money-back guarantee. If your item doesn’t arrive, arrives damaged or not as described, you’ll be able to request a refund from the seller. If you don’t hear back in three business days, eBay will step in to support. There is no extra fee for this protection, and it covers the entire purchase price, including shipping costs.

Returns policy

Delivery costs and return policies vary depending on the seller, but many offer free postage and easy returns. You can find full details on the product listing or, to make it even easier, filter your search results to show sellers who offer free postage and packaging or click and collect, as well as free returns.

Reduced buyer protection fee

Ebay’s buyer protection fees give you extra security when purchasing from private sellers. The fee is automatically added to all private purchases and includes 24/7 customer service, encrypted transactions and ensures sellers aren’t paid until after you have received the item. From 17 July, eBay has reduced the buyer protection fee to the following rates:

A flat fee of up to 10p per item

Seven per cent on the first £20

Four per cent on the portion from £20 to £300

Two per cent from £300 to £4,000

There is no fee charged beyond £4,000. For listings that started before the new rate on 17 July, the older rate applies: a 75p flat fee, plus four per cent up to £300 and two per cent from £300 to £4,000.

Give back with eBay charity shops

You can now even do your charity shopping online at stores like Oxfam, Sue Ryder and The British Heart Foundation. Just like high street charity shops, you can browse a wide selection of items, from fashion to furniture, with proceeds supporting a range of causes. You can browse by charity or product category to find thousands of items at bargain prices.

Helpful FAQs

Q How do I redeem an eBay discount code? Once you've found the offer you want to redeem, click the "See code" button and copy the code that appears on your screen. You can now head back to your basket and continue to the checkout. Once you have entered your payment information, you will see a "Vouchers" section where you can paste and apply your code. Q What are eBay voucher codes valid on? Ebay often releases promo codes with savings on selected items, sellers or categories, which we’ll list above. You’ll regularly find a 10 to 15 per cent discount on certain categories or products, such as mobile phones or summer essentials. Payday deals are also a regular occurrence, with up to 20 per cent off. Q Does eBay have a student discount? There are currently no eBay student discounts, however you can still take advantage of the many other offers listed on this page.

Why you can trust us

The Independent has been trusted by shoppers since 1986, helping readers find the best deals and testing products on their behalf. Our team of shopping experts are experienced in sourcing the best offers, discounts and finding the latest sales. We only select deals from brands that we trust and we understand that a great deal isn’t always the one with the highest discount.

Check out our dedicated deals section for the latest deals from your favourite brands

News.title: Why this far-flung national park tucked in the northeast corner of the US is worth a short break
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Floating gently on the calm Atlantic waters of a secluded pebbled cove as the sun beat down, it was impossible not to feel completely at peace.

For a while, there was no one else at this secret beach at the southern tip of Maine’s Acadia National Park, tucked in the Northeast corner of the United States, until a couple of hikers came by and asked how cold the water was — somewhere between 50F - 55F (10C and 13C) that morning.

A local guide who knew all of the hidden trails brought my husband and me to the beauty spot for “saltwater immersion therapy” – a wellness way of saying a cold dip in the sea. After the cold plunge, we were given robes and sipped hot honey and peppermint tea on the beach, feeling totally relaxed. The experience was provided by our accommodation, Terramor, a luxury glamping resort on the fringes of the park.

The concealed beach provided an escape from the crowds Acadia attracts. With 130 miles of stunning hiking trails to explore and 45 miles of carriage roads for cyclists, there’s a reason four million people flock to explore the coastal park every year.

And even in a country where 92 percent of households rely on a vehicle, exploring Acadia is doable, and arguably more enjoyable, without a car. From May through October, the free Island Explorer shuttle runs 12 routes around the island seven days a week.

open image in gallery A secluded cove in Acadia National Park where we enjoyed a cold plunge. The water was somewhere between 10 and 13C (50 - 55F) that morning, and we learned breathing techniques to make the most of the experience ( Rhian Lubin )



Stepping off the bus at the glorious Sand Beach, I couldn’t help but feel a little smug after watching others fight for a space in the packed car park. Although at the mercy of the bus schedule, it was frequent and reliably on time.

Secluded spots are aplenty in the park if you do your research, but the most popular hikes are also worth exploring. Cadillac Mountain is the highest point on the eastern seaboard, for which people get up at 2am to reach the summit to see the sunrise. (Parking permits need to be reserved in advance.) And the notorious Beehive Trail is so popular that a line often forms to scale its steep and narrow cliff face using metal rungs.

Both were too ambitious for our agenda, opting instead for a walk around the iconic Jordan Pond, a glacially formed lake that sits beneath the Bubble Mountains. On the loop, we took a detour and made the steep climb up to Bubble Rock, where the craggy forest trail soon gave way to sweeping views of Jordan Pond and, on a clear day, the surrounding islands. (Though beware: climbing back down was an experience). For a quieter hike, the Gorham Mountain trail that runs close to the coast is a great alternative. We only passed a handful of people on the trail and the views were spectacular.

open image in gallery A walk around Jordan Pond, a popular and easy hike in the national park, offers some of the best views in Acadia ( Visit Maine )

The town of Bar Harbor is a solid base for a few days of exploring Acadia, with bus services departing regularly from the Village Green. Main Street is lined with more souvenir shops than anyone could ever need, but there are plenty of bars and restaurants to kick back with a lobster roll and a blueberry ale — Maine staples.

Bar Harbor excels at seafood. Our favorites were The Barnacle for oysters, McKay’s Public House for seafood risotto, and Side Street Cafe’s lobster mac & cheese, followed by its famous blueberry pie. For an upscale dinner fit for a president, snag a reservation at Havana, a Latin-American restaurant. It proudly displays a photograph of Barack and Michelle Obama’s “date night” circa 2010 in the window, and is considered one of the best restaurants on the island.

open image in gallery With 130 miles of stunning hiking trails to explore and 45 miles of carriage roads for cyclists, there’s a reason four million people flock to explore Maine’s Acadia National Park every year ( Susan Cole Kelly )



There’s more nature to explore near town. At low tide, Bar Island is accessible for a short window on foot via the sandbar, a natural walkway that disappears when the tide comes rushing back in. Keep an eye on the time. Locals shared tales of tourists who either got stranded on the island for nine hours until the next low tide, or had to catch a lift back to the mainland from one of the lobster boats for a hefty fee.

From the amount of moose-themed merchandise Bar Harbor’s souvenir shops stock, you’d be forgiven for thinking you might spot one in Acadia. But the best chance of encountering wildlife is at sea. We saw bald eagles, ospreys, and grey seals on a two-hour sail aboard the Mary Todd schooner. On a kayaking trip around Bar Island and the Porcupine Islands (Coastal Kayaking Tours Inc.), there were more bald eagle sightings, and a curious harbor seal pup popped up close to our kayaks.

open image in gallery The town of Bar Harbor as seen from Bar Island, accessible for a short window on foot via the sandbar ( Visit Maine )

Rhian Lubin was a guest of Visit Maine

How to do it

Bangor is a short flight from New York airports. Flights from other US airports depart daily during peak season, including Boston Logan, O’Hare, and Washington, D.C. Return flights start from £224 ($297) approx.

If you’re not renting a car, catch the bus from Bangor Airport to Bar Harbor (May to October, Monday to Friday only). Alternatively, dozens of local taxi operators are listed on the Bangor Airport website; just make sure to book your return journey in advance. Uber and Lyft also operate in the Bangor area.

Where to stay

Terramor Outdoor Resort

Opened in 2020, Terramor is camping for those who want to connect with nature while still enjoying the luxuries of a hotel. And it’s a real treat. The canvas tents sleep solo travelers, couples, or families, and are furnished with soft comfortable beds, extra blankets, and heaters as it can get chilly at night. The bathroom has a double walk-in shower and his-and-hers sinks. Tents have electricity and wifi, a high-end electric kettle for tea or coffee, and a cooler.

open image in gallery One of the luxury tents at Terramor, which sleeps solo travellers, couples and families. At night, roast marshmallows around the fire pit ( Turner PR )

The resort, open seasonally from May through October, has a swimming pool and jacuzzi – perfect for relaxing after a hike. At night, dinner and drinks are served in the main lodge, where guests can unwind playing card games by the roaring fire. The only downside is that the resort does not allow guests to bring food purchased offsite, so you can’t cook at your fire pit. A buffet-style breakfast is included in the daily rate, with muffins, bagels, oatmeal, eggs and fruit.

Terramor arranges guided hikes and saltwater immersion therapy (aka the cold plunge in the Atlantic) for an additional cost. The best part, though, turned out to be free. Thanks to the lack of light pollution, the Acadia area has some of the darkest skies on the East Coast. On our last cloudless night, the stars put on a spectacular show as we roasted marshmallows over the fire.

Prices start from £212 ($280) per night approx

The Pathmaker Hotel

This boutique hotel in downtown Bar Harbor is located on Cottage Street and, despite being just a two-minute walk from the chaos of Main Street, it provides a quiet retreat. Rooms are spacious, and the beds are so comfortable that you’ll likely crash out as soon as your head hits the pillow.

Staff leave freshly-baked cookies at reception in the afternoons, and unlimited complimentary tea, coffee and hot cocoa is available 24/7.

The Pathmaker’s main draw was a slap-up breakfast, included in the room rate (excluding any tips). The menu is wide-ranging, from a plate of scrambled eggs and bacon to apple pie oatmeal and blueberry pancakes. The portions were so generous that we didn’t feel hungry even hours later while in the national park.

Prices start from £113 ($150) per night approx

News.title: Jack Lowden says former Mr Darcy actors sent him a ‘gorgeous’ email after landing Pride and Prejudice role
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Jack Lowden has revealed that Colin Firth and Matthew Macfadyen sent him a “gorgeous” joint email after he landed the part of Mr Darcy in Pride and Prejudice.

The 36-year-old Scottish actor takes on the role in Dolly Alderton's forthcoming Netflix series, playing the reserved love interest to Emma Corrin's Elizabeth Bennet.

Firth played Darcy in the 1995 series adaptation, while Macfadyen took the part in the 2005 film.

The series, based on the Jane Austen novel, also features The Crown actress Olivia Colman and Enola Holmes actor Louis Partridge.

open image in gallery Jack Lowden as Mr Darcy ( PA )

Appearing on The Graham Norton Show, Lowden said the two earlier Darcys contacted him once he had been cast.

He said: “They sent me a joint email which was titled, ‘The audacity sir’.

“It was gorgeous and they went on to give me so much support. They were lovely.”

Lowden described taking on the character as an “honour”, and said the new adaptation is “incredibly faithful to the book and the script is funny and beautiful”.

Discussing how he approached the role, Lowden said: “Colin Firth's and Matthew Macfadyen's portrayals of Darcy are so different from each other that I thought if I watched them enough, I would end up somewhere in the middle.

“Hopefully that's what I have done. It was an honour being asked to follow in those footsteps.”

Lowden is best known for playing River Cartwright, a British MI5 agent, in the hit Apple TV spy thriller Slow Horses.

open image in gallery Colin Firth as Mr Darcy in the BBC adaptation of Pride and Prejudice ( BBC )

In the first season, his character was exiled to Slough House, a dumping ground for agents who made serious mistakes.

The team answers to veteran agent Jackson Lamb, played by Sir Gary Oldman, who frequently clashes with the calculating Diana Taverner, played by Dame Kristin Scott Thomas, who takes over as head of Britain's MI5 secret service in season six.

Lowden said: “I love sneaking in to watch the other actors, particularly Kristin Scott Thomas and Gary Oldman.

“I particularly love watching such great actors making mistakes so I can see how they fix problems. Gary and Kristin have different methods which sometimes collide.”

“They don’t seem to sneak in when I am acting!” he added jokingly.

The Graham Norton Show airs on BBC iPlayer and BBC One on Friday at 10.40pm.

News.title: What shows to see on and off Broadway this holiday season
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Thousands of vacationers will descend on New York City this season, hoping to indulge in holiday cheer. But beyond the traditional holiday markets and ice skating rinks is a bustling theater scene with plenty of options beyond the usual seasonal fare.

The Radio City Christmas Spectacular and The Nutcracker will always delight, along with long-running shows like Wicked or The Lion King. However, there are a plethora of other options to choose from, both on and off Broadway, that you may not have heard about.

Hollywood royalty and stage veterans alike can be found on stages across Manhattan this holiday season. Julia Louis-Dreyfus is making her long-awaited Broadway debut alongside Allison Janney, while Tom Hiddleston returns to the Main Stem for the first time since 2019, with a fresh take on a Shakespeare classic.

There are also dozens of Off-Broadway productions that are worthy and deserving of attention as tourists descend upon the city around the holidays.

To help you decide what to see, find picks from The Independent’s New York-based Culture team below.

open image in gallery Billy Crystal is back on Broadway in ‘860’ ( Avery Brunkus )

860 (Broadway)

Starring: Billy Crystal

Where: Imperial Theatre (249 West 45th Street)

When: Through February 14, 2027

What: Crystal’s new one-man show about losing his home and his best friend in 2025

The Pacific Palisades fire may have claimed Crystal’s home, but it didn’t alter his sense of humor. The themes of loss and resilience are the core of Crystal’s latest one-man show. Through the 100-minute run time, audiences are treated to a handful of Crystal’s stories tied to memorabilia that was hanging in his office until all was lost to the fire. Despite the seemingly sad subject matter, the show is humorous, of course, but also incredibly heartfelt. His belongings may be gone, but Crystal proves the memories and anecdotes are more meaningful.

open image in gallery ‘Paranormal Activity’ has arrived on Broadway after runs in several other cities ( Matthew Murphy )

Paranormal Activity (Broadway)

Starring: Cher Álvarez and Travis A. Knight

Where: August Wilson Theatre (245 West 52nd Street)

When: Through February 28, 2027

What: A new play penned by Levi Holloway following a couple who recently moved to escape something dark that occurred in their former home

When you think of Broadway, a few images might come to mind: ensembles bursting into song, dramatic soliloquies delivered in a spotlight, or tear-jerking 11 o’clock power ballads. An image you might not immediately think of? Being repeatedly scared out of your seat. But that’s exactly what’s happening in the first-ever Broadway mounting of Paranormal Activity.

Holloway’s play lands in New York after engagements in England, Chicago, Los Angeles, Washington, D.C. and Boston, among others. Audiences need not be familiar with the 2007 film to understand what’s happening in this stage version; just be prepared to be spooked!

open image in gallery Matthew Pomeroy, Darcy Oake, Gabriella Lester, and James More in 'Now You See Me Live' on Broadway ( Jeremy Daniel )

Now You See Me Live (Broadway)

Starring: Gabriella Lester, James More, Darcy Oake and Matthew Pomeroy

Where: Al Hirschfeld Theatre (302 West 45th Street)

When: Through January 3, 2027

What: A fast-paced variety show filled with magic, illusions, and more

I’m not usually one for the gimmicky limited-run holiday shows that pop up on Broadway stages each year between November and January. However, Now You See Me Live was genuinely mind-bending and enjoyable (and has almost nothing to do with the 2013 film of the same name aside from a handful of references to the Four Horsemen). The stunts and illusions were jaw-dropping, and the sleight-of-hand magic tricks were done without a hitch. Expect a complete spectacle.

open image in gallery Liza Colón-Zayas, Adrian Martinez, Francis Guinan, and K. Todd Freeman in 'Downstate' ( Emilio Madrid )

Downstate (Broadway)

Starring: K. Todd Freeman, Francis Guinan, Thomas Sadoski and Liza Colón-Zayas

Where: Booth Theatre (222 West 45th Street)

When: Through February 14, 2027

What: A new play by Bruce Norris that grapples with questions of humanity

Full disclosure: this is not an upbeat play. It’s not even a comedy. Nothing about it screams “Happy Holidays!” It is deep, dark, and disturbing — dealing with moral and ethical questions around sex offenders, their victims, and how the public (and government) handle these cases — but also one of the best productions of the year.

The cast delivers incredible performances across the board, especially Colón-Zayas as a peace officer working with several sex offenders living in a group home. It’s a gutsy and grounded performance in a play that will actually twist your heart and your stomach. It is uncomfortable at times, but the discomfort is the byproduct of excellent writing, direction, and acting, all combining to deliver one of the great theatrical experiences of 2026.

open image in gallery The company of 'Traitorz: The Unauthorized Musical Parody' playing through January ( Jeremy Daniel )

Traitors: The Unauthorized Musical Parody (Off-Broadway)

Starring: Dylan Adler, Sean McManus, Rachel Schur, Daniel Barrett, Becca Kötte and Jeffrey Omura

Where: St. Luke's Theatre (308 West 46th Street)

When: Through January 31, 2027

What: A hilarious spoof of the hit NBC and Peacock series

My face still hurts from smiling after seeing this laugh-out-loud parody. It’s a dreamy combination for theater lovers and reality TV buffs alike, filled with pop culture references galore. The cast delivers uncanny impressions of personalities including Liza Minnelli, Jennifer Coolidge and Britney Spears, to the point that even if the reference they’re speaking or singing about is lost on you, you’ll wind up laughing along anyway. The original songs — some clearly influenced by existing musical theater and pop tunes — are catchier than those in several original Broadway productions I’ve seen recently. It’s pure comedy, schtick and fun. And who couldn’t use a bit more of that?

News.title: Australia embarrassed by remarkable Overton spell
News.content:
So often English cricketers have left the “Gabbatoir” looking dazed and confused after yet another horror show. This time, it was an insipid Australian side’s turn to be embarrassed and overawed by a remarkable showing from Jamie Overton. It was a batting display as ugly as anything Australian cricket has served up in the sandpaper civil war, which rumbles on.

As Australia were bowled for a meagre 108, Overton recorded figures of five for 12, the second-best in T20 by an Englishman and the best by any man in T20 fixtures between these old rivals. That was Australia’s lowest T20 total against England since the sides’ first meeting, ahead of the 2005 Ashes, when they were bundled out for 79 chasing 180. Back then, T20 was a bit of fun, now it is big business, and this was altogether more chastening.

A combination of rain, which delayed play three times and led to a DLS-reduced target, and Riley Meredith, who was gifted three wickets, meant that England’s batting lacked the freewheeling fun of their bowling performance.

But the chase was a formality, and England won by seven wickets. The Gabba was just a third full, with some hardy Barmy Army types in fine voice as England celebrated their win. With England leading the five-match series 2-1, it is hard to imagine too many Aussies racing to buy tickets for the final two games in Sydney and Canberra. England are flying out Rehan Ahmed and the uncapped Glamorgan batsman Asa Tribe as they manage a long list of absentees, which will include the South Africa-bound captain Harry Brook and keeper Jordan Cox by Canberra.

News.title: Colombia earthquake triggers surge in malaria cases
News.content:
Cases of malaria in rural Colombia have surged after a devastating earthquake left towns and villages in ruins, according to local charities.

Colombia has recorded over 74,360 cases of malaria this year, 40 per cent of which have been concentrated in Chocó – the epicentre of the earthquake which struck in August, killing at least 335 people and injuring 4,500 more.

The region has seen a 46 per cent surge in cases of the mosquito-borne disease compared to last year, up from 23,757 cases in 2025 to 34,759 cases so far in 2026.

Malaria can be very serious at any age, but it is the most dangerous for young children under five. If left untreated, it can become a medical emergency in as little as 24 hours and result in death.

While Africa accounts for around 94 per cent of global malaria cases, an estimated half a million infections occur in South America every year, mostly in the countries surrounding the Amazon basin – Colombia, Brazil, and Venezuela.

The earthquake hit at 7.4 on the Richter scale and was the strongest Colombia has seen in a decade, destroying roads and buildings. It hit during the rainy season, and water has collected in and around destroyed buildings, allowing mosquitoes, which breed in stagnant water, to survive and multiply, according to Save the Children.

Following the earthquake, thousands of people in Chocó have moved into overcrowded and unsanitary shelters after their homes were destroyed, increasing the spread of infectious diseases including malaria – which is carried between people via infected mosquitoes.

“The earthquake has worsened the conditions that favour the transmission of malaria,” Maria Mercedes Liévano, Save the Children’s Country Director in Colombia, told The Telegraph.

“Because we’re now seeing collapsed and damaged homes, families that are sleeping in overcrowded conditions out in the open, and are dealing with a health network that is overwhelmed,” Ms Liévano added.

News.title: Milk of human kindness: Brazil exports its donor breastfeeding programme worldwide
News.content:
When baby Luis Miguel was born in Guarapuava, Brazil, in February, he was unresponsive.

He had inhaled meconium, a newborn’s first stool, during delivery. It then entered his lungs and blocked his airways. Doctors at Hospital de Caridade São Vicente de Paulo resuscitated and intubated the baby boy, saving his life. He spent the next three weeks in the hospital’s neonatal unit.

His mother, 25-year-old sales assistant Luany Thainara Machado, could not produce enough breast milk and so hers was supplemented with that of a woman she had never met.

“While it might not make much sense for a mother to do this under normal circumstances it becomes very important when the need arises,” she said.

Nine months later, Luis Miguel is healthy and Machado is grateful that donor milk was able to support her son when he needed it most; so much so that today she donates 2.5 litres of her now plentiful supply every week. “Being able to help other mothers and other babies today, it feels really good,” she told The Telegraph, bouncing Luis Miguel on her knee as she spoke.

News.title: One person had a worse night than United keeper – the wretched referee
News.content:
Few Manchester United fans expected a positive result from Mauricio Pochettino’s first game in charge at Anfield, but the bar will not be set so low for Sporting in the Champions League this evening.

The manner of the 4-0 defeat against Liverpool, even accounting for Leny Yoro’s early red card, was dispiriting but not unexpected. The next few weeks will reveal how Pochettino intends to get a grip on the job.

When it comes to United’s Champions League prospects, the comeback win over Roma at the tail-end of Michael Carrick’s tenure made their position less perilous, but avoiding outright elimination is the first target.

United are 19th in the table, with the top 24 teams going through. Those between ninth and 24th go into a play-off round before the last 16. After Sporting away, United host RB Leipzig and Bayern Munich before a trip to Villarreal so there are stiff tests to come.

Sporting are well-placed after three wins from four, but their Champions League schedule is rather one-sided: in their final three matches they travel to Roma, before playing Barcelona and Manchester City. They reached the quarter-finals of the competition last season, losing narrowly to Arsenal over two legs.

They are third in their league, having been weakened by the summer sales of Geovany Quenda (to Chelsea), Morten Hjulmand (to Atletico Madrid) and Ousmane Diomande (to Nottingham Forest). The vast majority of goals are scored by Colombian striker Luis Suárez.

Bruno Fernandes, United’s captain, returns to his former club tonight and there is hope Luke Shaw could be back at left-back. Pochettino must decide whether or not to stick with Matthijs de Ligt, who was extremely rusty at Anfield but may need the minutes.

Yoro’s one-game suspension was overturned by the FA, and he would have been available for this one in any case.

News.title: ‘It blocks out the sun’: The toxic dust storms choking Uzbekistan
News.content:
In the early hours of the morning last June, Gulbara Aminova woke up with a violent fit of coughing. The 39-year-old got up to shut her bedroom windows. But as she did, she saw something disturbing outside.

“My car was covered in powder,” says Aminova, a resident of the town of Moynaq in western Uzbekistan. “It was like it had been snowing. But it was the summer.”

The fine dust on her car was far from a picturesque snow scene: it was in fact a toxic mix of salt and sand laced with pesticides and other chemicals, blown in by strong winds during the night. The dirty air had been making it difficult for Aminova and her three children to breathe at night.

For the residents of Moynaq, a former fishing town on the edge of the Aral Sea, these storms have become a public health emergency, with fears that they are behind not only air pollution spikes but high rates of cancer, tuberculosis and other diseases.

“Two of my daughters have asthma,” says Aminova. “I lost my father and my aunt to cancer. There is a lot of sickness here. I think it’s because of the dust.”

Today, sand and dust storms strike as many as a 100 times a year in Uzbekistan, many of them originating in the desiccated wastelands that decades ago were home to the world’s fourth-largest lake.

News.title: Mick Harford: ‘My prostate cancer diagnosis was a shock. As a footballer, I’d felt bulletproof’
News.content:
However, an MRI scan and a PSMA PET scan at UCLH, where I had been referred, showed only a little bit of growth on my prostate, and I was told I would be fine. But, while I was symptomless at the time, within around eight months I was getting up three or four times in the night to go to the toilet, and then feeling the urge to go back again only two minutes later. I instinctively knew something was wrong.

Upon my return to UCLH in December, I was told my PSA was now “very high”, at around 48 ng/mL – far more elevated than the 4.5 ng/mL considered healthy for my age group. Advanced prostate cancer was then confirmed with a biopsy. The first person I told was my son, William, in a phone call from the car at the hospital. It was horrible – it was not just me who would suffer, but my family too. I also needed to tell Luton Town, who were amazing and gave me as much time off work as I needed from my role as assistant manager.

Facing the opponent

My brilliant oncology team immediately had a plan for me. They got me on a course of hormone therapy medications called Enzalutamide and Zoladex, in preparation for me to begin radiation treatment from mid-August. I had 49 sessions over the space of about eight weeks, and it was daunting each time I travelled into London on the train from my home in Harpenden to go underground to the hospital’s Radiotherapy Department.

But I got through it, even with a bit of collateral damage. While my ongoing symptoms are not a pleasant conversation, it’s an important one, because it has affected my life in so many ways. My sleep is disrupted because I still need to get up multiple times during the night to go to the toilet so I can avoid an accident in bed. I also have to wear a nappy every day in case of leakage, and need to be careful when I’m out to ensure I’m close to a toilet.

I’m still on a hormone therapy called Triptorelin to block my testosterone, which feeds the cancer, and takes the form of an injection every six months. As a result, I’m going through the “male menopause”, which is not very nice and can cause tiredness, sleep issues and brain fog. It has given me lots of sympathy for women of my generation.

However, as I approach six years since my diagnosis, I’ve tried to stay proactive as much as possible. The discipline and drive instilled in me as a footballer have come in handy. To be a successful player, you need to stick to a routine. In the same way that I worked hard to ensure my teammates and coaches respected me on the pitch, so I’ve adhered to what all the doctors have advised – including trying to be diligent in terms of lifestyle.

Sports.title: Man Utd files: Why Pochettino staff reckon US stint is key to transforming players and fans get 25% off season tickets
Sports.content:

MAURICIO POCHETTINO hopes his experience as US national head coach will help him get his message across to Manchester United players in shorter spells.

The Argentine is accustomed to working with internationals in short stints between club and country and hopes to bring that approach to Carrington.



Sources say Poch’s staff believe it is the one big positive he can bring from his two years as an international manager.

Poch has introduced lengthy training sessions since arriving last Wednesday, with sources saying he believes his ideas are already starting to sink in.



United have nine games in the next 36 days, including eight in the Prem and a Champions League home match against RB Leipzig.

The former Chelsea and Spurs boss is extremely hands on with players in training and his number two Jesus Perez is his eyes and ears.

Perez will be a regular feature at press conferences and his influence goes well beyond that of an assistant manager.

The Spaniard helps translate Poch’s philosophy into groundwork and will play a key role in man-management and standards.

Huddle up

THE pre-match huddle is back again at United after it was scrapped towards the end of Michael Carrick’s reign.

Bruno Fernandes gathered teammates seconds before kick-off against former club Sporting on Wednesday.

The last time United players had assembled for a huddle was against Tottenham on October 10.

United also posted their full 22-man squad before a Champions League game for the first time this season.

United had not named travelling squads for Atletico or Como and are not obliged to under Uefa regulations, but Poch is relaxed about it.

Season ticket deal struck

PLENTY of United season ticket holders would quite like their money back after watching some of the performances on offer at Old Trafford this season.



Some disabled fans have received 25 per cent off their season tickets after complaining that their views were being blocked by other fans standing in front off them at the back of the Stretford End.

Affected fans were offered the opportunity to move but none wanted to do so, so as a goodwill gesture the club applied the discount – and even back dated it to games which had already taken place.

One affected fan told SunSport: “The disabled section is very good and the club look after us very well. But more and more people have been standing up below the section and its caused a few problems with the view.

“It was mentioned to the club and we ended up having 25 per cent of our season ticket refunded straight into our account.” Whether other fans who have non-restricted views now seek compensation remains to be seen.



Small tweaks

POCH continues to make noticeable and logical changes to United’s routines.

For the pre-match press conference in Lisbon, Fernandes fielded questions before it was Pochettino’s turn.

Under previous managers, the player spoke little given the understandable attention on the United coach and there was no consistent pattern. The United press officer occasionally had to request a journalist to ask the player a question.

Jose Mourinho used to insist on the player having his own audience with the press whereas every other United manager has sat next to one of their squad members.

Flight drama

UNITED stayed over in Lisbon, a throwback to Erik ten Hag’s days.



The squad were unable to fly out of Lisbon past midnight after the 2-2 draw on Wednesday due to local airspace restrictions.

Humberto Delgado Airport is subject to strict curfew rules due to intense noise pollution and its proximity to the city centre.

Ten Hag often preferred an extra night’s stay abroad for European away games and recovery sessions took place in hotels or at a nearby pitch that the club had booked.

With recovery sessions reintroduced the day after games by Pochettino, he and his staff were able to oversee them in Portugal.

United used their hotel gym facilities and pool.



Predictably, many players under Ten Hag started to tire of spending an extra night away from home.

SIR Alex Ferguson’s former kit man Albert Morgan took part in a panel during an Old Trafford Sleep Out event held by the Manchester United foundation.

Morgan was full of hope that United will one day return to the glory days and wished new boss Pochettino well.

The ex-midfielder has now embarked on a new career with YouTube channel AFTV, which is a fan-led page led by Robbie Lyle.

He was announced by the channel’s official account on X on Friday morning.



Their post read: “HERE WE GO! Jay Emmanuel-Thomas joins AFTV as our NEW presenter!”

A video alongside post showed the former football star playing for Arsenal as a youngster.

It then flashes to Emmanuel-Thomas in present day wearing a modern Gunner shirt.

He puts on a pair of sunglasses before pointing at the camera.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Emmanuel-Thomas previously discussed his prison ordeal with SunSport and said the 11 months he served “felt like five years”.

He said: “It is dog eat dog in there, it’s not nice. S**t happens on a daily basis, you have to focus on you personally and make sure you can get yourself out of there safely, in good health, and not want to return.

“It’s something that if you don’t adapt to, it can break you. There are a lot of people in there who have done really bad things.



“It gets to the point where you have to zone in on yourself and actually set a plan for when you leave. If you don’t have a goal when you get out, you’re going to be left in limbo.

“I didn’t serve as long as some others, I only did 11 months. But those 11 months felt like five years.”

Emmanuel-Thomas joined Arsenal at the age of eight in 1998 and went on to captain the Under-18s.

He won the FA Youth Cup with the Gunners but only made five appearances for his boyhood club before leaving for Ipswich in 2011.

He went on to become a journeyman in football after spells with Bristol City and QPR before playing in Thailand, India and Scotland.



Emmanuel Thomas rounded off his career with non-league club Kidderminster Harriers and Scottish Championship side Greenock Morton.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

He was playing for Greenock at the time of his arrest.

Emmanuel-Thomas was also set to fight fellow ex-pro Nile Ranger in an exhibition boxing match before it was scrapped at the eleventh hour.

Sports.title: Tonda Eckert wants Spygate to be forgotten - but Southampton aren't helping him
Sports.content:
Tonda Eckert wants Spygate to be forgotten - but Southampton aren't helping him

Southampton face Middlesbrough in a Championship clash packed full of intrigue and backstory on Friday night at St Mary's Stadium following the bitter Spygate saga

View 3 Images Tonda Eckert faces Middlesbrough in a Spygate rematch (Image: Matt Watson/Southampton FC via Getty Images)

Tonda Eckert wants everyone to move on.

‌



The Southampton boss has apologised, been punished and would prefer it if the Spygate saga was never mentioned again.

‌



But with Middlesbrough in town on Friday for a mouth-watering clash at the top of the Championship, that was never going to happen.

‌



Southampton have not shaken off the Spygate saga, which came to a conclusion in early October when the FA announced that Eckert had been fined £28,000 and given a suspended six-week ban from football to go with Saints' earlier four-point deduction from the EFL.

Eckert invited the Sky Sports cameras into his world this week for some soft-focus PR work, to emphasise the man behind the spying scandal. Southampton backed their manager, ignoring the calls to sack him over the summer before handing him a new contract last week, so they could do with his image being rehabilitated.

Black Friday special! Click here to sign up to Mirror+ for just £1 a month!

‌



Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

The humble words of Kim Hellberg this week helped their case, with the Boro boss saying he respects Eckert and considers it water under the bridge. "I will never hold a grudge against anyone in life, things will happen and you have to move on," Hellberg said.

‌



It was therefore not the wisest move by Southampton to commission an influencer to voice over a provocative social media video to ramp up the tension ahead of the Middlesbrough game.

The video recalls Southampton's play-off campaign, their two-legged win over Boro and how success was "ours... until it wasn't". It notes that Boro "got another go" before Oli McBurnie's winner at Wembley for Hull. "People talk about last season, but we're focused on this one," the narrator says without a hint of irony.

‌



Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

View 3 Images Southampton's video previewing the Middlesbrough game has ramped up the tension (Image: X/Southampton FC)

‌



Eckert has conceded that "there will be a different emotion" inside St Mary's on Friday night as Saints face Boro for the first time since their not-so-subtle spying was uncovered and everything unravelled.

The truth is that the only way the German will effectively move on from the saga is by achieving the objective he was hired for. Southampton are sixth in the Championship table, seven points behind pace-setters Boro in a tight contest.

‌



Having put their play-off final disappointment behind them, Boro have only lost twice this season in the league and, in Will Lankshear, have the Championship's best striker and top scorer. Spygate or no Spygate, they are currently the team Saints have to measure themselves against, with a trip to face second-placed Wolves on the horizon the following weekend.

View 3 Images Southampton have been exceptional at home this year (Image: Matt Watson/Southampton FC via Getty Images)

‌



Southampton have been exceptional at home this season, taking 22 points from a possible 24. They have not lost at home since January. It is away from the south coast where they have struggled, taking two points from the last nine on the road, against West Brom, Preston and Sheffield United.

With Leo Scienza and Caspar Jander back in contention after injuries and top scorer Cyle Larin back among the ranks, Southampton have the players to inflict Boro's third defeat of the season.

Article continues below

Ultimately, it is only victories in such matches that will help Eckert clean his image and develop a new reputation. It was his underhand approach that cost them a shot at promotion last season - and it is on him to right his wrongs this time around, starting tonight.

Sports.content:
Aston Villa make decision on Alejandro Garnacho as Unai Emery completes huge U-turn

Alejandro Garnacho has quickly seen his loan move from Chelsea to Aston Villa turn into a nightmare and the winger could be on the move again in January after Unai Emery made his mind up

View 2 Images Alejandro Garnacho could leave Aston Villa in January (Image: Marc Atkins/Aston Villa FC via Getty Images)

Aston Villa are open to offloading Alejandro Garnacho in January, having quickly changed their minds over the Chelsea loanee.

‌



‌



Garnacho joined Villa in the summer on a season-long loan deal but has failed to make his mark in Birmingham. He's made just seven substitute appearances and was left out of the squad for Tuesday's Champions League tie against Galatasaray.

‌



Unai Emery's explanation post-match summed up the bleak situation. "Today the players were here who I think are the best players to be here with us," the Villa manager said.

‌



The 22-year-old has played just 34 minutes in the Premier League this season and there are clear signs that Emery is repeating what he did with Harvey Elliott last season. Elliott joined Villa on loan from Liverpool with a £35million obligation to buy, but was frozen out after Emery decided he wouldn't reach the number of appearances needed to trigger the option.

Chelsea believed Garnacho's loan was akin to a transfer because the appearances needed to turn the loan into a £42.5m permanent move were deemed easily achievable. But The Athletic now reports that Villa are open to offloading Garnacho in January to avoid buying the Argentine.

For that to happen they would have to strike an agreement with an overseas club, with players unable to join two domestic teams on loan in the same season. That could be difficult as it would require the agreement of Garnacho and parent club Chelsea.

Sports.content:
Watch the 'terrifying' moment banned Polish ultras storm Sunderland home end as police step in

Sunderland's Europa League clash with Jagiellonia Bialystok was disrupted after supporters infiltrated the home ends at the Stadium of Light, despite a UEFA ban

Jagiellonia Bialystok fans in in the home end at the Stadium of Light

Sunderland's Europa League fixture against Jagiellonia Bialystok was thrown into chaos after Polish ultras invaded the home end.

‌



‌



The away section at the Stadium of Light had been shut down due to a UEFA ban, but that failed to deter some supporters.

‌



The Polish club had been blocked from selling away tickets to their fans following crowd trouble at a previous Europa League match. They were fined €20,000 and handed an immediate away-fan ban after violent disorder erupted between their supporters and Levski Sofia fans in Bulgaria on November 5.

‌



However, despite warnings urging them to stay away from the match - with the ban covering the entire ground - away supporters still made the journey to Wearside and infiltrated the home end in scenes that some Black Cats fans have described as "terrifying."

Sunderland had previously issued a statement acknowledging the ban, as they had suspected that several Jagiellonia Bialystok fans had purchased tickets for the fixture. They cautioned that anyone identified inside would be escorted from the stadium, reports Chronicle Live.

Sports.content:
Paul Pogba urges Man Utd to copy Arsenal as he gives Mauricio Pochettino verdict

Manchester United are in the early stages of a new era under Mauricio Pochettino and their former midfielder Paul Pogba believes he can turn things around, if given enough time

View 2 Images Paul Pogba has given his take on Manchester United's situation (Image: Franco Arland/Getty Images)

Paul Pogba believes that Mauricio Pochettino can be Manchester United's Mikel Arteta, if the club are patient enough and the players get on board with his approach.

‌



‌



Pochettino is just two games into his spell as United manager, having jumped ship from his job as the United States boss to replace Michael Carrick. His side were thrashed 4-0 by Liverpool before drawing 2-2 with Sporting Lisbon in a chaotic match in the Champions League.

‌



The former Tottenham and Chelsea manager has taken on a huge task at Old Trafford, with United sitting 19th in the Premier League after winning just one of their opening 11 matches. He will attempt to get his first win on the board when United face Brentford at home on Saturday afternoon.

‌



Ex-United midfielder Pogba knows all about the pressure of matching up to the high expectations at United. He played against Pochettino's previous sides in the Premier League and has called for a period of stability under the Argentine.

‌



Pogba told talkSPORT: “I'm happy that Pochettino has gone there because I think he's a great manager. And I'm sad also for Michael Carrick because I don't think he had enough time to show and prove himself.

“But I think we just need to give time to this team. We know there's a lot of fans all over the world and we all want Man United to win, and we all think that they should change manager.

‌



“All I think about this team - I’ve been there - is that you need time, you need to fix the stuff inside. Everybody needs to be in the same position and give time to the manager to do his things."

United have not won the league title in 14 years, having struggled since Sir Alex Ferguson retired in 2013 and Pogba drew a comparison with Arsenal.

‌

The Gunners lifted the Premier League trophy for the first time in 22 years in May, having backed Arteta and given him the time to implement his ideas. Arteta has been Gunners boss since 2019 and has completely turned around their fortunes.

“The players also have to perform, have to understand the manager. And this way, they can go somewhere - like Arsenal," Pogba added. "Arsenal had a great time with Thierry Henry. They had a great [era], they went to Champions League final, they won the Premier League. And they had a [long] time [before] winning again.

“It took how many years [between] the last time that Arsenal won the Premier League [and this year]? But the pressure - I know it's a big club, it's Manchester United - was way less. They let Arsenal make their own way back to the top.

“And that's all I think Manchester United need. We need to stop talking about them like they are the team that it was back then. You need to respect, you need to let them grow again and get back to the top.”

Sports.title: Liverpool have already made a huge change - and two players in starting XI prove it
Sports.content:
There are often two types of change. The first is the kind of seismic, leftfield jolt that can instantly force everyone down a very different path from the one to which they have long been accustomed.

And then there's the other more gradual, seemingly unassuming shift that takes place over a longer period of time that almost creeps up unannounced before it is widely noticed.

Having had far too much of the former during turbulent recent times, Liverpool are now embracing the latter route with Wednesday's impressive Champions League win at Club Brugge offering further evidence.

Consider this. Of the 11 players who started the game at a chilly Jan Breydel Stadium, only two - Alisson Becker and Dominik Szoboszlai - featured in the team that claimed the Premier League title just 18 months ago.

‌



Man Utd, Liverpool and Tottenham use same law firm to launch Man City legal claim READ MORE :

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

As well as the obvious new look in the dugout with Andoni Iraola and his coaching staff having replaced that of Arne Slot, the squad has undergone a huge overhaul since the record-equalling 20th championship was secured.

Of course, none of this is news. Much of last season was spent berating and belittling the mammoth £450million outlay in the summer immediately after the title win, and no club had a greater net spend in the most recent close season as Iraola, guided by now-departed sporting director Richard Hughes, looked to bolster a squad that had seen a host of established names depart.

What is different now, though, is few if any supporters are still lamenting those exits.

‌



View 4 Images Jeremy Jacquet has shone as Ibrahima Konate's de facto replacement

The outstanding start to the Anfield career of centre-back Jeremy Jacquet has prevented any hankering for Ibrahima Konate after his still surprising free transfer move to Real Madrid, and while Mohamed Salah's slow decline last year was on occasion painfully obvious, the pace of new arrivals Victor Munoz and Bradley Barcola, while both still very much raw in Liverpool terms, has demonstrated what was missing from the Reds attack in their title defence.

Left-back may still be a concern for many - although Milos Kerkez was defensively resolute dealing with Brugge dangerman Carlos Forbs on Wednesday - but there hasn't really been any great call for Andy Robertson. Like the Scotland international at Tottenham Hotspur, supporters have chosen to move on.

Then there's the next generation. Both Trey Nyoni and Rio Ngumoha were at Liverpool in 2024/25 and featured for the first team, but not in the Premier League. And while their opportunities were in retrospect understandably limited by Slot last term, the regular involvement in training and observation from the bench on what is required at the elite level has held both in good stead.

‌



View 4 Images Alisson was one of two title winners to start vs Club Brugge

The teenage duo were both impressive in Belgium, Nyoni from the start in one of the two deeper midfield roles alongside captain-for-the-night Szoboszlai. No player made more interceptions while only Florian Wirtz made more passes for Liverpool and just Wirtz and Kerkez had more touches. Not bad consider Nyoni was replaced after 72 minutes.

Ngumoha, forced into action early due to the injury suffered by Munoz, is now averaging 7.8 completed dribbles per 90 minutes in the Champions League this season - the most of any player in a single campaign since such records began 20 years ago. And one run ended with an assist for Wirtz's game-clinching second goal.

Winning always helps foster team spirit. But it was noteworthy last week when Kerkez, elaborating on his claim "the atmosphere is great in the locker room", stated: "I think it’s visible on the pitch that we fight really hard, we want to bring results, we want to bring points."

‌



Liverpool have already earned six positive results by coming from behind, and only in the Champions League defeat to Fenerbahce have they failed to win when scoring first this season. This is a team that, the collapse at home to Manchester City aside, is clearly fighting for each other. That wasn't always the case last term, even if the mitigating circumstances are too glaring to ignore.

View 4 Images Florian Wirtz is finally finding his best form with the Reds (Image: Getty Images)

Wirtz also offered another glimpse of the change in mindset when talking ahead of the Brugge match.

"Last season was a difficult season for all of us, players and the whole club," he said. "It was not easy to get ourselves in a good position where we could have a run or gain confidence as a team.

‌



"Since the start of the season, we made that better. That’s why I also think that the players, individuals, can shine more and show their qualities more."

Wirtz is just one of many players to benefit. This is no longer the Liverpool team of last season - this is one for the present looking to the future. The change has already happened.

Verstappen won a thrilling race in Las Vegas that saw Russell challenge him for the lead for long periods before crashing and finishing ninth, and afterwards the four-time world champion said the Brit is "so far below my level" before adding that it was "fantastic" seeing him make an error.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player A look back at some of the most heated clashes between Red Bull's Verstappen and Mercedes' Russell

Speaking exclusively to Martin Brundle during an interview that will air during Sky Sports F1's live coverage of the Qatar Grand Prix on Sunday, Russell said he found Verstappen's verbal attack on him "amusing", before drawing a comparison between the Dutchman and seven-time world champion Hamilton.

"He [Verstappen] is a ruthless competitor and I massively respect that, but there's also Lewis Hamilton, who I've spent three years team-mates with and watched my whole life," Russell said.

"And obviously Toto [Wolff, Mercedes' team principal] spent 12 years with [Hamilton], who is equally a ruthless competitor and absolute animal behind the wheel, but obviously has incredible values and grace and dignity.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Verstappen had a choice few words for long-time foe Russell after winning the Las Vegas Grand Prix

"And Lewis is somebody who I really look up to and who is an incredible role model for young kids coming through.

"But there is no right or wrong, there's just opinions. Everyone has different opinions, and some people like driver A and some people like driver B, and as I've grown older, I don't really let it affect me as much."

'I know where Toto stands on Verstappen off the record'

Wolff has previously tried to sign Verstappen from Red Bull with Russell telling Sky Sports F1 in June 2025 that his own contract extension was being delayed by Mercedes' attempts to recruit Verstappen.

Wolff was photographed holidaying with Verstappen, has rarely criticised the Dutchman in recent years. and in Las Vegas called the back and forth between the two drivers a "good factor of the entertainment" in Formula 1.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Russell and Verstappen collided with one another during final practice at the Las Vegas Grand Prix

Asked about Wolff's position on his clashes with Verstappen, Russell said: "Well I know where he [Wolff] stands off the record, so I won't probably repeat that.

"Toto and I were flying back after the race in Vegas and we did have quite a laugh about the comments that were said after the race.

"But we just know how certain people go about their business."

Russell: Verstappen comments would have affected me more a few years ago

Verstappen and Russell have clashed several times since the latter joined Mercedes in 2022, a move that made battles between the pair for top positions a more regular occurrence.

Their first collision came in the Sprint at the 2023 Azerbaijan Grand Prix on the opening lap, before their rivalry spectacularly ignited at the end of 2024 when Verstappen was given a one-place grid penalty for impeding Russell at the 2024 Qatar Grand Prix.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Verstappen had a choice few words for long-time foe Russell after winning the Las Vegas Grand Prix

Verstappen said Russell's conduct with the stewards in Qatar meant he had "lost all respect" for the Brit, who then responded with a remarkable explosive verbal attack on the Dutchman the following week at the season-ending Abu Dhabi Grand Prix.

Russell said at the time that Verstappen had threatened to put him "in the wall" in Qatar, and said that "people have been bullied by Max for years". Verstappen questioned the accuracy of Russell's claims and labelled him a "loser" and "backstabber".

Reflecting on his comments during the 2024 meeting with the stewards in Qatar, Russell said: "Well, I wasn't trying to let him off. I mean, I didn't go in there saying, 'that's fine'."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Russell provided his response after Verstappen said the Mercedes driver was 'so far below my level' following the Las Vegas Grand Prix

On the alleged threat that the Mercedes driver said followed in Abu Dhabi, Russell added: "That's how he [Verstappen] goes about his business. I've known him long enough that I know, again, that was a bit more of a laugh away comment, I thought."

The pair came collided at the 2025 Spanish Grand Prix after Verstappen felt Russell forced him wide and effectively retaliated by making contact with Russell and was given a 10-second time penalty for the incident.

Russell downplayed suggestions that the feud had begun during the pair's karting days, before insisting he hasn't let Verstappen's latest comments overly affect him.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Following their dispute at the Las Vegas Grand Prix, McLaren's Lando Norris says Verstappen and Russell 'don't have to get on'

"We actually didn't have that many comings together in karting," Russell said. "He's a year older than me so we only raced together once in 2011, and then obviously he fast-tracked his career.

"I found it all quite amusing afterwards. But obviously he won the race, I had a c**p race, and he's able to have the last laugh, so I'm sure he quite enjoyed that. A few years ago, it probably would have affected me a lot more, but we're different characters.

"I respect his driving talents immensely and everything he achieves on track. Obviously, maybe off track we do things slightly differently, but that's how it is."

Sports.title: Man Utd activate Fernandes contract extension clause
Sports.content:
Manchester United have triggered their 12-month option to extend captain Bruno Fernandes' contract.

His deal was previously expiring at the end of this season but will now run until summer 2028.

United have been in talks with Fernandes over extending his contract since the summer.

Sky Sports News understands both parties are in agreement that it makes sense to return to negotiations in the future - with full focus on improving the club's current position.

Triggering the club option now is logical from United's perspective, as clubs could have approached Fernandes over a pre-contract agreement in January. This contract clause activation prevents that.

More to follow.

Sports.title: Brighton's perfect blend: The duo key to Seagulls' rise
Sports.content:
It was a painful Sunday afternoon at Hull, but by the time Brighton pair Luka Vuskovic and Pascal Gross arrived at the beachside restaurant on Tuesday, you got the impression they didn't need too much of the bracing near-frozen sea air to boost the mood.

Yes, they were disappointed, but they weren't going to let a few minutes and Oli McBurnie overshadow a start to the season that has taken the Seagulls second in the Premier League table after 11 games.

Not many would have predicted such a lofty position for Fabian Hurzeler's team - including some of the Brighton team themselves - but the club are playing some thrilling football, and the 26 goals they have scored has helped them beat the likes of Arsenal and Man City already this season.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player FREE TO WATCH: Highlights from the Premier League match between Hull City and Brighton.

Sitting in front of me are two of the reasons why. They are both too modest to entertain that, but at the heart of this side's success is an almost seamless tactical and generational blend epitomised by Gross and Vuskovic.

Gross has been a revelation since his return earlier this year, something he admits he was nervous about doing. "You always hope for the best, but you never know. Coming back is not always easy."

The German international is making it look effortless. Opta have the 35-year-old top of their running stats, with 131.5km covered so far this league season, and only Declan Rice has more assists (4 vs 5).

But Gross' influence can't only be measured in numbers; this anchor or "connector" - as Hurzeler likes to call him - goes far beyond. No wonder his contract was recently extended for another season.

"I love the place, a lot of important things in my life happened here," he says.

"I have my family here, my kids are happy, my dog... it's a beautiful place with a lot of special people, where I feel really connected, really comfortable with the whole culture.

"We have so much talent and we have a lot of good people, but from different backgrounds. So that's really challenging, but I love the challenge because they're all good people we have in the dressing room.

"I was, at one point, a guy who came from another country, but I wanted to adapt, I wanted to be part of the culture. You need to help and support the guys. I really believe in what the club is doing. I think I can be a big part on and off the pitch."

The German international returned to Brighton after his dream move to Borussia Dortmund - the club he supported as a boy - ended early. He was desperate to show he could still perform at the highest level consistently. "I had to prove a point for myself, but also I wanted to repay the trust the club showed in me."

Do you remember playing better at any point in your career, I ask, telling him The Athletic had him as their number one player of the season so far.

"I don't believe in that. I don't see it like that. Maybe our start and the little things getting over-exaggerated.

"I think I am playing at my best, but maybe I think I'm a very good player in a good group who's working well, because everybody is improving. The way we set up, the way we play, I think everybody looks good."

Those stats, I say, are remarkable and again he down plays the praise. But he does concede: "They are really good, but because the team is playing well. If the team is playing well, everybody individually maybe looks a bit better."

Gross is honest enough to admit the start has surprised him. "No, I wouldn't say I expected that. I always hope for the best, but I know every game, like we saw on the weekend, is so different and so difficult that momentum can change quick."

Now, he says, comes the big challenge: the busy period. "It's a different sport, I always say". But you get the sense Brighton will be ready for it.

Brighton's next five Premier League fixtures November 29: Newcastle (H) - Live on Sky Sports

December 2: Bournemouth (A) - Live on Sky Sports

December 5: Nottingham Forest (A) - Live on Sky Sports

December 13: Everton (H) - Live on Sky Sports

December 20: Ipswich (H) - Live on Sky Sports

Alongside Gross, Vukovic has been another of the central characters in Brighton's success this season. He arrived in the summer from Tottenham in a club record deal worth £46m.

Vuskovic is no stranger to breaking records - two days after his 16th birthday, he became the youngest player to feature in Croatia's top flight. He is the fourth generation of his family to play football. Defending is very much the family business.

At 19, he has already played football in Croatia, Germany, Belgium and Poland, which has certainly helped him prepare for life as a central defender in the Premier League.

He says: "When you join as a 30-year-old guy, compared to say 15, instantly you have to grow up, you have to realise something in your life, and you have to mature.

"I had a really good group of people at Hajduk Split that made me mature fast enough, and they really helped me. In each of the countries, it was very helpful to develop, to grow as a human, as a football player."

Image: Vuskovic did not play a single first team game for Tottenham

Vuskovic's form in these first few months of the season has prompted a few questions about why Spurs let him leave in the summer and brought in Brighton's Paul van Hecke.

He doesn't see it as "rejection" and appreciates everything they did for him but, he adds: "In the end the coach came and said he didn't see me in his system, which is completely normal in football. I think in the end everybody earned (something). I gained experience, I moved to another club and I think we are all very happy about it.

"They told me they don't see me (as part of the plans), so there was no point in fighting for my place. I wanted to go somewhere where the coach would tell me, 'If you train well you will play', and that's exactly what happened here.

"The move, for me, was perfect. I love the players, I love the staff, the club. They've been all very nice to me since the first day I came, and I would change nothing."

For all the praise - and there has been plenty - Vuskovic is fiercely critical of himself. This is a player, after all, who employed a private analyst to make sure he was ready for the Premier League.

We talk about the two goals conceded late on against Hull he reflects: "I think I could have done more. We all could. We had our chances, but in the end, we didn't take them. Maybe we didn't have the luck. There's nothing to be sad or angry about, we can only learn from it and come back stronger."

If they keep learning and progressing what are this team capable of?

His reply? "Being at the top part of the Premier League, competing with all the top teams, also in Europe, if we are focused every game. Right now it's amazing, but we need to keep a clear head and just focus on what's next."

Pascal Gross and Luka Vuskovic were speaking at an American Express Shop Small campaign event aimed at encouraging people to support local businesses.

Sports.title: Premier League player dropped from squad after ‘unacceptable’ police incident
Sports.content:
Hull manager Sergej Jakirovic has confirmed that on-loan forward Robinio Vaz will play no part in Sunday’s Premier League clash against Crystal Palace.

The 19-year-old was allegedly detained by police in Paris earlier this week on suspicion of fraud regarding a hire car that had been flagged as stolen due to missed lease payments by its owner.



2 Jakirovic has Hull in 11th after promotion to the Premier League last season Credit: Getty

2 Vaz has made just five substitute appearances Credit: Getty

Although Vaz was apparently released without charge after authorities dropped the matter, Jakirovic has taken a firm stance, branding the off-field situation completely 'unacceptable'.

Questions also remain over whether the teenager had permission from the Tigers to make the midweek trip across the Channel.



Jakirovic added that Hull City are now in direct discussions with Vaz's parent club, AS Roma, as both sides look to agree on a swift resolution regarding his immediate future.

He has struggled to make an impact since joining the Tigers on loan.

Vaz has managed just 50 minutes of action, failing to displace Oli McBurnie from the squad.



McBurnie has four Premier League goals this season with the Tigers 11th in the table.

Sports.title: EFL star slapped with three-match ban for off the ball incident missed by officials
Sports.content:
EFL star slapped with three-match ban for off the ball incident missed by officials

Port Vale defender Connor Hall has been handed a three-match ban for violent conduct.

The 33-year-old has been suspended after an off-the-ball incident during his side's 2-1 defeat at Barnet on November 21.

2 Hall has been given a three-match ban for violent conduct Credit: Shutterstock Editorial

Despite being missed by the match officials at the time, Hall was subsequently charged by the FA.

He has now been banned with immediate effect and will miss his side's next three matches.

The incident occurred in the 73rd minute of the League Two fixture at The Hive Stadium.

It came during the same minute in which Valiants goalscorer Onel Hernandez was sent off.

The forward was shown a second yellow card after pushing Barnet's Tom Knowles as tempers flared between the two sides.

However, Hall had gone unpunished by referee Sam Mulhall after his offence was not spotted by the officials.

In a statement confirming the ban, an FA spokesperson said: "Port Vale’s Connor Hall has been suspended for three matches following an incident that occurred during their EFL League Two fixture against Barnet on 21 November.

"The player’s behaviour around the 71st minute wasn’t seen by the match officials at the time, but it was caught on video, and The FA alleged that this constitutes violent conduct.

"Connor Hall subsequently admitted the charge against him and accepted the standard penalty for violent conduct."

Hall will now miss Saturday's home league match against Newport County.

He will remain suspended for Tuesday's trip to Crawley Town and the FA Cup second round tie with Leyton Orient next weekend.

The 33-year-old can return to action away against Stockport County in the EFL Trophy on December 8.

Hall, who joined Port Vale in 2024, has made 14 League Two appearances so far this season.

Prior to his suspension, he had started all but one of their last 13 league matches.

Jon Brady's side currently sit 17th in the fourth-tier, six points above the relegation zone.

The Valiants have won two of their last six outings after following the loss to Barnet with a 1-1 home draw against Northampton Town on Tuesday.

2 Hall has been banned for an off-the-ball incident which was missed by the match officials Credit: Shutterstock Editorial

Following relegation last term, the club are back in League Two for the first time in two seasons.

Their last two campaigns at this level have both ended in promotion.

Sports.title: ‘Love you’ – Ryan Reynolds and Rob Mac share heartfelt messages after tough Wrexham decision
Sports.content:
Wrexham co-owners Ryan Reynolds and Rob Mac have paid tribute to Steve Parkin following his announcement to vacate his role as assistant manager.

After five-and-a-half years in the role, the 61-year-old announced on Thursday that now was the time to step away, but not before taking to the touchline for one last time as Wrexham welcome Portsmouth to the Racehorse Ground.



3 Wrexham assistant manager Parkin will leave the club this weekend Credit: Getty

Parkin played a pivotal role, alongside manager Phil Parkinson, in Wrexham's rise from the National League all the way up the football pyramid to the EFL Championship via three successive promotions

They secured their highest finish in team history last season when they finished in seventh - just one point adrift from earning a playoff place which would have afforded the outfit from north Wales the opportunity to compete for promotion to the top flight.

In a message to supporters, Parkin said: "My time at Wrexham has been truly special. "While the three promotions have been unforgettable achievements, it is the relationships that I will treasure most.



"The bond with our two co-chairmen, with Shaun (Harvey) and Humphrey (Ker), the players, staff and, of course our incredible supporters has made this journey so memorable.

"The people of Wrexham have made my family so welcome, and we have made friendships that will last a lifetime.



"To all the players who have been part of that journey, thank you for your hard work, commitment and for putting up with the demands we have placed on you day in, day out."

Now, the club's Hollywood owners have taken to their respective social media accounts to pay their own gratitude to Parkin for his role in Wrexham's fairytale rise up the ranks.



Reynolds and Mac pay tribute

Reynolds reshared Wrexham’s official announcement to his own Instagram story, and wrote alongside it, "Love you, Steve. Thank you for everything you’ve done for Wrexham on and off the pitch.”

Mac followed suit and echoed similar sentiments, writing "Good game, sir, good game. Thank you, Steve.”

Although the Red Dragons owners didn't make an official statement in his emotional farewell, Parkin later revealed that he had privately spoken to Reynolds and Mac instead.

3 Mac and Reynolds each paid tribute to Parkin on their social media accounts Credit: Getty



3 Parkin (R) has been by Parkinson's (L) side at four different clubs Credit: Getty

“I’ve spoken over text with Rob and Ryan,” he said. “Phil talked to them and then we’ve had ongoing conversations.

“They’ve been incredibly supportive, and there’s been some really emotional messages between the three of us. I can’t thank them enough for their understanding, but also for what they’ve done for the club.

"They’re two top blokes, and their desire and enthusiasm to get this club to the very top is unsurpassed by anybody—they’ve been fantastic with me.”



The club's acting CEO Shaun Harvey added of Parkin: "Steve is a special person, to whom Wrexham owe a big debt of gratitude.
