"His victory salute made famous in the documentary will be forever linked with our success and is recognition for the significant part he played in it. Go well Steve and enjoy the time at home, you have more than earned it."

Parkin - who also had spells managing Mansfield, Rochdale and Barnsley before teaming up with Parkinson at Bradford, Bolton, and Sunderland before they each made the move to Wales - leaves the Red Dragons fighting in 14th place in the Championship.

Amid a four-match unbeaten run, Wrexham sit just five points out from the play-off places, and 10 points clear of relegation ahead of Parkin's final game.

Sports.title: English football’s second-oldest club forced to quit league in existential crisis
Sports.content:
Hallam FC have withdrawn from the Northern Premier League Division One East amid fears the club could run out of money.

The Countrymen are the second-oldest football club in England having been founded in 1860.



3 Hallam FC have withdrawn from the Northern Premier League Division One East Credit: Getty

Meanwhile, their home of Sandygate is officially recognised as the world's oldest football ground.

However, the club are now at risk of becoming extinct as a financial crisis engulfs Hallam.

Saturday's home match against Bridlington Town has been postponed after the club announced they had withdrawn from the league.



Hallam had been second from bottom in the eighth-tier of English football after winning just two of their 19 matches.

It is their finances which have contributed to the decision with the board fearing they will run out of money as early as next month.



The club are also at risk of being £69,000 in debt before the end of the year.

Hallam FC statement

In a statement, Hallam said: "In this very challenging situation club officers discussed the options available to us, we very reluctantly agreed that withdrawal from the NPL East for the 26/27 season was the most appropriate action to take in the circumstances.



"In our view it would be dishonest for the club to continue to try to play fixtures in the NPL East when we know how difficult the financial position is.

"There is a high risk we would be asking players to commit to games and staff to attend to work when we know that there is a significant risk that we may not be able to pay them, similarly with suppliers. That would be a totally unacceptable situation.

"In making this agonising decision we are trying to do the right thing by the club, the players, our suppliers and the community.

3 Hallam say they are at risk of running out of money as early as next month Credit: Getty



"We did consider the possibility of fundraising but, given the financial position of the club, the timescale in which to achieve this would have been incredibly tight and with no firm prospect of significant success.

"It would have added a further major risk on top of the other risks and we concluded that it would not be appropriate in the circumstances."

Hallam have confirmed they intend to re-join the non-league pyramid for the 2027/28 season.

Club officials will seek to do so at the highest-level they are permitted to re-enter.



The current crisis at Sandygate comes just two seasons after they were promoted to the eighth-tier of English football.

It marked the first time the club had played at step four of non-league.

3 Founded in 1860, Hallam are the second-oldest football club in England Credit: Getty

As well as their status as the country's second-oldest club, Hallam also boast ex-England winger Chris Waddle amongst their former players.



Waddle came out of retirement to play for the club in both 2013 and 2023.

Sports.title: Tottenham beat Arsenal to highly-rated teenager as new signing quietly announced
Sports.content:
Tottenham beat Arsenal to highly-rated teenager as new signing quietly announced

Highly-rated teenager Isaac Allen has confirmed that he has joined Tottenham, who beat rivals Arsenal to his signature.

The 15-year-old became a hot commodity in the summer following his departure from West Ham's academy, with both north London clubs interested at the time.

3 Roberto De Zerbi welcomed 10 new senior players in the summer, while Allen arrived in his academy Credit: Getty

Arsenal had actively pursued Allen for weeks, before Spurs stepped in to hijack the deal in a busy transfer window for the club.

While it was reported in August that Spurs had won the race to sign the England Under-15 international, the player has now confirmed the move himself.

In an Instagram post, Allen posted a family photograph taken at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium, where he holds up the club's shirt.

He also shared an individual new signing photo, as well as several other snaps of him in the club's tracksuit.

Alongside it, Allen wrote in the caption: “Happy to be signed with Tottenham.”

Allen is part of Spurs' academy drive

Regarded as one of England's most promising young prospects, Allen is capable of playing at centre-back or in defensive midfield.

His arrival at Tottenham comes as part of the club's youth recruitment drive, as they look to poach top talent.

In last month’s Fan Advisory Board (FAB) meeting, Spurs revealed they had actively recruited players aged 16 and under and invested in the Under-10 to Under-17 age groups.

Their commitment to their academy can be clearly seen, with Allen one of a number of highly-rated talents to arrive at Hotspur Way.

In recent months, 19-year-old Cole Ramsey - the young brother of Newcastle midfielder Jacob - has signed from Aston Villa, while Kwasi Senyah (16), Gabriel Rigg (15) and Jake Maloney (14) have also joined.

3 Cole Ramsey also swapped Aston Villa for Tottenham as the club look to snap up top young talent Credit: coleramseyyy

As part of their sell to beat competition from rival clubs, Tottenham are understood to be pairing football development with private schooling and strong professional terms once players turn 17.

The move comes after Spurs have previously been unable to guarantee a pathway into the first team for academy stars.

In the past, the club has also failed to maximise players' value by selling them on if they don’t believe they have a future at the club.

However, this appears to have changed more recently, with 18-year-old Luca Williams-Barnett's heroics hoped to set an example.

The teenager scored and assisted on his full senior debut in the Premier League against Ipswich last weekend before being handed a new long-term contract.

Meanwhile, Spurs also appear committed to finding solutions for academy graduates struggling for first-team progression.

3 Williams-Barnett became Spurs' youngest Premier League goalscorer since Gareth Bale in 2007 by netting against Ipswich Credit: Getty

Will Lankshear joined Middlesbrough in a deal worth up to £20million in the summer, and has quickly hit the ground running.

The England Under-21 star leads the Championship goalscoring charts, seeing him tipped for a Premier League switch and a senior Three Lions call-up.

Sports.title: Lionel Messi’s heir makes £67million transfer decision – and Manchester United could benefit
Sports.content:
Nico Paz is reportedly opposed to returning to Real Madrid at present as clubs circle to sign the Como midfielder.

The 22-year-old joined the Serie A side from the Spanish giants in 2024.

3 Paz is opposed to returning to Real Madrid even if they trigger his buy-back clause Credit: Getty

His transfer included a £67million buy-back clause for Real Madrid if they decided to bring Paz back to the Santiago Bernabeu.

That release clause is only valid for 2027 and will expire after the end of the summer transfer window.

Paz's Real Madrid stance

However, The Athletic report that Paz currently favours not returning to the club if he were to leave Como.

It comes amid growing interest from clubs across Europe in the Argentina international.

Although he could change his mind if offered a key role in the side, there is no sign at present that he will, the report adds.

Manchester United are amongst the potential suitors eyeing a move for Paz, with their interest hinging on Bruno Fernandes leaving the club.

Tottenham Hotspur also previously pushed to sign Paz in 2025, but were unable to prise him away from Italy.

The Red Devils are said to appeal to Paz despite not being his first choice destination.

Notably, Paz's father Pablo was a team-mate of new United boss Mauricio Pochettino at Newell's Old Boys between 1992 and 1994.

Fernandes is out of contract at the end of this season, although the Red Devils hold the option of a further 12 months.

3 United are keen on signing Paz if Fernandes leaves the club Credit: Getty

Having already turned down two extension offers, talks over a new deal with the club captain are currently on hold.

A number of candidates have been shortlisted to replace Fernandes if he were to depart Old Trafford.

Who is Nico Paz?

As for Paz, he has just over 18 months remaining on his Como deal having signed a four-year contract upon his arrival from Real Madrid.

The playmaker is already seen as the heir to Lionel Messi's No.10 shirt for Argentina.

Despite only making his debut in October 2024, Paz has amassed six goals in 16 caps for the three-time World Cup winners.

Meanwhile, he is enjoying a stellar season at club level with Como once again impressing both domestically and in Europe.

3 Paz has been tipped to succeed Messi as Argentina's No.10 Credit: Getty

Across all competitions, Paz has scored six goals and provided eight assists in 16 appearances.

Those include a brace and an assist in their 4-1 win over United in the Champions League last month.

Sports.title: Cole Palmer will never play for England again – there are eight players in front of him
Sports.content:
Cole Palmer will never play for England again – there are eight players in front of him

Cole Palmer will never play for England again - there are eight better players than him in his position.

That's the hot take of talkSPORT's Adrian Durham, who insists the Chelsea star has already missed his chance with the national team through a lack of availability and inconsistent form.



5 Palmer hasn't played for England since March Credit: Getty

Palmer was left out of Thomas Tuchel's 25-man squad for the November international break, which saw his Three Lions exile continue.

Having been a high-profile omission in last summer's World Cup, the 24-year-old was then recalled in September, but withdrew due to injury.

Tuchel told talkSPORT that he did not speak to Palmer before his World Cup squad announcement, and then said in September the player 'misses too many opportunities to impress him' after his latest withdrawal.



The playmaker last played for England in March, with his continued absence representing a huge fall from grace after a promising start to his international career.

Palmer was seen as a future star when he scored in the Euro 2024 final defeat to Spain off the back of a stellar debut season for Chelsea.



He scooped the 2023/24 PFA Young Player of the Year award after notching 22 Premier League goals in his first year at Stamford Bridge, and was later named England's Player of the Year for the same season.

However, Palmer has struggled to hit these heights consistently since then - with injuries playing a part - and talkSPORT's Durham believes all of the above factors could now spell the end of his England career.



Game over?

On the latest episode of the Fiery Fridays podcast, Durham claimed Palmer is no longer the hot commodity he once was with England.

“England are not in desperate need of Cole Palmer right now. We are not crying out for him," began Durham.

“So my hot take is that Cole Palmer will never play for England again."

5 Palmer has been unable to lift Chelsea up the table with his performances this season, and has slipped down the England pecking order Credit: Getty



5 Thomas Tuchel appears to favour other attacking midfielders ahead of Palmer Credit: Getty

The No.10 role - Palmer's preferred position - is England's most hotly contested position, with Jude Bellingham currently a shoe-in to start.

And Durham insisted there can be no way back for Palmer into the Three Lions fold when he is being outperformed by many other English players in this position, pointing to his lack of influence in a Chelsea side sitting a lowly eighth in the Premier League.

He continued: “I can think of eight English No.10s I'd have ahead of Cole Palmer on form so far this season.



"Jude Bellingham, Morgan Gibbs-White, Morgan Rogers, Eberechi Eze, Jack Rudoni, Jack Hinshelwood, Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall, and James Maddison.

“This is an era where Chelsea are not winning the major trophies. I'm talking Champions League, Premier League. They're not even competing for them. They're not even in the Champions League."

Palmer's output and commitment questioned

Despite five goals and three assists in 13 games this term, Durham insisted Palmer isn't doing enough to merit an England recall.

5 Even if Palmer is recalled for England, he is unlikely to start ahead of the influential Jude Bellingham Credit: Getty



The Blues star has scored just once in his last nine Premier League outings, which came against Manchester United on October 31.

Durham continued: “Cole Palmer should be at the forefront of Chelsea trying to get back to that top table. And he's nowhere near it.

"He should be leading the charge. His numbers should be off the charts. They've got one of those easy seasons Manchester United had last year, and they should be top of the table and flying. And he's right off it. He's nowhere near it."

Questioning Palmer's commitment to England, he went on: “I don't know for certain, but I don't think he's particularly motivated by England.



"Otherwise he would have turned up for that extended break earlier this season, the first international window this season, but he didn't turn up.

“So, whatever his mates say, you have to question whether he really is motivated by England.

5 Cole Palmer has played 14 times for England since making his debut in 2023, scoring twice Credit: Getty

“He's talented. There's no doubt about that. We've seen that enough. Does he apply that talent smartly enough or frequently enough?



“And here's the clincher. This is why I don't think he'll play for England ever again. By the time of the next Euros, he's going to be 26. Tuchel doesn't trust him already.

“He's only played three times under Thomas Tuchel. I think his England career is over already. Cole Palmer's never going to play for England again.”

Sports.title: Liverpool could enter bidding war with Bayern Munich for 17-year-old German playmaker
Sports.content:
Teenage sensation Wael Mohya is expected to be in huge demand this summer.

The 17-year-old has been a shining light in a struggling Borussia Monchengladbach team this season.



3 Mohya has two goals and one assist in the Bundesliga this season Credit: Getty

Gladbach are bottom of the Bundesliga with just one win all season and look destined for relegation.

Mohya has been thrown in and performed well with the playmaker grabbing two goals in eight games.

This has also caught the attention of Germany manager Jurgen Klopp, who named him in his most recent squad.



Although he did not get on the pitch, it demonstrates just how highly he is thought of in his homeland.

This has, unsurprisingly, put him on the radar of a number of clubs around Europe.



Liverpool, Brighton, Bayern Munich, and Barcelona have all been credited with interest.

Should Gladbach be relegated, which seems likely as things stand, then they could be forced to cash in on their prized asset.



Mohya himself has already addressed the rumours, insisting he just wants to get his head down and play.

He said: “If there were interest, it would be nice recognition of my performances, but nothing more than that. Just let me play football.”

Mohya bidding war

European football expert Andy Brassell told talkSPORT.com that it could start a bidding war come the summer.

3 Klopp has already brought Mohya into the Germany national squad Credit: Getty



He said: “Bearing in mind that Borussia Monchengladbach have been in a very poor place so far this season, they've lost a lot of players in recent years and they're going to be in a relegation battle all season.

“I think the fact that Mohya has been able to make an impression shows what an enormous personality he's got.

“He's braver on the ball than a lot of his teammates. He wants to get the ball, he wants to take guys on, he wants to shoot.

“We've already seen him score and assist in the Bundesliga this season. Straight away it's clear that he's a pretty special talent.



“For him to come into a team where confidence is on the floor, where they're on to their second coach of the season already, they've brought in a coach that's a particularly defensive coach in Alexander Blessin because they're conceding goals absolutely left and right.

“I wonder if that plays into Mohya’s hands a little bit actually. It feels to me that the advantage of coaching Borussia Monchengladbach over St. Pauli, where Blessin was before, is that you think, okay, well, I've already shown I can get a team to defend properly, a struggling team to defend properly.

3 Mohya made his debut for Gladbach when he was 16 Credit: Getty

“What I need is someone to pull a rabbit from a hat at the other end of the pitch.



“It feels like not only has he got the talent to do that, he's got the bravery to do that. He's already started seven games this season, which would probably have been beyond his wildest expectations at the beginning of this season.

“The fact that it's gone badly for Gladbach has obviously helped him get more opportunities because already he's one of the better players in their squad, even though he's quite green and inexperienced.

“He's got a great opportunity to play loads for the rest of this season and to show exactly what he's got.

“If Gladbach do end up going down, then bring on the bidding war.”

Sports.title: England batter Australia in Brisbane: Jamie Overton's career-best haul delivers a shellacking of the highest order at the Gabba against abysmal Aussies
Sports.content:
After the cakewalk in Carrara, the battering in Brisbane. On Tuesday, the margin of victory was eight wickets with 41 balls to spare. Here, the buffers were seven wickets and 43 balls. Two thrashings of Australia in four days? England fans could get used to this.

The star, as they went 2–1 up with two to play, was Jamie Overton, whose career-best haul of five for 12 helped bundle the Australians out for 108 – their lowest total in home T20s – and were the best figures in games between these teams. Whichever way you sliced it, this was a shellacking of the highest order.

Australia, it must be said, were abysmal – to a degree rarely seen. This may be a weakened team, but they wouldn't lose to the Poms at tiddlywinks if they could help it, and the chaos that has descended on their game off the field is now being reflected by their efforts on it.

'Very disappointing,' said their captain, Mitchell Marsh. 'We've got to own that. The Gabba's an excellent place to bat, but some of our shot selection was off. I don't want this young group to fear making mistakes, but tonight was a chance to be a bit more calculated. No excuses: we've got to be better.'

Yet England are without several first-choice players themselves, and after the mockery the Bazballers endured here during the Ashes last winter, they should not feel too heartbroken that local opprobrium is now spewing in the other direction.

'It was an unbelievable effort,' said Harry Brook. 'Jamie Overton was outstanding. He had it on a string, and it felt like we could change the field and make them make a mistake.'

Jamie Overton's career-best haul of five for 12 helped bundle the Australians out for 108 – their lowest total in home T20s

Liam Dawson also chipped in with three wickets as England secured a second thrashing of Australia in four days

When Australia reached 55 for one inside the six-over powerplay, with six sixes already under their belt, it looked as if they were in the mood to hit back from their mauling on the Gold Coast.

But Sam Harper spooned Liam Dawson to Overton at mid-on – mirroring the earlier dismissal of Marsh – and Australia disintegrated in a manner more usually associated in these parts with the England Test team.

When Overton removed the next five, it meant he had had a hand in the first seven Australian wickets, culminating in a double-wicket maiden in which he had Chaudhary caught at long-on and Ben Dwarshuis edging a wild drive. Only Sam Curran, with five for 10 against Afghanistan at Perth in the 2022 World Cup, has returned a better T20 analysis for England.

'It feels pretty good,' said Overton. 'It's been a frustrating tour: I've felt like I've not been at my best. But it's funny how quickly things can change.'

Overton spent the day before the game working with bowling coach Tim Southee, who placed a glove on the top of off stump, and encouraged him to get his weight further forward.

He was aggressive too, clonking Chaudhary on the helmet and Tim David on the forearm. Next ball, David – possibly still unsettled – miscued a pull to Henry Crocombe at fine leg. 'You're not out to hit people, but it can be part of your armoury to intimidate them,' said Overton with a smile.

There were also three wickets for the increasingly dependable Dawson, while Adil Rashid conceded just 17 from his four overs. Only James Coles, who opened the bowling again with his left-arm spin, and Crocombe, his former Sussex team-mate, lacked control, costing 45 in four overs between them.

Aneurin Donald followed his Carrara fireworks with a punishing 32 off 13 balls before cutting tamely to point

Harry Brook takes evasive action from a bouncer - but his side can secure the series with victory in Sydney on Sunday

The likeliest obstacle to an England victory was the Queensland weather, with rain interrupting their innings three times and eventually reducing the target to 93 off 16 overs.

Riley Meredith struck twice shortly after the first break, including Aneurin Donald, who followed his Carrara fireworks with a punishing 32 off 13 balls before cutting tamely to point.

But Jordan Cox produced an attractive cameo of 33 off 14, including three fours in a row off Dwarshuis, and by the time he drove the winning two into the covers, the game was done and dusted inside 26 overs.

Victory on Sunday in Sydney, and they will head to Canberra for Wednesday's tour finale with both white-ball series here in the bag.

Their squad will be reinforced by the arrival of Rehan Ahmed and the uncapped Glamorgan batsman Asa Tribe, who will be available for the last two games.

Sports.title: The inside story of how England became winners again: NIK SIMON reveals the cultural reset from a night out in rural Argentina and tour of Rio, internal reviews by Joe Marler, Lee Blackett's freedom and a magician
Sports.content:
At the end of their summer tour following a fiery and hard-fought win in the far north of Argentina, England's players needed to let off some steam. They scrapped their team curfews, organised VIP wristbands and headed to Yamba Sabados nightclub on the outskirts of Santiago del Estero. The day after their night drinking rum and cokes in rural South America, the squad were scheduled to fly back to Heathrow. But what happened next was a decision that consolidated the bonds between the players. A group of players from different clubs – from Northampton's Fin Smith to Saracens' Ben Earl to Leicester scrum-half Jack van Poortvliet – diverted to Rio de Janeiro to spend a few extra days together. They bought matching Brazil football jerseys and took a trip to see Christ the Redeemer. Henry Pollock led the TikTok content. Whatever flaws might have existed with the England rugby team in the first half of 2026, a lack of camaraderie was not one of them. There have been moments throughout the year when England's playing group could have split. That hasn't happened, despite the worst Six Nations in their history and a thumping defeat in South Africa to begin their Nations Championship campaign. Shortly before the autumn leg, a damning newspaper article was published that claimed the England environment was broken. The players took it as a personal affront on their unity and it galvanised the group. Shortly before the autumn leg of the Nations Championship, a damning newspaper article was published that claimed the England environment was broken. It galvanised the group (L-R) Alex Coles, Fin Smith, Jack van Poortvliet, Freddie Steward, Ben Earl, Tommy Freeman, Henry Pollock and Guy Pepper donned Brazil jerseys for a tour of Rio de Janeiro

Your browser does not support iframes.

'Whenever you lose, it always presents an opportunity to throw your toys out of the pram and go against each other,' captain Maro Itoje said this week. 'What the best teams do is navigate those tricky periods and work on what you need to work on. Don't make an issue bigger than it is. Don't make it smaller than it is. But address the issues at hand.' At times, emotions ran close to the surface on the summer tour. In his final press conference in Argentina, when pressed on England's ill-discipline, Steve Borthwick snapped at the travelling media, labelling them his 'negativity committee'. Once the team returned home, the debrief began. The mediator may surprise you. Joe Marler is more familiar with the celebrity circuit these days. But the retired prop turned Celebrity Traitors star remains the welfare manager for the players' union. He gathered anonymous feedback from the group, which he relayed to the RFU's performance director, Conor O'Shea. Competitive tension is common in elite sport and there were undoubtedly some frustrations in the England camp. Some players felt a lack of emphasis was placed on attack. Some felt there was a lack of empathy from the top. Others were not keen on the overall game plan. Contrasting playing philosophies were summed up during England's Six Nations defeat in Italy. Itoje wanted to kick a penalty for three points. Fin Smith wanted to go for broke and push for a try. Itoje, loudly, slapped down his fly-half. The moment was laughed off after the match, but the tactical disagreement summed up England's scrambled thinking. Evolving the leadership group has been one of the biggest tasks. At the beginning of this World Cup cycle, Smith was an uncapped 21-year-old. Steadily, he has installed himself as England's No 10, attempting to fuse Northampton's free-flowing attacking philosophy with some of Borthwick's more pragmatic thinking. Finding the right blend has been a slow process. Borthwick namechecked Smith, Ollie Chessum, Fin Baxter and Van Poortvliet as some of the younger players who have found their voice. Eddie Jones is one of Borthwick's biggest mentors, and the pair have shared ideas throughout the autumn. 'We met the week after England played Japan and had a chat,' Jones told Daily Mail Sport. 'Steve's a peppermint tea guy, so we had a drink and talked about general coaching issues. It doesn't matter what the team is, the issues we have are always generally the same. How do you manage your assistant coaches? How do you get the message through to this generation of players? Fin Smith (right, with Jonny Wilkinson) has installed himself as England's No 10, attempting to fuse Northampton's free-flowing attacking philosophy with Borthwick's pragmatic thinking Ollie Chessum, the rampaging forward who scored tries against Australia and New Zealand, has stepped up as one of the key leaders in the team

Your browser does not support iframes.

'In 2018, we had Dylan Hartley as captain and then it became difficult for him to get into the team, so we had to evolve the leadership team again. It's a constant process. The direction of the leadership group is driven by Steve and that's one of the most important responsibilities he has. You have to look at the players and how they're growing. 'England now have a number of young guys who maybe have between 10 and 15 Tests that are all starting to find their feet. A good example is Smith. He looks a better international player to me this year than he did last year. You need to engage the players more and allow them to have more of a voice at the right time. There are a lot of moving pieces to get the right balance. It comes with experience.' Recalibrating the leadership group has created a lighter mood around the camp. This week, full-back Freddie Steward claimed it is now the most positive England environment since he made his debut in 2021. A magician visited the team, they spent an afternoon with sprinter Amy Hunt, and some of the players donned their best suits for a night at GQ's annual Men of the Year awards. On the pitch, there have been various tactical shifts. The gameplan changed drastically after the defeat in Rome, with England opening up their attack against France in the final round of the Six Nations. It ended in another painful last-gasp defeat, but putting 46 points on the championship winners was a big positive step. 'We spent a lot more time on our attack that week,' revealed hooker and former captain Jamie George. 'We put more emphasis on it and we had a good crack at France. But we still didn't win. We now know the identity of this team. Once you get that in place, it's a lot easier to mould that in and around opportunities you see from an opposition.' By allowing assistant coach Lee Blackett more time to work on the attack, England have built a game plan where they look to run from the middle third of the pitch. The return to fitness of George Furbank, their counter-attacking full-back, has added an extra dimension. At the beginning of the campaign, referee Christophe Ridley was a regular at training. He officiated live training sessions as England tried to fix their ill-discipline from the summer. It worked. Team GB sprinter Amy Hunt (centre) visited England training at Pennyhill Park Lee Blackett (left) has been allowed more time to work on the attack, while retaining the solidity introduced by defence coach Richard Wigglesworth (right) The return to fitness of George Furbank, England's counter-attacking full-back, has added an extra dimension During the three July Tests, they averaged 11 penalties per game and conceded six yellow cards. This month, they have averaged seven penalties per game and conceded just one yellow card. Selecting Ben Curry as a turnover specialist to prevent the opposition from building high-phase attacks proved to be one of the biggest shifts. Borthwick tapped into the database of old training sessions to revisit how England improved their starts ahead of the 2019 World Cup. They recreated the sessions and England have subsequently scored in the eighth, second and fourth minutes of their autumn Tests against Australia, Japan and New Zealand. 'Steve has spoken to me about that previously,' said Jones. 'He was assistant coach for seven years, so he knows everything we've done. It's about scripting the first three or four plays, knowing what you're going to do. 'When you start training, you start fast. We'd play Eminem to engage the players or show a clip from James Bond to get them going. You need to get used to starting fast, rather than building into a game. 'England were caught short during the Six Nations and they've been able to fix that. Guys like Maro and Ellis Genge are back at their intense best. It's hard to say how Lee's influence has changed but their attack looks more coherent than it did before. They've evolved their attack to suit the strengths of the players.' Significantly, England have welcomed back some influential big-hitters. Itoje has benefitted from his summer off. Furbank has added a second play-making dimension. And props Will Stuart and Baxter have returned from injury to provide England with two first-class scrummaging units. England have evolved into a team who impose the best version of themselves, rather than allowing their identity to be dictated by the opposition. Crucially, they have done so without sacrificing Borthwick's forensic attention to detail. It climaxed with last weekend's victory over the All Blacks, with Lewis Moody inspiring the team by joining the stare-down of the Haka and delivering an inspirational speech to the squad the night beforehand. Lewis Moody (centre) inspired the team by joining the stare-down of the Haka and delivering an inspirational speech to the squad the night beforehand Maro Itoje lifts the Hillary Shield after defeating the All Blacks for a second year in succession With less than a year to go until the World Cup, England's players are beginning to enjoy their rugby again 'Standing on the pitch after we'd lost in Rome was not that long ago, that was probably as low as I've been in my career,' Smith told the BBC this week. 'Now this campaign has been such good fun. 'If you were to say what has changed – one big thing, if anything – it would be we've been a lot more inwardly focused. The game plan has been very similar week to week. We've tweaked very small things. We're confident if we bring our best, it should be able to take care of what the opposition brings to the table. 'To have come from the Six Nations where it felt tense and tight and we weren't playing very well… for Steve and the coaches to change the environment and for the leaders of the team to change that narrative completely is some effort. It's been majorly good fun and long may it continue.' With less than a year to go until the World Cup, England's players are beginning to enjoy their rugby again. The bonds they strengthened on the beaches of Rio are being reflected in their performances on the pitch. They finally look like a team that are pulling in the same direction. Itoje: England need to be 'ruthless' in history quest Maro Itoje urged England to be 'ruthless' and 'aggressive' and become the first team in the nation's rugby history to win three consecutive games against New Zealand. Captain Itoje has led England to impressive autumn victories over Australia, Japan and the All Blacks so far this month and his men have the chance to end with a November clean sweep today (SAT). A rematch with New Zealand – who they secured a record 37-12 victory over last weekend – is England's final assignment of 2026. It presents the chance to move to six games unbeaten with what would be an unprecedented treble against the Kiwis. 'That's something we can aim to do. That's important and I would love to achieve that,' Itoje said. 'We always want to be ruthless. We want to be aggressive. We want to be the confrontational team. 'We'd be fools to think the All Blacks aren't going to come out firing and come with an aggressive mindset. I still believe there is more to come. 'But this is a team that is now understanding itself better.' England's calendar year began with their 12-match winning streak going up in smoke as part of the worst Six Nations in history. Steve Borthwick's side finished fifth with just one win. But this month, Itoje and Co have looked a team capable of being World Cup contenders in Australia next year. Another victory over New Zealand would rubberstamp that claim. The latest renewal between the two teams comes as part of the Nations Championship's 'finals weekend' at Twickenham. Wales against Japan is a pre-curser to England's action. Six games across three days at the home of English rugby culminate tomorrow (SUN) afternoon with France and South Africa competing for the inaugural title. Tournament organisers have said 70 per cent of general admission tickets have been sold for the Wales and England double header, with that figure rising to 75 on Sunday. Hospitality tickets have sold out across both days. Asked how England have turned around their fortunes this month, Itoje said: 'We have become more and more cohesive. I also think we have by no means cracked it. 'We are not where we want to be. As with anything, when you go through tricky times, as we have done in the past year, it just sharpens your mind. 'That has a way of bringing us together. This week we have an amazing opportunity to show our internal motivation. That's the motivation that is long lasting.' By Alex Bywater

Sports.title: Nathan Lyon is revealed to be Australia star who suggested ball-tampering in first Test after Sandpapergate, as scandal takes new twist
Sports.content:
Nathan Lyon is revealed to be Australia star who suggested ball-tampering in first Test after Sandpapergate, as scandal takes new twist

Australia’s ball-tampering scandal has taken yet another twist after off-spinner Nathan Lyon was named as the player who suggested using mints on the ball in their first post-Sandpapergate Test match, against Pakistan in Dubai in October 2018.

Less than seven months after the Australians were caught using sandpaper to achieve reverse swing on their now infamous tour of South Africa, Lyon allegedly asked team-mates in the UAE: ‘Who’s got the mints? Who’s doing the ball today?’

According to SEN broadcaster Gerard Whateley, he was put in his place by Travis Head, who told him: ‘You’re f****** kidding me. We’re not doing that shit again.’

Tim Paine, who had taken over the captaincy from the banned Steve Smith, ensured the mints or lollies – the Australian word for sweets – never reached the field of play, while Justin Langer, who had replaced Darren Lehmann as head coach, later screamed at the entire team for even considering the ploy.

Usman Khawaja, who played in that game, confirmed this week – without naming Lyon – that the incident had taken place, telling The Grade Cricketer podcast he remembered Langer’s ‘blow-up’.

He added: ‘I remember it was very targeted at one player, then the whole team. What I remember from it was like: “If any of you guys ever even think about this again, you will not play for Australia again.”’

Nathan Lyon (second from right) has been identified as the Australia star who suggested ball-tampering again in the first Test after the Sandpapergate scandal erupted - pictured during that match against Pakistan in Dubai

But Khawaja confirmed that the player in question had also played at Cape Town, where the sandpaper controversy first blew up, which narrowed the field to six players, two of whom were Khawaja himself and Paine.

A subsequent investigation by Australian media outlet Code Sports, who spoke to ‘multiple sources’, emboldened them to name Lyon as the guilty party. A Cricket Australia spokesperson said that the independent forum announced last week by David Boon and Todd Greenberg, CA’s chair and chief executive, was ‘the appropriate place for any information to be provided’.

The latest bombshell came on the day CA laid out the forum’s terms of reference, which will include the Test team’s ‘ball-management practices’ during the 2017-18 Ashes, when England’s players suspected the Australians were breaking the laws en route to a 4–0 win.

In the aftermath of the Cape Town Test, Daily Mail Sport revealed that David Warner had told the England players during post-series drinks that he had tampered with the ball.

But the forum’s scope will not extend beyond the South Africa series, which means the mints incident in Dubai will not be investigated.

The forum, which will be overseen by Fiona McLeod, a prominent barrister, will remain open for six weeks. And while its broad findings will be made public, individual testimony will remain confidential. No player or backroom staff member is obliged to take part, and there will be no retrospective punishments.

Boon said: ‘We are acutely aware of the enormous toll the renewed focus on this tour eight years ago has had on those involved and their welfare remains our main priority.’

Meanwhile, Lyon is set to be left out of Australia’s squad for the first Test against New Zealand at Perth, starting on December 9, though his likely omission is thought to have nothing to do with the latest revelations.

Sports.title: Man United launch new matchday mental health and suicide prevention hub at OId Trafford for Brentford clash
Sports.content:
Manchester United will launch a new matchday mental health and suicide prevention initiative at Saturday’s game against Brentford at Old Trafford.

Working with the Premier League and Talk About It Mate, a support group based in Salford, United will host 10 sessions of The Check-In this season aimed at providing a welcoming space where supporters can drop in to talk with trained counsellors and volunteers.

Rhys Bennett, who was the captain of United's last FA Youth Cup-winning team in 2022, has spoken about the benefits of a recent Talk About It Mate session at Salford Lads Club. Bennett’s father David tragically took his own life last year.

‘It’s probably the most powerful thing I’ve ever done,’ said Bennett. ‘I’ve never done anything like this before. It’s made me feel even better than I did when I came in the door two hours ago. I’ve enjoyed every minute of it.

‘My dad passed at 51 and I think he grew up in the, “you’ll be alright, just crack on” (generation). He was an honest working man, and he went about his daily business until it became too much for him.

‘For him it would have been a really important thing to get things off his chest. A judgement free zone. It would have helped him massively. People are sharing the same experiences, people sat in a circle all going through different things.

Manchester United will launch a new matchday mental health and suicide prevention initiative at Saturday’s game against Brentford at Old Trafford

Rhys Bennett (right), who was the captain of United's last FA Youth Cup-winning team in 2022, attended a recent Talk About It Mate session at Salford Lads Club

‘To be honest, I was a little bit nervous. I'm not a nervous kind of person, but I think within five minutes, it's just no judgment and having that full confidence in being able to talk about how I'm really feeling.

‘I'm coming up for a year of my dad's passing. My dad committed suicide, and I played football for a living. I think it's hard navigating through being in a high-pressure environment.

‘I think it is the judgment thing, and not wanting to burden other people. But I think it's so important that you realise that most of the time it's not a burden.’

Bennett, who made a permanent move to Fleetwood in the summer and played in the League Two club’s shock Carabao Cup win over Arsenal last month, added: ‘You put the brave face on, and I feel weaker. But the more I talk about it, and the more I let my emotions out, that definitely does make me stronger in day-to-day life.

‘I used to just shut it out because I'm rocking up on a Saturday and a Tuesday in front of fans, and I've got to perform, and I feel everything. You get the adrenaline and everything of a football match, and then I'm back down to square one.

‘Just how open everyone was and how open I could be myself, really did surprise me. There wasn’t at any point that I couldn’t share something I was feeling. Everything came from the heart, it was really authentic and really powerful.’

Running five weekly men’s groups across Salford and with more than 1,000 group sessions delivered, Talk About It Mate creates spaces where men can connect, share experiences and support one another.

With a community-led approach to improving mental health and well-being, the organisation helps men build connections and reduce isolation.

United will host 10 sessions of The Check-In this season aimed at providing a welcoming space where supporters can drop in to talk with trained counsellors and volunteers

Bennett, whose father David tragically took his own life last year, spoke about how the session gave him 'full confidence in being able to talk about how I'm really feeling'

Man United say their partnership with Talk About It Mate will provide a welcoming space where supporters can access help on matchdays

Mike Richard, founder of Talk About It Mate, said: ‘We've spent years creating spaces where men feel safe enough to open up, and we're proud to be working with Manchester United to bring that approach to supporters.

‘Football has an incredible ability to bring people together, but being surrounded by thousands of people doesn't necessarily mean you feel connected. We know that some of the most important conversations can start in ordinary, familiar places – that's the kind of environment we want to create at Old Trafford.

‘This isn't about waiting until someone reaches crisis point. It's about making conversations around mental health a normal part of everyday life.’

According to The Samaritans, 5,738 suicides were registered in England in 2025, which equates to 11.1 deaths per 100,000 people.

The male suicide rate was 17.2 per 100,000 – compared to 5.4 per cent among females – with men aged 50-54 having the highest rate of any population group.

Rachel Fraser, United’s internal communications and inclusion director, said: ‘Our fans give so much to this club, and ensuring they feel supported in return is incredibly important to us.

‘Through our partnership with Talk About It Mate, we are proud to provide a welcoming space where supporters can access help on matchdays.

‘Football creates friendships and communities for fans that span generations. The Check-In builds on that sense of connection and seamlessly fits into the matchday routine, providing a safe and accessible space for those needing support.’

If you are affected by any of the issues raised in this article, please call the Samaritans for free on 116123.

Sports.title: Tyson Fury is CLEARED to fight Anthony Joshua: Gypsy King clears medical checks after Netflix schizophrenia claim threw $150m bout into jeopardy
Sports.content:
Tyson Fury has been given the medical all clear for his British bonanza fight against Anthony Joshua.

The mega millions world heavyweight title battle at Cardiff's Principality Stadium on December 11 was in jeopardy following claims that the Gypsy King is suffering from schizophrenia.

British Boxing Board of Control general secretary Robert Smith accelerated a review by doctors who found him fit late last night.

Smith says: 'All up to date medicals satisfactory and the promoters informed this morning.'

US streaming giant Netflix have deleted the panic inducing portion of their Fury documentary in which his wife Paris was pushed to suggest he was schizophrenic as well as bipolar.

Such a condition would have obliged the Board's medics to deny permission for the Gypsy King to enter the ring.

Tyson Fury has been given the medical all clear for his British bonanza fight against Anthony Joshua

The mega millions world heavyweight title battle at Cardiff's Principality Stadium on December 11 was in jeopardy

In which case hundreds of millions of dollars would have been lost by all involved in this huge promotion.

Fury's wife, Paris, tried desperately to row back on her original claims, saying Tyson 'doesn’t have' schizophrenia and 'has never received a diagnosis'.

Netflix confirmed that Paris's suggestion has been removed from the documentary.

A statement read: 'Following new information shared by the family relating to Tyson’s official mental health diagnosis, we have worked alongside them to update the documentary accordingly ahead of launch.'

After that 'new information' was received, Paris said: 'I want to clarify a statement I made in the original version of the Tyson Fury documentary.

'I recalled a conversation from many years ago when discussing Tyson’s condition and I used the word "schizophrenic".

'Whilst Tyson did show some symptoms associated with schizophrenia, he doesn’t have this condition and has never received a diagnosis.

'Mental health is complex, and it isn’t always easy to find the right words, especially when you’re living it with someone you love.

'I’m so proud of Tyson for really opening up in this documentary and want to say thank you for all the support we’ve received as a family.'

His wife Paris now insists that he is not schizophrenic having originally claimed he had 'mild schizophrenia'

Fury had no chance of being allowed to fight Joshua unless doctors were convinced he is mentally stable

Smith, the general secretary of British Boxing's Board of Control, confirmed Fury had no chance of being allowed to fight Joshua unless doctors were convinced he is mentally stable.

'Only one thing is certain,' he said. 'That Tyson will not be allowed to enter the ring unless our doctors are satisfied there is no risk to his health.

'We are reviewing all the information about his mental condition and will come to a decision about authorising the fight in the next few days.'

In the 90-minute documentary, Fury opens up on his mental health, admitting: 'Words can’t explain the darkness I was in.

'It was like the living version of the pits of hell’s fire. I 100 per cent thought I’d end up in a padded room with the door locked and that scared me so much.'

Fury and AJ are in line to bank $150million between them for the night's work, while the Principality Stadium, Saudi Arabian backers under His Excellency Turki Alalshikh and hotels, bars and restaurants in Cardiff would also have been stung if the fight was unable to go ahead.

Netflix want to use the all-British showdown to cement their move into major boxing.

The start time of the fight was moved to the early hours of the morning at Netflix's request in a bid to cater to an American audience and maximise the numbers tuning in.

That meant Cardiff Council had to grant special dispensation for a 1.30am UK fight time on December 11 and locals complained the extended curfew could cause issues in the surrounding area.

Despite early reports of an 80,000-plus sell-out in just an hour on the day tickets went on the market, there are still hundreds of seats for sale. Some being pushed with an offer of beer being thrown in.

This raises further concern about the impact of alcohol on the traditionally rowdy Friday night in Cardiff when the Stadium empties the crowd onto the street at around 3am. So much so that the police are considering breathalysing late arrivals at the fight.

Sports.title: Germany star Manuel Neuer, 40, hit with cheating claims as estranged wife suggests goalkeeper was unfaithful while she was pregnant - as he grows closer to physio, 23
Sports.content:
Germany star Manuel Neuer, 40, hit with cheating claims as estranged wife suggests goalkeeper was unfaithful while she was pregnant - as he grows closer to physio, 23

Manuel Neuer's estranged wife Anika has shared a post declaring that 'cheating on pregnant women is a whole different level of evil' following her split from the Bayern Munich and Germany star.

The couple, who had a civil wedding in 2023 and held a larger wedding celebration in 2025, welcomed the birth of their second son in late August.

German newspaper Bild reported that Neuer had informed Anika that he no longer wished to continue their marriage days after the birth.

Neuer has since been photographed with an unidentified woman, who BILD reported as being a 23-year-old physiotherapist that the goalkeeper has worked with.

The goalkeeper was spotted with the woman in Brazil this month, but reports have since emerged that they had also been seen on holiday in Sicily back in September.

While Anika did not specifically accuse Neuer and there is no evidence to suggest he has been unfaithful, she has since reposted a message on social media which criticised men who have cheated on their pregnant partners.

Manuel Neuer reportedly informed his wife Anika he wanted to end their marriage days after the birth of the couple's second child

Anika reshared a post on social media which criticised men who cheat on their pregnant partners

The couple had their second child in August. Pictured: Anika watching Bayern Munich training in July

'Cheating on a pregnant woman is a whole different level of evil,' the post read.

'Imagine looking at the woman carrying your child, watching her body change, seeing her struggle, get tired, and go through everything that comes with pregnancy and you still have the audacity to betray her behind her back.

'She's carrying YOUR child while you're out there entertaining someone else. The woman who should be feeling loved, protected, and supported is instead left dealing with pain that you caused.

'That's not a 'mistake.' That's a choice. A selfish, heartless, disrespectful choice.

'If you can betray the woman carrying your own child, especially when she needs you the most, you don't just lack loyalty, you lack basic decency and respect.

'DISGUSTING.'

Neuer, who reportedly moved out of the family home in October, has not spoken publicly about the separation or reports of a new relationship.

The 40-year-old, who is currently recovering from injury, has faced a backlash in Germany with relationship counsellor Ruth Marquardt accusing him of 'abandoning his wife and children'.

The Germany and Bayern Munich goalkeeper married Anika in 2023 with the couple having two children

Anika, who is Neuer's second wife, is a professional handball player but halted her career in 2025 to focus on parenting

Neuer has faced a backlash in Germany following reports of his split from Anika

The post was liked by the wives of Neuer's Bayern Munich team-mates Joshua Kimmich and Konrad Laimer, as well as the goalkeeper's ex-wife Nina, who he separated from in 2020.

Neuer has also been criticised by Germany and Bayern Munich legend Lothar Matthaus on his show 'Lothar Takes Off'.

'It's certainly not something they discuss in the locker room, but I understand - we do have freedom of speech in Germany - that a wife of Joshua Kimmich or Konrad Laimer might like the video, because I think they can perhaps empathise with the situation, that it's not good for Mrs. Neuer in any way,' Matthaus said.

'And the timing is just adding insult to injury. It's an unfortunate situation for Manuel, but everyone has to deal with it privately as they see fit. But of course, what's happened in recent weeks is certainly not the best thing for Manuel's reputation.

'He made that decision, but I think it wasn't the best time. On the other hand, he has to sort it out for himself, he has to try to solve his personal problems himself.

'I also don't know what the agreement is between him and his wife. He's old enough and actually clever enough.

'And from that perspective, it did surprise me that he was going on vacation or to rehab in Sicily and Brazil at this particular time. Those are his private matters, but he could have arranged it better in terms of timing.'

Neuer, who won 128 caps for Germany and was a key part of their 2014 World Cup winning squad, is currently sidelined with an ankle injury.

Neuer, 40, is currently sidelined with an ankle injury and is expected to return in the New Year

Bayern Munich board member Max Eberl confirmed earlier this month that the veteran star had been given time off to relax, with his rehabilitation expected to see him return to action in the New Year.

Sporting director Christoph Freund admitted on Thursday that Neuer is currently going through a ‘difficult period in his life’.

'Manu is back [in Munich] now. He's obviously going through a difficult period in his life, particularly with this latest injury,’ Freund said.

'Manu naturally wants to spend as much time as possible with the team and be out on the pitch as much as possible. But I think this short period away, when he wasn't here every day in the rehab area, has done him quite a bit of good.

‘He seems positive now. He wants to get back, the pain has subsided, and he's making good progress.

‘The other matters are Manu's private matters, and I don't want to comment on those. Of course, information spreads very quickly these days.

‘I think you always have to be very, very careful about what you associate yourself with when you don't know the exact circumstances. I know that's a rather general statement, but I think it's important to be extremely cautious.’

Sports.title: How Leeds United turned into Champions League contenders: Insiders reveal the ways 'manager's dream' Ethan Ampadu drives standards on and off the pitch, a hidden tougher side to Daniel Farke - and the club's January transfer window strategy
Sports.content:
How Leeds United turned into Champions League contenders: Insiders reveal the ways 'manager's dream' Ethan Ampadu drives standards on and off the pitch, a hidden tougher side to Daniel Farke - and the club's January transfer window strategy

He may not realise it yet, but the key member of Leeds United’s ever-improving team might just become one of their next great managers.

Leeds have been deservedly praised for their impressive start to the season, which sees them a point away from the likely Champions League places ahead of Saturday’s clash with Coventry.

Boss Daniel Farke is re-establishing the club in the top flight. Dominic Calvert-Lewin has signed a new contract and is an England player again. Towering centre back Tarik Muharemovic looks the buy of the season. The 49ers Enterprises Group are shrewd and careful owners.

But what about the guy who knits it all together? Ethan Ampadu had played for six clubs in three countries before he joined Leeds in 2023 but now he has found his home. Nearly half of Ampadu’s senior appearances have been in a Leeds shirt.

Ampadu’s work on the pitch and his behaviour off it suggest a manager in the making. Team-mates turn to him instinctively during matches and off the field, too, he makes Leeds tick.

‘I don’t know what Ethan’s plans are when he's finished playing but he has the stature and could offer a lot to the game beyond his playing career,’ says Stuart Dallas, who helped Leeds return to the Premier League in 2020 during an outstanding nine-year career at Elland Road.

Here Daily Mail Sport looks at why Leeds are on the rise – starting with their inspirational captain.

Inspired by brilliant new signings including Tarik Muharemovic (left) and James Trafford, Leeds are on the rise and in contention for the Champions League spots

Captain Ethan Ampadu makes Leeds tick on and off the pitch and is perceived as a manager in waiting

In the here and now, boss Daniel Farke is doing a superb job, having narrowly avoided being sacked in previous seasons

The Ampadu factor

Though Dallas retired due to injury at the end of Ampadu’s first campaign at Leeds, he liked what he saw in those months.

‘I was at the training ground recently and the players had a later start – they were preparing for a Sunday game,’ Dallas, now a regular television pundit, tells Daily Mail Sport. ‘He was the first to turn up for the session. If you’re a young player coming through, it’s fantastic to see the captain setting that example.

‘He is an intelligent guy who takes responsibility. In his position you have to front up when things are not going well and protect people when they need it. He understands that.

‘A manager doesn’t want 20 different people knocking on his door. Ethan will take a lot of those minor problems away and I know how much of a privilege it is to him to captain Leeds.’

Ampadu takes the role extremely seriously. Daily Mail Sport understands he ensured Under-21 players who train regularly with the first team were included in the players' bonus pool. He also made sure they were listed as first-team squad members on the club website.

Ampadu wants the squad to feel like a family and will organise team bonding trips and meals out. Little things like that go a heck of a long way.

The club's leadership group comprises Ampadu, Calvert-Lewin, Jaka Bijol, Joe Rodon and James Justin – but third-choice goalkeeper Alex Cairns is another hugely respected figure in the squad.

Prolific striker Dominic Calvert-Lewin (pictured scoring in Leeds' 4-1 rout of Chelsea last weekend) has signed a new contract with the club

Calvert-Lewin (with Noah Okafor, right) is part of the team's leadership group, led by Ampadu

‘Ethan is a manager’s dream,’ explains former Leeds boss Simon Grayson, now a regular pundit on Leeds’ in-house TV channel LUTV. ‘Someone like that makes the manager’s job much less stressful.

‘If there’s an incident on or off the pitch, sometimes the captain can deal with it before it reaches the manager’s door. Ethan will do that. He has a level of respect from the other players so if he says something, it’s no different from Daniel Farke saying it.’

Farke is usually cautious when bringing back players from injury. When they are as important as Ampadu, though, he is prepared to make an exception.

The 26-year-old does not immediately catch the eye. He does not make spectacular passes or beat three opponents with a piece of skill. He has only three goals in 139 appearances.

Instead, he steps back into defence to cover the forward runs of Justin or Jayden Bogle. He makes sure he is in the right spot to stop counter-attacks. He is the one to notice when a team-mate has drifted out of position when defending a set-piece. Scouts see this and this is why Ampadu was considered by clubs in the so-called ‘Big Six’ before he signed a new four-year deal with Leeds last June.

‘He’ll go in and smash someone – fairly – if it’s a quiet game because it will wake the crowd up a bit,’ smiles Grayson. ‘You only realise how much you miss players like that when they are not in the team.’

Ampadu is just as popular with the fans. ‘As Leeds captains go, Gary McAllister and Lucas Radebe set a high bar when I was growing up,' says Rocco Dean of the Leeds, That! podcast. 'Although Ampadu has a little way to go, it's not inconceivable he could one day rank alongside those greats.'

At any time, there will usually be two or three players in a squad who are not popular with supporters. It is difficult to find them in the current Leeds side. ‘The players want to play for Leeds and it’s not just a "job",’ adds Mike Chard, who runs the All Leeds TV YouTube channel. ‘They don’t seem like a team. They seem like a family.’

‘As Leeds captains go, Gary McAllister and Lucas Radebe set a high bar when I was growing up... but Ampadu could one day rank alongside those greats'

Farke’s World

Leeds have a broad agreement with Farke over a new contract and he deserves it. If Leeds beat Coventry, it will be his 80th win as boss in 162 games. Bielsa reached 80 in 163 matches.

In front of the cameras, Farke is open and affable – but he is no soft touch with his squad or coaches. The staff member who wore a snood over his head to training this week will be forced to don shorts and T-shirt for the remainder of the winter. His crime? Acting ‘big time’.

Footballers like to fool about when they are together but few would dare risk it when Farke is nearby. Daily Mail Sport has heard of one player who was acting the goat in the canteen and turned white when he realised he had failed to notice Farke entering the room.

Some bosses will encourage players to ask why they have been left out of the team. That is not typically the case with Farke. Generally, he makes his choices and then it falls to players to prove him wrong through their displays in training.

He can still forge close relationships with players, though. His rapport with Calvert-Lewin was a factor in the striker’s new deal and he has a similarly strong understanding with Noah Okafor.

Farke is probably as powerful now as he has ever been during his three-and-a-half seasons at Elland Road. At different points during his two Championship campaigns in charge, Farke was vulnerable to the sack. Even early last season, things looked a little dicey for him.

Switching to a back three in the 3-2 defeat at Manchester City last November turned it around for Leeds but this is about much more than a simple change of formation.

Despite his affable exterior and close bonds with certain players, Farke has a disciplinarian streak

Most of Leeds’ medical and conditioning team have been at Elland Road for more than a decade and unlike at many clubs, there is complete trust between them and Farke. The result? No injuries to first-team players as things stand.

On their instruction, Farke restricted Okafor to a 20-minute substitute appearance against Tottenham earlier this month. The Swiss attacker still scored the only goal.

In a typical week after a Saturday game, players will report to Thorp Arch for a recovery session on Sunday and have Monday off. Wednesday is usually the toughest day – gym in the morning followed by a training session, and more gym work in the afternoon.

Farke and his staff favour two particular possession drills: a four-a-side game with three ‘floating’ players who work with whoever has the ball, and a 10-a-side exercise with two floating players.

Brighton and Brentford have set the standard for recruitment in the last decade yet since promotion Leeds have not been far behind. Chairman Paraag Marathe has worked for global management consultants Bain, who rely heavily on data.

Led by sporting director Adam Underwood, Leeds do the same – though they mix art with science. New signings are shown videos of the celebrations in the city when Leeds were promoted in 2025. The current brief is to find physically robust, athletic players and unlike many clubs, Leeds are not obsessed with youth. The average age of their starting XI for the 4-1 win at Stamford Bridge was 27 years and 107 days. That figure has not dipped below 26 in any league game this season.

Underwood and his team anticipate a quiet January window in which no key players are expected to leave – dashing any hopes rivals may have had of stealing Muharemovic. The defender joined from Sassuolo for £30.1million last summer and his value is already much higher.

Under chairman Paraag Marathe (right), Leeds rely heavily on data in their recruitment. Their transfer track record has been excellent in recent years

What happens next?

The pinch point for the 49ers is coming. They aim to make Leeds worth £1billion by 2030. That will require significantly greater revenue: in 2024-25, when Leeds were promoted from the Championship, their revenue was £137m. That was a record for the second tier but they will likely need to exceed £300m in the coming years to hit the 49ers' £1bn target.

An expanded Elland Road should plug some of this gap when work is complete. Leeds are working on each stand in turn and hope the project will be finished by the end of 2030, giving them a 53,000 capacity.

Earlier this month, Leeds instructed US bank Allen & Co to seek additional investment, though it is thought a full sale is not currently on the cards.

Christian Purslow offers a different perspective. The former Aston Villa CEO, who also held senior positions at Liverpool and Chelsea, knows how tough it is for clubs outside the Big Six to break into that wealthy elite.

Speaking on The Football Boardcast, Purslow said: ‘If I were Paraag Marathe, I’d be looking at what’s gone on at some of my natural peers – Newcastle, Aston Villa, West Ham, Leicester, Everton. It’s so precarious when clubs like these try hard to push up against the so-called Big Six.

‘These guys (the 49ers) might conclude: "We’ve done our job, we’ve enjoyed the journey, let’s let someone else have the problem of competing with the Big Six in a world where Premier League and UEFA financial rules make it increasingly difficult." I would not rule that out in the next couple of years.’

‘They are allowed to dream big and enjoy themselves,’ Farke said of Leeds' supporters this week

Leeds are in no hurry. The sense at Elland Road is that the 49ers will not seek a shortcut by raising the wage bill or appointing a manager on a huge salary. They are prepared to go slow and steady.

As Purslow highlighted, if Newcastle – who have some of the world’s wealthiest owners – have accepted they cannot change the status quo, what chance does anyone else have?

After spending much of this century feeling gloomy, though, Leeds fans do not want to think about it too deeply.

‘They are allowed to dream big and enjoy themselves,’ Farke said this week. ‘After nearly three decades of suffering, it is a joy to bring this hope and belief back into the hearts, heads and souls of our supporters. This is why we are working so hard.’

Sports.title: Netflix deletes Tyson Fury schizophrenia revelation from documentary after Paris claimed boxer has NOT been medically diagnosed with condition - after bombshell plunged $150m Anthony Joshua fight into chaos
Sports.content:
Netflix has been forced to remove a revelation that Tyson Fury has schizophrenia from their documentary on the boxer after it threatened to put his $150million fight with Anthony Joshua in jeopardy.

The bombshell had come from Fury's wife Paris, who had said 'he’s a mild schizophrenic' in promotional material for the programme, which was released this morning.

The disclosure had put Fury's upcoming heavyweight bout at risk of being cancelled as official regulations state boxers cannot fight with 'any psychological disorder such as depression, schizophrenia or hyper-mania', as reported by Daily Mail Sport.

It sparked panic at Netflix, which is also broadcasting the lucrative showdown and expects 60 million subscribers to watch.

Fury, 38, now needs to be rigorously assessed to determine whether he is mentally fit to fight AJ on December 11 and cash in on the enormous $150million (£115million) pot to be split between them.

It would be disastrous, and hugely expensive, for Netflix and the fight's venue, the Principality Stadium in Cardiff, if Paris's original statement led to the fight being cancelled and she has now retracted her claim.

The 36-year-old has tried desperately to row back on her original claims, saying Tyson 'doesn’t have' schizophrenia and 'has never received a diagnosis'.

Tyson Fury (left) will be rigorously assessed by doctors before his fight with Anthony Joshua can go ahead as they check his mental capacity to compete

Netflix confirmed that Paris's suggestion has been removed from the documentary.

A statement read: 'Following new information shared by the family relating to Tyson’s official mental health diagnosis, we have worked alongside them to update the documentary accordingly ahead of launch.'

After that 'new information' was received, Paris said: 'I want to clarify a statement I made in the original version of the Tyson Fury documentary.

'I recalled a conversation from many years ago when discussing Tyson’s condition and I used the word "schizophrenic".

'Whilst Tyson did show some symptoms associated with schizophrenia, he doesn’t have this condition and has never received a diagnosis.

'Mental health is complex, and it isn’t always easy to find the right words, especially when you’re living it with someone you love.

'I’m so proud of Tyson for really opening up in this documentary and want to say thank you for all the support we’ve received as a family.'

Robert Smith, the general secretary of British Boxing's Board of Control, confirmed Fury has no chance of being allowed to fight Joshua unless doctors are convinced he is mentally stable.

'Only one thing is certain,' he said. 'That Tyson will not be allowed to enter the ring unless our doctors are satisfied there is no risk to his health.

His wife Paris now insists that he is not schizophrenic having originally claimed he had 'mild schizophrenia'

Fury's fight with AJ has been years in the making and has been plunged into chaos yet again

'We are reviewing all the information about his mental condition and will come to a decision about authorising the fight in the next few days.'

The board's consultants will be checking if there is any proper medical evidence to support the anecdotal broadcast. Or if the now-deleted allegations in the documentary are at best exaggerated or at worst sensationalised.

In the 90-minute documentary, Fury opens up on his mental health, admitting: 'Words can’t explain the darkness I was in.

'It was like the living version of the pits of hell’s fire. I 100 per cent thought I’d end up in a padded room with the door locked and that scared me so much.'

Even if Fury is not diagnosed as schizophrenic, doctors will also have to confirm he is not currently suffering from the depression that has plagued him at various points during his career that he regularly refers to in the documentary.

If the BBC's medical team find him to be in the grip of the illness again, they will not be able to allow the heavyweight superstar to step in the ring for one of his biggest paydays.

Fury and AJ are in line to bank $150million between them for the night's work, while the Principality Stadium, Saudi Arabian backers under His Excellency Turki Alalshikh and hotels, bars and restaurants in Cardiff would also be stung if the fight was unable to go ahead.

The British Boxing Board of Control could have to pull the fight if Fury is found to be suffering from schizophrenia or even depression

Netflix want to use the all-British showdown to cement their move into major boxing but persisting public doubts still linger about whether the fight for which the sporting world has waited for a decade will indeed take place in a fortnight.

The start time of the fight was moved to the early hours of the morning at Netflix's request in a bid to cater to an American audience and maximise the numbers tuning in.

That meant Cardiff Council had to grant special dispensation for a 1.30am UK fight time on December 11 and locals complained the extended curfew could cause issues in the surrounding area.

Despite early reports of an 80,000-plus sell-out in just an hour on the day tickets went on the market, there are still hundreds of seats for sale. Some being pushed with an offer of beer being thrown in.

This raises further concern about the impact of alcohol on the traditionally rowdy Friday night in Cardiff when the Stadium empties the crowd onto the street at around 3am. So much so that the police are considering breathalysing late arrivals at the fight.

For now, Netflix and all of the many parties with an interest in the fight going off without a hitch will be sweating on the outcome of Fury's medical review in the coming days.

Sports.title: Heavyweight Matty Harris hungrier than ever under Peter Fury
Sports.content:
Heavyweight Matty Harris hungrier than ever under Peter Fury

Matty Harris continues his career in Denmark this weekend looking to make his mark in the heavyweight division

View 2 Images Matty Harris with trainer Peter Fury

Matty Harris knows how it feels to think you’re unbeatable – and the cost when you’re not.

‌



‌



The 26-year-old heavyweight boxer was flattening his opponents early until a heavy defeat arrived at 23. Now, revitalised under trainer Peter Fury, he has a different mindset ahead of an eight-round fight in Copenhagen on Saturday night. “I was ending fights very quickly and it was working – until it didn’t,” chuckles Harris, echoing the famous Mike Tyson quip: “Everyone has a plan until they get punched in the mouth.”

‌



Matty is refreshingly honest about why his usual plan went wrong. Injuries had wrecked his build-up, he hadn’t been sparring, and his coach wanted him to pull out. “But I didn’t listen,” admits Harris. “When you’re younger and that confident, it can slide into arrogance, so I said, ‘Don’t worry, I’ll soon get him out of there.’ And then I got beat.”

‌



Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources

Giving up boxing was never an option: “I’ve never been a quitter,” he says. That stubbornness had enabled Harris to fund his own training through a string of jobs – Asda delivery driver, labourer, warehouse worker and even Starbucks barista, where, at 16, he once served coffee to major boxing promoter Eddie Hearn.

“I told him I would box for him one day,” Harris says, showing the ambition that eventually led him to a career rebirth under the care of Fury. Harris had trained with Fury years earlier and reckons he boxed his best then. Looking for a change of coach after his shock defeat at 23, he vowed: “I wasn’t going with anyone else other than Peter. And I quickly learned what real discipline is, in every sense – how I eat, how I train, how I sleep, how I recover.”

‌



Defence and footwork top the agenda. Sparring, something he once rarely did, is now routine, including 10- to 12-round sessions to teach him how to pace a long fight – something he failed to do before. Coventry-born Harris also recalls running up a mountain near a Fury training camp, reaching the top after a lung-bursting 15 minutes, only for Peter – who had been following in his car – to pick him up, drive him back down and tell him to do it all again.

Yet there’s no hint of resentment, especially as Peter trains alongside his fighters: “When I’m training, he’s training,” says Harris, clearly impressed when Peter recently joined his charges on a 10km run. The Fury diet is just as strict – eggs, rice, fish, chicken and veg, all cooked by Harris himself – though Peter is a big foodie and occasionally treats the team to meals at top restaurants.

‌



View 2 Images Matty Harris in action against Franklin Ignatius

Fury training has taken the stable to the Netherlands, Fuengirola near Marbella, and Valencia, and Harris is pleased with the regime: “I’m lighter, hitting harder. And I’m faster.” His Copenhagen fight is against German-based boxer Rashad Karimov. Harris only recently learned he’d be facing the quick, sharp contender, but he’s unfazed: “I do fear not performing well, but never the man.”

Article continues below

The longer-term plan is the English heavyweight title, then the British, with Harris promising to be British champion by the end of 2027. He turns 27 on 14 January and wants to be “moving on to bigger and better things” by then. Boxing has been in his life since he started kickboxing aged four. A possible football career beckoned, including spells with the Coventry City and Aston Villa academies, but was derailed by leg and ankle injuries – and Harris says he never loved the game anyway.

Boxing, by contrast, is all-consuming, leaving no time for hobbies and making Harris realise he could be back serving coffee for a living were it not for Fury. Instead, with the star trainer in his corner, the arrogance has gone, the discipline is in place – and the hunger is greater than ever.

Sports.title: Tosin Adarabioyo lifts the lid on 'unbelievable' teammate and his Tottenham idol growing up
Sports.content:
Tosin Adarabioyo couldn't help but laugh when he was quizzed about whether he grew up supporting Tottenham Hotspur, as though he'd been caught out.

The 29 year old finally made his way to Spurs this summer after several near misses over the years, completing a £10million move from Chelsea through the Hotspur Way doors, with a further £2million in potential add-ons. Upon his arrival, eagle-eyed fans unearthed old tweets from his teenage years that appeared to indicate the centre-back had been a Tottenham supporter all along.

Thirteen years on from those tweets, Tosin couldn't suppress a grin when the subject was raised.

"There was a time, yeah. There was a time where Spurs were one of my favourite teams to watch. You obviously see Van der Vaart was one of my favourite players. So there was a time, yeah," he told Football London, before acknowledging that his summer transfer had brought things full circle.

‌
