Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

"Yeah, of course [it does]. There were a few times where there were talks [to join previously], but everything happens at the right time, and I'm here now and I'm very happy to be here as well.

"[Roberto De Zerbi] is a manager that I've loved for a long time and I think I'm a player that he's loved for a long time, so it's working well."

‌



The former Fulham centre-back has already made his mark in his two appearances to date against Liverpool and Coventry, and it speaks volumes about how rapidly he has won over supporters at the north London outfit that several Spurs teammates attended the launch this week of his new trading card shop in London, Card Cop.

Micky van de Ven, Marcos Senesi, Archie Gray, Ben Davies, Destiny Udogie and Tosin's close friend Dominic Solanke, alongside former Spurs players Dele Alli and Kyle Walker-Peters, were amongst those who visited the new premises in Borough Yards, which officially opens on Thursday as a venue for those engaged in the card trading scene, which is enormous in the USA and expanding quickly in the UK.

"It's a testament to what we're like as a team. We're all very close and very supportive of each other. The boys didn't have to turn up today, but they did. It's amazing. I'm very thankful to them," Tosin said.

View 3 Images Tosin Adarabioyo has quickly impressed Tottenham supporters

‌



The Manchester City academy product is relishing the competition with Van de Ven, Senesi and Jan Paul van Hecke, with Tottenham at last possessing genuine depth in the heart of De Zerbi's defence.

"It's amazing. The quality of the team is top, so it helps for these games where we're able to rotate. You could see at the weekend when Marcos came in and played absolutely amazingly," he said. One Tottenham player commanding attention at the moment is 18 year old Luca Williams-Barnett.

The teenage forward bagged a Premier League goal and assist on his full debut for the club against Ipswich on Saturday before penning a substantial new five-year contract on Tuesday.

When questioned about the youngster, Tosin let out a big whoosh of air before saying: "What a player, man. He's unbelievable. He's a top, top player and to coincide with what we're doing here, his rookie cards are going to go through the roof! It's nice to see."

‌



Spurs are gathering momentum following a difficult opening to the season with four victories from their last five fixtures, including three consecutive wins at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium, and the towering centre-back attributes it to one factor.

"It's our trip to Marbella," he confessed with a chuckle. "It's our trip to Marbella, man. We had a great time. We bonded together. We learned a lot about each other and we're all striving to put this club where we think it belongs."

View 3 Images Teenager Luca Williams-Barnett has already wowed his teammates (Image: Mark Leech/Offside)

The squad put their mobile phones aside during the days in Spain and instead grew closer as a unit in one another's presence.

‌



"It was nice, you know. We're all the same. We all look at our phones way too much. It's nice to have a time away from our phones and just live life how it's supposed to be lived," Tosin remarked.

"We just went for dinner. We went for lunch. We had some nights out together, and we bonded really well."

Spurs will be hoping to maintain that momentum as they travel to 18th-placed Sunderland on Sunday afternoon in the Premier League.

Tosin's new London venture has been a long time coming, with backing from former Chelsea teammates Reece James and Levi Colwill, as well as ex-Tottenham defender Walker-Peters.

‌



"It's been in my mind for a long time. It's something I'm very passionate about, something I love doing, so it's always been in my mind to have the dream to open up a shop. Today has come to fruition and I'm very happy," he said.

"When you're a kid you do all sorts of collecting. Then in 2020 I started collecting small cards again, went to a card show in 2021 and it was amazing. I just completely fell in love with it again."

So which card does he treasure most from his collection?

‌



"Don't ask me that! I've got a Neymar that's locked away. I'm not going to tell you which one, but I've got a nice Neymar that's locked away!" said the defender.

Reflecting on the broader worth of cards, he added: "It can be the luck of the draw with the pack that you open, and it can go from £1 all the way to £1million. The prices can be crazy.

"To be honest, when I started collecting it had nothing to do with the monetary value. For me it's an amazing community, a way for players like me to connect with fans and for fans to connect with their favourite players.

"It's something I really enjoy and then okay you get the monetary value at the end of it, which is a plus and you get a lot of people in the space for that reason, but for me it's just the pure love."

‌

Sports.title: Jamie Carragher thinks Erling Haaland could leave Man City very soon on one condition
Sports.content:
Jamie Carragher thinks Erling Haaland could leave Manchester City soon, if Premier League punishments mean they will no longer be in a position to compete for honours.

City are still awaiting their fate after being found guilty of 114 of 115 charges for breaches of financial regulations. An independent commission adjudged City to have artificially inflated its revenue by £900million through “sham” commercial deals between 2009 and 2018.

Etihad bosses vehemently deny the charges and will their appeal will be heard in December, before a final verdict is confirmed in the new year.

If that initial finding is upheld, the Premier League have the power to lay down huge punishments, ranging from transfer embargoes and fines, to whopping points deductions and even expulsion from the top flight.

Three Premier League clubs want Man City owners to be forced into sale after guilty verdict READ MORE :

Black Friday special! Click here to sign up to Mirror+ for just £1 a month!

City’s players have continued to be asked questions on the matter, despite many - including Haaland - not being with the club during the impacted years.

Haaland had continued to be in blistering form despite the off-field noise, but has now gone three league games without a goal, with City failing to win their last four.

And Carragher, writing in his column for the Telegraph has suggested it is only human nature that the current crop of players will be considering their options.

“There is no questioning that commitment,” he explained. “Haaland’s goalscoring performance at Anfield in the first game after the guilty verdict was announced – and the sight of his father, Alfie, celebrating with fans in the away end – was symbolic of him being all-in with City’s appeal.

View 3 Images Haaland has gone three games without scoring and has cut a frustrated figure

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

“But Haaland also made a point of stressing how the charges pre-dated his time at City, even listing the youth teams he was playing for at the time of the misdemeanours to emphasise how little they had to do with him and his achievements.

“No matter how strong the protests, or insistence that an appeal is ongoing, it is human nature that players will be considering all possibilities, speaking publicly about their faith in the club, but privately wondering what will happen next and what it means for their careers.”

Haaland signed a blockbuster nine-and-a-half-year contract extension at the start of last year, meaning he is tied to the eight-time champions until 2034. But Carragher still thinks if City are no longer in contention for major honours, he could have his head turned by the likes of Real Madrid and Barcelona.

The Liverpool legend added: “Regardless of what is going on off the field this season, with all due respect to City, I have always felt one of the Spanish giants would be Haaland’s final destination.

“They must be awaiting the punishment imposed by the independent commission on behalf of the Premier League, believing it is bound to determine Haaland’s future.

View 3 Images Jamie Carragher thinks both Barcelona and Real Madrid could be options for Haaland (Image: James Gill - Danehouse/Getty Images)

“Should City get the kind of punishment which fits their guilty verdict, Haaland cannot be expected to spend the next four or five years of his peak at a club who are not competing for titles.”

Carragher goes as far to say that Haaland could leave in the next year, if City are hit with the kind of sanctions many expect.

Speaking after the midweek draw with Napoli, Haaland cut a deeply frustrated figure, admitting their current malaise was making the squad question everything.

"We tried to push but we couldn't. It's not good enough," he said. "We let them in too easily and were unable to control or attack the game as we want.

"Football can be so difficult and easy. When you win games, everything is easy, and you know exactly what to do, when you don't win you start to question everything. The perfect thing would be to don't think, but it's difficult in these moments."

Sports.title: Police recover part of 2003 Melbourne Cup stolen in robbery and 2kg of melted gold
Sports.content:
Police recover part of 2003 Melbourne Cup stolen in robbery and 2kg of melted gold

Three trophies won by the legendary Makybe Diva were stolen from a display at Flemington racecourse after this year’s Spring Carnival while a Caulfield Cup also went missing

View 2 Images Part of the Melbourne Cup and melted gold recovered by police (Image: Police Victoria)

Detectives hunting for four Melbourne Cups stolen in a robbery this month have recovered part of one trophy and melted gold.

‌



‌



Three trophies won by the legendary mare Makybe Diva, the only horse in history to win the big race three times, went missing with another cup while they were on display at Flemington racecourse during the Spring Carnival. The Caulfield Cup trophy was also reported stolen from Caulfield racecourse at around the same time.

‌



Police in Victoria have now made a breakthrough in their search for the priceless collection, which had been loaned to Flemington by Makybe Diva’s owner-breeder Tony Santic.

‌



A police statement said: “Moorabbin Crime Investigation Unit detectives have recovered part of one of the Melbourne Cups allegedly stolen from Flemington earlier this month.

Cheltenham switches December meeting from New to Old course due to lack of rain READ MORE :

“It’s alleged four Melbourne Cups were stolen from Flemington on 16 November.

‌



“The top part of a 2003 Melbourne Cup has been seized during a search warrant on Orrong Road in Elsternwick on 26 November. Approximately two kilograms of melted gold was also located by police during the warrant. This melted gold will be analysed as part of the ongoing investigation.”

The statement continued: “Detectives have also discovered what is believed to be the melted down 1948 Caulfield Cup that was allegedly stolen from Caulfield on 4 November. This was located in the Melbourne area after allegedly being on sold to a third party.”

‌



View 2 Images Makybe Diva: the only horse in history to win three Melbourne Cups

Police said a 39-year-old man was arrested on 16 November in relation to the Caulfield theft and charged with two counts of burglary, two counts of theft and possessing a drug of dependence.

Article continues below

The same man was re-arrested on 17 November in relation to the Flemington theft and charged with burglary, theft, two counts of handling stolen goods, two counts dealing in property suspected of being proceeds of crime, two counts of obtaining financial advantage and two counts of obtaining property by deception. He has been bailed to appear at Moorabbin Magistrates’ Court 1 March.

A 36-year-old Mount Waverley man was arrested on 19 November in Cheltenham in relation to the alleged Melbourne Cup thefts and charged with two counts of burglary, two counts of theft, committing an indictable offence whilst on bail and dealing in property suspected of being proceeds of crime. He has been remanded to appear at Melbourne Magistrates’ Court on 23 February.

Sports.title: Man Utd identify Bruno Fernandes replacement after captain makes contract stance clear
Sports.content:
Man Utd identify Bruno Fernandes replacement after captain makes contract stance clear

Manchester United have been forced to consider a future without captain Bruno Fernandes, who is out of contract in the summer, and have shortlisted Como star Nico Paz

View 2 Images Bruno Fernandes could leave Manchester United in 2027 (Image: Catherine Ivill - AMA/Getty Images)

Manchester United have reportedly shortlisted Como star Nico Paz as a possible replacement for Bruno Fernandes.

‌



‌



Fernandes' current contract is set to expire at the end of the season and there is doubt over his plans after he said negotiations are on hold over a new one. The United captain has reportedly turned down two proposals to stay at Old Trafford.

‌



The 32-year-old has pushed back against reports that he has asked for more money or a longer contract, but his decision to postpone talks has raised the possibility of his departure. United are desperate to keep Fernandes, yet have begun making contingency plans.

‌



They saw first-hand how impressive Paz can be, with the 22-year-old attacking midfielder tearing them apart and scoring twice in Como's 4-1 win in October. And The Athletic says United have Paz on their list of potential targets for 2027, although the deal would be complicated.

Como signed the Argentina international from Real Madrid in 2024 for just €6million (£5m) and the Spanish giants have a buy-back option. Real can sign Paz for €80m (£66m) in the summer of 2027, although the midfielder is understood not to favour a return to Madrid, where he wouldn't be guaranteed a starring role under Jose Mourinho.

If Real opted not to trigger their buy-back clause then Como would be free to sell as normal. Whether United would be able to attract such a talented young player in their current malaise - especially if they fail to qualify for the Champions League - remains to be seen.

‌



United do have some things in their favour, however. Paz shares the same agent as United boss Mauricio Pochettino and the club's history still carries some weight.

Paz has contributed six goals and eight assists in 16 appearances for Cesc Fabregas' side this season and is sure to have other suitors next year. His record of 25 goals and 25 assists in 91 games in total for Como, as well as his six goals in 16 games for Argentina, show his credentials.

‌



But Fernandes' boots would be big ones to fill at United, with the Portugal international having been their chief playmaker ever since his arrival from Sporting in 2020. He has previously been courted by Al-Hilal and Fenerbahce and was keen to emphasise his decision when they approached him when discussing his current situation this week.

"The club offered me a new contract, so I think that, from their side, shows that they want me to stay," Fernandes told Sky Sports. "There's no negotiations ongoing, but I've seen people saying that 'he's asked for more money, he's asked for more years'. If I wanted more money, I wouldn't be here.

"I had somewhere to go to get much more money than being at Manchester United. I could have been in a place that is much warmer than Manchester. Two summers ago, three summers ago, last summer, I always had the chance to leave and I always chose to be here."

Sports.title: Three Premier League clubs want Man City owners to be forced into sale after guilty verdict
Sports.content:
Three Premier League clubs want Man City owners to be forced into sale after guilty verdict

Manchester City are waiting for their appeal to be heard after being found guilty of breaking the Premier League's financial rules and their rivals are calling for action to be taken

View 3 Images Sheikh Mansour has owned Manchester City since 2008 (Image: Getty Images)

A trio of Manchester City's Premier League rivals want their owners to be forced to sell as punishment for their systematic breaking of financial rules.

‌



‌



City were found guilty in September of breaking the Premier League's financial rules over a nine-year period. An independent commission found them guilty of 114 of the 115 charges levelled against them, finding they had used "sham" contracts to inflate revenues or reduce costs by more than £900million.

‌



The club has always professed its innocence and their appeal is expected to be heard in December ahead of the final verdict being given in the new year. While City remain confident they will be exonerated, their rivals are already focused on potential punishments.

‌



City could be relegated from the Premier League, hit with a huge points deduction, stripped of past titles, given a transfer ban or fines. But that isn't all, with the Independent Football Regulator (IFR) possessing the power to go even further and target the club's owners, Abu Dhabi United Group, who are owned by Sheikh Mansour.

Black Friday special! Click here to sign up to Mirror+ for just £1 a month!

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



The IFR's chair David Kogan said this week that they have the "stomach" to take on Sheikh Mansour if the appeal fails and that would please some of their rivals. According to BBC Sport, three Premier League executives feel that the only fitting punishment is for City's owners to be expelled.

One Premier League executive has argued that City's punishment is 'irrelevant' unless the club's owners are forced out. Another anonymous executive believes the league's credibility has been damaged by City's rule-breaking between 2009 and 2018 and that they wouldn't be able to move on if their owners weren't forced to sell by the IFR.

‌



Speaking to MPs on the Digital, Culture, Media and Sport select committee this week, IFR chair Kogan suggested that is exactly what they would do.

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

‌



View 3 Images David Kogan says the IFR are ready to take action

“If you look at the specific sanctions we can impose, we have everything from deciding there is not sufficient evidence to take any action or removing them as directors and from any involvement with the club or English football going forward," he said.

‌



"But let’s be blunt. The two things I was asked about were: would we be subject to political pressure and did we have the stomach to take action?

“The answers are: We won’t be. And we have the stomach for that. We can’t be an independent football regulator and ignore our duties because the club is of a certain size.

‌



“Would I, given my choice with an organisation that has a relatively new, fairly young staff that’s been going for less than a year, would I have chosen to have this particular issue in our laps this early?

View 3 Images Man City were found guilty of 114 of the 115 charges brought by the Premier League

‌



"Well, probably not. But the truth is, if we don’t act, assuming those circumstances are triggered, if we don’t act, what is the purpose of having a football regulator?”

It comes after Emanuel Macedo de Medeiros, the co-founder and global chief executive of Sport Integrity Global Alliance (SIGA), warned that "justice" needs to be served quickly in order to protect the Premier League's credibility.

‌



“Whatever the final ruling will be, the process must follow applicable rules, established findings and due process," Medeiros told Mirror Football. "What is also indisputable is that football – and not just the parties involved – needs an outcome that is reasonable, credible and capable of commanding confidence.

"Because there is no doubt that there’s been rivers of ink and controversy around this case. I think that justice needs to prevail on its own terms without any constraints, but also with the notion that for justice to be justice, it needs to be served swiftly. That is very important."

Sports.title: Mauricio Pochettino suffers fresh Man Utd transfer blow after outlining January priority
Sports.content:
Mauricio Pochettino suffers fresh Man Utd transfer blow after outlining January priority

Mauricio Pochettino wants to sign a striker in the January transfer window but one of Manchester United's targets appears to have ruled himself out of a move already

View 2 Images Dominic Calvert-Lewin has signed a new contract with Leeds (Image: Malcolm Bryce/Leeds United via Getty Images)

Leeds have tied Dominic Calvert-Lewin down to a new contract amid interest from Manchester United. Calvert-Lewin, 29, has committed his future at Elland Road by putting pen to paper on a deal which runs until 2029.

‌



‌



The striker had 18 months left on his existing contract, but Leeds have rewarded him for his 21 goals in 52 games since he arrived as a free agent in 2025. Calvert-Lewin has also proven his fitness with Leeds, having struggled with injuries throughout his time at Everton.

‌



United had shortlisted him in their pursuit of a centre forward in the January transfer window. New manager Mauricio Pochettino has made the position a priority, with the Red Devils languishing in the Premier League relegation zone.

‌



But Calvert-Lewin's name can now be chalked off, with his new deal serving as a hands-off message. United are expected to look at alternatives, with Ivan Toney and Folarin Balogun both linked.

Toney, 30, is reportedly pushing to leave Saudi Arabia and play in the Premier League again following a prolific spell with Al-Ahli. As for Balogun, the 25-year-old worked with Pochettino at international level for the USA.

Joshua Zirkzee got the nod up front for United's 2-2 draw with Sporting Lisbon in the Champions League on Wednesday, with Matheus Cunha having led the line against Liverpool. Benjamin Sesko, who was their undisputed No.9 last season, has missed most of the campaign with a shin injury.

That is going to take us a massive step forward, that's going to deliver a richer experience for our fans and our community, that's going to allow more people to be in the stadium because Old Trafford has a capacity of just under 75,000 and we're aiming to build a stadium that's going to be 100,000."

Sports.title: Tyson Fury Netflix documentary edits schizophrenia claims at 11th hour as Paris speaks out
Sports.content:
Tyson Fury Netflix documentary edits schizophrenia claims at 11th hour as Paris speaks out

EXCLUSIVE - The documentary called Tyson Fury is released tomorrow but Netflix have edited one scene out which has been the subject of many headlines in recent days

View 3 Images Tyson speaks candidly in the doc ahead of his fight with Joshua in December (Image: Courtesy of Netflix)

Netflix have made a last-minute edit to their Tyson Fury documentary - after it emerged the boxer has not been medically diagnosed with schizophrenia.

‌



‌



The former heavyweight champion, 38, bravely speaks about battling his demons and overcoming suicidal thoughts in the two years which followed his victory over Vladimir Klitschko, in November 2015.

‌



And recalling that period of his life, wife Paris Fury had said in an interview for the documentary he had “mild schizophrenia” in this period.

‌



However, the film has now changed and in a statement, Paris told the Mirror: "I want to clarify a statement I made in the original version of the Tyson Fury documentary. I recalled a conversation from many years ago when discussing Tyson’s condition and I used the word ‘schizophrenic’.

"Whilst Tyson did show some symptoms associated with schizophrenia, he doesn’t have this condition and has never received a diagnosis. Mental health is complex, and it isn't always easy to find the right words, especially when you're living it with someone you love.

"I’m so proud of Tyson for really opening up in this documentary and want to say thank you for all the support we’ve received as a family."

‌



Tyson Fury says money can't make him happy despite million pound bank balance READ MORE :

First photo of Tyson Fury's reclusive mum Amber released after family heartbreak READ MORE :

View 3 Images One scene with Paris Fury in the documentary has been edited out (Image: Getty Images for Como 1907)

The film will be released on schedule as planned tomorrow at 8am with the change. In a statement, Netflix said: "Following new information shared by the family relating to Tyson’s official mental health diagnosis, we have worked alongside them to update the documentary accordingly ahead of launch.”

‌



The change to the documentary came as the initial comments about schizophrenia from Paris appeared to increase the scrutiny around Tyson Fury’s heavyweight clash with Anthony Joshua next month.

The British Boxing Board of Control regulations prohibit boxers from going into the ring if they have “any psychological disorder such as depression, schizophrenia or hyper-mania.”

‌



BBBofC General Secretary Robert Smith insisted Fury wouldn’t be able to take part in the Cardiff fight in December unless doctors are “satisfied” he’s completely sound of mind.

In the original version of the Netflix documentary seen by the Mirror, both Tyson and Paris spoke candidly about the tough times they faced a decade ago.

‌



In one scene, Paris recalled when Tyson saw doctors and a psychiatrist. She said: "He's a mild schizophrenic, and even then, the penny didn't drop. It was like, don't be silly.

“What's she on about schizophrenic? Maniacs are schizophrenic. You're not schizophrenic. You know? I'd never heard of bipolar. What's bipolar? I don't know, what's bipolar?

‌



"When somebody actually explained it to me, like, some days you can be as happy as anything, like, oh yeah, yeah, yeah, let's go, let's go, and then something can switch in it and be like, 'no, I can’t go outside today'. It's like, wow, that's him to a tee."

View 3 Images Paris and Tyson in the Netflix doc (Image: Courtesy of Netflix)

‌



Tyson also recalls in the film when he went to hospital fearing he was having a heart attack which turned out to be a severe anxiety attack.

Looking back he said: “Words can't explain the darkness I was in. It was like a living version of the pits of hellfire. And I 100 percent thought at times I'd end up in a padded room with the door locked, and that scared me so much.”

‌



Recalling his time in hospital he recalled: “The radio starts talking to me. Literally having a full conversation with me, like no one’s untouchable. We can get you at any time. If you don't behave yourself, we're gonna kill your father.

“So I'm thinking, okay, you're all involved. Your best friend set you up. I’m being drugged with anthrax. I'm dying. I've had a heart attack. I've been drugged. Something's happening to me. Am I not really here? Am I dead? I must be dead.”

‌



In an interview with the Mirror at the weekend, Paris was full of praise for her husband for speaking out and making the documentary with director Lucy Wilcox.

She said: “I'm really proud of Tyson in general because he's fought off many demons and he’s achieved greatness and he's a good person with it. He's a really really good person. People who meet him are actually surprised because they may have a preconception of what they believe Tyson is, and really he's a gentle giant.”
