Sports.title: UK Boxing Pundits Worry Saudi Gravy Train Is Stopping
Sports.content:
All-expenses-paid trips to Riyadh are becoming scarce, and some in the British boxing media worry the Saudi gold rush is running dry.

Ade Oladipo and Gareth A. Davies are remembering when they had it good during the brief two-year span from 2023 to 2025, when UK commentators got used to the red-carpet treatment of traveling to Saudi Arabia for big events.

“It felt like we were out there every week. Like we were in the sky on the way to Riyadh every single week for these big cards that you never thought were going to stop,” Oladipo said on talkSPORT Boxing.

Those big events have largely disappeared, leaving Ade and Gareth wondering if Turki Alalshikh will close up shop for UK fighters after Tyson Fury (36-2-1, 25 KOs) fights Anthony Joshua (30-4, 27 KOs) on December 11. You kind of knew it would end sooner or later, with wealthy, underperforming fighters doing the minimum to win and events that failed to attract PPV buys.

Oladipo harped about it being six or seven months since he was flown out to Riyadh, saying he was not even sent over for Canelo Alvarez’s fight against Christian Mbilli on October 31. That was an expensive event for fans, who had to pay $79.99 in the U.S. and £24.99 in the UK.

Not Built for U.S. Fans

Gareth questioned whether the British media are now “at the close of a particular era” when the Fury vs. Joshua event concludes in Cardiff. For Riyadh Season, that would be them finishing with a bang, but only because they are giving UK fans the fight they wanted, not because it is a matchup that non-Brits want to see.

If this is it for Turki and Riyadh Season, it is not a great deal for Americans, watching two heavyweights 10 years past their prime fight it out for the vacant WBA Super belt.

Riyadh Season Did Not Leave Boxing

Turki has not stopped spending money on the sport entirely. Instead, he is putting money into Zuffa events, which are less costly than massive cards like Canelo Alvarez vs. Terence Crawford and Fury vs. Joshua.

The difference is that Zuffa cards involve less well-known fighters who put on surprisingly more entertaining fights than the well-paid superstars. What those fights have shown is that Zuffa does not have to pay huge money to get good action.

For the last three years, British promoters leaned on Saudi budgets to bail out domestic matchups that could not sell on UK pay-per-view alone. If Saudi money disappears for average British cards in 2027, UK promoters will have to pay fighters based on what they actually bring in for ticket and PPV sales. It is going to be a shock for British promoters to go back to the old ways of putting events together.

Sports.title: Dmitry Bivol Puts Canelo Alvarez Rematch Odds At Five Percent
Sports.content:
Dmitry Bivol doubts that Canelo Alvarez will fight him again, rating it as just a 5% chance. Both Canelo and his trainer, Eddy Reynoso, said last month they want to fight Bivol or Terence Crawford next, following Canelo’s win over Christian Mbilli on October 31. Interestingly, Bivol says his team has never received any offer from Canelo for a rematch.

Bivol (25-1, 12 KOs) is defending his IBF, WBA, and WBO light heavyweight titles next month against Callum Smith (31-2, 22 KOs) in Ekaterinburg, Russia, at the UMMC Arena.

“To be honest, I’m feeling like on 5% it could happen,” Bivol told The Stomping Ground. “Yeah. Just kind of past that.”

Canelo lost a 12-round unanimous decision to Bivol in May 2022 in Las Vegas. Despite the close scorecards, the fight was one-sided. Bivol dominated Canelo with combinations and in-and-out movement.

“Well, look, I would like an immediate rematch with Crawford. Hopefully, Crawford can return to boxing, which I think he already said he might come back, and I would like the rematch with him. And if that is not possible, someday also have a rematch with Bivol,” said Eddy Reynoso to Fight Hub TV Español.

Saudi Funding And U.S. Box Office Reality

The lack of movement on a rematch with Bivol may not be entirely Canelo’s fault. For the fight to happen, the Saudis would need to finance it. Canelo is signed with Turki Alalshikh and Riyadh Season and is being paid well, reportedly in the hundreds of millions, with his per-fight purses being large.

Unless Riyadh is willing to fund rematches with Bivol and Crawford, those fights have little chance of happening because of the purse requirements. Those two would want large purses as well, perhaps as much as Canelo.

The problem is, Bivol isn’t a big name in the U.S., so the PPV buys wouldn’t likely cover the guaranteed purses for him and Canelo. The interest from casual fans isn’t enough to make the rematch worth funding. Moreover, Bivol’s inactivity has hurt the measure of popularity that he’d gotten from his wins over Canelo and Artur Beterbiev.

It makes sense for Riyadh Season to not pursue rematches between Canelo and Bivol or Crawford. If Canelo loses again to one or both, his value to the Saudis declines. Also, what fans may be overlooking is how boring those fights were.

Bivol just boxed Canelo from the outside and rarely stood in front of him to go toe-to-toe, as fans like to see from their fighters. If the Saudis want to see pure action, they can get more return by targeting fighters with more entertaining styles for Canelo.

Bivol admitted that Canelo has a lot of options for other fights to keep him busy in this late stage of his career. Canelo doesn’t need him.

The Saudi spending changes have also been seen affecting Bivol’s trilogy fight with Artur Beterbiev, which still hasn’t taken place after they fought for the second time in 2025, due to Riyadh Season no longer choosing to finance it. With both fighters reportedly getting $10 million each for their first two fights that were funded by the Saudis, fighting for less than that without their involvement doesn’t work. It’s too risky a fight for Bivol and Beterbiev to take without receiving outside financing.

Why Bivol Rejects The Easy Rematch Talk

“Never. Never. Second fight is never easier against anybody. Maybe it even harder,” Bivol said when asked if a rematch with Canelo, now 36, would be easy, believing the adjustments the Mexican star would make would present a problem.

If the Canelo vs. Bivol rematch is going to happen, the Saudi financiers will need to come up with the money to fund it. Ideally, it would be great if Bivol agreed to take a smaller purse just so he could make the rematch happen, but that doesn’t sound realistic. If anything, he’d want a massive purse that doesn’t balance out with the low number of PPV buys the match would likely bring in.

Sports.title: Agit Kabayel Brushes Off Pressure Ahead Of Nelson Hysa Defense
Sports.content:
Agit Kabayel says he feels no pressure going into Saturday night’s title defense of his WBC heavyweight belt against fringe contender Nelson Hysa at the Merkur Spiel-Arena in Düsseldorf, Germany. This is the type of fight where Kabayel can win and receive absolutely no credit. It’s considered a pure 100% mismatch.

Kabayel (27-0, 19 KOs) will be making his first defense of his WBC belt against the 42-year-old Hysa. It’s not the ideal type of fight for Kabayel, but the top contenders were all busy, leaving him with limited options. He’s in the ‘who needs him’ club, where he’s too risky for big-money stars like Anthony Joshua, Tyson Fury, or Oleksandr Usyk to face. That leaves Kabayel stuck, fighting no-names like Hysa, and not getting much press because of that.

Since Hysa (25-0, 23 KOs) is also with Queensberry, it was a no-brainer match-up to be made. It’s an in-house fight, and a large crowd of nearly 50,000 is expected.

“I was the underdog over and over again, and then right now I’m the favorite, and there is no pressure,” Kabayel said at Thursday’s DAZN Boxing press conference via a stage translator. “I am Agit Kabayel. I want to be better in every fight and I want to show that to the people, and there’s no pressure for me.”

Spencer Brown Calls Out The Resume Gap

Hysa made a big deal during the buildup for this fight, boasting about having done well in sparring with Kabayel in the past, and criticizing him about his delay in signing.

“About that I call him rabbit, it was before that he and his team accept the fight,” said Hysa. “He’s not a rabbit. He’s a good guy. He’s a good boxer.”

Hysa had to say something to get fans into the fight, because this match-up had been largely ignored by people for obvious reasons. Hysa is not a household name, has never beaten anyone recognizable, and is not exactly young at 42. In situations like this, there’s desperation to come up with trash talk that gets the attention of fans.

“He can talk so much bullst, you know, this is no problem,” said Kabayel. “I give him, you know, he’s the better trash talker than me, but in the ring you must fight. After that, he say, ‘You are afraid from me.’ So bro, I never scared from one guy in the heavyweight division.”

Well, Hysa looked powerful in his last fight, knocking out previously unbeaten Thomas Narmo (14-1, 14 KOs), but he was facing a guy with a resume filled with second-tier opposition. Hysa beat him, but he was just as unknown as his previous 24 opponents.

“Let’s have a look at the levels of the different fighters that you’ve faced and he’s faced,” Brown told Hysa on the dais. “Let’s not get into it because they’re completely different levels. Anybody they’ve thrown in front of him, he has taken them out. These are world-class one, two, three boys.”

Returning Heavyweight Boxing To Düsseldorf

Saturday’s heavyweight championship event in Düsseldorf, Germany, will be the first one at the venue since Tyson Fury defeated 39-year-old Wladimir Klitschko in 2015. That fight wasn’t the most entertaining to watch, as there was very little action between the two large heavyweights. Kabayel vs. Hysa should provide more sparks while it lasts in their fight live on DAZN.

“The fight 11 years ago when Wladimir Klitschko lost to Tyson Fury, it was bad for Germany, but Tyson Fury kind of inspired me, and now I got the same manager, and this was kind of the starting point,” said Kabayel.

Kabayel will surely take the fight to Hysa immediately, targeting his body, looking to wear him down and score a stoppage to please the large German crowd.

Sports.title: Canelo Alvarez Eyes Willy Hutchinson To Escape 168 Minefield
Sports.content:
Canelo Alvarez would be showing genuine bravery if he actually returned to light heavyweight to face WBC champion Willy Hutchinson in the first quarter of 2027. Hutchinson is the target right now over the three super middleweights, Osleys Iglesias, Lester Martinez, or Hamzah Sheeraz.

“Canelo has given the green light,” said talkSPORT Boxing host Ade Oladipo.

Trainer Eddy Reynoso will have a say in whether Alvarez signs for this fight. Hutchinson (21-2, 14 KOs) defeated Joshua Buatsi on November 7 to win the vacant WBC light heavyweight title, switch-hitting, moving, jabbing, and landing clean shots.

He had Buatsi tied in knots throughout that fight with his versatility. Hutchinson showed that he can punch, move, and take a shot. At 28, the 6’1″ Hutchinson is confident, and he’s not going to fight timidly against Canelo the way unbeaten contender Christian Mbilli did in their fight on October 31.

“Willie Hutchinson could sneak a points victory against Canelo in my view,” said talkSPORT analyst Gareth A. Davies. “I’ve seen enough from Willie now in the last couple of years to know this guy walks into the ring just so confident and has the style as a mover to cause Canelo problems. Those are the fighters that have caused the big man problems.”

Canelo (64-3-2, 39 KOs) looked overmatched the last time he fought at 175 against the pure boxer Dmitry Bivol in May 2022, losing a 12-round unanimous decision. In a sign of resignation and defeat, Canelo never attempted to avenge the loss by signing for a rematch with Bivol. Instead, he moved on toward softer targets, fighting 40-year-old Gennady Golovkin and John Ryder.

The 36-year-old Canelo’s mobility is slower now than it was in 2022, and he would have to find a way to improve that for him to have a chance of dethroning the 28-year-old Hutchinson in early 2027. The way Canelo looked against Mbilli, slow and always waiting near the ropes, he’d get picked apart by Hutchinson.

Reynoso has no easy outs for Canelo at 168. Against Mbilli, it was the perfect situation: fighting a guy who changed his normal fighting style of volume punching and instead attempted to outpunch Canelo with single shots. Even with the fight slipping away, Mbilli never switched to plan B by returning to his normal fighting style.

If Canelo stays at super middleweight, he can’t count on IBF champion Osleys Iglesias (16-0, 15 KOs) or interim WBC titlist Lester Martinez (21-0-1, 17 KOs) mentally undermining themselves by changing their normal fighting styles in an attempt to beat him at his own game. They’d both stick with what’s worked for them, which is an attack-oriented style that provides no rest breaks for their opponents.

Choosing Hamzah Sheeraz would result in Canelo being ridiculed by fans, who view the British fighter as a classic example of a fake manufactured hype job. Reynoso has been around long enough to know what the fan perception is of Hamzah by now, and he would recognize ahead of time what the reaction would be if Canelo picked him as his next opponent. It would be a PR disaster.

For Canelo, the best strategy would be moving back up to 175 pounds to face Hutchinson to try and figure out this difficult puzzle. He would be gambling by facing him, but staying at 168 could be far worse. If Canelo loses at 168, he won’t have the weight excuse he gets by moving back up to light heavyweight.

Sports.title: Joseph Parker Ready To Break Daniel Dubois Will Again
Sports.content:
Could Daniel Dubois quit if Joseph Parker takes him into the later rounds and he feels the fight slipping away? Dubois has proven to be a royal basket case when the going gets tough in fights. He’s fine when things are going well, but he goes to pieces when dealing with adversity.

We may see that happen before our eyes on January 30 when he defends his WBO heavyweight title against the experienced veteran Parker at the Co-op Live in Manchester, England. Parker is accustomed to war in the trenches and thrives on conflict. You can’t say the same thing about Dubois.

Queensberry Promotions is trying to sell this thing as unfinished business from February 2025 in Riyadh, where Dubois pulled out during fight week sick, and Parker knocked out an out-of-shape Martin Bakole in two rounds. Plenty of boxing fans still think Dubois got cold feet back then rather than being ill.

All I can say is he didn’t look thrilled sitting across from Parker on DAZN. He had fear in his eyes, being stared down by Parker. From that brief meeting, it’s easy to believe he pulled out of the fight because of stage fright.

Dubois (24-3, 23 KOs) will be favored to win, yet his reckless style leaves him wide open for a fast veteran counterpuncher. He marches forward behind a hard jab, which worked well for him against Jarrell Miller and Anthony Joshua. It’s going to take more than a jab to defeat Parker because he’s well equipped to neutralize that weapon.

If Parker gets inside and forces Dubois onto his back foot, Dubois tends to mentally crumble fast. Once Dubois hits the deck, he appears to give up on himself, looking at his corner for help.

Dubois has been through a lot of brutal fights since 2022, and we’ve all seen his chin give out when somebody survives his early bum rush and hits him flush, just like Oleksandr Usyk and Kevin Lerena did. You could see the look of resignation on Dubois’ face in those fights. He got lucky against Lerena when his opponent gassed out.

Parker (36-4, 24 KOs) is coming back after a year out since Fabio Wardley stopped him in the eleventh round in October 2025. He served a suspension, but chose not to take a tune-up. It makes sense because he wasn’t going to pass up this golden opportunity to relieve a vulnerable champion of his WBO belt,

“I almost feel like there’s a bit of me that thinks Joseph deserves it,” said Ade Oladipo on his YouTube channel.

It makes sense why Frank Warren is making this fight. He also promotes WBC heavyweight champion Agit Kabayel and IBF belt holder Filip Hrgovic. Matching the aging, soon-to-be 35-year-old Parker against Dubois removes the risk that would be there if he put him in against Kabayel or Hrgovic. Parker is a safer opponent on paper, and even if there is an upset, the WBO title still stays with Queensberry. Although Dubois did beat Hrgovic in the past, it would be risky putting him in with him now after Hrgovic’s win over Moses Itauma. The last thing Warren needs is for Hrgovic to beat Dubois.

Parker’s hunger still makes him a real threat to beat Dubois. If Parker is still standing past the midpoint of the fight, he could break Dubois down and make him quit like he did against Usyk and Joe Joyce. As the saying goes, once a quitter, always a quitter.

Sports.title: British Fans Rip Weak Fury vs. Joshua Undercard Lineup
Sports.content:
Turki Alalshikh revealed the full card for the Tyson Fury vs. Anthony Joshua event on December 11 at Principality Stadium in Cardiff, Wales, and the fan reaction has been negative, particularly among Brits.

With the Fury vs. Joshua fight being billed as the biggest domestic heavyweight bout in years in the main event, fans are hopping mad that the undercard looks like it’s been thrown together without any care about quality.

Fans are finally realizing they’re basically paying for the Fury vs. Joshua fight and getting nothing else worth watching.

Virtually all the undercard bouts, including the co-feature pitting Deontay Wilder vs. Martin Bakole, have been bashed as pure 100% garbage. Fans who subscribed to Netflix just to see the event aren’t happy about it. I’m not surprised.

We saw the same thing with Floyd Mayweather Jr. vs. Manny Pacquiao and Canelo Alvarez vs. Terence Crawford. All the effort and dough went into the main events for those two mega-events, and man, did the undercards look like junk of the highest kind.

Matchroom promoter Eddie Hearn got one of his fighters, former two-time super featherweight champion Joe Cordina, onto the card. The kicker is that Cordina, 35, has been placed on the preliminary portion of the card, fighting Mauricio Lara, out of sight, out of mind.

If Hearn thought this was Cordina’s big chance to win back the fans he lost when he was knocked out by Anthony Cacace in the eighth round in May 2024, he can forget it.

“What about Joe Cordina?” Hearn said when discussing the lineup. “What about a two-time world champion from Wales? Absolutely mental.”

Hearn had been banging the drum about wanting Cordina to fight on the main card against Manny Pacquiao, WBO lightweight champion Abdullah Mason, or Sam Noakes. Instead of fighting one of them in a highly visible fight, Cordina will be hidden away on the prelim card that will be shown on Netflix, TikTok, and The Ring social channels.

Hearn has got to be hopping mad, seeing his fighter fail to make the grade for the main card. I can totally understand the organizers’ decision to place the Cordina vs. Lara fight on the prelim card. Neither of these two fighters has beaten anyone halfway decent since losing. Cordina beat a fringe contender in Gabriel Flores Jr. and a lower-level fighter in Jaret Gonzalez Quiroz since losing to Cacace.

As for Lara, he’s won his last five fights against obscure opposition in confidence builders after fighting to a draw against Daniel Lugo in February 2024 and losing to Leigh Wood by a 12-round unanimous decision in May 2023.

The main card is just as abysmal, with Deontay Wilder facing replacement opponent Martin Bakole in the chief support bout after Jai Opetaia’s injury pullout, Zuffa heavyweight Da’Mazion Vanhouter battling Michael Essomba, and Moses Jolly fighting Igor Adiel Macedo.

Hearn blasted Zuffa promoter Dana White and Zuffa’s influence for the poor undercard, and British fans are replying in droves to Turki’s undercard lineup, echoing Hearn’s thoughts. The people who paid good cash for tickets to see the event live in Cardiff are harping about the scarcity of UK fighters, the 1:30 a.m. local start time for the headliner, and the lack of quality fights beyond the Joshua vs. Fury fight.

The rest of the preliminary lineup is filled with obscure prospects and names that even hardcore boxing fans won’t recognize, aside from Tyson’s younger brother Roman Fury. If you’re tuning in on December 11, you don’t need to set your alarm until right before the main event.

Sports.title: WBA Sets 75-25 Split for Teofimo Lopez Against Jack Catterall
Sports.content:
It’s not looking good for Teofimo Lopez to dodge his mandatory obligations at welterweight. Today, the WBA called a purse bid for December 4 in Cypress, Texas, for a fight between WBA welterweight Super Champion Teofimo and Jack Catterall with a slanted 75/25 purse split.

Financially, that should make Teofimo happy. Even with three-quarters of the money guaranteed, he’s shown no eagerness to sign to fight the mandatory he inherited after his win over WBA champion Rolando ‘Rolly’ Romero by majority decision on August 22. Lopez needs a special permit from the WBA to avoid Catterall (33-2, 14 KOs), but he may not get his wish. It’s understandable why Teofimo doesn’t want to fight Catterall. It’s a style that he’s struggled with, and it’s unlikely he would win.

Teofimo (23-2, 13 KOs) wants to face WBC welterweight champion Ryan Garcia in what would be a lucrative unification, where even if he loses, he’d still do well financially. He needs the WBA title for purse negotiations more so than it being a valuable chip to create more interest in a fight with Ryan.

Teofimo’s title isn’t why fans are interested in seeing the fight. For him, it’s just a negotiation tool to get a better deal, because he lacks Ryan’s popularity to get an even split. Even with a title, you can argue that Teofimo doesn’t rate a 50/50 purse split.

Catterall Risk Explains Lopez Delay

If this were an easy mark, Lopez would be overjoyed at receiving a 75/25 gift split from the WBA. Catterall’s style is similar to Shakur Stevenson’s, which left Teofimo baffled and helpless in a unanimous decision loss over 12 rounds earlier this year at Madison Square Garden on January 31. Teofimo looked embarrassingly bad in that fight. The judges scored it 119 to 109 on all three cards, and he was outlanded 165 to 72.

Defensively, Catterall isn’t as sharp as Shakur, but he’s close enough to be the same kind of nightmare for Teofimo. On offense, Catterall is superior to Shakur, and coupled with his defensive ability, he would be a difficult problem for Teofimo to try and figure out. Besides all that, the pressure that Teofimo would be under would be severe if he needs to defeat Catterall to get to the lucrative payday fight against Ryan Garcia.

If he gets beaten by Catterall, he can forget about fighting Ryan for the time being. Unlike his loss to Shakur, Teofimo wouldn’t be given a straight title shot immediately after. He’d have to rebuild and get in line, which is what he should have had to do after losing to Stevenson instead of being given a crack at Rolly’s WBA title.

Catterall captured his WBA regular welterweight title by beating former mandatory Shakhram Giyasov by a wide 12-round unanimous decision last May. Giyasov was the mandatory challenger that Rolly was avoiding. Now, we’re seeing the new WBA champion Teofimo trying to give Catterall similar treatment. The WBA can stop this cycle by rejecting Teofimo’s request for a special permit.

It’s easy to predict what Lopez’s next move will be if the WBA rejects his appeal. Vacating the WBA belt will be the easiest way of getting Catterall out of his path to a fight with Ryan. Teofimo will still get a nice payday against Ryan, but probably not as nice as it would be if he still had his WBA title.

Sports.title: Brian Mendoza Replaces Keith Thurman in Weak Vergil Ortiz Jr. Co-Feature
Sports.content:
PBC and Golden Boy Promotions made it official today with Brian Mendoza replacing Keith Thurman as Vergil Ortiz Jr.’s opponent for his 10-round co-feature middleweight bout on December 5 at the Desert Diamond Arena in Glendale, Arizona.

Ortiz Jr. and Mendoza will be fighting on the undercard of WBA and WBO cruiserweight champion David Benavidez’s unification bout against WBC champion Michal Cieslak on DAZN PPV and Prime Video.

The addition of Mendoza (23-5, 17 KOs) has received mixed views from fans. Many of them view the 32-year-old as a poor replacement, given his 1-3 record in his last four fights. That’s not exactly top shelf unless losing is the benchmark requirement used to get enlisted as a fill-in opponent for Vergil Ortiz Jr.

Back in Mediocrity Since Fundora

What Mendoza has got going for him is that he knocked out Sebastian Fundora in the seventh round in April 2023 in a huge upset at the time. Fundora was beating the living daylights out of Mendoza for the first six rounds until he got careless in the seventh and got clipped. Since then, Mendoza’s career has slipped back to what it was before that win. That was his textbook Cinderella night, where he got lucky in a fight that he was getting beaten up in.

What’s interesting is that fans online see this as an upgrade over 38-year-old Thurman, just because of his win over Fundora. If you look at Mendoza’s results since that upset, he’s a major downgrade, and that’s saying a lot because Thurman was not a great opponent. He’s not a middleweight, and definitely not young.

Tim Tszyu beat Mendoza by a wide 12-round unanimous decision in October 2023. That fight was an example of Mendoza being brought back down to earth. It wasn’t even slightly a close fight. It looked like Mendoza wandered into the ring from the crowd, and Tszyu took advantage by beating the stuffing out of him. Serhii Bohachuk did the same thing to Mendoza in a clash for the interim WBC junior middleweight title in March 2024.

The only win for Mendoza in the last three years came against journeyman Jesus Antonio Rojas (12-11-2, 10 KOs). It took that level of opponent for Mendoza to snap his two-fight losing streak. In Mendoza’s last fight, he returned to his losing ways, getting trounced by Yoenis Tellez by a one-sided 10-round unanimous decision in March 2026.

Basically, what we’re seeing here is not a dangerous threat being used as a replacement opponent for Ortiz Jr. (24-0, 22 KOs), who recently looked like pure gold in wins over Israil Madrimov, Bohachuk, and Erickson Lubin.

A Cheap Showcase for Ortiz Jr.

Yanking Mendoza out of his fight with Eric Priest enabled Sampson Boxing, TGB Promotions, and Golden Boy Promotions to save money on finding a quality opponent. It’s a showcase fight for Ortiz Jr. Ideally, they should have spent some money to enlist a quality middleweight contender like Yoenli Hernandez to put Ortiz Jr. in a sink-or-swim fight.

What Mendoza does have going for him is a strong chin, as he’s never been knocked out in his career. So if the idea is for Ortiz Jr. to get some rounds in to sharpen up after a year on the shelf, Mendoza is the guy for the job. However, the referee may step in and halt this fight anyway because of the likely one-sided nature of it.

Entertainment-wise, Mendoza eating hard shots from Ortiz Jr. is not fun to watch in a PPV co-feature slot. Fans want competitive fights, not slaughters.

Ortiz Jr. is 28 years old, making the move up to middleweight, and has still accomplished little in his career. It’s got to bug him that he sees fighters like Jaron ‘Boots’ Ennis taking the express route to superstardom, leaving him behind. The difference is, Ennis has been a risk-taker from day one, hasn’t feasted on weak opposition, and has stayed active. In contrast, Ortiz Jr. hasn’t fought the best, and he’s missed a lot of time in his career due to health and promotional issues.

Ghana News.title: Empress Gifty to perform at 2026 Guinness Ghana DJ Awards
Ghana News.content:
Ghanaian gospel musician Empress Gifty is set to perform at the 2026 Guinness Ghana DJ Awards, scheduled for Friday, December 4, at the Palms Convention Centre in Accra.

Her performance will be one of the highlights of this year’s awards ceremony, which will celebrate and honour disc jockeys (DJs) for their contributions to Ghana’s music and entertainment industry.

The announcement comes as anticipation builds ahead of the awards night, which is expected to bring together DJs, entertainment industry stakeholders, sponsors, media personalities and music enthusiasts.

Ghanaian musician Black Sherif has also praised DJs for their role in promoting music and supporting artistes, describing them as the foundation of the music Ghana exports to the world.

In a message to DJs, the award-winning artiste expressed gratitude for their contribution to the music industry and offered prayers for their success and financial prosperity.

“Big ups to our DJ. We love you so much. We love you guys. It’s because of you that we stand. You guys are the roots to all the music we try to export. May God bless you. May God guide you guys. May God fill your pockets. DJs, we love you,” he said.

The 2026 edition of the Guinness Ghana DJ Awards, powered by Smirnoff, was officially launched at Eden Gardens Hotel in Accra, the event’s official hospitality partner.

The launch unveiled the roadmap for the new awards season, leading up to the grand ceremony and the platform’s 15th anniversary celebration next year.

The grand awards ceremony is expected to be broadcast live to an estimated audience of more than 17 million viewers across 48 African countries.

This year’s awards season is being held under the theme “All Out”, celebrating the passion, resilience and creativity of DJs who continue to push boundaries and shape Ghana’s entertainment industry.

The organisers say the 2026 edition will feature fresh initiatives, new rewards and an expanded awards scheme, with continued support from Guinness Ghana through Smirnoff.

Ghana News.title: Road signs not for adverts or political campaigns – NRSA warns
Ghana News.content:
The National Road Safety Authority (NRSA) has cautioned businesses, religious organisations and political parties against using road signs and other road infrastructure for advertising, publicity and campaign activities, warning that the practice poses serious risks to road safety.

The Authority said it had observed an increasing trend of posters, banners and promotional materials being attached to road signs, traffic signs, road medians, gantries and other public infrastructure, with some existing signs being defaced or obstructed in the process.

It described the development as unlawful and warned that such activities could compromise the safety of motorists, motorcyclists, cyclists and pedestrians who rely on road signs for essential traffic information.

In a statement, the NRSA stressed that road signs were installed primarily to regulate traffic, provide directions and alert road users to potential hazards, rather than serve as spaces for promotional activities.

“Road signs and road infrastructure are provided primarily to regulate, guide, and inform road users. They are not authorised spaces for commercial advertising, religious or political campaign displays,” the Authority stated.

It explained that obstructing or altering road signs could prevent drivers from accessing critical information needed to make safe and timely decisions, increasing the likelihood of confusion and road traffic crashes.

“Covering, altering, obstructing or distracting attention from these signs can impair road users' ability to make safe and timely decisions, increase the risk of confusion and contribute to road traffic crashes,” it warned.

The Authority further noted that materials placed on road medians, gantries and other unauthorised locations could obstruct visibility and distract motorists, creating additional dangers for pedestrians and other road users.

It said the risks were particularly significant for people unfamiliar with particular routes, who depend on road signs and directional information to navigate safely.

NRSA warns of sanctions against offenders

The Authority has consequently urged businesses, religious groups, political parties, candidates, supporters and campaign organisers to immediately stop attaching posters, banners and other publicity materials to road signs and infrastructure.

It advised the groups to ensure that promotional and campaign materials were displayed only at locations approved by the relevant authorities.

As part of enforcement measures, the NRSA said it would collaborate with road and local government authorities to identify and remove unauthorised materials from public infrastructure.

“The Authority will work with the appropriate road and local government authorities to identify and remove unauthorised posters, banners and other materials placed on road signs and road infrastructure,” it said.

It further cautioned that individuals and organisations responsible for the violations could face financial liability or be referred to the appropriate authorities for action under applicable laws.

“Persons and groups responsible for such violations may also be surcharged or referred to the appropriate authorities for further action under applicable laws,” the statement added.

The NRSA called on the public to demonstrate greater responsibility in the use of public infrastructure, emphasising that promotional and political activities should not undermine road safety.

“Acts of publicity must never compromise the safety of road users,” the Authority stressed.

Ghana News.title: Early BECE registration fuels examination malpractice – Africa Education Watch
Ghana News.content:
File photo: Students at an examination

The Executive Director of Africa Education Watch, Kofi Asare, has defended the Education Minister’s directive restricting the premature registration of candidates for the Basic Education Certificate Examination (BECE), arguing that the practice undermines the integrity of the national assessment system.

He says the practice allows some parents to manipulate the examination registration process by arranging for their children to be presented as final-year Junior High School (JHS) students before completing the required three years of basic education.

Speaking on the ongoing debate surrounding the directive, Mr Asare explained that the West African Examinations Council (WAEC) requires BECE school candidates to obtain 30 per cent of their overall results from continuous assessment, with the remaining 70 per cent coming from the final examination.

He said the continuous assessment component is accumulated across JHS One, Two and Three, meaning candidates are expected to complete all three years before sitting the examination.

However, he alleged that some parents collude with school authorities to fabricate the missing JHS Three continuous assessment records for children who have been fast-tracked into the examination.

“Immediately a child jumps JHS Three, invariably, the meaning is that a headteacher somewhere will cook a JHS Three continuous assessment for that child,” he said.

According to him, the arrangement involves parents and school heads creating the impression that the child has completed the required three years before being presented to WAEC as a final-year student.

Mr Asare disclosed that Africa Education Watch began investigating the practice around 2021 and uncovered instances where parents allegedly paid substantial amounts to secure early BECE registration for their children.

He cited investigations conducted around the Osino area in 2023, where some parents were reportedly paying as much as GH¢10,000 to fast-track their children’s examination registration.

He explained that some parents, particularly those whose children attended private JHS institutions, travelled from Accra to schools in outlying communities to secure the arrangement.

The practice, he said, was partly driven by the introduction of the 30 per cent Category A placement protocol for candidates from public junior high schools.

Some parents reportedly sought to have their children registered through public schools to benefit from the placement arrangement while simultaneously cutting short a year of their children’s education.

Mr Asare maintained that the practice goes beyond accelerating the academic progression of gifted children, describing the fabrication of continuous assessment records as examination malpractice that threatens the credibility of the BECE.

He stressed that talented children should have the opportunity to benefit from accelerated placement, but insisted that such arrangements must be based on an independent assessment of their academic abilities and socio-emotional development.

“Talented kids have the right to be identified and assessed independently and based on their talents, both academic and socio-emotional, and given accelerated placement. That should happen,” he said.

He added that having a structured framework for identifying gifted learners should not be confused with the alleged manipulation of examination records to facilitate premature BECE registration.

Ghana News.title: Ecobank opens up initiatives including “Elevate programme” for women led Businesses
Ghana News.content:
Head of Commercial Consumer Products at Ecobank Ghana, William Nana Danso Abiam, is advising Small and Medium Enterprises to approach the bank for support and take steps to develop their credit history by investing in their business operations in order to boost the confidence of banks to support their growth.

According to him this will help the bank to accelerate financing initiatives to women businesses in the small and medium sector.

He made the call at the third Ecobank Joybusiness Financial Dialogue series under the theme; investing in impact; empowering women led businesses to thrive.

“We are here to support your business so get closer to us and let’s talk, our initiatives are been scaled up so many women can benefit from it. I can talk specifically about the Ecobank Elevate which has been running for sometime now with a financial package that is being doubled for next year. The funds are available so develop your cashflows and take advantage”.

“We are serving as a bridge between those who has money and those who need money but we also have to be able to provide support to viable businesses and as we always do at Ecobank, we are committed to helping you to grow” he said.

The third Financial Dialogue series is a platform provided by Joybusiness and Ecobank Ghana to support business growth and economic empowerment.

He also advised women entrepreneurs to reach out to the various Ecobank offices to enquire about the elevate initiative and other products that are aimed at promoting and supporting women businesses across the country. He assured that Ecobank is the pillar for business foundations after supporting more than two hundred small businesses to grow.

Director for Micro Small and Medium Enterprises at the Ghana Enterprises Agency, Habiba Sumani urged women led SMEs to take advantage of digital opportunities in the ongoing internet revolution to develop skills to support their operations.

“Take advantage of digital platforms and banking systems that are provided online to grow your business as a woman, you can speak to Ecobank or come to our offices both the regional offices and the National Headquarters to seek for support. We have offices across the regions and the various District Assembly Offices in case you may need to speak to anyone” she said.

The dialogue is the final series for the year hosted by the Bank and Joybusiness for women-led businesses across the country.

Ghana News.title: Ghana loses $1.9bn yearly to air pollution, Clean Air Fund warns
Ghana News.content:
Ghana loses an estimated $1.9 billion annually to ambient air pollution, the Country Lead for the Clean Air Fund, Desmond Appiah, has disclosed, calling for greater investment in cleaner air as part of efforts to tackle non-communicable diseases (NCDs).

Mr Appiah believes the government's MahamaCares programme should look beyond treating NCDs to addressing environmental factors, particularly air pollution, which contributes to the development of several health conditions.

He argued that tackling air pollution should form part of the government's broader public health strategy, rather than treating it as a separate environmental concern.

Speaking on the economic impact of polluted air, Mr Appiah cited research conducted by the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) with support from the Clean Air Fund.

"UNDP has done work which we supported and established that Ghana loses about $1.9 billion a year to ambient air pollution," he said.

He called on the government to consider allocating some resources under MahamaCares to interventions that address the root causes of NCDs, including exposure to polluted air.

According to him, such an approach would complement healthcare delivery by reducing environmental risks that contribute to illness and place additional pressure on the health system.

Mr Appiah said the Clean Air Fund was supporting efforts to strengthen the evidence and advocacy for effective air pollution control in Ghana.

"That is why we are supporting all these kinds of work to make the case stronger," he added.

He stressed that sustained investment in cleaner air would be essential to reducing the health risks associated with pollution while easing its economic burden on the country.

Ghana News.title: GEA pushes for financial discipline among women-led businesses
Ghana News.content:
The Ghana Enterprises Agency (GEA) has urged women entrepreneurs, particularly market traders and small business owners, to adopt sound financial management practices, including separating personal finances from business transactions, keeping proper records and opening dedicated business bank accounts to strengthen their enterprises.

The Agency's Director for Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises, Habiba Sumani, said these practices were essential to improving business accountability, tracking financial performance and positioning women-led enterprises to access formal financing.

She made the call during a panel discussion at the third Ecobank-JoyBusiness Financial Dialogue on Friday, November 27, under the theme ‘Investing in Impact: Empowering Women-Led Businesses to Thrive’.

Addressing the financial management challenges confronting women traders across the country, Ms Sumani encouraged entrepreneurs to stop keeping business proceeds in shops, personal safes and other informal storage arrangements.

“First and foremost, let's realise one fundamental truth. Separate the business from yourself as a person by separating your business transactions in its entirety,” she advised.

She said maintaining separate business and personal finances would enable entrepreneurs to monitor their income and expenditure more effectively and establish a clearer picture of how their businesses were performing.

“Get a bank account today. Stop keeping money under the desk. Stop keeping money in the small safe, wooden safe within the store,” she urged.

Daily monitoring key to business accountability

Ms Sumani further encouraged women entrepreneurs to make daily financial reconciliation part of their business operations by comparing sales made with the money received at the end of each working day.

She said the practice would help business owners identify discrepancies, monitor their earnings and strengthen accountability among employees.

“You can't do everything. You have to leave your business premises sometimes even before the shop is shut. Who is that trusted person who can continue to handle the business like your operational manager of a sort when you are not there?” she asked.

She encouraged traders to identify trustworthy employees who could oversee daily operations and maintain proper supervision when business owners were unavailable.

Beyond financial management, Ms Sumani urged women entrepreneurs operating without formal business registration to take advantage of the Agency's support services to formalise their enterprises.

Ms Sumani maintained that separating personal and business finances, keeping accurate records and registering enterprises were practical steps women entrepreneurs could take to strengthen their businesses.

She said these measures were important to improving business survival, building financial credibility and creating opportunities for women-led enterprises to grow and operate sustainably.

Ghana News.title: Chinese CAITEC Group celebrates 30 years of business excellence, investment and job creation in Ghana
Ghana News.content:
From a modest trading operation in 1995 to a diversified business conglomerate employing more than 2,000 Ghanaians, CAITEC Group has marked three decades of remarkable growth and investment across strategic sectors of the economy.

Speaking at a special anniversary celebration attended by government representatives, members of the diplomatic corps, traditional authorities, business leaders, customers, partners and members of the media, CAITEC Group Chairman, Mr Tang Hong, described the milestone as a celebration of vision, resilience, friendship and shared economic development between Ghana and China.

Mr Tang reaffirmed the company's enduring commitment to Ghana's economic development as the diversified business conglomerate celebrates 30 years of successful business operations in the country.

Reflecting on the company's remarkable journey, the Chairman recounted how he first arrived in Ghana in 1996 as a young Chinese businessman with the responsibility of exploring business opportunities.

Although his initial experience presented several challenges, including infrastructure limitations, logistical difficulties, communication barriers and cultural differences, he said Ghana's peaceful environment, political stability, economic prospects and the hospitality of its people convinced him that the country offered tremendous opportunities for long-term investment.

"Although doing business was challenging due to infrastructure limitations, logistical difficulties, communication barriers and cultural differences, I quickly recognised Ghana's enormous potential, its political stability, peaceful environment and, most importantly, the warmth and hospitality of its people," Mr Tang stated.

He explained that rather than allowing the challenges to discourage him, he considered them opportunities to establish something meaningful, a decision that eventually inspired him to make Ghana his permanent business home and relocate his family to the country.

"Looking back, that decision remains one of the most important and rewarding decisions of my life," he said.

FROM GENERAL TRADING TO A DIVERSIFIED BUSINESS GROUP

The CAITEC Group Chairman traced the company's beginnings to the establishment of CAITEC Delta Limited, which started with general trading and the importation and distribution of Chinese-made tyres.

Over the years, the company expanded its product offerings to include air conditioners, car batteries, automotive spare parts, lubricants and power-generation equipment, gradually building a strong customer base and distribution network within the Ghanaian market.

The group's growth subsequently paved the way for the establishment of CAITEC Motors Limited, which extended its operations into the automotive and transportation industry.

Through the company, CAITEC Group diversified into the importation, distribution, sale and servicing of commercial vehicles, pick-ups, trucks, construction equipment and spare parts.

These operations have positioned the group as an important supplier of mobility and machinery solutions to individuals, businesses and institutions requiring reliable transportation and construction equipment.

MMrTang explained that the group's expansion into different industries was driven by its determination to identify market needs and provide products and services capable of supporting economic activities.

"Our growth has been guided by a simple philosophy: identifying market needs, providing dependable products and services, creating employment and investing in sectors that contribute to Ghana's economic development," he emphasised.

CHAIRMAN ACKNOWLEDGES GHANA'S LEADERSHIP AND BUSINESS ENVIRONMENT

Mr Tang also used the anniversary occasion to express appreciation to successive Presidents of Ghana and their respective governments for the political stability, investment opportunities and business environment within which CAITEC Group has operated over the past 30 years.

He acknowledged the contributions of the late former President Jerry John Rawlings, under whose administration he first arrived in Ghana in 1996; former President John Agyekum Kufuor; the late former President John Evans Atta Mills; former President Nana Addo Dankwa Akufo-Addo; and President John Dramani Mahama.

He also recognised the ministries, departments, agencies and public institutions that have engaged with the group's businesses and provided regulatory guidance and cooperation over the years.

The Chairman extended appreciation to Ghana's business community, suppliers, distributors, corporate clients, dealers, contractors and service providers, describing their cooperation and confidence as instrumental to the group's growth.

"To every individual and organisation that has supported our businesses, purchased our products or partnered with us, I extend my sincere appreciation. Your confidence in the CAITEC name has helped us remain relevant and competitive for 30 years," he stated.

STRENGTHENING GHANA-CHINA BUSINESS RELATIONS

MMrTang further highlighted the importance of the longstanding relationship between Ghana and China, describing business cooperation, trade, investment and cultural understanding as important pillars for the continued development of both countries.

Drawing on his previous experience as President of the Ghana Association of Chinese Societies and President of the Ghana-China Chamber of Commerce, he reaffirmed his commitment to strengthening business relationships and promoting mutually beneficial partnerships between Ghanaian and Chinese enterprises.

He expressed optimism that the friendship and cooperation between the two countries would continue to create opportunities for investment, trade and economic development.

A LEGACY BUILT ON INVESTMENT, PEOPLE AND FAMILY

The CAITEC Group Chairman reserved special appreciation for the company's hardworking employees, particularly its Ghanaian workforce, whose dedication and professionalism have contributed significantly to the organisation's success.

He also paid a heartfelt tribute to his wife for relocating to Ghana with him and supporting their family journey over the years, expressing gratitude for their three children.

His remarks reflected the personal commitment and family values that have accompanied the company's growth from its early beginnings to its present position as a diversified business group.

AMBASSADOR KOJO BONSU COMMENDS TANG HONG; WOOS MORE INVESTORS

In a solidarity message, Ghana’s Ambassador to China, Mr Kojo Bonsu, shared fond memories and spoke highly of MMrTang Hong’s resilience.

“I have known Mr Tang Hong for the past 16 years, and I can confidently say that his journey has been remarkable. As you may have seen in the documentary, my friend has evolved over the years and successfully established the CAITEC conglomerate after arriving in Ghana. As an Ambassador, one of my primary mandates is to attract Chinese investors to Ghana, and I am proud of my achievements in this regard. It remains one of my key performance indicators (KPIs),” he stated.

He added that when you have Chinese companies such as CAITEC, which have consistently demonstrated growth and excellence over the years, it shows that MMrTang Hong saw the potential and the vision when he first came to Ghana.

“As he indicated in the documentary, he had a vision for Ghana. Even at a time when the roads were in poor condition, internet connectivity was limited, and other challenges existed, Mr Tang saw opportunities rather than obstacles. If you look at Ghana-China relations over the past 65 years, you will realise that we have maintained a strong and cordial relationship with the Chinese people, dating back to the era of Dr Kwame Nkrumah and Chairman Mao.

He also condemned the negative perceptions Ghanaians have about the Chinese.

“I can confidently say that the perception held by some people that Chinese people are not good is a lie. I have travelled to China and worked with the Chinese, and I can attest to their commitment to business, discipline and integrity. In every human institution, there are good and bad people, but we cannot generalise or conclude that everyone is bad based on the actions of a few. Ghana has witnessed several Chinese investors coming to contribute to the country's development. We are also working to attract many more Chinese investments into the country.”

He threw his support behind Mr Tang’s vision and vowed to continue attracting businesses to Ghana, creating employment opportunities and contributing to national development.

“That is why I am confident that we will continue to make progress. All I can say today is that we are committed to continuing this journey and doing even more to strengthen Ghana-China relations, attract investments and support businesses that create opportunities for our people.”

GUEST OF HONOUR MOHAMMED ADAMS SUKPARU URGES CAITEC TO INVEST MORE, EMPLOY MORE GHANAIANS

Deputy Minister of Communications, Digital Technology and Innovation, Hon. Mohammed Adams Sukparu, on his part, urged CAITEC Group to deepen its investment in Ghana, embrace digital innovation and strengthen local partnerships.

Speaking as Guest of Honour at the company's 30th anniversary celebration, Mr Sukparu said CAITEC's three decades of operations represented a significant achievement built on resilience, adaptability, sustained investment and the confidence of customers and business partners.

“Thirty years in business is no small achievement. It represents resilience, adaptability, sustained investment and, above all, the confidence of customers and business partners,” he stated.

On behalf of the government, he congratulated the company's management, employees, distributors and business partners, commending its decision to celebrate the milestone alongside its distributors and the launch of a new product under the Sankoto brand.

He noted that the anniversary should serve not only as an opportunity to reflect on past accomplishments but also to position the company for future growth.

Mr Sukparu emphasised the importance of private-sector investment in Ghana's economic development, arguing that government alone could not build a prosperous economy without the active participation of businesses in investment, innovation, job creation and wealth generation.

“Government must provide the right policies, services, infrastructure and enabling environment, while the private sector drives investment, innovation, job creation and wealth generation,” he said.

He further encouraged CAITEC to align its business expansion with Ghana's broader economic transformation agenda, particularly through initiatives such as the 24-Hour Economy and the Export Development Programme.

According to him, investments must deliver benefits beyond corporate profitability by creating decent jobs, developing skills, supporting local enterprises and contributing to communities where businesses operate.

Addressing the company's involvement in the mobility and transportation sector, Mr Sukparu said motorcycles and other two-wheeled transportation solutions played an important role in supporting commercial activities, facilitating the movement of goods and services and creating opportunities for traders, delivery operators and small-business owners.

However, he charged industry players to prioritise product quality, rider education, road safety and after-sales support, insisting that corporate responsibility must extend beyond the point of sale.

“A company's responsibility should not end when a product is sold. It must extend to the safety, reliability and overall satisfaction of the people who use it,” he emphasised.

He also encouraged the company to pay attention to emerging opportunities in electric mobility and environmentally sustainable transportation, which he said were increasingly shaping the future of the global automotive industry.

He also pointed to the African Continental Free Trade Area, headquartered in Accra, as an opportunity for businesses operating in Ghana to expand into other African markets and strengthen the country's position as a regional trade and distribution hub.

Ghana News.title: Kasapreko posts GH¢296m nine-month profit, up 14.3%
Ghana News.content:
Kasapreko PLC has reported a profit after tax of GH¢296 million for the nine months ended September 2026, representing a 14.3% increase over the corresponding period last year.

The Ghanaian beverage manufacturer disclosed the results at the Ghana Stock Exchange's (GSE) Facts Behind the Figures session, where it presented its third-quarter 2026 performance and outlined its financial position and expansion plans.

Revenue increased by 8.8% to GH¢2.79 billion, while gross profit rose by 4.6% to GH¢826 million.

Operating profit also grew by 11% to GH¢480 million, supported by efforts to keep operating expenses in check. Finance costs declined by 12.5%, helping improve the company's net profit margin to 10.6%, from 10.1% in the corresponding period last year.

Managing Director Richard Adjei said the performance reflected the financial discipline the company had promised investors during its June initial public offering (IPO).

"These numbers show the discipline we promised investors in June," he said.

Kasapreko generated GH¢385 million in operating cash flow during the nine months, while its debt-to-equity ratio declined significantly to 0.29 times from 1.0 times, indicating an improvement in its capital structure.

The company raised GH¢700 million through its June IPO, with proceeds being channelled partly into the expansion of its manufacturing facility at Adeiso to support increased production capacity and future growth.

Credit rating agency Agusto & Co. has assigned Kasapreko a long-term rating of Aa(Gha) and a short-term rating of A1+(Gha), both with a Stable Outlook.

From a small garage to an international beverage manufacturer

Founded in 1989 by businessman Dr Kwabena Adjei, Kasapreko started as a small operation in a garage in Nungua, Accra, with five employees.

The company has since grown into a major Ghanaian-owned beverage manufacturer with a diversified portfolio of alcoholic and non-alcoholic products.

Its flagship product, Alomo Bitters, is a herbal-based alcoholic beverage developed using locally sourced ingredients. The company also manufactures and markets products across several categories, including gin, whisky, brandy, liqueurs, carbonated soft drinks and wine.

According to its corporate profile, Kasapreko has developed more than 100 product lines and exports to 16 countries, with distribution partnerships across West, East and Southern Africa.

The company also says it employs more than 500 professionals, alongside hundreds of contracted workers, and has invested in production technology, research and development and quality-control facilities.

The latest financial performance comes as Kasapreko pursues further investment in its manufacturing operations following its successful capital raise, with the Adeiso factory expansion expected to support its next phase of growth.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.

World.title: Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing
World.content:
Washington —

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

The balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person said, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

A US intelligence official told CNN on Monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the High Altitude Balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the United States does not appear to have provided critical new insights to the People’s Republic of China.”

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have said.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it says is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

CNN has reached out to the National Security Council at the White House and the Pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the new intelligence.

Video Ad Feedback Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33 • Source: CNN Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33

The balloon first crossed into US airspace over Alaska in late January before passing through Canada and down into Montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the US to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

A senior State Department official said in February that, as the balloon floated across the US, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations.”

Gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, said at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese.”

The surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small Chinese province of Hainan, officials told CNN. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

Still, China did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

World.title: Beijing promised to 'fight back' over Taiwan leader's US visit. But this time it has more to lose
World.content:
Hong Kong —

An anticipated meeting between Taiwan’s President Tsai Ing-wen and US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy in California this week has sparked concerns of a repeat of the pressure campaign China launched last year when then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei.

At that time, Beijing encircled the island democracy with unprecedented military drills – firing multiple missiles into its surrounding waters and sending dozens of warplanes speeding across a sensitive median line dividing the Taiwan Strait.

It also cut off contact with the United States over a number of issues from military matters to combating climate change, in retaliation for what it viewed as a violation of its sovereignty.

This time, Beijing has already threatened to “resolutely fight back” if a Tsai-McCarthy meeting goes ahead.

Video Ad Feedback See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32 • Source: CNN See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32

It also slammed Washington for allowing Tsai to stopover in the US while en route to and from official visits in Central America, warning it could lead to “serious” confrontation between the two powers.

A defiant Tsai staked out her own ground, pledging as she took off on her 10-day trip not to let “external pressure” stop Taiwan from connecting with the world and like-minded democracies.

But the optics of the meeting, taking place in California and not Taiwan, and its timing – at a particularly thorny moment in China’s foreign relations and ahead of a presidential election in Taiwan that could reset the tone of its relationship with Beijing – may see Beijing tread more carefully this time, or at least not escalate further, analysts say.

“This puts the burden on China not to overreact, because any overreaction is only going to push China further away from the world,” said Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington.

That doesn’t mean, however, that Beijing won’t be closely watching Tsai’s movements as it calibrates its response – and decides how much military might to flex over her meeting with an American lawmaker on American soil.

The opacity of China’s system – and the potential for competing interests within its vast bureaucracy – also make it difficult to accurately predict its response.

“Every time Taiwan does anything that China doesn’t like, the Chinese react with their own military coercion,” Sun said. But in the current situation, “they have to consider the consequences of overreaction,” she added.

House Speaker Kevin McCarthy talks to reporters at the Capitol in Washington on March 24, 2023. J. Scott Applewhite/AP

Rising pressure

The expected meeting, which McCarthy’s office announced earlier this week would take place on Wednesday, also comes at a precarious moment in US-China relations.

Washington and Beijing are struggling to stabilize their communication amid flaring tensions over issues from a downed suspected Chinese surveillance balloon to semiconductor supply chains – raising the stakes of potential damage to that relationship if Beijing lashes out as it did when Tsai met Pelosi.

Taiwan is still feeling the fallout of that response last August, with Chinese military forces now regularly making incursions over what had previously been an informal but largely respected border of control between Beijing and Taipei in the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan’s official Central News Agency also reported Monday that Tsai would meet with McCarthy, citing Tsai’s presidential office.

Video Ad Feedback See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05 • Source: CNN See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05

But a meeting between Tsai and the leader of the Republican majority in the US House of Representatives, who ranks second in line to the Presidency, would mark another symbolic moment for Taiwan and the US, which only maintain unofficial ties.

For Tsai, who is entering the final year of her two-term presidency, “it’s clearly a capstone event,” according to Wen-Ti Sung, a political scientist at the Australian National University’s Taiwan Studies Program. “She has this image as the Taiwanese president who has taken US-Taiwan relations to new heights, and who … has been able to give Taiwan almost unprecedented international visibility,” he said.

That increased visibility – and enhanced cooperation with the US – has followed China’s mounting pressure on the island, which sits fewer than 110 miles (177 kilometers) from the mainland coast.

China’s Communist Party claims the self-governing island democracy as its own despite never having controlled it, and has vowed to take the island, by force if necessary.

The party has undertaken a sweeping expansion of its military capabilities over the past decade under leader Xi Jinping – and ramped up its pervasive economic, diplomatic and military pressure on Taiwan.

That’s driven concerns, among some in Washington, that Beijing is preparing for an invasion, though China’s official language still suggests that scenario is not its preferred option for achieving the claimed goal of “reunification.”

It is those pressures – and how to support Taiwan against unilateral actions by Beijing – that are likely to be on the table when Tsai, McCarthy and a bipartisan group of US lawmakers sit down on Wednesday.

Congress has been a pillar of increasing American support for Taiwan in recent years. Lawmakers regularly visit the island and drive bipartisan legislation enhancing support and cooperation.

While the US switched its diplomatic relations to Beijing decades ago, it maintains unofficial ties with Taiwan and is bound by law to provide the democratic island with the means to defend itself.

Under Washington’s longstanding “One China” policy, the US acknowledges China’s position that Taiwan is part of China, but has never officially recognized Beijing’s claim to the island of 23 million.

Though McCarthy does not have Pelosi’s decades-long record of advocacy regarding China, the California Republican is now a leading voice pushing for closer scrutiny of Beijing, and meeting Tsai could help him to burnish that image.

Last month, McCarthy told reporters that meeting Tsai in the US would not impact whether he travels to Taiwan in the future – something he had earlier said he wanted to do.

Fighter jets of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Eastern Theater Command conduct joint combat training exercises around Taiwan on August 7, 2022 in this photo released by Xinhua News Agency. Gong Yulong/Xinhua/AP

Beijing watching

A meeting in California, on US soil, is widely seen as less likely to provoke Beijing than a McCarthy visit to Taiwan.

Pelosi’s trip – the first from a lawmaker of that rank to the island in 25 years – generated a fever pitch of nationalist and anti-US rhetoric in mainland China.

This time, so far, domestic conversation in China’s heavily controlled media sphere has been significantly muted.

But the stakes remain high – including for Beijing itself – over how it responds, analysts say.

As Taiwan prepares for a presidential election in January, a fierce response could push voters away from Taiwan’s main opposition party Kuomintang (KMT), widely seen as more friendly toward Beijing.

It could also jar with another high profile trip happening now: a tour of mainland China from former Taiwan president and senior KMT member Ma Ying-jeou, the first visit from a current or former Taiwan leader since the end of the Chinese Civil War in 1949.

Ma’s tour is a “once in a half a century opportunity to send a conciliatory message between the two sides, Beijing shouldn’t want to tank that,” said Sung, the political scientist.

China is also acutely aware that its actions toward Taiwan are under a significantly brighter global spotlight following the invasion of Ukraine by Russian President Vladimir Putin, a close diplomatic partner of Xi. Putin’s rhetoric over Ukraine has echoes of how Xi speaks of Taiwan.

Beijing has recently sought to position itself as an agent of peace in that conflict – especially as it aims to repair frayed ties with Europe.

This week, as Tsai is expected to meet with McCarthy, French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will head to China – an important opportunity that Xi may not want to overshadow with military posturing.

An aggressive response also risks stoking confrontation with the US, not yet six months after Xi and US President Joe Biden called to enhance communication during a face-to-face meeting in Bali.

“(A less overtly aggressive response) would imply that Beijing does not wish to escalate tension with the US to a level that can risk getting out of hand,” said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London.

“A reset in US-China ties is not on the agenda, but an easing of tension is not beyond the realm of possibility.”

World.title: Why did Georgian police clash with Turkish football fans over Palestine?
World.content:
Georgia’s Interior Ministry says 16 people were detained and three ministry employees injured during clashes.

Share Why did Georgian police clash with Turkish football fans over Palestine? on social media

Police in Georgia have detained at least 16 people following clashes between football fans at a game between Turkish and Israeli clubs.

The Europa League fifth round match between Turkiye’s Besiktas and Israel’s Hapoel Be’er Sheva was hosted in Georgia instead of Turkiye.

The coastal Georgian city of Batumi was selected last month as a neutral territory to host the game for “safety and security reasons” because of fears of protests over Israel’s genocidal war on Gaza, according to the European football association, UEFA.

Despite the precaution, tensions between fans spilled over into the stadium and the match was suspended for 30 minutes. Once play resumed, Besiktas won the game 2-1.

It is not the first time violent clashes have marred football matches involving Israeli clubs since Israel’s genocidal war on Gaza began in October 2023.

Here’s what we know about the latest unrest:

What happened?

Tensions between fans had already been rising before kickoff in Batumi on Thursday.

According to the Georgian news outlet Civil Georgia, videos on social media showed groups of Besiktas fans marching through Batumi and physical confrontations between fans and police officers.
