World.title: Orange Level 5 warning as severe thunderstorms threaten parts of Gauteng
World.content:
Orange Level 5 warning highlights the risk of severe thunderstorms, flooding, hail and damaging winds in parts of Gauteng. Image: Unsplash

The South African Weather Service (SAWS) has issued an Orange Level 5 warning for severe thunderstorms covering parts of Gauteng on Saturday, 28 November.

The storms could bring heavy rain, large amounts of small hail and damaging winds, raising the risk of flooding and damage to infrastructure.

The warning map places the highest alert over parts of Gauteng, including the area around Johannesburg and Ekurhuleni.



Extended weather forecast for today and tomorrow, 27-28 November 2026:

Partly cloudy and cool to warm, but hot in places, with isolated to scattered showers and thundershowers reaching widespread in places in the east.#saws #weatheroutlook #Warning pic.twitter.com/gIWx1BkzGN — SA Weather Service (@SAWeatherServic) November 27, 2026

Flooding and damaging winds expected

Heavy downpours could flood roads, settlements and bridges in the affected areas.

The storms could also produce large amounts of small hail, while damaging winds may cause damage to infrastructure.

Residents should prepare for possible disruption and avoid travelling through flooded roads or crossing swollen streams.

Residents urged to take precautions

People in the affected areas should stay alert as the storms develop.

Motorists should avoid flooded roads and seek shelter during severe thunderstorms.



Residents should also secure loose outdoor items and stay away from trees during strong winds.

SAWS has urged the public to take the warning seriously and follow updates as conditions change.

World.title: SAWS issues severe weather warnings for the weekend
World.content:
Yellow Level 2 warning for four provinces on Friday, with Level 4 storms expected in KwaZulu-Natal on Saturday. Image: iStock

The South African Weather Service (SAWS) has issued severe weather warnings for parts of South Africa as thunderstorms, hail, damaging winds and possible flooding threaten the country heading into the weekend.

A Yellow Level 2 warning for severe thunderstorms is in place for parts of the Eastern Cape, Free State, North West and Northern Cape on Friday, 27 November.

The storms could bring heavy downpours, excessive lightning, damaging winds and hail, potentially causing damage to property and infrastructure.



SAWS has also issued a Yellow Level 4 warning for severe thunderstorms over the eastern parts of KwaZulu-Natal on Saturday, 28 November.

The warning includes the risk of flooding and damage to infrastructure.

Extended weather forecast for today and tomorrow, 27-28 November 2026:

Partly cloudy and cool to warm, but hot in places, with isolated to scattered showers and thundershowers reaching widespread in places in the east.#saws #weatheroutlook #Warning pic.twitter.com/gIWx1BkzGN  November 27, 2026

Four provinces under severe thunderstorm warning

The Yellow Level 2 warning covers several areas where severe thunderstorms could develop on Friday.

In the Eastern Cape, hail is possible over the Joe Gqabi, Chris Hani, Amathole and OR Tambo districts, as well as Dr Beyers Naudé and Blue Crane Route local municipalities and Buffalo City.

The eastern parts of the Northern Cape are also at risk, along with the central and western parts of the Free State and North West.



SAWS warned that the storms could result in:

Strong and damaging winds

Damage to settlements and property

Localised flooding of roads, low-lying areas and bridges

Disruption to electricity and communication services

Hail in some areas

The weather service said a surface trough over the western interior, together with upper-air disturbances over the Eastern Cape interior, would contribute to showers and thundershowers.

KwaZulu-Natal faces Level 4 warning on Saturday

The severe weather threat is expected to continue into Saturday, when a Yellow Level 4 warning has been issued for the eastern parts of KwaZulu-Natal.



The storms are expected to be accompanied by heavy downpours, damaging winds, hail and severe lightning.

The conditions could lead to flooding and damage to infrastructure, with residents urged to remain alert as thunderstorms develop.

The unsettled weather is expected to bring showers and thundershowers to parts of the eastern country, with rainfall becoming widespread in places.



Extreme heat and fire danger in other areas

While thunderstorms threaten parts of the country, other areas are expected to experience extremely hot conditions and high fire danger.

Extremely high fire danger conditions are expected over most of the Northern Cape, the south-western parts of the Free State, and parts of the Western and Eastern Cape.

Areas of concern include the Drakenstein, Central Karoo and Little Karoo regions, as well as Dr Beyers Naudé, Blue Crane Route and Chris Hani.



SAWS has also warned of extremely hot and uncomfortable conditions in parts of the Western and Eastern Cape.

Beaufort West, Prince Albert and Oudtshoorn are among the Western Cape municipalities affected by the heat advisory.

In the Eastern Cape, hot conditions are expected in parts of Sarah Baartman, Inxuba Yethemba and Amathole, with hot and humid weather along sections of the coast and adjacent interior.



Residents urged to take precautions

The weather warnings come as South Africa enters a period of increasingly unsettled summer weather.

Residents in areas affected by thunderstorms are advised to monitor SAWS updates and take precautions against lightning, flooding and damaging winds.

Motorists should avoid crossing flooded roads or bridges, while people in low-lying areas should be alert to rapidly rising water levels.



Residents should also take care during periods of extreme heat and avoid activities that could spark fires in areas where fire danger is high.

SAWS continues to update its warnings and forecasts as weather conditions change.

World.title: MKP's Mxolisi Phakathi elected eThekwini mayor
World.content:
DURBAN - uMkhonto weSizwe Party's Mxolisi Phakathi was elected eThekwini Metropolitan Municipality mayor on Friday.

Phakathi has defeated the Democratic Alliance's Haniff Hoosen.

Hoosen received 75 votes, whereas Phakathi received 139 votes in council.

Earlier on, the ANC's Thabani Nyawose was elected eThekwini council speaker.

World.title: Retief Odendaal returns as NMB mayor
World.content:
DESPATCH - The Democratic Alliance's Retief Odendaal has been elected Nelson Mandela Bay Metropolitan Municipality mayor on Friday.

He has listed job creation, economic growth and service delivery as his top priorities over the next five years.

He says the metro must create a more conducive environment for businesses to operate, amid concerns over manufacturing giant Continental.

Odendaal previously served as mayor from September 2022 until he was ousted in a motion of no confidence vote in May 2023.

World.title: Joburg City Parks urges families to check on graves after recent torrential rains
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Johannesburg City Parks and Zoo (JCPZ) is urging loved ones to check on their family members' graves, following torrential rains in the last few days.

Some graves may be damaged and as a result of soil saturation, localised flooding and subsidence.

In some instances, some headstones and tombstones may have collapsed or been displaced.

According to the JCPZ, the ongoing weather conditions have accelerated vegetation growth, placing additional pressure on cemetery maintenance teams.

The entity has ongoing interventions to assist with affected areas from time to time. Additional intervention from family members is also necessary.

Spokesperson Jenny Moodley says the continuous maintenance of graves remains with the families. This includes the safeguarding, filling, the reinstatement of installation and plants on individual gravesites.

These include the reinstatement of tombstones and other memorial structures.

"While we are responsible for the general communal maintenance of municipal cemeteries, the responsibility for preserving the integrity of the actual gravesites rests with the families," says Moodley.

With the festive season approaching, families are encouraged to visit and inspect their loved ones' gravesites.

They must also report sunken graves that might require additional topsoil from cemetery officials.

They are also requested to repair, fill in and reinstate damaged or collapsed headstones, tombstones and other memorial installations.

World.title: LIVESTREAM | City of Joburg council elects new leadership
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - The battle for Johannesburg is on, City of Johannesburg's council meets to elect a new Speaker, mayor and deputy mayor.

The first sitting on Monday was postponed due to ongoing coalition talks between political parties.

Friday's agenda is clear, electing the executive mayor, deputy mayor, Speaker and chief whip.

World.title: It's official: Mkhwanazi is the new Hawks boss
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Lieutenant-General Nhlanhla Mkhwanazi has officially been appointed national head of the Directorate for Priority Crime Investigation (DPCI), better known as the Hawks.

The appointment was announced on Friday by Minister in the Presidency Khumbudzo Ntshavheni during a post-Cabinet media briefing.

Last month, acting Police Minister Firoz Cachalia initiated the process to appoint Mkhwanazi to the position, which had been vacant since Godfrey Lebeya retired in May 2025.

Cachalia subsequently submitted a memorandum to Cabinet seeking approval for the appointment, which has now been granted.

The appointment process is governed by the South African Police Service Act, which requires Cabinet concurrence and formal reporting to Parliament.

Mkhwanazi will now head the DPCI, which is responsible for investigating serious, organised crime, corruption and other priority crimes.

World.title: ConCourt dismisses NHI Act challenge
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - The National Health Insurance (NHI) Act has survived a major legal challenge after the Constitutional Court dismissed attempts by the Board of Healthcare Funders (BHF) and the Western Cape government to have the law declared invalid.

The two applicants challenged the legislation, arguing that Parliament had failed to conduct adequate public consultation, neglected to provide key costing details and ignored objections raised by provincial governments during the legislative process.

READ | Solidarity claims NHI victory

However, the Constitutional Court rejected the BHF’s application and dismissed the Western Cape government’s challenge, although the latter decision was not unanimous, with five of the court’s 11 judges dissenting.

World.title: DA proposes to ‘donate’ eThekwini mayorship to ANC
World.content:
DURBAN – The Democratic Alliance (DA) in KwaZulu-Natal has offered to give up the eThekwini mayoral position to the African National Congress (ANC) in a last-ditch effort to finalise coalition agreements.

In a letter to ANC KwaZulu-Natal provincial task team convenor Mike Mabuyakhulu, the DA said it was willing to accept the deputy mayor position, while the Inkatha Freedom Party (IFP) would take the Speaker position.

“The DA has always placed itself as a party of reason and compromise, especially in a coalition environment. Understanding that these values need to be expressed in the eThekwini Municipality, the DA has taken the decision to donate the position of mayor to the ANC, with the DA accepting the position of deputy mayor and the IFP occupying the position of Speaker,” wrote DA provincial chairperson Dean Macpherson.

The DA also proposed taking the position of chief whip.

The offer marks a shift in the party’s previous position, in which it had maintained that it wanted the mayoral position or nothing.

The DA said it was prepared to compromise, taking into account the respective seat allocations of the parties, with the ANC holding 57 seats and the DA 37.

On portfolio allocations, the party proposed that responsibilities be distributed proportionally.

“On the matter of portfolios, we propose that we will be able to deal with this and ensure a distribution of responsibility through proportionality,” the letter stated.

World.title: Chaos as pepper spray released at Emfuleni council sitting
World.content:
VEREENIGING - The second council sitting of the Emfuleni Local Municipality was temporarily suspended after pepper spray was released inside the meeting chamber.

The incident forced the evacuation of the venue as councillors and other attendees were removed from the chambers.

The first council sitting, scheduled for Monday, was postponed after proceedings were disrupted by chaos.

The municipality is under pressure to elect its leadership, with Friday marking the legal deadline for councils to elect their municipal leadership.

World.title: Court halts Maseno University VC appointment
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

The Employment and Labour Relations Court in Mombasa has issued temporary conservatory orders in a petition challenging the recruitment and proposed appointment of Maseno University’s next Vice-Chancellor over alleged irregularities in the selection process.

Justice Nelson Abuodha on Friday certified as urgent an application filed by Willy Otieno Sawe and issued temporary orders in terms of prayer two of the motion dated November 26, pending further directions.

The respondents have been granted seven days from the date of service to file their responses, with the matter scheduled for mention on December 8 for directions on its hearing and disposal.

In the petition, Sawe questions the reported outcome of interviews conducted on April 14 and 16, 2026, in which 10 candidates were shortlisted for the university’s top job.

According to the results cited in the petition, Prof Bulitia Godrick Mathews emerged top with 79 marks, followed by Prof Bernard O. Aduda with 77.5 and Prof Francis Jakim Mulaa with 77 marks.

Prof Kimani Chege Gabriel scored 76, while Prof Mary Jepkemoi Kipsat and Prof Joseph Ouma Rasowo each obtained 74 marks. Prof Stephen O. Odebero scored 71.5, while Godfrey S. Mise got 67. Prof Erick Otieno Nyambedha was reportedly not ranked, while Prof Charles O.A. Omwawadho declined to attend the interview.

The petitioner alleges that the first, fourth and fifth-ranked candidates were recommended for further consideration and appointment, while the second and third-ranked candidates were left out.

He argues that the reported departure from the interview rankings, without disclosure of the reasons behind the final recommendations, raises questions about transparency and accountability in the recruitment process.

“The Petitioner does not ask this Honourable Court to assume that the highest interview score, by itself, confers an automatic right to appointment,” the petition states, adding that the court should scrutinise whether the selection and recommendation process complied with the applicable law and recruitment criteria.

Sawe further argues that where the final recommendations departed from the reported interview rankings, the respondents should demonstrate “the lawful criteria, reasons and evaluation process” upon which the decision was made.

He also wants an explanation for the failure to assign Prof Nyambedha a ranking despite his reported participation in the interviews, saying the assessment records and reasons for the omission should be disclosed.

“The recruitment process should be capable of withstanding public scrutiny,” the petitioner argues, insisting that all candidates should have been evaluated consistently, fairly and in accordance with the applicable criteria.

The petition names the Education Cabinet Secretary, the Attorney-General, Maseno University Council and the Public Service Commission as respondents.

The candidates whose interests may be affected, alongside several university staff unions, have also been listed as interested parties.

Among the documents the petitioner wants disclosed are interview scores, assessment and evaluation records, the criteria used in the selection, minutes of relevant meetings and the recommendations made by those involved in the recruitment.

The petitioner also raises concerns over an alleged meeting scheduled for November 26 to consider or advance the appointment, as well as claims that students could be mobilised to cause disorder at the university.

He says the latter allegation requires investigation and verification.

The respondents will have an opportunity to respond before the matter proceeds for further directions on December 8.

World.title: Wamalwa ousts Natembeya, Savula as DAP-K deputy leaders
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Democratic Action Party of Kenya (DAP-K) leader Eugene Wamalwa at the party's headquarter in Nairobi on November 26, 2026. [Benard Orwongo, Standard]

Democratic Action Party of Kenya (DAP-K) leader Eugene Wamalwa has removed Trans Nzoia Governor George Natembeya and Kakamega Deputy Governor Ayub Savula as the party’s deputy leaders, replacing them with Mumias East MP Peter Salasya and former Cabinet Minister Kipruto Arap Kirwa.

The changes, announced on Thursday at the party headquarters, mark a significant reorganisation of DAP-K’s leadership amid growing political differences between Wamalwa and the two ousted officials.

Natembeya’s removal follows months of disagreements with Wamalwa over the party’s leadership, political direction and ambition to expand its national influence.

The governor had in July 2026 declared his intention to leave DAP-K, arguing that he wanted to transform the party into a national political movement. He subsequently pursued political mobilisation through the TAWE Movement, before aligning himself with the Linda Mwananchi Movement.

His political realignment gathered momentum after Nairobi Senator Edwin Sifuna unveiled him as Chairperson of the movement’s Board of Trustees and head of its presidential campaign ahead of the 2027 General Election.

The appointments were announced on October 30, 2026, during the launch of the movement’s national headquarters in Lavington, Nairobi.

Savula’s exit, on the other hand, follows an earlier political break with Wamalwa that dates back to the November 2025 Malava by-election.

The former Lugari MP openly defied DAP-K by backing United Democratic Alliance (UDA) candidate David Ndakwa against the party’s candidate Seth Panyako. Ndakwa eventually won the seat, exposing divisions within the party’s Western Kenya political base.

On January 6, 2026, Savula publicly declared that he had moved on from DAP-K and intended to work with the government.

He subsequently formally joined UDA in February and declared his interest in the Kakamega gubernatorial seat.

He was later appointed Deputy Coordinator of President William Ruto’s Western Kenya campaign team, while UDA grassroots delegates endorsed him for a deputy party leader position, which he accepted.

The two departures have therefore left DAP-K with the challenge of rebuilding its leadership structure as political realignments gather momentum ahead of the August 2027 General Election.

Wamalwa appeared to take issue with leaders who, despite benefiting from their political parties, engage in activities that undermine the organisations.

"Let them also respect our party because you cannot bite the hand that feeds you. Heshima si utumwa," he said, in an apparent reference to the disagreements surrounding Natembeya’s political engagements.

Wamalwa had previously warned Natembeya to exercise restraint and, if he intended to join another political outfit, leave DAP-K respectfully.

He, however, dismissed suggestions that their differences were personal, maintaining that he had supported the governor’s political journey, including his successful 2022 gubernatorial campaign.

The party leader has also repeatedly called for unity among opposition leaders, warning that internal divisions could undermine efforts to challenge President William Ruto in the 2027 elections.

Beyond the changes involving Natembeya and Savula, Wamalwa said the proposed appointments of Salasya and Kirwa were part of a wider effort to invigorate the party and strengthen its leadership ahead of the polls.

World.title: Wetang'ula orders CCTV review as Sabina Chege renews missing phone
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

National Assembly Speaker Moses Wetang’ula has ordered a fresh review of CCTV footage capturing a member of Parliament allegedly picking up a mobile phone during a confrontation in the House in June 2023, following renewed demands by nominated MP Sabina Chege to have her device returned.

Wetang’ula, who chairs the Powers and Privileges Committee, said he would recuse himself from the proceedings and appoint another MP to review the recordings and present findings to the House, in a move aimed at ensuring the matter is handled appropriately.

“As your Speaker, I will take the following action. Although I am the Chairperson of the Powers and Privileges Committee, I will recuse myself from chairing this matter. I will forward the CCTV footage to the Committee and appoint another Member to act on my behalf, review the footage and present a report to this House,” he said.

The decision follows fresh revelations by Chege, who told Parliament that she had never recovered her phone, which allegedly disappeared during the confrontation involving several female legislators on June 8, 2023.

Chege narrated how she realised the device was missing after her colleague, Rosa Buyu, picked up her handbag while coming to her rescue during the altercation.

She said the phone was a newly purchased iPhone 16, barely a week old, and that she immediately raised the alarm but was assured by officers from the Sergeant-at-Arms that it could not disappear within the parliamentary chamber.

“That phone was an iPhone 16, Mr Speaker. I had just bought it. It was actually one week old. I had colleagues who were around me, whom I even asked to give me back my phone,” she said.

Chege explained that she was advised to seek medical attention following the confrontation and subsequently tracked the phone from Nairobi Hospital, where its location initially showed that it was still within Parliament.

She said the device's location later shifted to an area around Protection House, near Bunge Towers, before it was eventually traced to Donholm.

“When I got to Nairobi Hospital, we tracked my phone and established that it was still within Parliament. An hour later, its location had changed to an area near Protection House and Bunge Towers. The next day it was tracked somewhere in Donholm and from that time I did not get my phone,” she said.

The nominated MP said she reported the incident to parliamentary police, the Clerk of the National Assembly and the House Powers and Privileges Committee but had yet to recover the device.

“I want to say, till today, I have never recovered my phone,” she told the House.

Chege appealed to Wetang’ula to identify the person captured in the CCTV footage or ask them to return the phone before the current parliamentary term ends.

“To save the image of this House, please name the person. At least my phone should be returned,” she said, adding that a colleague had previously claimed to know who took the device but declined to disclose the identity.

However, her remarks triggered sharp exchanges, with some legislators questioning the manner in which the matter was being presented and warning against damaging Parliament's reputation.

Homa Bay Town MP Millie Odhiambo dismissed the incident as an issue that should not be elevated into a question of institutional integrity, arguing that members could contribute towards replacing the device.

“You can make a WhatsApp group and donate a phone for her. Don't tarnish the name of Parliament because you are a crying baby. You make people think Parliament steals people's properties,” Odhiambo said.

Ruaraka MP TJ Kajwang expressed concern that the allegations risked further damaging the reputation of legislators, saying the House needed to address issues that had become associated with its members.

“I have been in this House for 15 years. I do not want to end my term and request a renewal of my term with a tag of a thief,” he said.

Kajwang added that allegations circulating about MPs, including claims of selling recruitment opportunities, were damaging public confidence and needed to be addressed.

Lamu East MP Ruweida Obo also weighed in, declaring that most legislators did not engage in stealing other people's property.

“Sisi wengi si wezi, sisi hatuibi cha mtu na chetu hatutaki kiibiwe,” she said.

Wetang’ula, in his defence of the decision to review the footage, maintained that the recordings would help establish what happened and clear members who may have been wrongly implicated.

He clarified that he had not declared any legislator a thief, but had only indicated that CCTV footage showed a male member picking up a phone from a seat after the altercation.

“The Speaker never said there was a thief. The Speaker said a member took the phone. It is not right and morally comprehensible for anyone to take another person's property without their consent,” he said.

He cautioned MPs against relying on social media speculation and artificial intelligence-generated images to accuse colleagues, saying the CCTV review would provide an opportunity to establish the facts.

“It is easy and juicy to go on social media and use AI and amplify things and call people names. The CCTV will absolve everybody,” he said.

World.title: Ledama Ole Kina court battle over Sh1.2m dispute takes new turn
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Narok Senator Ledama Ole Kina has been granted a stay of execution in a Sh1.2 million compensation dispute with former Narok County Assembly employee Zakayo Rotiken.

The court has given the senator an opportunity to raise funds and settle the outstanding amount.

The Employment and Labour Relations Court, sitting in Nairobi, issued the orders on Tuesday, November 24, 2026, and scheduled the matter for mention on February 18, 2027.

The development follows a protracted legal dispute arising from Rotiken's dismissal, in which the court awarded him Sh1,220,737.61 in compensation.

During Tuesday's proceedings, Ole Kina sought between 30 and 45 days to raise funds and settle the outstanding amount.

The court subsequently granted a stay of execution pending further proceedings in the matter.

In a statement, Rotiken's lawyer, Tonge Yoya, said the stay of execution did not invalidate, overturn or extinguish the original judgment, insisting that the senator remained legally obligated to settle the award.

The claimant's legal team also told the court that it intended to challenge pending applications by Ole Kina, arguing that some of the issues had already been determined in previous proceedings.

The lawyers said an application dated November 19, 2026, seeking to amend a preliminary objection filed on September 25, 2026, was directed to be served upon them.

Ole Kina was further directed to file and serve written submissions on the preliminary objection within 14 days.

The objection is anchored on the doctrine of res judicata, which bars parties from reopening matters that have already been conclusively determined by a competent court.

Rotiken's lawyers contend that a previous application by the senator seeking a stay of judgment was dismissed on April 24, 2026, and argue that subsequent applications touching on the same issues should not be entertained.

However, the Parliamentary Service Commission (PSC) is considering a request to release funds to settle a court-awarded compensation to Zakayo Rotiken, a former employee of Narok Senator Ledama Ole Kina, in a labour dispute that has resurfaced following a dramatic confrontation between the senator and auctioneers.

In a letter addressed to the parties in Employment and Labour Relations Court Cause E165 of 2021, Rotiken versus Ledama Ole Kina, the Commission confirmed that it had received a request seeking the release of funds to settle the decretal sum and costs awarded by the court.

The letter signed by the Commission's Director of Litigation and Compliance, Anthony Njoroge, states that the request has been placed before the Commission for consideration, with a decision expected once deliberations are concluded.

"The Commission's decision shall be communicated to you as soon as the Commission has concluded its deliberations on the matter," reads part of the letter.

The development comes against the backdrop of a viral video showing Senator Ole Kina threatening to shoot a female auctioneer who had gone to repossess a milk delivery lorry belonging to his Enkanasa Cow Milk Company over an outstanding financial obligation.

The confrontation sparked public outrage, with questions emerging over the circumstances surrounding the attempted repossession and the senator's conduct towards the auctioneers.

The dispute is linked to a labour case filed by Rotiken, who had been employed by Ole Kina before his dismissal. The former employee moved to court seeking redress over his termination, resulting in a monetary award against the senator.

The dispute stems from a court case filed by former Narok County Assembly employee Zakayo Rotiken against Senator Ledama Ole Kina at the Employment and Labour Relations Court in Nairobi. The court awarded Rotiken KSh 1,220,737.61 in compensation following his dismissal.

The latest communication from the Parliamentary Service Commission signals that the institution is considering facilitating settlement of the court award, although it has not yet made a final commitment to release the funds.

World.title: Ruto backs Didmus Barasa for Bungoma governor in 2027
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Kimilili MP Didmus Barasa with President Ruto at a political rally in Mt Elgon during the President’s development tour in the Western region. [PCS]

President William Ruto has thrown his weight behind Kimilili MP Didmus Barasa in the race to succeed Bungoma Governor Kenneth Lusaka in 2027, setting the stage for a contest over the county's political leadership.

During his ongoing tour of Western Kenya, the President rallied support for Barasa, signalling his preference for the legislator in the battle for control of Bungoma County after the next General Election.

Barasa has expressed confidence in securing the United Democratic Alliance (UDA) party nomination, citing his development record and grassroots mobilisation in Kimilili as the foundation of his gubernatorial bid.

The MP has urged Bungoma leaders aligned with Kenya Kwanza to unite behind his candidature, arguing that a common political front would strengthen the region's bargaining power within the national government.

He said he intends to replicate his development model in Kimilili across the county's 45 wards, prioritising healthcare, education and youth empowerment.

“I want to take the development model we have implemented in Kimilili and extend it to all the 45 wards in Bungoma. Our people deserve better healthcare, improved education infrastructure, functional vocational training centres and quality early childhood education facilities,” he said.

The legislator pledged to strengthen county hospitals, improve the availability of medicines and expand access to healthcare services at the grassroots.

He also promised to invest in vocational training centres to equip young people with practical skills for employment and entrepreneurship, while improving Early Childhood Development and Education (ECDE).

Barasa identified agriculture, trade, infrastructure and youth entrepreneurship as key sectors requiring investment to unlock Bungoma's economic potential. He said his proposed administration would prioritise accountability, efficient use of public resources and improved service delivery.

His bid has received backing from a section of county leaders, including Senator Wafula Wakoli of Ford Kenya and Webuye East MP Martin Pepela.

However, Ruto's apparent preference for Barasa has attracted opposition from Sirisia MP John Waluke, who has questioned the endorsement and instead declared support for Westlands MP Tim Wanyonyi, who is associated with the Linda Mwananchi Movement (LMM).

Waluke argued that Bungoma residents should determine their next governor without external political influence.

“Bungoma belongs to its people, and the people must decide who will lead them in 2027. We cannot allow the gubernatorial contest to be determined through political endorsements from outside. Residents must be given the freedom to choose a leader who represents their interests,” he said.

The contest is also unfolding amid political differences between Barasa and National Assembly Speaker Moses Wetang'ula, adding to the competing interests shaping Bungoma's succession politics.

World.title: Shun leaders inciting you to cause chaos, PS Omollo tells youth
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Internal Security Principal Secretary Raymond Omollo. [File,Standard]

Internal Security Principal Secretary Raymond Omollo has warned young people against political violence, saying the destruction of public property costs lives and diverts resources meant for development.

The warning comes amid concerns over political violence in Embu following the September 12 incident at Nembure Stadium, where a meeting attended by Deputy President Kithure Kindiki was disrupted, leaving one person dead, six vehicles torched and three others vandalised.

Speaking during a Mass at St Thomas More Kairuri Parish in Embu County, Omollo challenged young people to question leaders who ask them to disrupt meetings, block roads or destroy property.

“Before you leave home to disrupt a meeting, ask that leader whether they would allow their own child to do what they are asking you to do,” he said.

“Ask them what they are doing to help you access education, training and employment.”

Omollo said young people should also question what political leaders were doing to improve their access to education, technical training and employment.

He said the Government was working to expand opportunities for young people through education, technical training and employment.

The PS welcomed efforts in the technical and vocational education and training (TVET) sector to equip young people in Embu with skills to pursue their ambitions.

At the same time, Omollo commended county leadership for working with the national government to combat illicit alcohol and drug abuse.

Omollo said proposed legislative changes targeting the sector had passed the first reading in Parliament and urged residents to participate in the next stages of the legislative process.

On security, the PS acknowledged calls for more police vehicles, saying the Government was investing in personnel, vehicles and equipment.

However, he challenged residents to help protect public investments, citing reports that 10 police vehicles had been burned in Embu.

“We use our taxes to buy police vehicles, build markets and construct roads. We cannot pay for development and then allow a few individuals to destroy what belongs to all of us,” he said.

Omollo warned that anyone suspected of destroying property would be taken to court in accordance with the law, where the judiciary would determine their cases.

He maintained that political differences should not be used to justify vandalism, endanger lives or disrupt public services.

“The Constitution protects the right to express ourselves peacefully and unarmed. Political differences cannot be an excuse to vandalise property, endanger lives or disrupt the services our communities depend on,” he said.

Those present included Public Service, Human Capital Development and Special Programmes Cabinet Secretary Geoffrey Ruku, Embu Governor Cecily Mbarire, Senator Alexander Munyi and Deputy Governor Kinyua Mugo, among others.

World.title: Narok Senator under fire after threatening to shoot auctioneers in Sh1.2m dispute
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Narok Senator Ledama ole Kina is at the centre of a national uproar after a viral video captured him threatening to shoot individuals during a volatile confrontation involving auctioneers and a former Senate office employee.

The dramatic standoff erupted when court-backed agents attempted to seize a milk delivery truck over an unresolved legal dispute and has since ignited intense public debate regarding political accountability and the rule of law.

The controversy surrounds long court battle after Zakayo Rotiken, who served sacked as Narok North Constituency Coordinator between 2017 and 2020, was sacked.

According to records, the claimant was illegally dismissed amidst unpaid salary arrears.

On October 31, 2023, the Employment and Labour Relations Court ruled in Rotiken's favour , a decision that was subsequently upheld when the Senator lost his appeal.

With accrued interest, the court decree now stands at Sh 1.2 million.

Consequently, when the debt remained unsatisfied, licensed auctioneers moved in to execute lawful warrants which in turn provoked a furious reaction from Senator Ole Kina, who fiercely framed the entire episode as a political witch-hunt.

The lawmaker argued that Rotiken was hired by the Narok Senate office rather than his personal capacity, maintaining that any resultant liabilities ought to be handled by the Parliamentary Service Commission (PSC) rather than attaching his private property.

Defending his harsh words in the widely circulated footage, the senator dismissed the agents as trespassers and asserted action against them.

"Anybody who trespasses will get a bullet in their head or leg because that is trespass," said Ole Kina.

“Nitakupiga Risasi!” Senator Ledama Ole Kina embroiled in confrontation with alleged auctioneers over unpaid car loan https://t.co/k4OSXpNsdi November 21, 2026

The claimant's legal team condemned the threats made against statutory court officers emphasizing that a court judgment is an enforceable command rather than a mere suggestion, calling upon the Inspector General of Police of Police and the Director of Criminal Investigatons to urgently investigate the alleged death threats.

Rotiken noted that he merely sought justice through proper judicial channels and should not be penalized or intimidated for pursuing his lawful entitlements.

"When I was illegally dismissed with unpaid salary arrears, I did not resort to violence or politics—I went to the Employment and Labour Relations Court. Nobody is above the law, and I appeal to the police to protect the officers doing their job so that justice can finally be served," he said.

Ultimately, as pressure mounts on security agencies to look into the firearm threats, the unfolding saga highlights a tense intersection between public office obligations and the absolute sanctity of judicial decrees.

While the senator maintains that his assets were unjustly targeted by political rivals, legal experts and the public continue to demand that the rule of law must prevail without exception.

World.title: Ruto defends IEBC, challenges rivals to present alternative policies
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

President William Ruto during his tour of the Western region. [PCS]

President William Ruto has launched a scathing attack on opposition leaders over their demands on the Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission (IEBC), accusing them of attempting to interfere with the electoral agency because they fear losing the 2027 General Election.

The President challenged opposition leaders to allow IEBC to prepare independently for next year's elections, saying they should instead focus on identifying their presidential candidate, developing a manifesto and presenting alternative policies to Kenyans.

Ruto accused his competitors of attempting to play the roles of both contestants and referees by seeking to influence decisions on the procurement of election materials and equipment.

He spoke a day after opposition leaders walked out of a meeting convened by IEBC, alleging bias by the commission.

“Please give IEBC a chance to arrange the elections next year. The people of Kenya will decide. You go and first look for your candidate, find your policies, agenda and plans and sell them to the wananchi. We shall meet at the ballot,” said Ruto.

Speaking during his development tour of Western Kenya, Ruto questioned why opposition politicians were concentrating on determining how IEBC should procure election materials instead of preparing to face voters.

“How can somebody who is in a competition want to decide where the pitch will be, who the referee will be and where the ball will be placed? Leave IEBC alone. Those who will vote are the citizens, and they are the ones who will decide,” he said.

The President accused his opponents of lacking a clear political agenda and capacity to deliver, claiming their campaigns were centred on slogans and personal attacks against him.

He challenged them to explain what they would do differently in agriculture, education, healthcare, infrastructure and employment rather than mobilising Kenyans around the slogan 'Kasongo Must Go'.

“The reason why my competitors cannot develop a plan is that they have no capacity. The reason why they have no agenda is that they have no knowledge. The reason why they cannot develop anything is that they know they have no capacity to deliver on anything that they will say,” he said.

His remarks were echoed by Kakamega Governor Fernandes Barasa and National Assembly Speaker Moses Wetang'ula, who rallied Western Kenya leaders behind his re-election bid and defended IEBC against what they termed unnecessary political pressure. President William Ruto during his tour of the Western region. [ Benjamin Sakwa, Standard]

Speaking in Butere, Barasa said the region's political leadership, including Prime Cabinet Secretary Musalia Mudavadi, Cabinet Secretary Wycliffe Oparanya, Wetang'ula and trade unionist Francis Atwoli, was united behind Ruto's development agenda.

“IEBC will conduct the elections according to the law. Opposition leaders should leave IEBC alone and allow it to do its work,” he said.

Wetang'ula maintained that IEBC was independent of both the government and the opposition and should be allowed to conduct its work without interference.

“IEBC is independent of the government and independent of the Opposition. You stand there to do your work fairly, truthfully and equally,” he said.

He added: “Just as Arsenal supporters cannot dictate what uniform the referee should wear, the referee's responsibility is to ensure the game is played fairly and the winner emerges through a legitimate process.”

The exchanges underline the growing political contest over the management of the 2027 elections, with the government side accusing the opposition of undermining the electoral agency before campaigns gather momentum.

Beyond the political exchanges, Ruto used his Western Kenya tour to highlight development projects, saying his administration was committed to correcting years of neglect and unequal distribution of national resources.

He also announced plans for a second phase of the Nyota programme targeting an additional 200,000 young people, each expected to receive Sh50,000 to establish or expand businesses.

The government is also targeting 100,000 college graduates for internships from January, with each expected to receive a monthly stipend of Sh20,000.

Ruto's tour comes amid growing competition for Western Kenya's support ahead of the 2027 General Election, with emerging opposition alliances seeking to challenge his influence.

World.title: Brad Pitt and Angelina Jolie reach out-of-court settlement over French winery dispute
World.content:
Brad Pitt and Angelina Jolie have resolved a protracted legal battle over the ownership of a French winery a decade after the high-profile couple separated, according to reporting cited from Euronews.

Ownership and the joint statement

Control of Château Miraval, a prominent estate in France’s Var region, stood at the center of the dispute between Pitt, 62, and Jolie, 51, who acquired a controlling stake in the property in 2008 and married there six years later.

In a joint statement announcing the end of the winery fight, the actors said they had reached an out-of-court settlement in their family’s best interest and would offer no further comment.

Claims, counterclaims, and aftermath

In the litigation, Pitt alleged that Jolie sold her interest in the estate to Russian businessman Yuri Shefler without his permission, contending the two had agreed not to dispose of their stakes without mutual consent.

Jolie filed a counterclaim accusing Pitt of assaulting her and their children while intoxicated aboard a flight, an incident that prompted her to file for divorce in 2016. Pitt denied the allegations, and no charges were filed following inquiries by the FBI and child welfare authorities.

The two reached a divorce settlement in 2024 after eight years of legal proceedings. All six of their children have since reached adulthood, with several dropping their father’s surname.

World.title: Donations exceed LE 255.7 million for Al-Warraq victims
World.content:
Contributions and financial pledges to support the families of the deceased and the injured in the Ring Road fuel tanker fire in Al-Warraq surpassed LE 255.7 million by Thursday evening, amid a broad wave of backing from business leaders, banks, corporations, civil society groups, political parties, and public figures across Egypt and the wider Arab world.

Business leaders and corporations

Business figures and private companies led the donor list with a combined LE 91 million. Businessman Mamdouh Abbas pledged LE 20 million, while LE 10 million each was announced by Hisham Talaat Moustafa, Ahmed Ezz, Yasseen Mansour, Mohamed Lotfy Mansour, Ahmed Abou Hashima, and Tatweer Misr CEO Ahmed Shalaby. Dr. Nawal El-Degwi contributed LE 5 million, and both Samir Rayan, chairman of Rayan Automotive Egypt, and GLC Paints committed LE 3 million.

Banking, aviation, and regional support

Institutional and regional pledges added substantial momentum to the relief effort. Following a directive from the Central Bank of Egypt, the Federation of Egyptian Banks coordinated with local lenders to provide an initial LE 60 million in support, while the civil aviation sector earmarked LE 30 million for families of the dead and injured. From Saudi Arabia, Turki Al-Sheikh, chairman of the General Entertainment Authority, announced a pledge of LE 43 million—comprising LE 30 million for families of the deceased and LE 13 million for the injured.

Civil society, parties, and public figures

Civil society organizations accounted for LE 24 million in contributions: LE 5 million each from Misr El Kheir Foundation, Al Orman Association, and Al-Shar’ia Association; LE 3 million from Takafol; and LE 2 million each from Life Makers Foundation, the National Foundation for Family Development, and the Coptic Evangelical Organization. Political parties also stepped forward, with the National Front Party and Homeland Defenders Party pledging roughly LE 7.5 million combined. Actor Yasser Galal announced LE 200,000 for one of those affected who lost both a vehicle and a livelihood in the disaster.

Telecom matching, relief channels, and state compensation

In the telecommunications sector, the National Telecommunications Regulatory Authority, acting on directives from the Minister of Communications and Information Technology, launched a one-month initiative with all four mobile operators to match citizens’ donations made through mobile wallets, with no set ceiling on total contributions.

Meanwhile, the Ministry of Solidarity designated Nasser Social Bank account number 55555 under the name “Al-Warraq Ring Road Incident” to collect donations and oversee distribution to eligible recipients. The government is also studying exceptional compensation measures, including periodic-return investment certificates for the families of the deceased and replacement vehicles for drivers who lost theirs.

Officials expect total pledges to climb further in the coming days as community initiatives continue, noting that the figure announced so far reflects both donations and pledges—not necessarily funds already transferred—and excludes state compensation as well as individual contributions not yet tallied.

World.title: Egypt and Sudan reiterate 1959 water rights and reject unilateral dam moves
World.content:
The pledge followed a Tuesday visit to Cairo by Sudanese Transitional Council Prime Minister Kamil Al-Tayeb Idris and a senior delegation, during which he met President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi and handed over a message from Sudanese Sovereignty Council head Abdel Fattah Al-Burhan.

In their joint statement, both governments tied water security directly to human survival and economic growth, framing dialogue and mutual benefit under international law as their guiding principles while welcoming African backing for downstream states’ rights to safeguard vital resources and develop on equal footing with the rest of the continent.

Addressing Ethiopia’s unilateral dam project, Egypt and Sudan reiterated that unilateral steps in the Eastern Nile basin breach international law, create serious repercussions, and pose an ongoing hazard downstream. They urged Addis Ababa to abandon unilateralism and return to cooperative norms grounded in no significant harm, prior notification, consultation, and consensus.

Coordination mechanisms and regional basin talks

Looking across the wider basin, Egypt and Sudan highlighted the central importance of the Nile Basin Initiative and pointed to shared regional momentum to finish consultations and rebuild consensus toward an inclusive basin-wide commission.

They also praised the consultative mini-committee chaired by Uganda alongside Rwanda and South Sudan for its report urging steps to restore full participation, including revising and updating the framework agreement so every stakeholder’s concerns are accommodated.

World.title: Egypt orders pretrial detention and drug testing for Al-Warraq crash suspect
World.content:
Egypt’s Public Prosecution ordered the detention of the driver of the vehicle responsible for the fuel tanker collision and fire on the Ring Road in the Al-Warraq area, which killed 31 people and injured others.

In a statement Thursday evening, the prosecution said it decided to refer the suspect to the Forensic Medicine Authority for blood sampling and toxicology testing to determine whether he was under the influence of narcotics at the time of the crash. It also announced that it had finished questioning all injured victims whose health conditions allowed.

The prosecution stated that it ordered the 21-year-old suspect held in pretrial detention pending investigations following his interrogation.

In a related move, the prosecution ordered the Forensic Medicine Authority to collect DNA samples from the families of the deceased and conduct matching tests to identify remains that could not otherwise be recognized.

Earlier on Thursday, the prosecution announced the arrest of the driver responsible for the collision, noting that he admitted driving at 110 kilometers per hour and weaving between lanes before hitting the rear of the tanker. That impact caused a tire to blow out and sent the tanker swerving off course before hitting the concrete barrier and exploding.

The crash set several surrounding vehicles ablaze, charring at least 27 vehicles, according to a prosecution statement the day before.

World.title: Sharp surge in gold: Global and Egyptian prices rise
World.content:
Spot gold contracts rose on Friday’s trading, with the ounce gaining approximately $106.25—a 2.98 percent increase—to reach $3,673.09.

The price traded between a low of $3,558.05 and a high of $3,680.16.

Looking at performance over extended periods, gold recorded an annual decline of 11.66 percent, a drop over the past six months of 17.62 percent, and a decrease over the past three months of 20.18 percent.

World.title: Meteorologists warn of sharp weather shift and rain across Egypt within 72 hours
World.content:
The Egyptian Meteorological Authority (EMA) warned of a shift in weather conditions starting Monday, November 30, 2026. Only 72 hours separate us from weather fluctuations, as Egypt will experience a low-pressure system, temperature drops of up to 6°C, and rainfall.

According to forecasts from the General Authority for Meteorology covering the period from Saturday, November 28, through Wednesday, December 2, 2026, mild autumn weather will prevail during the day across most regions, turning hot in Southern Upper Egypt, and cool to cold at night and in the early morning.

Rainfall map and weather phenomena

The Meteorological Authority warned of morning mist (fog) forming between 4:00 AM and 9:00 AM on roads leading to and from Northern Egypt, extending to Greater Cairo, the Suez Canal cities, Central Sinai, and Northern Upper Egypt. This mist may become dense at times on certain roads.

Weather maps forecast chances of light rain—with an approximate 40% probability—on Sunday, November 29, across intermittent periods in parts of the Northern Coasts, the Northern Nile Delta, the Red Sea mountain range, South Sinai, and the Gulf of Aqaba.

Starting Monday, parts of Northern Egypt will experience unstable weather conditions accompanied by:

Chances of rainfall of varying intensity.

A drop in temperatures alongside active winds in some areas, increasing the sensation of cold weather.

Disrupted maritime navigation along parts of the Mediterranean coast.

Regarding expected temperatures, Greater Cairo and the Nile Delta will record a high of 23°C and a low of 15°C on Saturday. Temperatures will rise on Sunday to a high of 25°C and a low of 16°C, before dipping to 24°C and 15°C on Monday. On both Tuesday and Wednesday, they will reach a high of 22°C and a low of 14°C.

World.title: Artists are quitting Instagram and Facebook over fears AI will steal their work
World.content:
Matty Burnham, a watercolor artist in the United Kingdom, said he discovered a Pinterest account impersonating his illustration in 2024. The account created AI versions of his watercolors and listed them on fake profiles via Shopify, Facebook and Instagram, he told CNN.

Although Burnham tracked the Pinterest account to Ho Chi Min City, Vietnam, he does not know who was behind it.

It’s part of a wave of AI-generated artwork that’s taking business away from the creators themselves, and is especially prevalent on Meta-owned Instagram and Facebook. CNN spoke with over a dozen artists on how they are navigating the current AI landscape.

AI-generated art profiles “monetize Facebook,” Burnham said. “They have hundreds of thousands of followers who believe these fake profiles are genuine artists and direct users to various websites with shops and ads.”

The problem has pushed some independent artists to pull back from Instagram, Facebook and other Meta platforms, especially with the tech giant’s proposed updates to its terms of service. Some have considered leaving Meta-owned social media platforms entirely, pausing posting or turning to other online creator communities such as Patreon or Substack.

Matty Burnham, a watercolor artist in the United Kingdom, said he discovered a Pinterest account impersonating his illustration in 2024. Courtesy Matty Burnham

Tim O’Brien, board member at the Society of Illustrators, said he believes artists deserve meaningful consent, fair compensation and accessible ways to challenge unauthorized exploitations of their work.

“For many artists, this is not merely a legal dispute. It is a question of livelihood, creative ownership, consent and basic fairness,” O’Brien said.

Meta’s updated terms would still allow automated software to scrape external websites and extract large amounts of data without permission from business account owners. This includes personal portfolios, online stores, and links to Facebook, Instagram, WhatsApp and Threads business accounts.

The terms were originally supposed to go into effect October 30, then got pushed back to November 20. The company announced on November 5 that the updates were delayed indefinitely.

“We’re pausing the changes as we continue to engage with stakeholders and take our time to get this right. In the meantime, our existing terms remain in effect,” a Meta spokesperson said in a statement to CNN.

Still, even with the latest delay, the proposed updates have already caused another wave of artists to leave Meta.

Samantha Waldron, co-owner of Dutcher Photography in Madison, Wisconsin, told CNN that she deleted all business and personal Facebook pages earlier this month and has since transitioned her Instagram business accounts to personal accounts, deleted a vast majority of posts, and removed all external website links from Meta account bios.

Samantha Waldron, co-owner of Dutcher Photography in Madison, Wisconsin, told CNN that she deleted all business and personal Facebook pages this month. Courtesy Samantha Waldron

“It was the last straw that was a long time coming. I’m frankly relieved not to have to worry about keeping up on social media moving forward,” said Waldron.

Under the updated terms, independent artists’ images, style, and property could be scraped without their knowledge to train generative AI models, creators told CNN. Those AI models could then replicate or replace human-made art — and potentially impact artists’ businesses on those sites.

Megan Wimberley, founder of Cowgirl Artists of America in Tulsa, Oklahoma, is in the process of deleting all of her Meta accounts. She told CNN that she considers these new terms a major breach of trust. Wimberley believes everyone – not just artists – should be concerned about posting their personal images, video and audio due to potential AI scraping.

Megan Wimberley, founder of Cowgirl Artists of America in Tulsa, Oklahoma, said she is in the process of deleting all of her Meta accounts. Courtesy Megan Wimberley

“I actually view Meta as a company trying to lead the way in AI and that their social media platforms are no longer really about social media but more about free licensing to train their AI,” said Wimberley. “If you’re a mother and you’re posting your children, you’re potentially licensing Meta to use your children to train their AI.”

Some even chose to “go dark” on Meta platforms from October 30 through November 6 when the updated Meta terms were initially planned to kick in, refraining from posting or sharing content in protest of the updated terms. Wimberley said she started the “Meta blackout” campaign on October 22, and it took off from there.

Nicole McKay, artists relations director at The Guild of Artists and Artisans, told CNN in a statement that many artists in the United States have begun removing their accounts from Meta platforms in response to the upcoming policy change with AI model training. Many artists have posted “goodbye” messages on Instagram and Facebook, citing Meta’s politics.

“For artists who rely on these platforms to showcase and sell their work, connect with customers, and build their businesses, leaving Meta presents a difficult choice between protecting their work and maintaining their livelihoods,” McKay said.

Artists traverse ‘AI slop’

AI-generated artwork has serious repercussions on the creator economy, artists told CNN. Online imitators are forcing artists to change their strategy on how they reach an audience.

Andrew Scott, a contemporary artist in Rochester, New York, said he directly messaged an AI art impersonator in September about copying his work.

He said the person admitted to using Scott’s original work as a starting point to build her own AI-generated art videos. The person behind the impersonating profile then shared AI clips on Instagram, giving the impression she created the actual art. Scott noted one of her posts with AI artwork received 50 million views.

Scott said he explained to the impersonator how the AI versions could potentially hurt his business. She has since unfollowed him on social media but continues to create the AI-prompted knockoffs, he said.

Andrew Scott, a contemporary artist in Rochester, New York, said he directly messaged an AI art impersonator in September about copying his work. Courtesy Andrew Scott

Nancy Chen, a ceramic artist in Canada, posts videos on social media that show how she makes sale pieces. But she understands those clips could also be vulnerable to AI model training. Chen says she’s been wary lately of posting polished images of her work on Meta platforms but hasn’t decided to leave yet.

“It makes me wonder how independent artists can present their work to the world when their transparency can be weaponized,” Chen told CNN. “AI can outpace any individual artist, so I definitely feel some pressure to compete in price, even though I feel my labor is already underpriced.”

One of the main concerns for creators is the scale and speed that AI can push content, especially compared to human-made work that can be time-consuming. That concern is compounded by questions of how generative AI is trained on artwork, usually without artists’ say, and how copyright law applies to AI.

Nancy Chen, a ceramic artist in Canada, said she’s been wary lately of posting polished images of her work on Meta platforms. Courtesy Nancy Chen

Isaiah Steinfeld, an American Institute of Graphic Arts Board Member who builds with AI, said that protecting artists and embracing the technology don’t have to be opposing views. He noted that artists can still register work for copyright, pursue infringement claims and get unauthorized copies taken down.

For instance, Meta said creators can report instances of AI impersonators and submit takedown requests via its Intellectual Property Reporting Center.

“So, provenance has to cut both ways: protect creators from having their work appropriated and protect people using new (AI) tools from having their actual contributions erased,” Steinfeld said.

Google released an online tool, SynthID Detector, this month to the public. The free site allows anyone to upload a file to check if that image, video or audio file was made by AI from Google and partners such as OpenAI, Nvidia and Kakao.

In a press release, Google said the platform has watermarked over 180 million images and video and regularly sees over a million verification requests each day.

But this is only the beginning, and independent artists agree these changes do not go far enough. Many still grapple with whether to share content on social platforms at all, but in their line of work, it’s about brand awareness.

“Personally, I don’t trust that there will be enough done to protect artists,” Burnham said. “The UK government seems more concerned about not limiting profitable start-up tech companies than protecting artists. My hope is that the public continues to reject gen-AI in this current model.”

When CNN reached out for comment, a spokesperson for the UK Department for Digital, Culture, Media and Sport said: “The government has engaged extensively with creatives, industry bodies and AI firms and we are taking time to ensure we find the right approach to this issue.”

“We have been clear that we will not proceed with any course of action which does not work for our creative industries and our AI sector,” they added.

World.title: Putin showed ‘restraint’ by not using nuclear weapons, Kushner says
World.content:
Russian President Vladimir Putin has “shown restraint” by not using nuclear weapons in the conflict with Ukraine, White House envoy Jared Kushner has said, while describing the Russian leader as a “grand man of politics.”

In a wide-ranging interview with Politico, Kushner – who is President Donald Trump’s son-in-law – said he was convinced Putin wanted peace.

“My assessment is that he does not only want peace; he wants to try and change the relationship with America, and he does want to try and see if there’s maybe a way to start a new beginning.”

“So far Putin has showed restraint; he’s agreed not to use nuclear weapons, which obviously is a big thing, and he’s reassured us that that’s not his intention,” he added.

Kushner and his fellow US negotiator Steve Witkoff have met Putin several times, most recently this month at the Kremlin.

“He’s definitely a grand man of politics, he’s a historic figure,” Kushner said.

Russian President Vladimir Putin, left, greets US Special Envoy Steve Witkoff, center, and Jared Kushner during a meeting at the Kremlin in Moscow, Russia, on November 12. Vyacheslav Prokofiev/Sputnik/Reuters

“He takes a lot of notes when we’re speaking, and he transmits very specifically. But it’s very clear he has a very deep understanding of the issues.”

Kushner rejected suggestions that the US had applied pressure on Ukraine to make concessions to Russia.

Ukraine has said that the US Defense Department has delayed shipments of vital air defense missiles and intelligence sharing has been disrupted.

As for efforts to reach a settlement that would include issues of territorial control, Kushner said: “This isn’t about fairness or who’s right or wrong.”

Kushner said border lines in Europe had changed over time.

“I do believe that when people see long-term durability and a pathway to peace, I think they’ll be a little bit more flexible on where do you draw the line.”

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said earlier this month that US negotiators had floated the idea of Ukraine withdrawing its remaining forces from the eastern Donbas region in exchange for membership of NATO.

“The Americans raised a question: ‘What if Ukraine joins Nato? Would Ukraine withdraw from Donbas?’ This was the first time this had been raised,” Zelensky said after meeting Kushner and Witkoff.

Ukraine’s President Volodymyr Zelensky, right, attends a meeting with Kushner and Steve Witkoff at Casement Aerodrome in Baldonnel, Ireland, on November 12. Paul Faith/AFP/Getty Images

Ukraine has long resisted the idea of ceding land to Russia, which launched an unprovoked full-scale invasion in 2022.

Zelensky said if he received a “comprehensive security package” – which would include a strong Ukrainian army and guarantees from NATO and the European Union – he would put a proposal to the public.

Alluding to that possibility, Kushner told Politico, “Without a security guarantee from America, Ukraine will not be safe in the future… President Trump has to determine that a security guarantee is in the interests of America to give.”

Zelensky has previously said that Russia would not stop at taking the Donbas – whose two regions comprise nearly 10% of Ukrainian territory – but would plan further attacks.

As for negotiations, Kushner said: “I wish there was a fast way to do this… There’s a lot we agree on. We all want long-term peace.”

“Once we’re able to define that post-war relationship, I think the issue of territory will become much easier to resolve because right now there’s no way to bridge that last issue.”

Without a settlement there was a real risk of escalation, Kushner said.

“Europe is funding and arming Ukraine against Russia, and it won’t take a lot of miscalculation for this thing to escalate massively,” Kushner warned.

The ultimate goal, Kushner said, was that “if you can end this war in a way where Ukraine is sovereign, secure, prosperous, and free, they could join the EU. They have a post-war economy plan. They have credible security guarantees. They have strong deterrence capabilities. That’s a huge victory for Ukraine and for Europe.”

World.title: Tubman University Graduates 256 at 13th Commencement, Highlights Academic and Infrastructure Gains
World.content:
The university’s 13th Commencement Convocation brought together government officials, international guests, education stakeholders and families as President Dr. Olu Q. Menjay outlined institutional progress, Founding President Dr. Elizabeth Davis-Russell urged graduates to provide worthy service, and Valedictorian Abraham Washington challenged them to uphold integrity and contribute to national development.

HARPER, Maryland County — William V.S. Tubman University has graduated 256 students from six colleges, with university officials highlighting developments in research, technology and infrastructure while challenging the graduates to use their education to address Liberia’s development needs.

By Peter P. Toe, Jr., [email protected]



The ceremony, held at the Tubman University Pavilion in Harper on Monday, November 23, 2026, brought together international guests, including representatives of partner institutions and donor organizations, national government officials, members of the university’s Board of Trustees, the Foundational Board, local authorities, education stakeholders, parents, guardians, faculty and staff.

Delivering his institutional message, TU President Dr. Olu Q. Menjay outlined developments in research, academic technology, student services and campus infrastructure, describing them as part of the university’s efforts to improve the quality of higher education.

Dr. Menjay said the university had been ranked first among Liberian universities in research publications by the Association of African Universities, of which TU is a full member.

He also announced that the university’s Institutional Review Board is operational, following Federalwide Assurance approval granted on January 28, 2026, and valid through January 28, 2030.



The President said TU’s digital library provides access to more than three million electronic books, journals and research documents. He also cited the introduction of plagiarism detection software as part of efforts to strengthen academic integrity and research standards.

The President further announced plans to introduce a paid campus vacation employment program in 2027. Under the initiative, sixty students, ten from each college, will be selected to gain practical work experience and develop professional skills.

On entrepreneurship, Dr. Menjay challenged graduates to become job creators rather than depend solely on the search for employment. He said the university plans to purchase liquid soap produced by its students for institutional use beginning next year.

The President also reported renovations to the College of Education, named after Dr. Elizabeth Davis-Russell, the academic complex and the capital housing complex. He said renovation work on the university’s College of Arts and Sciences building was continuing, with half of the building fully completed and already in use by students for classes, while the first phase of a new engineering complex was nearing completion.

He also acknowledged international support, including a donation of assorted university supplies from Howard Payne University in Brownwood, Texas, which he said was being shipped to Liberia.

For her part, Keynote speaker and TU Founding President Dr. Elizabeth Davis-Russell challenged graduates to use their education to provide what she described as “worthy service” that makes a meaningful difference in people’s lives.

Dr. Davis-Russell, 84, traveled from California, United States, to attend the ceremony. She also chairs the university’s Foundation Board.

She reminded graduates that TU was founded on values including excellence, integrity, civility, ethics, genuine care, professionalism, intellectual engagement, dependability and trustworthiness.

She said the university’s responsibility extends beyond its immediate surroundings, emphasizing that its focus must remain local, national and international.

“This university is not parochial,” she said, adding that its responsibility was to address local and national needs while maintaining an international outlook.

She urged the graduates to use artificial intelligence responsibly to address national challenges, including food insufficiency and diseases such as malaria.

“Are you going to become a passive participant or a diligent mover?” she asked, challenging graduates to use AI ethically to improve the human condition.

Dr. Davis-Russell called on graduates to build on practical projects and community initiatives undertaken by students who preceded them.

She urged graduates of the College of Education to advance earlier efforts in early childhood education that involved parents in children’s learning and care.

Business Administration graduates were challenged to help local business owners improve their practices, while Agriculture graduates were urged to contribute to making Liberia self-sufficient in rice production.

Graduates of Nursing and Health Sciences were reminded of earlier community health screening and public education efforts, including during the Ebola outbreak. She challenged them to continue promoting good health practices in communities.

She also urged Arts and Sciences graduates to preserve Liberia’s cultural heritage and work with health professionals to address infectious diseases and high maternal mortality.

As they enter the workforce or pursue further studies, Dr. Davis-Russell cautioned graduates against allowing rumors, popular opinion or the desire for power to influence their decisions.

“Know which lines you are unwilling to cross,” she told them, warning against compromising personal values to gain access to friendship or positions of power.

She urged the graduates to regularly examine their conduct and decisions by asking whether they could be proud of the person they see when they look in the mirror.

Valedictorian Abraham Washington used his address to reflect on his journey through poverty, hunger and financial hardship, saying determination and the support of others helped him reach graduation.

He paid tribute to his late mother, who raised and supported him throughout his education but died shortly before the ceremony.

Washington said her prayers, sacrifices and guidance would remain part of his success story.

Addressing his fellow graduates, he said the value of their education should not be measured only by the degrees they receive, but by how they use their knowledge to improve the lives of others.

He called on graduates to reject corruption, tribalism, political intolerance and the abuse of public resources, urging them to demonstrate integrity and accountability in their professional and personal lives.

Washington also acknowledged the contributions of the university’s international partners and sponsors, including the Boe Peace Foundation Africa, Waz Foundation, MOPP and other supporters.

He challenged graduates from the different colleges to apply their knowledge to national problems, including challenges in education, business, agriculture and healthcare.

“If our education cannot improve the lives of others, ask yourself, what greater purpose should my education serve?” he asked.

He concluded by reminding his classmates that while their academic journey at the university had ended, their responsibility to learn, serve and lead was only beginning.

With 256 graduates now entering the workforce and other areas of professional life, attention turns to how effectively their academic training will translate into practical solutions to Liberia’s longstanding challenges, from unemployment and food insecurity to poor healthcare, weak infrastructure and governance concerns.

Their contributions in the coming years will ultimately test the value of the education they have received and the university’s promise of producing graduates capable of making a difference.

World.title: Cummings Says Boakai’s US$5.7 Billion Gold-for-Infrastructure Deal Could Trade Away Liberia’s Birthright
World.content:
MONROVIA – A day after President Joseph Nyuma Boakai signed what his government calls the largest infrastructure program in Liberia’s history, the opposition’s most prominent economic voice has asked a pointed question: who pays?

By Rodney D Sieh

Addressing a news conference Thursday, Alternative National Congress (ANC) political leader Alexander B. Cummings compared the deal to the biblical Esau, who sold his birthright for a single meal. “We must not become an Esau Generation,” he said.



What Was Signed

Boakai promised to deliver four new power plants, a national transmission network and 14 major road and bridge projects within five years under the US$5.7 billion agreement he signed Wednesday with Bea Mountain Mining Corporation. Under the Master Infrastructure Development Agreement (MIDA), the deal would add 270 megawatts of electricity through four new power plants, more than three times the capacity of the Mount Coffee hydropower plant, and build a 146-kilometer highway.

The government’s case rests on how the deal is paid for. The President said the government would use higher gold prices to “ring-fence new revenue streams” from BMMC beginning in 2027 to fund the projects, and BMMC also agreed to a US$500 million bridge financing facility to keep construction on schedule. In other words, Liberia pays no cash up front. It pays with gold revenue it expects to collect in the future.

Two Speeches, Two Days



Set side by side, the President’s speech on Wednesday and Cummings’ remarks on Thursday agree on what Liberia needs. They part ways on the price.

Both start with the same hardship. Boakai spoke of ordinary people the deal would reach, saying “It will provide power for the welder, the tailor, the barber, and the shopkeeper,” and pointing to children studying at night and clinics keeping equipment running. Cummings opened on the same ground: roads that cannot be used in the rainy season, millions without reliable electricity, and farmers who cannot get their produce to market. “Liberia desperately needs roads. Liberia desperately needs energy,” he said. On the problem itself, there is no disagreement.

Both reach for a food metaphor. Boakai anticipated his critics in the language of the market: “I know some Liberians will ask, ‘Da What will we Eat?’ That is a legitimate concern.” Cummings answered with Esau’s meal: “His hunger was real. His need was genuine. But the price he paid was far greater than the temporary relief he received.” Boakai’s message is that Liberians will see real benefits from the deal. Cummings’ warning is that satisfying today’s hunger could cost the country something far more valuable.

Both speak for future generations, to opposite ends. Boakai called the signing “a historic day for Liberia as we lay the foundations for tomorrow.” Cummings warned that “in our urgency to solve today’s problems, we must not mortgage tomorrow’s possibilities.” To the President, the deal is a gift to future generations. To Cummings, it is a bill they may be left to pay.

They disagree on whether this is debt. The government insists the deal adds no borrowing. The President’s legal adviser, Keita, said “So we are not going to be adding to the government’s debt, and that is a big deal for all of us.” Cummings rejects the premise: “There is no such thing as free infrastructure. Someone ultimately pays.” His concern is precisely that pledging future revenue lets the government take on a debt-like obligation “outside traditional public debt transparency mechanisms.” The two sides are not arguing about the same numbers. They are arguing about whether committing future income counts as borrowing.

Both claim value for money.
