World.title: Campaña elecciones generales 29-N, en directo | El PP denuncia ante la Junta Electoral presuntas irregularidades en el voto por correo y el reparto de la propaganda electoral
World.content:
Bustinduy: “España no se pone de acuerdo en si la tortilla tiene que llevar cebolla o no, pero todo el país coincide en que Colau ganó el debate”

El debate a cuatro de este jueves ha transformado el estado de ánimo en la izquierda. A dos días de que se abran las urnas, el portavoz de campaña y ministro de Derechos Sociales, Pablo Bustinduy, ha vaticinado que Frente Amplio dará “la sorpresa” este domingo. “España es un país en el que es difícil ponerse de acuerdo, no nos ponemos de acuerdo sobre si la tortilla tiene que llevar cebolla o no, pero todo el país está de acuerdo en que Ada Colau ganó por goleada el debate de anoche”, ha manifestado en declaraciones a los medios esta mañana en la sede de Más Madrid, que ejerce de oficina electoral de la coalición de izquierdas en esta campaña. En opinión del dirigente, la candidata tuvo ayer “un desempeño extraordinario”. “Ganó el debate por convicción, por claridad, por programa, por honestidad, por sinceridad, por ser capaz de representar todo lo que había estado ausente en el debate cara a cara anterior en esta campaña electoral. El derecho a la vivienda, la desigualdad, que los ricos paguen lo que les corresponde, la defensa de los servicios públicos, la defensa de los derechos de las mujeres frente a quienes vienen con sed de venganza a arrebatarle todo lo que se ha conquistado en las últimas décadas”, ha asegurado.

“Llevamos días diciendo que la campaña del Frente Amplio va a ser la sorpresa en este domingo electoral. Cada uno de los debates que ha habido, el debate económico, el debate a ocho, el debate contra García Albiol, el de ayer, los ha ganado el Frente Amplio. Los apoyos a nuestra candidatura se han multiplicado en los últimos días (…) El Frente Amplio va a ser la sorpresa este domingo y vamos a ganar las elecciones”, ha sostenido antes de asegurar que el debate puede haber ayudado a decantar el voto de los indecisos a favor de FA. “Hoy cerramos nuestra campaña en Madrid. Quiero hacer un llamamiento a que la gente venga, a que se haga partícipe de esta gran remontada épica que va a hacer que el resultado que parecía escrito en estas elecciones le demos la vuelta y que haya un gobierno de izquierdas en España”, ha animado Bustinduy sobre el mitin de cierre que se celebra a partir de las siete de la tarde en La Nave de Villaverde y en el que intervendrán cuatro ministros y habrá, además, actuaciones musicales.

World.title: “Y usted, calladita”: la polémica frase de Feijóo a Colau durante el debate
World.content:
La candidata de Frente Amplio reprocha al líder del PP que mantenga aforado a Mazón y este cuestiona que ella estuviera “calladita” cuando Sánchez “salió huyendo de Paiporta”. Feijóo amaga con retirar la frase, pero luego se reafirma

Nada más pronunciar la frase, la respuesta de Alberto Núñez Feijóo a Ada Colau en el último debate del 29-N sonó polémica. La líder de Frente Amplio había cuestionado que el candidato del PP mantenga aún hoy aforado al expresidente de la Generalitat Valenciana Carlos Mazón tras la dana de octubre de 2024. “Vergüenza, con más de 230 víctimas mortales y usted mantiene a Mazón aforado. ¿Cómo puede decir que eso es buena gestión? Más de 230 víctimas que aún están esperando justicia y reparación”, subrayó. Feijóo le contestaba de inmediato: “Buena gestión es ponerse al frente de una emergencia nacional y no salir huyendo de Paiporta. Y usted, calladita”, llevándose el dedo índice a la boca en posición vertical. Aunque se trata del gesto de pedir silencio, lo que el líder del PP le reprochaba es que no hubiera dicho nada entonces. Colau no estaba en el Gobierno y se había retirado del Ayuntamiento de Barcelona cuando ocurrió la dana.

El candidato del PSOE, Pedro Sánchez, reprochó enseguida a Feijóo sus palabras. “¿Por qué habla de calladita, señor Feijóo? Un poco de respeto”, le dijo a continuación. “Pero qué machismo es este, señor Feijóo”, añadió, a lo que el dirigente popular contestó: “Señor Sánchez, no manipule”.

01:59 Feijóo insiste en el "usted calladita" a Colau tras el debate

A la salida del debate, aparentemente molesto con las preguntas de los periodistas, Feijóo ha hecho un amago de disculparse. “Si he molestado a alguien, por supuesto lo retiro, pero ya está bien de hacer teatrillo”, ha dicho, deslizando que sus palabras se han sacado de contexto, porque no “mandó callar” a Colau, como ella misma le reprochó durante el debate. Aun así, el diminutivo y el gesto con que lo ha pronunciado han sido interpretados como un gesto de displicencia del líder del PP a Colau.

Al llegar a la sede del PP, sin embargo, Feijóo ha aparcado cualquier disculpa y se ha reafirmado. Ya en la sede de la calle Génova de Madrid, ante sus afiliados y simpaticantes, ha insistido, aunque hablando en esta ocasión de que “los de Sumar, el Frente Amplio, el Frente Estrecho o como se quieran llamar han estado calladitos y calladitas durante todos los años de corrupción”. Y ha insistido una y otra vez en que habían estado “calladitos y calladitas”, incluyendo así a hombres y mujeres, y tratando de conjurar las acusaciones de machismo. “¿Pero de verdad tan mal les ha salido el debate que lo que intentan es manipular?“, se ha quejado.

“Nada de ‘calladita’, señor Feijóo. No nos callaremos ni para pedir justicia y reparación a las víctimas de la inoperancia de Mazón, ni porque un hombre crea que pueda mandarnos a callar”, había escrito en la red social X Frente Amplio. La candidata de la coalición de izquierdas, en un turno posterior en el debate, le afeó su conducta: “Señor Feijóo: ya me ha llamado antes calladita, demostrando su feminismo. Dice que creció entre mujeres y le enseñaron, pero no le enseñaron mucho porque interrumpe mucho y encima me manda a callar”, le ha dicho la exalcaldesa de Barcelona.

Colau ha marcado perfil propio desde el arranque al recordar como primer punto a las víctimas de violencia machista, un asunto ausente en el cara a cara de hace una semana entre Sánchez y Feijóo. La líder de FA ha obligado al resto de aspirantes a posicionarse, una forma de retratar a Vox, que niega esta lacra.

A su llegada a la sede del PSOE, Pedro Sánchez también ha explotado la polémica. “Hemos visto a dos candidatos de la derecha y la ultraderecha que solamente insultan, que solo mienten, y que encima, aunque ya lo sabíamos, ha quedado bastante evidente para los ciudadanos y, especialmente, para las mujeres de este país, que son abiertamente machistas”, ha dicho.

“Uno no condena la violencia de género”, ha seguido, “y el otro manda a callar a las mujeres”, ha dicho en una interpretación muy forzada de la intervención de Feijóo que no se atenía al sentido de sus palabras. “Desde luego, no conocen a las mujeres. Callarse no se van a callar. El próximo domingo van a votar y van a expresar alto y claro que no quieren la involución que representan Feijóo y Abascal”, ha remachado.

World.title: ¿Quién ha ganado el debate? Los analistas de EL PAÍS se decantan por Ada Colau
World.content:
Siete expertos, cuatro mujeres y tres hombres, analizan para EL PAÍS las intervenciones de los candidatos del PP, Vox, PSOE y la candidata de Frente Amplio en el debate electoral celebrado este jueves. Valoran sus argumentos, la solidez de sus propuestas y su capacidad para defenderlas. Cristina Monge, Najat El Hachmi, Daniel Gascón, Jordi Amat, Máriam Martínez-Bascuñán, Diego S. Garrocho y Berna González Harbour ofrecen sus impresiones sobre los momentos que han marcado la noche.

Los analistas coinciden por unanimidad en señalar a Ada Colau como ganadora del debate. El encuentro se ha articulado en torno a cinco bloques temáticos: vivienda, economía y fiscalidad; política social y servicios públicos; corrupción y regeneración democrática; y, por último, migración y política exterior.

¿Qué candidato ha logrado destacar y qué balance hacen los expertos de las intervenciones?

World.title: “A otro perro con ese hueso”: Sánchez hace un giro de estrategia total y reactiva el ánimo de los suyos
World.content:
Pedro Sánchez es un político capaz de reinventarse varias veces, de cambiar de opinión otras tantas, de “hacer de la necesidad virtud”, como suele decir, y de dar un giro de 180 grados cuando las cosas no van bien. El debate a cuatro fue una especie de autoenmienda, un giro de estrategia completo tras el evidente fracaso en el cara a cara.

Sánchez cambió el tono de forma radical, volvió a parecerse a sí mismo, improvisó, interrumpió, salió al ataque contra Alberto Núñez Feijóo y Santiago Abascal, entró de verdad al debate, buscó golpes dialécticos y sacó toda la artillería que se había guardado de forma sorprendente la semana pasada, incluido el “aticazo” de Isabel Díaz Ayuso o el escaso inglés del líder del PP. Y se aferró además a un discurso nítidamente progresista, de defensa de los servicios públicos, en vez de focalizarse en esos mensajes al centro de la semana pasada.

Era exactamente lo que le reclamaban los suyos, muy frustrados por lo que consideran una oportunidad perdida en el cara a cara. Y rápidamente cambió el ambiente en el Gobierno y en el PSOE, y también en el Frente Amplio, entusiasmados con el papel de su candidata, Ada Colau. “Impresionante, los está vapuleando”, se entusiasmaba una persona cercana al presidente, que la semana pasada quedó muy frustrada y criticó en privado la estrategia del cara a cara y dijo que “salió a empatar y perdió”. “No hay color. Te puede no gustar Sánchez, pero está a años luz del resto”, señalaba un miembro del Gobierno.

La exalcaldesa de Barcelona también ayudó mucho a Sánchez, porque le lanzó algunas pullas buscando recuperar parte del voto que se le ha ido al PSOE, pero sobre todo se unía a él y le reforzaba en el combate dialéctico contra Feijóo y especialmente contra Abascal.

Los candidatos a la presidencia en el plató antes de que empezara el debate a cuatro. Claudio Álvarez

Sánchez buscó la sintonía con Colau igual que hace tres años la encontró en Yolanda Díaz en un debate igual a este, pero con la ausencia de Feijóo. Sobre todo cuando ambos intentaron que Abascal condenara la violencia machista, sin éxito. “Ada, no va a condenar la violencia de género, no merecen gobernar, y usted, señor Feijóo, pacta con los que no condenan”, le dijo Sánchez, al que ella llamaba “Pedro”.

En varios momentos, Sánchez y Colau hicieron una pinza a Feijóo, que estaba situado en medio de los dos, y se apoyaron para presionarlo, tanto que Abascal bromeó con que parecía que lo habían ensayado y el líder del PP se quejó: “Esto es dos contra uno”. Feijóo se inquietó con esa presión e incluso llegó a decir una palabra muy delicada que le lanzó a Colau: “Y usted, calladita”. Sánchez saltó inmediatamente: “Qué machismo es este, señor Feijóo, qué es esto de calladita, un poco de respeto”. Abascal había jugado también al límite: “Usted solo no se basta y necesita a esta señora”, le dijo a Sánchez.

Sánchez arrancó ya desde el principio de una manera completamente diferente a la semana pasada, directo contra el antisanchismo, hablando a la cámara. “Que no os confundan, estas elecciones no van de mí, van de vosotros, de vuestro empleo, de vuestro salario; no le demos a los de las motosierras el control de lo público. No le demos el Gobierno a los representantes de la internacional ultraderechista que ha hundido Argentina, que ha entrado en recesión”, lanzó.

Era evidente que Sánchez había cambiado por completo. “Es que es otro debate diferente”, se justificaban los suyos. Pero la realidad es que era otro político, mucho más parecido al de los mítines. “Hemos visto a Ayuso pagar su aticazo con el dinero de los madrileños. ¿Por qué no lo denuncia, señor Feijóo? ¿Tiene miedo de pasar como Casado a la historia del PP?“, le lanzó al jefe de la oposición, que no le contestó y se quedó con el golpe, como había hecho la semana pasada el líder del PSOE con casi todos los que le lanzaba su oponente. El presidente soltó toda la artillería, incluso las fotos de Feijóo con Marcial Dorado, condenado por narcotráfico.

Captura de la señal de la Academia de Televisión del debate a cuatro con los candidatos a la presidencia de Vox, PSOE, PP y Frente Amplio.

Sánchez llevaba golpes preparados como este, y se notaba mucho. Pero en ocasiones también improvisaba, algo que no se le suele dar bien y que esta vez sí logró. Especialmente cuando Abascal le lanzaba algún insulto. “Los ataques personales al reality. Esto es un debate, señor Abascal”, le lanzó. También Colau entró ahí a defenderle cuando el líder de Vox llamó “buitre” al presidente, negándose a normalizar el insulto.

El efecto de esa pinza era completamente diferente a los silencios constantes de Sánchez la semana pasada con los ataques de Feijóo. “A otro perro con ese hueso”, llegó a lanzarle a Abascal, bromeando con su apodo, Perro Sanxe. “No saben ni de lo que hablan”, le espetó en otra ocasión. “Las matemáticas del señor Feijoo son como su nivel de inglés”, le lanzó al líder popular. “Me conmueve ver a Feijóo y Abascal disfrazados de Robin Hood cuando han votado en contra de la subida de pensiones o se han posicionado en contra de la subida del salario mínimo”, remató en otro momento, en una secuencia clara de frases preparadas.

Sánchez y Colau también se unieron para hacer sufrir a Abascal porque ha cobrado el bono térmico y para explotar que su portavoz económico, José María Figaredo, ha hablado de un recorte de 112.000 millones. “Y le parece moderado”, se reía Sánchez, que esta vez parecía otra persona, mucho más cómodo, bromeando en ocasiones, con zascas preparados, pero sobre todo con una flexibilidad mucho mayor, entrando al debate y a la ofensiva. “Mucho patriota, pero aquí el único que hice la mili fui yo”, les soltó a Abascal y Feijóo. Entró a casi todo, también a inmigración, interrumpió y busca quedar por encima, al contrario que la semana pasada.

La sensación que deja el debate en el mundo progresista es completamente diferente. Sánchez sigue confiando en una movilización de última hora que dé la vuelta a las encuestas. Para eso necesitaba algo que cambiara el eje de la campaña. Ahora queda por ver si lo hizo este debate, que generó un entusiasmo en la izquierda que es mayor aún por el contraste con la decepción de la semana pasada y también porque llega en la recta final, a tres días de votar. Ahora todo está ya en manos de los ciudadanos; solo queda un cierre de campaña y la jornada clave del domingo.

Sánchez en Ferraz: “Los candidatos de la derecha y ultraderecha son abiertamente machistas”

Al son de Soltad a los perros de Arde Bogotá, Pedro Sánchez ha sido recibido con una gran algarabía por los 250 militantes y cuadros del partido que han seguido el debate en la sede del PSOE en Ferraz. Lo primero que el presidente ha hecho ha sido felicitar a la candidata de Frente Amplio, Ada Colau, “que ha hecho un magnífico debate”. Acto seguido ha compartido su alegría por haber hecho “un pedazo de debate”.

Sánchez considera que el bloque progresista ha ganado “por goleada” un debate a cuatro en el que se han contrapuesto dos modelos de sociedad de los que PSOE y Frente Amplio salen mejor parados que PP y Vox. “Los candidatos progresistas hemos reivindicado la buena política, la buena educación, y en frente hemos visto a dos candidatos de la derecha y la ultraderecha que solamente insultan, mienten y que encima, aunque ya lo sabíamos pero ha quedado bastante evidente para los ciudadanos y especialmente para las mujeres de este país, son abiertamente machistas”, ha recalcado. “Uno —en alusión a Abascal— no condena la violencia de género después de habérselo preguntado tanto Ada Colau como yo muchísimas veces a lo largo del debate. Y el otro —Feijóo— llama o manda callar a las mujeres. Los dos son tal para cual. Vamos, desde luego no conocen a las mujeres. Callarse no se van a callar el próximo domingo, van a votar y van a expresar alto y claro que no. Así que, bueno, yo desde luego después de este debate tengo claro que cada vez veo más cerca esa mayoría progresista el 29 de noviembre”, ha apostillado Sánchez.

El presidente ha animado a un último empujón tras agradecer el trabajo de la militancia. “La movilización que estamos viendo en la calle, en los actos, en las redes sociales, es maravillosa y eso también tiene mucho que ver con el trabajo que todos y todas hacéis desde aquí, en vuestras agrupaciones locales. Sois el corazón, el alma del Partido Socialista Obrero Español y yo quería agradecéroslo”. Y ha concluido instando a dejarse la piel “por convencer, por movilizar, por persuadir a los ciudadanos que todavía no tienen claro para votar progresista para que voten al PSOE”, ha finalizado. Informa José Marcos.

World.title: Feijóo salva el debate en medio del fuego cruzado contra su alianza con Abascal
World.content:
Alberto Núñez Feijóo salía con las expectativas muy altas después del cara a cara en el que se le dio por vencedor, y el debate a cuatro se reveló un formato mucho más incómodo para el candidato del PP. Feijóo trató de abrir brecha percutiendo contra Pedro Sánchez con la corrupción desde el primer momento, pero le costó más, en medio del fuego cruzado de los dos candidatos de la izquierda, Sánchez y Ada Colau, contra su socio, Santiago Abascal. El líder del PP también tuvo que encajar un dos contra uno por los ataques de los líderes del PSOE y Frente Amplio, que avanzaban coordinados. A diferencia de la izquierda, Feijóo y Abascal no se coordinaron en los ataques, aunque protagonizaron un debate de guante blanco entre sí. El desempeño del líder popular dejó más frío al PP, tras la euforia por el primero, aunque en las filas populares se le vio “sólido y bien”, y muy mal a Abascal. “Muy flojo Abascal. Ni suelto, ni solvente”, cuestionaba un barón del PP al líder de Vox.

El cambio de estrategia de Sánchez, que salió a la ofensiva y ayudado por Colau, también muy al ataque, puso en más problemas a Feijóo, que no pudo liderar el debate, como había conseguido en el cara a cara. Al candidato del PP se le vio acorralado en ocasiones por los dos líderes de la izquierda, sin que Abascal le ayudara. Tanto fue así que en uno de esos choques se escuchó a Feijóo decir: “Dos contra uno”. Y quejarse de que “tanto necesita el señor Sánchez a la señora Colau”.

En uno de esos enfrentamientos, Feijóo reprochó a Sánchez su actitud cuando visitó Paiporta tras la dana, y soltó a Colau que ella había estado “calladita”. El propio Sánchez y la candidata del Frente Amplio le reprocharon el “machismo” en esas formas al dirigirse a Colau. La expresión del “calladita” persiguió a Feijóo, que primero se disculpó nada más salir, pero después, preguntado de nuevo por los periodistas, optó por reafirmarse. “Si ha molestado a alguien, por supuesto lo retiro, pero basta ya de hacer teatrillo”, dijo a los periodistas saliendo del plató. Después, a su llegada a Génova, Feijóo cambió el paso y contestó a los medios: “Han estado calladitos y calladitas durante todo este tiempo. Lo reitero, no se puede callar ante la indecencia. Y la señora Colau, con todos los respetos, le digo que han estado calladitos con el Gobierno más corrupto”. Ante los militantes del PP en Génova, el líder popular volvió a referirse al incidente. “¿Tan mal les ha salido el debate que lo que intentan es manipular? Que vea toda la gente lo que he dicho", se quejó, visiblemente molesto.

El líder del PP llevaba un golpe de efecto preparado. Lo sacó a relucir cuando el presidente socialista le preguntó si iba a respetar el resultado electoral, sea cual sea, después de las insinuaciones de fraude que él mismo ha alentado. “Le subo la apuesta”, contraatacó Feijóo. “El que no presida el Gobierno asume la responsabilidad de dimitir, dejar el escaño y dejar el aforamiento. ¿Lo hará usted? Yo sí”. Por sorpresa, el líder del PP se comprometió a dimitir si no consigue alcanzar el poder este 29-N.

El presidente de Vox, Santiago Abascal, el presidente del Gobierno, Pedro Sánchez, el líder del PP, Alberto Núñez Feijóo y la candidata por Frente Amplio, Ada Colau. Claudio Álvarez

Génova había previsto reeditar la estrategia al ataque del cara a cara con Sánchez, y avisaba de que el objetivo de Feijóo iba a ser el candidato del PSOE, con el propósito de “hacerle sufrir”, y no el de Vox. El candidato del PP cumplió el guion y atacó sobre todo al líder socialista con la corrupción. Repitió, como en el cara a cara, la pregunta a Sánchez de “quién ha financiado sus primarias”, mencionó a “Jessica y Andrea” y advirtió al presidente de que “tenga cuidado” porque si él llega al Gobierno, “va a hacer una auditoría de arriba a abajo”. “Y tenga cuidado también Zapatero”, avisó. “¿Ustedes se apoyan entre sí o se están encubriendo?”, cargó contra los candidatos de la izquierda.

Feijóo obvió en cambio a Abascal y no entró al choque con el líder de Vox, a quien sabe que necesitará si hay suma para gobernar. El debate a cuatro suponía la primera vez que Feijóo y Abascal se veían frente a frente, porque el candidato del PP dejó la silla vacía en el de hace tres años. Y, de la misma forma que durante toda la campaña, evitaron los ataques mutuos y respetaron un acuerdo de no agresión para no desmoralizar a la derecha. A algunos dirigentes les inquietaba que el líder de Vox, que según los datos internos del PP ha ido perdiendo apoyos durante toda la campaña, pudiera hacer algún movimiento extraño para frenar su caída. No fue así y Abascal apenas buscó el cuerpo a cuerpo con Feijóo. Solo cuestionó su propuesta sobre el Mundial de fútbol, defendiendo que España no puede celebrarlo con Marruecos mientras Ceuta “siga invadida”.

En las filas populares se vio a Abascal “fatal”, “insultando y un poco fuera de lugar” y “sin saber defenderse” ante los ataques. “Creo que no están ni bien ni mal. Los debates múltiples son muy complejos”, analizaba un presidente del PP, reflejando la sensación de ni frío ni caliente que dejó el segundo duelo tras el entusiasmo por el primero.

World.title: Dutch destinations: an autumn getaway in Middelburg, Zeeland
World.content:
The Dutch flock to Zeeland in the summer to take advantage of the wide beaches, the seafood and hopefully the sunshine. But it is also a great location for an autumn or winter break, with the provincial capital Middelburg making the perfect base.

Middelburg, on the former island of Walcheren, can trace its history back to 880 and was awarded city rights in 1217, making it nearly 100 years older than Amsterdam.

In 1585 Middelburg opened its gates to refugees after the fall of Antwerp in the Eighty Years’ War with Spain, and the Flemish influence is still palpable in some of the architecture. In 1705 the first chocolate mill was set up on the outskirts of the city and its railway station opened in 1872.

Today its medieval centre is elegant, compact and well worth a wander around. Check out the names of the houses along the Rotterdamsekaai and the area around the magnificent Oostkerk, which now hosts concerts, and you will see plenty of testimonials to its past. We spotted an Edinburg and an Edenberg, a Groot Brittangie, a Spaerpot (piggy bank) and a strangely named “de twee harde Bollen” among the signage.

Five things to do

Stroll through the Abdij

Middelburg’s centre is dominated by its abbey, an impressive complex of buildings, with a garden, various towers and a wide, tree-filled square which is used to host cultural events. The abbey dates back to 1100 when the first parts were built by the Norbertine monks. Today it is home to the provincial council offices and the Zeeuws Museum. Note, the Lange Jan tower is closed to the public for the winter season.

Visit a museum

The Zeeuws Museum is one of our favourite provincial museums because it does not overwhelm you with information and is happily lacking in infotainment. The first two floors are devoted to temporary exhibitions and the third floor focuses on the history of the province. Carefully selected objects – children’s cloth caps, pottery, portraits of notables – nod to important stages in the city’s past.

The top floor has three “cabinets of curiosities” compiled from the museum’s collection such as the skeleton of a cat coupled with pottery moggies from 1850. It’s easy to cover the entire museum in a couple of hours.

Catch up on Christmas shopping

Middelburg has a main drag full of the brands you would expect, interspersed with local stores and a number of specialty outlets such as a store selling kites and juggler’s equipment. There are several chocolate specialists to choose from and wine shops selling local Zeeland wine.

For souvenirs, pick up some Zeeuwse bolus – a sticky spiral pastry with cinnamon and dark brown sugar or a packet of Boterbabbelaar, a buttery sort of toffee.

Walk in the woods

De Manteling is a coastal nature reserve near the seaside resort of Domburg, some 15 minutes’ drive from Middelburg. It is based around several former country estates, the main one of which is now a youth hostel. There are several routes to follow winding through the oak forest, and the blue one, which is four kilometres long, will take you out to the beach.

Visit Veere

Only 10 minutes from Middelburg by car, the village of Veere used to be open to the sea, and its wealth stems from its position as a major port in the wool trade with Scotland back in the 15th century. The splendid Schotse Huizen museum on the waterfront is well worth a visit and goes into this history in more detail. Veere gets very busy with coach parties in the summer.

Where to eat

Middelburg has masses of places to eat, and you would be advised to book if you plan to have dinner in one of the more highly-rated places. Lots of cafés and restaurants are based around the main market square, where you can get a burger, ribs or local fish. The Herberg is a favourite with the locals and offers more adventurous fare. You’ll find more choice on the Dam next to the abbey.

We had lunch at Brasserie 1600 which was pretty standard for a Dutch café lunch – croquettes on bread, warm goat’s cheese broodjes – but cheaper than the big cities and with friendlier staff.

In the evening we ate at the Packhuys on the Kinderdijk which offers an interesting seafood-based tasting menu of four to seven courses in a converted warehouse. Restaurant Scherp is in a city centre townhouse and also has two rooms where guests can stay. Basalt also comes highly recommended.

Where to stay

There are lots of options in Middelburg but you would do well to book up in plenty of time for your trip if you are coming at the weekend. It’s a popular place.

We stayed in a “city loft” in Hotel St Joris, which originally dates from 1582 and is close to the abbey walls, and paid €156 for the night including breakfast by booking directly. Ask for a room on the first two floors if you are not good with stairs. The nearby Poorthuys B&B comes highly recommended, as does the Zilver Reiger.

How to get there

It takes about two hours to reach Middelburg by car from Amsterdam, depending on the traffic, and there is plenty of parking on the edge of town. Inner city parking is pricey and nothing is far away on foot. There are regular trains from Amsterdam and The Hague, and you can pick up an OV-fiets (bike) at the station if you want to explore the countryside.

Anything else

When we were in Middelburg, in late November, the Stadhuis, or town hall, was wrapped in scaffolding as part of a major renovation project. The main market square had also been filled with an artificial ice rink and the café terraces had been turned into ski chalets for the winter season.

World.title: Prosecutors open investigation into neo-Nazi cage fights
World.content:
The prosecution service has begun an investigation into the neo-Nazi events that were exposed by a Zembla documentary last week, in which politicians, teachers and a health care professionals were seen attending cage fighting tournaments organised by extreme-right groups.

Since the documentary was released, which was based on an undercover investigation, six members of the far-right FVD have been expelled from the party.

A Rotterdam lecturer who acted as a medic, a high school teacher and a psychiatrist were also identified. The psychiatrist has also worked as an expert witness in judicial cases and previously had a firearms licence.

The footage shows members repeatedly throwing up Nazi salutes and shouting Sieg Heil, and members of one group holding an annual commemoration for Adolf Hitler in Luxembourg.

The former chief of the Dutch national intelligence agency AIVD, Rob Bertholee, told news programme Nieuwsuur that the groups and neo-Nazi symbols should be banned. The issue is that they were held as private events. Public displays of Nazi symbology can be punished in some cases.

Bertholee also said investigating connections between political parties and neo-Nazi organisations is complicated. Individuals can be held to account but investigating inherent links with entire political organisations, as some have called for with the FVD, would be sensitive.

A total ban would be easier said than done because of freedom of speech, he said, but he also voiced concerns that the far-right ideology is spreading throughout society. “We used to associate the far right with skinheads. We know now: people who adhere to this ideology look like anyone and can practice any profession.”

World.title: Abattoirs face closure for threatening and abusing inspectors
World.content:
Junior agriculture minister Silvio Erkens wants start shutting down slaughterhouses if inspectors are threatened there. This follows revelations recently that food safety authority workers are afraid to inspect some abattoirs because of the violence and intimidation they face.

Erkens told MPs during Wednesday’s debate on the agriculture budget that one option was a three-strikes principle, under which a slaughterhouse could be closed after, for example, three violations, broadcaster NOS reported.

“There should be no place in the Netherlands for slaughterhouses like this,” he said, though he did not name any particular culprits.

In the debate, Erkens said inspectors had reported intimidating phone calls, threats and being followed, sometimes by someone with a guard dog, and in some cases even into the toilet. Staff had also faced discrimination, physical aggression, and sexual intimidation, and some had been targeted in their private lives along with their families.

“It happens too often and too widely,” Erkens said, adding that these were not isolated incidents. He declined to name the slaughterhouses involved.

The NVWA can already halt slaughter at a plant until a problem is resolved. Erkens said that made sense for a single incident, but that a pattern called for a permanent solution.

MPs from left-wing PRO, the anti-immigration PVV, the Party for the Animals (PvdD), and centrist D66 had urged him the day before to take tougher action rather than rely on talks with the meat industry. Erkens said appealing to the sector had not worked.

He said he would set out early next year whether the legislation will go ahead and how it would work.

“A rebel with a strong cause.” That’s how prince Constantijn described Ghanaian artist and poet kąrî’kạchä seid’ou when presenting the Prince Claus Fund 2026 Impact Award on Thursday.

Set up in 1996 as a 70th birthday gift for the late husband of princess Beatrix, the fund awards international artists and creators in places “where cultural expression is under pressure”.

“Known for his radical and democratic approaches to artistic practice and teaching, seid’ou has been a key catalyst for artistic innovation in Ghana and across West Africa since the early 1990s,” the fund said.

According to NOS, seid’ou, who was born in 1968, does not believe that art needs to meet any conditions, and is less concerned with exhibitions or sales than with how artists are trained.

seid’ou travelled outside the African continent for the first time to accept his 50,000 euros during a ceremony in Amsterdam.

He “works with quiet discretion, preferring to remain out of the limelight while working from his base in Kumasi,” the fund said.

World.title: November set to be coldest in almost 30 years after record night
World.content:
This November is on course to be the coldest in the Netherlands since 1998, after many weather stations recorded their coldest November 27 night on record, broadcaster NOS reported on Friday.

The temperature in Twente dropped to -8.1° overnight, and 26 other stations also set a new cold record for the date, NOS said.

The month has had an unusually high number of frost nights. The normal November average is around 7°, according to weather forecaster Weerplaza.

Temperatures will stay around or just above freezing on Friday, with sunshine all day and a moderate easterly wind. In some places the temperature may not rise above zero at all.

The cold has made natural ice skating possible in several places. The first marathon on natural ice was held in Winterswijk on Thursday evening, won by Jade Groenewoud in the women’s race and Christiaan Haasjes in the men’s.

Friday night will be cold again, with lows of -4° to -7°. Temperatures will rise slightly on Saturday and there will be more cloud. Sunday will be wet, with highs of 2° to 5°, and the rain may start as wet snow.

A mural appeared on the outer wall of the Dutch embassy in Moscow on Thursday, depicting flying missiles with the words “flowers of Dutch diplomacy” written in their blast trail.

The mural, for which no one has claimed responsibility, appeared days after the dispute over Dutch defence company Destinus, who publicised the use of its weapons on the Crimea bridge.

The Russian embassy in The Hague was quick to respond that staff from the company may be considered legitimate military targets if so and asked if The Hague was “joining the conflict”.

A subsequent investigation by the NRC found that Destinus employees may have been personally engaging in drone battles.

Shortly after, the Dutch embassy in Kyiv was struck during a barrage of drone strikes. Whether the building was an intended target remains unclear.

Prime minister Rob Jetten said the Netherlands would not be intimidated by Russian threats.

The Russian embassy has lodged a formal request for clarification over the involvement of Destinus staff in the conflict.

Ajax, AZ and NEC all won their European matches on Thursday evening, with NEC moving into the Europa League’s automatic qualification places.

Ajax beat Swiss side FC Thun 4-0 at the Johan Cruijff Arena in the Conference League. It is the Amsterdam club’s third win in a row after an opening defeat at Hajduk Split, and it lifts them to third place for now, with other matches still being played.

The top eight after six rounds go straight through to the last 16.

AZ came back from 2-0 down at half-time to win 4-2 at Sparta Prague in the Europa League.

NEC beat French side Stade Rennais 3-1 at De Goffert in Nijmegen. NEC are now eighth in the Europa League table with 10 points, a position that would give them a direct place in the last 16.

The number of young people receiving benefits is up over last year, according to new figures by the Dutch statistics agency.

The CBS found that 43,000 people aged under 27 were on welfare at the end of September, an increase of 6.3% over 2025.

In the second quarter of 2026, the number of young people receiving assistance was also up, by 5.6%, compared to a year earlier.

The number of recipients also increased in the 27 to 45-year-old bracket, but only by 1.2% compared to a year earlier.

For those aged 45 to state pension age, the number of people receiving social benefits decreased by 0.1%.

Overall, 411,000 people were receiving a social assistance benefit at the end of September, an increase of 4,000 over 2025.

The government-backed judges who have taken control of Poland’s Constitutional Tribunal (TK) have issued a decision suspending chief justice Bogdan Święczkowski, who was appointed to the tribunal under the former government, for 12 months. The news was welcomed by justice minister Waldemar Żurek. However, Święczkowski has rejected the validity of the decision, saying that the “robed usurpers” currently claiming control over the TK are acting unlawfully. Sąd dyscyplinarny TK zawiesił Bogdana Święczkowskiego na 12 miesięcy za bezprawne blokowanie sędziów wybranych przez Sejm. Skończył się czas prywatnego folwarku, który chronił… — Waldemar Żurek (@w_zurek) November 26, 2026 The move marks the latest twist in a long-running battle for control over the TK, which dates back a decade to the unlawful appointment to the court of three judges under the former national-conservative Law and Justice (PiS) government. As a result, Tusk’s centrist government, which took power from PiS in 2023, had effectively ignored the court and its rulings until this year, when it began appointing new judges to fill a growing number of vacancies on the TK’s 15-person bench. However, opposition-aligned President Karol Nawrocki has refused to swear in five of the eight judges chosen by Tusk’s coalition in parliament, citing concerns over their qualifications or method of appointment. Events came to a head on 30 October, when those eight judges seized control of the court and announced that Święczkowski had been provisionally suspended for a month. Święczkowski, backed by Nawrocki and PiS, rejected their actions as an illegal “coup d’état” and maintains he is the rightful head of the court. On 3 November, the eight government-backed judges held their first general assembly. It was boycotted by the TK’s seven other judges, including Święczkowski, who were all appointed to the tribunal when PiS was in power. The general assembly approved moving forward with disciplinary proceedings against Święczkowski for alleged violations of his duties in leading the court, including refusing to accept the five judges chosen by parliament but whom Nawrocki has refused to swear in. On Thursday this week, the TK’s disciplinary court, made up of three government-backed judges, issued a decision to suspend Święczkowski for 12 months, saying that it would provide time for the disciplinary proceedings against Święczkowski to be fully resolved. A lawyer representing Święczkowski told the hearing that the disciplinary court was improperly convened, noting that two of the three judges had not sworn their oath before the president. He also said that the entire takeover of the TK and subsequent decisions made by it were unlawful, reports Gazeta Wyborcza. The International Commission of Jurists has criticised the takeover of Poland’s constitutional court, saying it “contravenes international standards on the independence of the judiciary” But it also criticised the president for refusing to swear in judges https://t.co/2kBv3GT20d — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) November 4, 2026 Święczkowski, who did not attend the hearing, afterwards condemned the entire process, calling the judges involved “usurpers dressed in robes” and saying that “the decisions of this body are illegal and have no legal effect”. He also argued that they had violated the basic judicial principle of judges not being permitted to rule on their own cases, given that the disciplinary proceedings against him concerned his refusal to accept judges not sworn in by Nawrocki, two of whom were on the disciplinary panel. The TK’s decision was, however, welcomed by Żurek, the justice minister, who said that it was another step in “the tribunal returning to serving the public” rather than being Święczkowski’s “private fiefdom”. However, Święczkowski’s position was effectively endorsed last week by the Supreme Court – a separate body from the TK – which issued a resolution stating that TK judges are only legitimate if sworn in by the president. The government has rejected the legitimacy of that resolution itself given that it was issued by Supreme Court judges who were themselves appointed unlawfully. Meanwhile, earlier this week the government moved to restore funding to the TK after its accounts were frozen at the central bank, whose governor, Adam Glapiński, was appointed under PiS and is a close associate of the party’s leader, Jarosław Kaczyński. World.title: Court overturns Warsaw mayor’s ban on protest outside Constitutional Tribunal
World.content: Keep our news free from paywalls by making a donation to support our work! A court has overturned the mayor of Warsaw’s decision to ban the ongoing demonstration taking place outside the Constitutional Tribunal (TK) in protest against the takeover of the TK by a group of government-backed judges. While the mayor, who is a deputy leader of Prime Minister Donald Tusk’s centrist Civic Coalition (KO) party, argued that the gathering threatened public safety, Warsaw’s district court found that banning it completely was too “radical” a step. Sąd uchylił decyzję stołecznego ratusza odmawiającą przedłużenia zgody na zgromadzenie pod TK#PAPinformacje pic.twitter.com/kBLm9kT9vc — Polska Agencja Prasowa/Polish Press Agency (PAP) (@PAPinformacje) November 26, 2026 Protesters have been present in front of the TK since mid-September, fearing that the government would make a move to take control of the tribunal from its chief justice, Bogdan Święczkowski, who was appointed to the court under the former national-conservative Law and Justice (PiS) government. On 30 October, a group of eight judges appointed to the TK this year by Tusk’s parliamentary majority – but five of whom opposition-aligned President Karol Nawrocki has refused to swear in – did indeed seize control of the tribunal and announced that Święczkowski had been suspended. They avoided the demonstrators who were blocking the tribunal’s main gate by entering through a side entrance that leads in from the prime minister’s chancellery. On Wednesday this week, city hall announced that mayor Rafał Trzaskowski had refused a request from the organiser of the protest for the public gathering in front of the TK to be allowed to continue from the end of November through to early January. The municipal authorities said that the demonstration had blocked the busy road outside the tribunal, thereby hindering access for emergency vehicles. They also pointed to a number of “dangerous incidents”, including aggression towards the police by participants in the protest. Such developments “have caused the gathering to lose its peaceful character”, wrote city hall. There are also “grounds to assume that the intention is, in effect, a long-term blockade of the entrance to the Constitutional Tribunal and the street itself”. The mayor’s decision was condemned by the opposition, with PiS party leader Jarosław Kaczyński calling it “authoritarianism in its purest form” and a “trampling of citizens’ constitutional rights” to freedom of assembly and speech. Warsaw's mayor, who is deputy leader of Poland's main ruling party, has refused permission for opposition protests outside the constitutional court to continue, saying they threaten public safety. The opposition has condemned the "authoritarian" decision https://t.co/b6fIsqXzDH — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) November 25, 2026 The organisers of the gathering had the right to appeal the decision within 24 hours, which they exercised. And late on Thursday, Warsaw’s district court announced that it had overturned Trzaskowski’s prohibition of the gathering. The information provided by city hall “does not provide grounds to assume that the assembly violates the rules for organising assemblies and may pose a threat to people’s life or health or to property to a significant extent”, found judge Anna Bonkowska-Kubek. “The court holds the view that the most radical measures in the form of a ban on demonstrations can only be applied in very exceptional cases, and the authorities must always first consider actions and decisions that would enable the peaceful holding of the planned assembly,” she added. A prohibition of a gathering “can only be applied in absolute exceptional circumstances, and the authorities must always first consider actions and decisions that would enable the peaceful holding of the planned assembly”, said the judge. Kolejni sędziowie nie chcą ochraniać nielegalnych decyzji polityków Koalicji Obywatelskiej, a tym samym żyrować ich swoim nazwiskiem. To… — Jarosław Kaczyński (@OficjalnyJK) November 26, 2026 The court’s ruling was welcomed by Kaczyński, who said that it showed how “judges are refusing to protect the illegal decisions of Civic Coalition politicians”. He called on supporters to join him for a further protest outside the TK at 3 p.m. on Sunday. However, Bonkowska-Kubek’s decision was questioned by Tusk’s justice minister, Waldemar Żurek. “I’m always a supporter of freedom of speech and the right to protest,” he told broadcaster RMF on Friday morning. “However, I would very much like the court to approach this rationally.” Żurek said that, due to the effective blockade of the TK by the demonstrators, it is not possible for people to exercise their right to file cases to the tribunal in person. Later on Friday morning, Trzaskowski announced that, while he “respects the court’s decision”, the city would exercise its right to issue a further appeal against Bonkowska-Kubek’s ruling. Blokowanie ulicy przez ponad miesiąc – nie. — Rafał Trzaskowski (@trzaskowski_) November 27, 2026 The legal situation at the TK itself remains under dispute. The group of eight government-backed judges have begun holding meetings and processing cases, including stripping Święczkowski of legal immunity to face criminal charges. However, Święczkowski and Nawrocki continue to insist that the actions of those judges are unlawful and that their decisions have no legal effect. World.title: Polish PM orders alternative financing channel for constitutional court after central bank freezes accounts
World.content: Keep our news free from paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. Prime Minister Donald Tusk has issued an order for the National Development Bank (BGK) to provide financing for the Constitutional Tribunal (TK) after Poland’s central bank froze the TK’s accounts following a disputed takeover of the court by government-backed judges. The relevant funds for the TK to function will be allocated by the finance ministry, announced government spokesman Adam Szłapka on Thursday morning, a day after the cabinet approved a resolution authorising the move. However, the ousted chief justice of the court has condemned the government’s actions as “completely unlawful” and said that they make the court’s current leadership “directly subordinate” to the prime minister. Premier @DonaldTusk wydał dyspozycję, by Bank Gospodarstwa Krajowego zapewniał finansowanie Trybunału Konstytucyjnego, a środki na ten cel zabezpieczy minister finansów. Państwo musi działać. — Adam Szłapka (@adamSzlapka) November 26, 2026 The move marks the latest twist in a long-running battle for control over the TK, which dates back around a decade to the unlawful appointment to the court of three judges under the former national-conservative Law and Justice (PiS) government. As a result, Tusk’s centrist government, which took power from PiS in 2023, had effectively ignored the court and its rulings until this year, when it began appointing new judges to fill a growing number of vacancies on the TK’s 15-person bench. Events came to a head on 30 October, when the eight judges appointed by Tusk’s majority in parliament – five of whom opposition-aligned President Karol Nawrocki has refused to swear in – seized control of the court. They announced that the chief justice, Bogdan Święczkowski, who was appointed under PiS, had been suspended. Święczkowski, backed by Nawrocki and PiS, rejected their actions as an illegal “coup d’état” and maintains he is the rightful head of the court. The disputed status of the TK’s leadership led the National Bank of Poland (NBP) to announce earlier this month that it had frozen all outgoing transfers from TK accounts. The central bank cited conflicting claims over who had the authority to manage the institution, saying it “has no authority to decide who is legally entitled to control the Constitutional Tribunal”. The NBP is led by Adam Glapiński, who was appointed under PiS and is a longtime associate of party leader Jarosław Kaczyński. Tusk’s government condemned the bank’s decision as politically motivated and pledged to find alternative ways of securing the tribunal’s finances. Meanwhile, both Święczkowski and Anna Korwin-Piątkowska, the government-backed judge who has assumed leadership of the court, each appealed to Glapiński to unblock the Constitutional Tribunal’s accounts and recognise their respective authority to manage the court’s funds. Poland’s central bank has frozen outgoing transfers from the bank accounts of the Constitutional Tribunal, citing conflicting claims over who has the authority to manage the court following a takeover by a group of judges backed by the government https://t.co/ZYkzoneojO — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) November 17, 2026 On Wednesday, the government adopted a resolution “on taking measures necessary to prevent a crisis situation related to the functioning of the Constitutional Tribunal” due to the NBP’s decision to freeze its accounts. “At a time when, after many years, an opportunity has arisen to overcome the constitutional crisis, restricting the Constitutional Tribunal’s ability to exercise its constitutional powers will negatively affect the level of legal certainty for individuals, including citizens,” the resolution reads. It requires the prime minister and finance minister to take “appropriate measures to protect the interests of the State Treasury and to ensure the state’s internal security and public order.” Szłapka subsequently announced that Tusk had instructed BGK, a state-owned development bank, to provide financing to the tribunal. The dispute around Poland's constitutional court risks entrenching a system of legal dualism in which judicial authority depends on political allegiance rather than broad constitutional consent, writes @AleksSzczerbiak https://t.co/mtgutqSTQh — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) November 10, 2026 Jan Grabiec, head of the prime minister’s chancellery, on Thursday morning told broadcaster TVN24 that the tribunal had an “auxiliary account” at BGK. This would allow its day-to-day operations to be financed despite the NBP’s decision to block payment orders, he added. “It is not just a matter of ordinary tribunal staff potentially not receiving their salaries,” said Grabiec. “The State Treasury also bears responsibility for contracts entered into by the tribunal’s previous leadership that include specific payment deadlines.” “This creates a liability for damages, potentially amounting to losses of many millions of zloty,” he added. “We cannot allow the State Treasury to be exposed to losses resulting from such politically motivated decisions of the National Bank of Poland.” The International Commission of Jurists has criticised the takeover of Poland’s constitutional court, saying it “contravenes international standards on the independence of the judiciary” But it also criticised the president for refusing to swear in judges https://t.co/2kBv3GT20d — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) November 4, 2026 On Thursday, Święczkowski condemned the government’s decision to channel money to the TK through BGK, calling it “completely unlawful”, reports the Dziennik Gazeta Prawna daily. “If this usurper Anna Korwin-Piotrowska accepts money from Tusk’s government, it will mean she is directly subordinate to Tusk,” he added. At the time of writing, the NBP had not publicly commented on the government’s decision to channel funding to the tribunal through BGK. BGK, meanwhile, told PAP that it could not comment on the details of its arrangements with other parties, citing banking secrecy. World.title: Warsaw hospital accused of offering “VIP access” for politicians fined 2.3 million zloty

The Warsaw hospital at the heart of a recent scandal over allegations that politically connected patients were given preferential treatment has been fined 2.3 million zloty (€520,000) after an investigation found that it admitted patients out of turn and doctors were absent during scheduled shifts. The doctor at the centre of the scandal, who was a local councillor for Poland’s main ruling party, was charged with fraud in October and is now also facing disciplinary proceedings over alleged breaches of medical ethics and professional standards. Niestety – Dawid K. jednak nie posiadł daru bilokacji, cudu nie było. Z ustaleń kontrolerów Narodowego Funduszu Zdrowia wynika, że po prostu oszukiwał. Ale to nie jest tylko sprawa jednego młodego medyka z legitymacją Koalicji Obywatelskiej w torbie. Cały ten przypadek wiele… pic.twitter.com/DfC35LLUpo — OficjalneZero (@OficjalneZero) November 26, 2026 The audit was conducted by the National Health Fund (NFZ), which finances public healthcare in Poland. It was carried out following a series of revelations in June by media outlets about alleged irregularities at the hospital. Many of the claims centred around a young doctor, who can be identified only as Dawid K. under Polish privacy law due to the criminal proceedings against him. He served as coordinator of emergency services at the Southern Hospital. News outlet Zero.pl was the first to report that the doctor, who also served as a local politician for the centrist Civic Coalition (KO) party that leads Poland’s ruling coalition, worked a seemingly impossible number of hours at four different hospitals and earned 1.6 million zloty last year alone. The website alleged that the doctor had declared shifts when he was actually not present and cited instances in which he reportedly appeared in local media during hours when he was officially listed as being on duty at the hospital. ❗️ Błyskawiczne przyjęcia, wykonywanie pakietów kilkunastu, a nawet kilkudziesięciu badań w bardzo krótkim czasie, możliwość przebywania w innym pomieszczeniu niż ogół pacjentów. W Warszawskim Szpitalu Południowym stworzono nieoficjalnie szybszą i bardziej komfortową ścieżkę… pic.twitter.com/3aanpRVeBu — Patryk Słowik (@PatrykSlowik) June 17, 2026 Over the following weeks, Zero.pl and two other news websites, Wirtualna Polska and Onet, revealed further alleged cases of huge salaries for some doctors and impropriety at the Southern Hospital, including preferential treatment for patients with political connections. This included claims that there was a “VIP lounge” in which patients with connections to KO were given more comfortable facilities than others and that such patients were often allowed to skip the queue and receive treatment more quickly. In its audit of the Southern Hospital, the NFZ found that certain patients had been admitted out of turn. Inspectors also identified cases in which patients in stable condition were admitted to the emergency department ahead of others whose health condition warranted more urgent attention. The NFZ also found that doctors were absent during scheduled shifts and and that medical services were sometimes provided by staff without the required qualifications. The audit raised further concerns about the appointment of an inexperienced doctor as the coordinator of the emergency department. In a statement published on Wednesday, the hospital acknowledged the NFZ’s fine but noted that it was a preliminary decision and that the hospital could submit objections. It said that its board was reviewing the details before deciding on its next steps. Poland’s health minister has unveiled a set of reforms intended to “rebuild trust” in public hospitals following a series of reports about exorbitant pay for some doctors and that politically connected patients could skip queues and use a "VIP lounge" https://t.co/pidAHxohc4 — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) July 8, 2026 After announcing the end of its audit, the NFZ noted that it would forward the findings to prosecutors who have been investigating reports of irregularities at Southern Hospital. Prosecutors last month charged Dawid K. with fraud, alleging that he submitted fraudulent or unreliable invoices to the hospital worth more than 583,000 zloty. He has pleaded not guilty. Prosecutors are also investigating other cases of alleged wrongdoing at the hospital. However, a spokesman last month said that the findings so far do not confirm reports of a “VIP lounge” at the hospital. Meanwhile, on Thursday, the spokesman for the National Chamber of Physicians (NIL), Poland’s medical professional body, announced that they had decided to bring disciplinary proceedings against Dawid K. The claims against him concern alleged improper performance of medical duties, breaches of professional ethics, and conduct that undermined public trust in the medical profession. Zgodnie z obietnicą przekazuję do wiadomości publicznej: Rzecznik Odpowiedzialności Zawodowej podjął decyzję o przedstawieniu zarzutów Dawidowi K. Dotyczą one rzetelności wykonywania zawodu, naruszenia etyki i podważenia zaufania do zawodu lekarza. Będziemy informować o… — Piotr Pisula (@PanPisula) November 26, 2026 In the wake of the allegations against him, Dawid K. resigned from his seat on the local council, left KO, and stopped working at the Southern Hospital. His former party also distanced itself from him. Jan Grabiec, the prime minister’s chief of staff and head of the KO in the Mazovia province, which includes Warsaw, told reporters in June that the scandal “has no connection to KO, but since he was a KO councillor, we will be all the more stringent in holding those responsible to account”. In July, the health minister, Jolanta Sobierańska-Grenda, unveiled a series of reforms intended to “rebuild trust” in the healthcare system. They include caps on doctors’ salaries, a requirement for them to work at least half their statutory working time at a designated hospital, and a new electronic waiting list system. Meanwhile, the mayor of Warsaw, Rafał Trzaskowski, who is also a deputy leader of KO, ordered a separate municipal audit of the hospital, which revealed a number of irregularities, including in relation to Dawid K.’s activities. It concluded with 44 recommendations that Trzaskowski said were being implemented. World.title: Poland plans no-fly zone on eastern border to aid downing of Russian missiles
World.content: Keep our news free from paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. Poland’s defence ministry has announced plans to establish a no-fly zone along the country’s eastern border with the aim of making it easier to shoot down Russian missiles and drones that violate Polish airspace. Meanwhile, foreign minister Radosław Sikorski has again suggested that Poland should be allowed to shoot down Russian missiles that are over Ukraine but heading towards the Polish border. However, the defence ministry acknowledged today that NATO is so far opposed to the idea. Wiceminister obrony Cezary Tomczyk zapowiedział wprowadzenie strefy zakazu lotów przy wschodniej granicy Polski. Jak poinformował minister Tomczyk, rozporządzenie trafiło do rządowego zespołu, strefa ma obejmować od kilkunastu do 50 kilometrów przy granicy wschodniej Polski i ma… pic.twitter.com/3xF68uNNRU — Dariusz Wiewiorka (@darekwiewiorka) November 25, 2026 Speaking on Wednesday at the opening of a new military satellite imaging centre, deputy defence minister Cezary Tomczyk announced that his department “will request the government to establish a no-fly zone on the country’s eastern border, to ensure Poland’s security”. Tomczyk acknowledged that, after three Russian missiles struck southeastearn Poland last Friday, NATO had offered support, including the deployment of an Airborne Warning and Control System (AWACS) to Poland. “But at the same time, the Polish military must do everything possible to protect our interests here and now,” he added. The defence ministry recently took one such step by allowing easier identification of objects that can be shot down, said Tomczyk. “The no-fly zone at the state border will be an additional factor supporting the operations of the Polish Air Force.” At a subsequent press briefing, Tomczyk provided more details of the plan. The proposed no-fly zone would stretch for a distance of between “a dozen or a few dozen kilometres from the border”, he said. “When a Polish fighter pilot knows that an aircraft is entering Polish airspace from Ukraine, is flying at a certain altitude and speed, is entering the no-fly zone and is detected on radar, this constitutes grounds for shooting down such an object…We will also urge NATO as a whole to establish such a rule on the eastern flank.” The deputy minister said that a relevant regulation had already been submitted and “will be processed in the coming weeks”. He expressed hope that the measures could be in place by the end of December or in early January. As well as last Friday’s missile strikes, on Monday this week a Russian drone entered Poland from Ukraine and spent a few minutes in Polish airspace. The Polish military had been authorised to fire upon it, but eventually did not do so after it turned back towards the border. Poland is changing the procedures under which its military can fire upon foreign aircraft, citing the "growing threat from Russia". Visual identification of targets will no longer be required, with other forms of data to be used instead https://t.co/foCWsBDazH — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) September 29, 2026 The government’s plans for a no-fly zone were, however, questioned by Mariusz Błaszczak, a former defence minister and now head of the parliamentary caucus of Law and Justice (PiS), the main opposition party. Błaszczak noted that current regulations already allow the introduction of a temporary no-fly zone. He suggested that what the government had announced was simply a “cosmetic measure” and asked what “real operational capabilities” it would provide to the military. Earlier on Wednesday, Bloomberg reported, based on unnamed sources, that Poland had, at a NATO meeting called on Monday to discuss last week’s Russian missile strikes in Poland, asked about the possibility of shooting down Russian missiles that are over Ukraine but heading towards NATO states. Asked about the issue, Tomczyk said that he could not confirm Bloomberg’s reporting, but noted that discussion of shooting down Russian missiles over Ukraine had been going on for months. “NATO is not in favour of this in any way,” said Tomczyk, quoted by broadcaster TVN. “If we want to make any decisions that concern the space over Ukraine, it must always be a decision of the entire NATO…Many months ago NATO decided that such a procedure was out of the question. And that’s where we stand now.” NATO has approved the deployment of an Airborne Warning and Control System to Poland in response to three Russian missiles striking Polish territory last week. Hours after the decision was announced, Poland’s airspace was again violated by a Russian drone https://t.co/gudQJsPlQ5 — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) November 24, 2026 On Wednesday morning, before Bloomberg’s report had been published, Sikorski, the foreign minister, was asked during an interview with Polskie Radio about the idea of shooting down missiles over Ukraine before they reached Poland. “A missile or drone approaching our airspace already poses a direct threat to us, so I believe that shooting [it] down over Ukraine at Ukraine’s request would fall within the definition of self-defence,” said Sikorski. However, he acknowledged that any such policy would need to be agreed by NATO. As far back as 2024, Poland proposed the idea of shooting down Russian missiles over Ukrainian territory. But it was rejected by NATO, whose then-secretary general, Jens Stoltenberg, said that it would risk NATO “becoming part of the conflict”. The mayor of Warsaw has refused permission for opposition protests outside the Constitutional Tribunal (TK), which was taken over last month by a group of government-backed judges, to continue. City hall, which is under the control of Poland’s main ruling party, the centrist Civic Coalition (KO), says that the demonstration threatens public safety. However, opposition figures have condemned the decision as “authoritarian” and one of the organisers of the protest has pledged to challenge it in court. Bum. Jest zakaz organizacji kolejnej manifestacji przed Trybunałem Konstytucyjnym.https://t.co/Ol8gQxC3A1 pic.twitter.com/bUqAkdojxe — Tomasz Skory (@TomaszSkory) November 25, 2026 On 30 October, a group of eight judges chosen this year by the government’s parliamentary majority – but five of whom opposition-aligned President Karol Nawrocki has refused to swear in – effectively took control of the TK. They declared that the tribunal’s chief justice, Bogdan Święczkowski, who was appointed under the former national-conservative Law and Justice (PiS) government, was suspended. Meanwhile, riot police surrounded the court and held back protesters, including Święczkowski himself. Since then, the demonstrators have maintained a constant presence outside the court, while Święczkowski has also periodically appeared. He and Nawrocki argue that the actions of the eight “usurper” judges are illegal and that Święczkowski remains chief justice. Given the ongoing demonstration in front of the court, the judges currently controlling the TK have used a separate entrance that leads in from the next-door chancellery of Prime Minister Donald Tusk. On Monday this week, Anna Korwin-Piotrowska, the judge who has declared herself acting head of the court, arranged a meeting with Warsaw’s mayor, Rafał Trzaskowski, and the commander of Warsaw police, Krzysztof Ogroński, to discuss the protest. She argued that, by preventing access to the tribunal, the demonstrators were “violating the constitutional and European standard of the right to a court”. On Wednesday morning, Warsaw city hall announced that Trzaskowski, who is a deputy leader of Tusk’s centrist KO party, had rejected a request for permission to continue the public assembly outside the TK from the end of November until January. ‼️ Rafał Trzaskowski zakazał zgromadzenia pod Trybunałem Konstytucyjnym! Protest trwa tam od września i dotyczy sporu o to, kto ma w TK zasiadać. W poniedziałek osoba podająca się za „Zastępującą Prezesa TK” zaprosiła ratusz i Policję, by „przywrócić” wstęp do Trybunału. Dwa… pic.twitter.com/a0EzqVzRDn — Magdalena Majkowska (@MagdaMajkowska) November 25, 2026 “While the freedom to organise and participate in peaceful assemblies constitutes a fundamental constitutional freedom, it is not unconditional,” wrote the municipal authorities. They noted that the current gathering outside the TK has been ongoing since 17 September (as protesters anticipated an attempted takeover of the court) and that the organisers had given assurances that they would not obstruct the roadway. In fact, tents, a television stage and other structures have blocked the road, wrote city hall. This “causes significant disruption for local residents” and “undoubtedly hinders emergency service vehicles, thereby threatening the life and health of residents”. The authorities also noted that, while the protests were initially peaceful, there had later been a number of “dangerous incidents”, including attempts to block vehicles from entering the TK and scuffles with police, which included throwing objects at officers, physical confrontations, verbal abuse and spitting. Such developments “have caused the gathering to lose its peaceful character”, wrote city hall. There are also “grounds to assume that the intention is, in effect, a long-term blockade of the entrance to the Constitutional Tribunal and the street itself”. One of the organisers of the protest, Adam Borowski, told Polsat News that it is a “lie” that they are preventing the TK from functioning properly. It is the judges “illegally occupying” the tribunal who are responsible, he said. Borowski announced that they would appeal against the city’s decision in court. They have 24 hours from the issuing of the decision in which to do so. PiS leader Jarosław Kaczyński, meanwhile, declared that the decision to ban the protest was “authoritarianism in its purest form…trampling citizens’ constitutional rights”. Russia has “categorically denied” that the three missiles which struck Poland last week were Russian and has accused Warsaw of seeking to “stoke anti-Russian sentiment” around the incident. Its remarks came after Poland’s foreign ministry on Tuesday summoned Russia’s ambassador, Georgy Mikhno, to present him with a protest over the missiles. Today, foreign minister Radosław Sikorski said that expelling the ambassador is “one of the options” Poland could take, though it remains unlikely. ⚡️Komentarz Ambasady Rosji w Polsce 24 listopada 2026 r. JE Pan Gieorgij Michno, Ambasador Federacji Rosyjskiej w Rzeczypospolitej Polskiej, został zaproszony do MSZ kraju przyjmującego, gdzie przekazano mu protest w ramach rzekomego „powiązania” naszego kraju z incydentami… pic.twitter.com/GUJB0RWZgt — Russian Embassy, PL (@rusemb_pl) November 24, 2026 On Friday morning last week, three objects struck at different locations in southeastern Poland, not far from the Ukrainian border, amid large-scale Russian attacks on Ukraine. Subsequently, on Monday night this week, a Russian drone entered Polish airspace from Ukraine and spent a few minutes above Poland before turning back into Ukraine. On Tuesday, Mikhno was summoned to the Polish foreign ministry, which said it had presented him with “a very strong diplomatic note” regarding the missile strikes. Afterwards, Mikhno read a statement to the media saying that “Russia categorically rejects the accusations of involvement in the incidents”, which were being made based on “political judgements and unsubstantiated assumptions”. He also condemned what he said was “openly Russophobic rhetoric around the incident”, which suggests “a desire to exploit the situation to further stoke anti-Russian sentiment”. The ambassador claimed that “no convincing and verifiable evidence has been presented” to establish the origin of the missiles. He then refused to answer journalists’ questions before leaving. Russia has installed an exhibition titled “Ten Centuries of Polish Russophobia” outside a cemetery for thousands of Poles murdered by the Soviets in the 1940 Katyn massacre. It opened just before Poland marked its annual day of remembrances for victims https://t.co/HcfmeNrerB — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) April 16, 2026 Mikhno’s claims were immediately rejected by the Polish foreign ministry’s spokesman, Maciej Wewiór, who said that it was “beyond dispute” that the missiles were Russian and that Moscow “knows [this] perfectly well”. On Sunday, Polish prosecutors said that the remains of the missiles leave no doubt they are Russian, and added that preliminary findings even indicate which specific factory they were manufactured in and when. A number of Poland’s NATO allies, as well as the alliance’s secretary general, Mark Rutte, have also condemned Russia over the missile incident and expressed solidarity with Warsaw. NATO has approved the deployment of an Airborne Warning and Control System to Poland in response to three Russian missiles striking Polish territory last week. Hours after the decision was announced, Poland’s airspace was again violated by a Russian drone https://t.co/gudQJsPlQ5 — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) November 24, 2026 On Wednesday morning, Sikorski was asked during an interview with Polskie Radio whether a “strong diplomatic note” was a strong enough response, given Russia’s repeated and continued hostile actions towards Poland. When it was put to the foreign minister that Poland should expel the Russian ambassador, Sikorski said that “this is one option” and “of course, it can be done”. However, he added that “we won’t pursue it yet” and noted that any such action would be met with an equivalent response from Moscow. In 2024 and 2025, Sikorski successively ordered Russia to close all of its consulates in Poland in response to Russian acts of sabotage. Moscow responded by shutting down all Polish consulates on its territory. 🗣️ "Czy jest sens rozmawiania z ambasadorem Rosji? To symboliczny gest pokazania dezaprobaty. World.title: Poland and US sign defence technology cooperation agreement
World.content: Keep our news free from paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. Poland and the United States have signed an agreement on defence research, development, testing and evaluation, concluding 17 years of negotiations and opening the way for deeper technological cooperation. The agreement establishes a framework for joint defence projects, as well as the exchange of technical data and expertise, giving Poland – which is already a major importer of US arms – a formal role in the development of American defence technologies for the first time. Under Secretary Emil Michael (@USWREMichael) and Mr. Cezary Tomczyk, Poland’s Secretary of State at the Ministry of National Defence, signed the Agreement Between the Government of the United States of America and the Government of the Republic of Poland for Defense Research,… pic.twitter.com/7EAgK3nD2i — Department of War CTO (@DoWCTO) November 23, 2026 The agreement was signed at the Pentagon by Poland’s deputy defence minister Cezary Tomczyk and US under secretary of war for research and engineering Emil Michael. According to the Department of War, the deal will help “turn research and development into validated military capabilities to jointly support US and Polish warfighters”. Tomczyk said the agreement would allow Polish universities, research institutes and companies to participate in joint research and development work on defence technology with US partners and would enable such technologies to be tailored more closely to the requirements of the Polish armed forces. During a briefing in Washington, Tomczyk admitted that the agreement had been negotiated for what he described as a “probably record-breaking” 17 years, but he noted a “significant acceleration in relations” between the US and Poland over the last six months. General Marcin Górka, who oversees innovation in the Polish armed forces and accompanied Tomczyk to the United States, likewise welcomed the agreement, which he said would “open the doors to American military laboratories for our scientists and engineers”. Górka also said the agreement would enable Poland and the United States to jointly develop anti-drone systems and advanced drones, with testing taking place in both countries. Poland is a major importer of US military hardware. Between 2021 and 2025, it was the biggest overall importer of arms in NATO, with around 44% of that equipment coming from the US, including F-35 fighter jets, Abrams tanks, Patriot air defence systems and HIMARS rocket launchers. But Poland has recently sought to move from being a client of the US defence industry to more of a partner. Earlier this month, Polish defence minister Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz and Secretary of War Pete Hegseth signed a declaration on expanding bilateral defence-industrial cooperation. Poland and the US have signed a statement of intent on strengthening defence industry cooperation. Polish defence minister @KosiniakKamysz said his country would be "the US ambassador in the EU", including seeking EU funds for jointly produced equipment https://t.co/SKHrxTEKIW — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) November 11, 2026 Last month, Poland was chosen as the location for a planned Patriot missile maintenance and servicing facility, the first of its kind outside the United States. In May, an agreement was signed to establish a centre in Poland for servicing the engines of Abrams tanks. This year, Polish state defence group PGZ was chosen as the first European producer of American Barracuda-500M cruise missiles, while US defence giant Northrop Grumman and Polish arms manufacturer Niewiadów-PGM announced plans to jointly produce artillery shells in Poland. Poland is also seeking to host a new permanent US military base, with Tomczyk reiterating during his Washington visit that a decision is expected from the Trump administration in early December. NATO has approved the deployment of an Airborne Warning and Control System to Poland in response to three Russian missiles striking Polish territory last week. Hours after the decision was announced, Poland’s airspace was again violated by a Russian drone https://t.co/gudQJsPlQ5 — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) November 24, 2026 The new agreement on defence technology was signed amid heightened tensions with Russia. On Friday, three Russian Kh-101 cruise missiles struck separate locations in southeastern Poland, near the Ukrainian border. Tomczyk said the Polish delegation had briefed Pentagon officials on the missile strikes, which he described as a “provocation” by Russia. The Polish minister was also asked about US President Donald Trump last week calling Russia’s Vladimir Putin his “friend”. “One thing is certain: Vladimir Putin is not our friend; he is a threat to us,” replied Tomczyk. “This is the most important message that should come from Poland and resonate with the people of the United States.” Subsequently, on Monday night, a Russian drone entered Polish airspace from Ukraine for a few minutes before turning back.
