World.title: PM Radev says EC’s proposal that Bulgaria be fined over excessive deficit is unfair
World.content:
Prime Minister Roumen Radev said on November 26 that European Commission’s proposal that Bulgaria be fined for its excessive budget deficit is unfair, given the country’s efforts to improve public finances and that other EU countries are also in an excessive deficit procedure but are failing to reduce it.

Radev, speaking to reporters on arrival for a special two-day meeting of the European Council said that Bulgaria was the first for which such a fine is proposed under the new European rules, and he described the reasons as procedural, not political.

“I see purely procedural reasons, because for the first time there is a change in the rules for sanctioning, and for the first time this is happening precisely with the arrival of the Bulgarian budget,” Radev said.

“Don’t forget that this is not a standard budget, it came in August. That’s how we found ourselves – the change in the political situation, the elections in April, a new government in May, a budget only at the end of July,” he said.

“So for the first time our budget encountered a change in the rules. And they are that the fines were much larger. Over 10 times larger and many countries before us had excessive deficits and they were sanctioned under this old procedure,” Radev said.

“But because it has a large ceiling on fines, it has never come to actual fining. Now the ceiling is very low, you know, 0.02 per cent. But we are the first country to come with an excessive deficit under these new rules.”

This fine is “symbolic” in financial terms, Radev said.

“But it is of course reputational and is used with great enthusiasm by the opposition in Sofia, which is actually the reason we got here.”

Under no circumstances will we fulfill the opposition’s nihilistic dreams of having European funds and payments under the Recovery and Resilience Plan stopped, he said.

“There is no question of this at all and it will definitely not happen. Because Bulgaria is very clearly implementing a strict financial policy in our face and this is appreciated. There can be no question of any suspension of EU funds. This is a standard procedure that was necessary due to an excessive deficit and exactly at the moment when our budget was released. So things are clear there.”

According to Radev, the European Commission gave a positive assessment of the government’s measures for the 2027 Budget.

“That is, the assessment of our Budget, which we are making for 2027, is positive and encouraging, that Bulgaria, with the measures taken in this budget, is already starting to significantly reduce its deficit,” Radev said.

“Otherwise, it is unfair, it is unfair, because we have the largest gradient of deficit reduction from 2026 to 2027. And I expect that there will still be reason here, because we should be encouraged for reducing the deficit with such a gradient, while there are other countries that simultaneously have an excessive deficit and fail to reduce it at all. The procedure will be activated for them next year as well.”

The European Commission must analyse its abilities to realistically assess the financial situation in the member states, Radev said.

“Why did the European Commission suddenly find that Bulgaria has such an excessive deficit?” he said.

“How did it suddenly find that we have macroeconomic imbalances? But excuse me, these macroeconomic imbalances do not happen in three months, nor in six months. They accumulate over years.

“How did the Commission now find out that budget funds are being spent indiscriminately in Bulgaria, without the necessary control? How did Bulgaria suddenly, in April and May of last year, lower its inflation enough for the convergence report to be published,” he said.

“And in August, inflation again went beyond any criteria. There are things here that the European Commission must analyse in terms of its ability to realistically assess the financial situation in the member states. If it does not do so, it means that there are political motives, not economic ones, behind our admission to the euro zone.”

Radev commented on what Bulgaria’s position will be in discussing the EU budget.

“There are three important pillars of our demands,” he said.

“First of all, we must not back down from cohesion, we know that this is the main instrument for the unity of the union, for the economic development of the union.

“Second, we insist on clear financial support for the Black Sea region, and not just mentioning it. We all know how much countries like Bulgaria and Romania are involved in the actions in the Black Sea, especially with the attacks on merchant ships,” he said.

“These are significant costs for us and they must be taken into account. Next, this is the refusal of own resources based on the European emissions trading system and tobacco excise duties. For us, this approach is unacceptable because it harms Bulgaria disproportionately. These are our lines of action under this budget.”

“What we are negotiating with President Antonio Costa is a plus for Bulgaria. At least as far as our income in the European budget is concerned. And the amount is not small at all, so I really hope we can find a good balance that will benefit our country.”

He was skeptical that an understanding will be reached on November 26.

“There are many contradictions that we need to iron out. But I rely on the will and responsibility of all member states so that we can reach a consensus. Our view is that the budget must be achieved within this year. So that from 2028 we can already work on this new financial framework.”

Bulgaria wants to implement a new approach to the Ukrainian loan, as Bulgaria is ready to be included in the budget for non-military support, Radev said.

“I want there to be a very clear difference between Bulgaria and Czechia, Slovakia and Hungary. Czechia, Slovakia and Hungary have refused from the very beginning and are not part of the countries that guarantee this loan. From the very beginning. Both 2025 and 2026. They said ‘no’ from the very beginning and are not.”

“While the government of Zhelyazkov and then confirmed by the government of Gyurov, we have so far been guarantors of two loans – 45 billion from last year, 45 billion from this year,” he said.

“That is, Bulgaria has already undertaken to be a guarantor for a loan of 90 billion and we pay the interest within the framework of the general European budget on these loans,” Radev said.

“The question is from now on for next year, the request for another 45 billion for a loan. At our explicit insistence, and I am glad that this is already being accepted by the European institutions and by Antonio Costa, we will also talk today with Mrs. Von der Leyen, but she has already expressed support for our position that this loan is divided into two components.

Twenty-five billion euro goes to military support and 20 billion for budgetary non-military support, he said.

“We are ready to join in non-military support and with a clear request that our support as guarantors go specifically targeted to the areas with a compact Bulgarian population from our historical community,” he said.

“We have over 300 000 Bulgarians in Ukraine. They need healthcare, they need heating, electricity, transport, so I hope the European Commission will accept our approach, which we will insist on, because we, on the other hand, cannot abdicate from our obligations as a state and as a society to our historical diaspora, to our compatriots in Ukraine.”

Radev also commented on the EC’s request to ban Russian athletes from participating in competitions in Europe, as part of the proposed 22nd package of sanctions against Moscow.

“Not just about athletes. We’re also talking about tourism related to sports events and activities, even cultural events. And I think we’re going too far to politicise sports and cultural events in this way. So we have our reservations there,” Radev said.

World.title: Bulgarian Parliament approves draft 2027 Budget package at first reading
World.content:
Bulgaria’s National Assembly passed the 2027 Budget Act at first reading late on November 25, with 126 MPs from Prime Minister Roumen Radev’s ruling Progressive Bulgaria group in favour and 81 opposed.

Earlier in the day, MPs also approved at first reading the health care and pensions budgets, which are separate from state budget and part of the Budget package.

Given Progressive Bulgaria’s majority of 131 MPs in the 240-seat National Assembly, the Budget is expected to pass without much difficulty well before the end of the calendar year 2026.

If that is indeed the case, it would be a rather rare occurrence in Bulgaria’s most recent parliamentary history, where political instability resulted in eight elections in five years, producing short-lived parliaments that often adopted budgets very late. Of the last five Budget packages, only the 2024 Budget Act was passed before the end of the previous calendar year.

The 2027 Budget package tabled by the Cabinet envisions a consolidated fiscal programme with revenues of 51.07 billion euro and 55.97 billion euro in spending, with a target deficit estimated of 4.91 billion euro in real terms, or 3.5 per cent of gross domestic product (on a cash basis, rising to 4.2 per cent with additional defence spending).

The economic growth target set in the Budget is 2.5 per cent and sets the debt ceiling at 44.4 billion euro, with the government allowed to issue 8.6 billion euro in new debt in 2027.

World.title: PM Radev, Finance Ministry, try to shift blame as Bulgaria faces possible fine over excessive deficit
World.content:
Prime Minister Roumen Radev and his Finance Ministry have tried to shift blame on to previous governments as Bulgaria faces a possible fine because of its inaction to address the excessive deficit.

Radev’s comments at a November 25 regular meeting of the Cabinet came nine days after he told his ministers to stop blaming previous governments.

The Bulgarian government information service quoted Radev as telling the November 25 meeting: “Yesterday, the European Commission slapped a resounding slap on everyone who over the years spent recklessly without attracting investments, who borrowed without developing the economy, lied about the real deficit to get us into the euro zone, and led the finances to an excessive deficit and catastrophe”.

According to Radev, the European Commission’s good forecast for next year “is a clear confirmation that the course taken by the government to restore state finances is correct”.

“So we will not fulfill the nihilistic dreams of the opposition to stop our European funding and payments under the RRP (Recovery and Resilience Plan),” Radev said.

Radev said that the government “will continue with the reforms and the elimination of inherited inefficient and corrupt practices in public enterprises”.

“Since the beginning of the year, foreign direct investment has increased by more than 100 per cent, and this percentage is increasing even more,” he said (In fact, going by Bulgarian National Bank data, as reported by The Sofia Globe, the increase in FDI in January – September 2026 is about 66 per cent on an annual basis).

A statement by the Finance Ministry on November 24, when the European Commission announced its recommendation that Bulgaria should be fined, offered similar arguments.

“Today’s assessment by the European Commission (EC)—part of the European Semester’s Autumn Package—points to a significant deviation from the recommended trajectory for net expenditure for 2026, as well as the risk of sanctions for failing to comply with the Council’s recommendation of July 10 2026,” the Finance Ministry said.

“This situation is a direct consequence of accumulated systemic problems and the political crisis of recent years—issues for which all political forces bear shared responsibility,” the ministry said.



According to the Finance Ministry “it is important to clarify that such a sanction has no bearing on the fifth payment under the Recovery and Resilience Plan, nor is it expected to block funds from European sources”.

“The government will continue to restore the state’s financial stability, while strictly safeguarding key social commitments, support for vulnerable groups, and predictability for citizens and public services,” the ministry said.

“The responsibility now lies with the National Assembly—we expect all political parties to demonstrate statesmanship during the adoption and implementation of the 2027 Budget, so that the flawed practices leading to EU sanctions may be consigned to the past once and for all,” it said.

Of the eight governments that Bulgaria had between January 2017 and January 2026, while Radev was president, he appointed four as interim administrations. Of those four, one was in office for 308 days, from 2022 to 2023. It was headed by Gulub Donev, who currently is Radev’s Finance Minister.

Assen Vassilev, leader of opposition party We Continue the Change and a former finance minister, alleged that Radev was lying, saying that the evidence was in the reports of the European Commission on the economy and finances of Bulgaria in the years before 2026.

Vassilev said that the European Commission report clearly states that the 2026 Budget is the one with a problematic deficit.

This budget was written by the Radev Cabinet and adopted by the Progressive Bulgaria MPs – even though the opposition in the form of We Continue the Change and Democratic Bulgaria had warned that it could lead to European sanctions for refusing to optimise spending.

“If there weren’t 1.5 billion euro more for expenses to support the administration, we could easily have a 4.1 per cent deficit, which with the derogation for military spending would have allowed us not to enter an excessive deficit procedure,” Vassilev said.

The derogation to which he was referring is an EU decision that allows a deficit above the three per cent ceiling in the euro zone if the expenditure that leads to it is in the field of defence. The exception is due to the threat to European security from Russia and the war it is waging in Ukraine.

The European Commission said that it also has concerns about the draft Budget for 2027 and will monitor Bulgarian finances closely in the first six months after January 1 due to the risks facing the economy.

Vassilev said that the European Commission’s reports on Bulgaria for each year are public and none of them have mentioned an excessive deficit or a problem with the financial framework.

So far, Bulgaria has not been sanctioned for unbalanced finances, as the Commission is now threatening.

Vassilev said that next year’s Budget, currently at first-reading stage in Parliament, is “even worse” than the criticised Budget 2026, because “it hits the foundation of the economy, investments and consumption and will bring us a recession”.

He again called for the draft Budget to be withdrawn by the Finance Ministry and revised. And for a new version to be submitted “by different Finance Minister”.

(Photo: government.bg)

World.title: European Parliament approves 2027 EU budget
World.content:
In a vote on November 25, the European Parliament gave its final greenlight to the last annual budget of the 2021-2027 EU long-term budget framework.

In the 720-member European Parliament, the 2027 budget was adopted by 406 votes to 184, with 69 abstentions.

In a deal reached on November 11, the European Parliament and member state governments agreed to set the overall level of commitment appropriations (legal promises to pay in the same year or later) at 199.7 billion euro, and payment appropriations (actual payments made to beneficiaries) at 211.5 billion euro.

In commitment appropriations, this sets the 2027 budget at 0.99 per cent of the EU’s gross national income (GNI).

The European Parliament secured an additional 300 million euro for its priorities compared to the European Commission’s proposal, boosting investment in research, transport and energy networks, Erasmus+, civil protection, border management, military mobility, the EU’s neighbourhood, and humanitarian aid. The deal also includes stronger cybersecurity and security capabilities for the EU institutions and delegations.

Key increases compared with the European Commission’s proposal include 39 million euro for the EU’s Southern and Eastern Neighbourhood, 30 million euro for humanitarian aid and 30 million euro for border management and migration.

MEPs secured more research funding through Horizon Europe with 21.5 million euro extra, and for transport and energy networks an additional 22.5 million euro.

For education, the Erasmus+ programme receives an additional 14 million euro and the civil protection mechanism is reinforced by 13.5 million euro.

Further increases support military mobility (10 million euro), and climate and environmental action (10 million euro).

The 4.9 billion euro NextGenerationEU over-run costs are to be dealt with as agreed previously through a “cascade mechanism”, designed to manage the borrowing costs and protect flagship programmes.

The amount allocated to servicing the Ukraine Support Loan debt is set at 650 million euro, in line with the European Commission’s proposal.

The European Parliament, Council and Commission have also acknowledged in a joint statement the possibility of covering the loan’s debt service costs by mobilising the Ukraine Support Loan special instrument in 2027.

As The Sofia Globe reported previously, the Council of the European Union formally adopted on November 23 the EU’s budget for 2027.

World.title: Vukovar Resolution: We Know Who in Serbia Has Information on Missing Persons
World.content:
November the 27th, 2026 – The Vukovar Resolution was formally adopted yesterday, and now the focus is who exactly in Serbia has information on those still listed as missing.

The European Parliament has adopted a resolution marking the 35th anniversary of the fall and destruction of Vukovar. Index reports that the document pays tribute to the victims, condemns the glorification of war criminals and calls on Serbia to open its archives in order to clarify the fate of the missing. The resolution, however, has drawn opposition from the Student Movement that is taking power in Serbia, instead of serving as an incentive for confronting the past. The topic was discussed on HRT’s programme Otvoreno.

what does the vukovar resolution actually mean?

MEP Karlo Ressler (HDZ) said that this was a cross-party initiative supported by all Croatian MEPs. “That was a precondition for broad support from all European colleagues. Thirty-five years after the fall of Vukovar it was important to speak about this openly in the European Parliament,” he said. He believes the main goals of the resolution have been achieved.

“I think we’ve achieved the main tasks with this resolution, and they concern conveying the message that Vukovar is a symbol of the resistance of a small number of defenders against a superior aggressor. We pay tribute to all Croatian defenders and all civilian victims, but we also open the issues of the missing and other questions arising from the Homeland War,” Ressler stated. He added that the resolution calls on the Serbian authorities to prevent the glorification of convicted war criminals. “The state funeral of Ratko Mladić is explicitly mentioned, but the horrific crimes at Ovčara are also clearly mentioned. The camps to which Croatian defenders were taken are named,” Ressler said. He emphasised that it is important to speak about Vukovar on the basis of clear historical facts. “Vukovar is a topic that unites us in Croatia, but it also has strong lessons for the entire European continent,” he concluded.

“serbia isn’t providing useful information”

Croatia is still searching for 1,725 people, of whom 320 are from the Vukovar area. Ana Filko, director of the Directorate for Detained and Missing Persons at the Ministry of Croatian Veterans, stated that Croatia has to date received no content-wise usable information from Serbia for finding the missing.

“We’ve identified concrete documentation. We’ve identified specific units, mainly rear engineering units that participated in the sanitation or concealment of graves. We’ve also identified which persons are located in the territory of Serbia and who may have that knowledge. We have forwarded that knowledge to the Serbian commission, but we have not received a concrete response,” Filko explained. She stressed that a “vow of silence” is one of the key problems in the search for the missing. “It is linked to the fact that these persons are not prepared to give information out of fear of a certain retaliation from the Serbian side, but also to the fact that finding the missing is linked to uncovering the crime committed,” she said.

Filko added that Croatia does not depend on Serbia in the search, as the results show. In the past ten years, 343 missing persons have been identified without any help from Serbia. “They could speed up the process in order to alleviate the agony of the families. We cannot change the past, but we can influence the future of every family. We will not give up until we find the last missing person,” she said.

Nataša Kandić, founder of the Humanitarian Law Centre, believes that an important message is at the end of the resolution, but that it communicates poorly with everything that was said before. Ressler replied to her: “We wanted to achieve that we are clear, that we do not speak about the suffering of Vukovar in abstract, general terms. We speak about murders, rapes, the persecution of the Croatian population after the occupation of the city, we speak about the causes of the war. It is important that 35 years after Vukovar there is no relativisation around this and we are now trying to weave it into the common European memory.” The resolution also mentions Boris Tadić’s visit to Ovčara in 2010, when he apologised for the crimes. Kandić said that this apology remains forever.

“That is recognition of how much the crimes and the destruction of Vukovar are a shame that belongs not only to the JNA but also to the citizens of Serbia who were mobilised, who were taken, many against their will,” Kandić said. She added that she would have liked the paragraph on joint responsibility to have been expanded in the resolution and for all countries to come together.

a call to serbia’s new government

Sandra Rapčak Škomrlj, president of the Association of Children of Fallen and Missing Croatian Defenders of the Homeland War, said that the mere change of power in Serbia does not mean a change of rhetoric. “We know that they rebelled when they found out about the resolution.

The new authorities must be aware that without resolving the past we cannot build the future,” she said and called on the Serbian authorities to cooperate. “Someone must answer for the war crimes committed. I call on them to bring those who committed the crimes to justice, to open the military archives so that they can provide information about the missing, and not for future generations to take on the burden of the past,” Rapčak Škomrlj stated.

Through the association, families have for years been filing lawsuits for the payment of war reparations from Serbia. More than 20 lawsuits have been filed and war reparations have been paid, while some proceedings are still ongoing. “We invite all those whose loved ones were killed and identified at Ovčara to contact us if they wish to file a lawsuit,” she said.

World.title: €100 Million Investment for New Jadrolinija Fleet Launched
World.content:
November the 27th, 2026 – A €100 euro investment for a new Jadrolinija fleet has now been launched, with 10 brand new vessels planned.

Part of the tenders for the construction of new ships has already been published and is in the implementation phase. Sinisa Malus reports for Poslovni that the Minister of Maritime Affaits, Transport and Infrastructure Oleg Butković stated this week that the recapitalisation of Jadrolinija is now ready. He added that the accompanying contracts will soon be signed for the implementation of the shore power supply system for ships at the Brajdica and Zagrebačka obala container terminals in Rijeka.

fleet modernisation

“Jadrolinija is going into recapitalisation, that is ready. We are going in two directions – with the recapitalisation of Jadrolinija and with the World Bank. Part of the tenders for the construction of new ships has already been published and is in the implementation phase, so Jadrolinija expects to sign contracts for the construction of new ships next year,” Butković revealed. Unofficially, it has been learn edthat the recapitalisation of Jadrolinija should be worth up to €100 million. It is closely linked to modernisation and should secure Jadrolinija’s financial position until 2043. It is a combination of different sources. Jadrolinija Management Board President Robert Blažinović revealed to us that the tenders should be published by the end of November.

“I think that within the next ten days or so we will also proceed to contracting the construction of the first ship,” Blažinović told us. This was preceded by a competitive procedure with negotiations for construction and design. Jadrolinija’s strategy of building ships with alternative propulsion and electric propulsion is well known, and the locations where they will sail have been determined in advance – the Šibenik, Zadar and Dubrovnik areas. The ships with alternative and electric propulsion will sail in the waters around Šibenik, Zadar and Dubrovnik.

alternative fuel vessels

Blažinović revealed that the Ministry of Transport has established very active cooperation with the World Bank and the International Finance Corporation (IFC). It has been known for some time that the company has a mandate letter with the IFC, which is working with Jadrolinija on preparing a sustainable financing model for the fleet renewal programme, as well as on assessing projects from the financial, technical, environmental and organisational aspects. We’re talking about a programme that can cover up to ten new ships and represents one of the largest investment phases in the recent history of this state-owned company. At the same time, the possibility of co-financing from EU funds in the segment of green technologies is also opening up, where maximum co-financing can be secured.

“The new ships should bring greater energy efficiency, reliability and comfort, with capacities adapted to the needs of individual lines. At the same time, we must continue investing in the existing fleet, digitalisation and the knowledge of our employees in order to maintain a leading position in maritime passenger transport and continue building the trust of passengers that we have been gaining for eight decades. The greatest challenge will be to align the scope of the necessary investments with the financial sustainability of operations. The green transition requires significant capital, but its implementation also depends on the availability of alternative fuels and the development of appropriate infrastructure. Jadrolinija must be business-efficient and competitive while at the same time ensuring the connectivity on which the daily life of islanders, the local economy and tourism depend. Our transformation is therefore part of a broader development strategy,” Robert Blažinović concluded.

World.title: New Pension Increases Announced for Croatian Retirees in 2027
World.content:
November the 27th, 2026 – Further pension increases have been announced for Croatian retirees in 2027, commenting on their previous growth and on the economy.

Prime Minister Andrej Plenković commented on the growth of pensions and the societal position of pensioners, emphasising that both wages and pensions have risen in the recent period, and announced additional changes that come into force from 2027. Poslovni reports that Croatia will apparently achieve economic growth of around 2.4 percent this year. During the terms of the current Government, absolute GDP has increased from €47 billion to €101 billion. Today, 1.76 million people are employed in Croatia, while the number of unemployed is around 70,000.

Plenković emphasised that as of the 1st of January 2027, the payment of income tax by pensioners is being abolished, which will further increase pensions for more than 540,000 pensioners. In November, 571,945 pensioners paid almost €20 million in tax into the budgets of cities and municipalities, or an average of €34.62 per pensioner. The opposition has warned that by tax relief for some pensioners the Croatian Government will shift the cost onto local budgets.

The state budget for 2027, presented in the Croatian Parliament, according to the Prime Minister’s words also has an important role in preserving social cohesion. The Government plans to allocate around €11 billion for pensions, which is €875 million more than this year.

wage growth will be reflected in pension growth

Plenković recalled that in recent years, Croatia has faced major external shocks and crises, as well as the devastating earthquakes in Zagreb and Banovina. €5.3 billion has so far been allocated for reconstruction. Croatia has recorded 22 consecutive quarters of economic growth, and projections for next year envisage growth of 2.1 percent. A budget deficit of 2.9 percent and a slowdown in inflation to 2.7 percent on an annual basis are also expected. Such trends should enable further growth in the wages of employees in public services, agreed with the trade unions. The wage base will increase by three percent as of the 1st of January 2027, and as of the 1st of April a meal allowance of €30 is being introduced. This will be followed by an additional one-percent increase in the base from 1 August and an increase in the meal allowance by a further €20 as of the 1st of October. Wage growth in the public sector will also be reflected in pensions through their regular adjustment.

World.title: Croatia Can Expect €15.9 Billion in Revenue From Tourism
World.content:
November the 27th, 2026 – Croatia can expect to bring in €15.9 billion in revenue from tourism alone, with the prime minister discussing the second most important visitors.

Croatia should finish this year with slightly better tourism results than it recorded last year, and the value of fiscalised invoices is growing significantly faster than the number of invoices issued. Croatia should end 2026 with approximately €15.9 billion in tourism revenue, around 22 million tourist arrivals and 110 million overnight stays, Prime Minister Andrej Plenković stated on this week at a government session.

Reflecting on the results presented during last week’s Days of Croatian Tourism (Dani hrvatskog turizma) in Poreč, the Prime Minister emphasised that positive movements were recorded this year both in arrivals and overnight stays, as well as in the value of tourist spending. According to the data presented at that event, during the first ten months 21.3 million arrivals and 109 million overnight stays were recorded, representing growth of two percent in arrivals and one percent in overnight stays compared with the same period last year.

an 18% increase in fiscalised invoices in tourism

Particularly notable is the growth in the value of fiscalised invoices in the tourism sector. In the first ten months of the year, invoices worth approximately €8.6 billion were fiscalised, which is 18 percent more than in the same period of 2025. At the same time, around 410.4 million invoices were issued, or six percent more than last year. The value of invoices is thus growing significantly faster than their number, which points to an increase in the average fiscalised amount. A distinction should be made here between fiscalised turnover and revenue from foreign tourists, which is recorded separately in the statistics of the Croatian National Bank.

croatian tourists are now right behind the germans

Plenković particularly singled out the importance of domestic guests for Croatian tourism. According to him, Croatian tourists occupy second place among the most important tourist markets, right behind guests from Germany. Data presented at the Days of Croatian Tourism show that domestic guests recorded approximately 3.1 million arrivals and 13.6 million overnight stays this year. The Prime Minister also emphasised the importance of further investments in the development of continental tourism, especially projects that connect healthcare services, rehabilitation and the tourist offer. The government expects the continuation of positive trends during the post-season as well, along with preparations for the next tourist year. Although the final financial result for 2026 still needs to be confirmed, the indicators so far point to another year of growth for Croatian tourism.

World.title: Conference League: Sint-Truiden Beats Hajduk 2-0 at Poljud
World.content:
Hajduk were beaten 2-0 by Sint-Truiden at a near-empty Poljud on Thursday night in the fourth round of the Conference League, with Samed Baždar’s strike in first-half stoppage time and a superb Shinkawa goal after the break leaving Garcia’s side on six points with two league-phase matches to play.

Hajduk hosted Belgian side Sint-Truiden at Poljud on Thursday night in the fourth round of the Conference League league phase. A win would have taken Gonzalo Garcia’s side a big step towards the knockout phase and a first European spring in 32 years.

Because of UEFA’s punishment for crowd trouble at the Ajax match, Hajduk played without their usual support. Under UEFA rules, organized groups of children under 14 were still allowed to attend, and around 8,000 of them filled the east stand.

Sint-Truiden had backing of their own. The Belgian club bought 195 VIP tickets for a total of €15,600 and handed them out to their supporters free of charge.

Lineups

Hajduk (4-2-3-1): Silić; Acapandié, Hadžikadunić, Marešić, Hrgović; Fayad, Del Moral; Bamba, Dalisson, Šotiček; Martin

Sint-Truiden (4-3-3): Kokubo; Hata, Taniguchi, Musliu, Pupe; Shinkawa, Sissako, Ishiwatari; Vanwesemael, Baždar, Sebaoui

García left first-choice striker Michele Šego on the bench and handed Martin the start up front, with Marko Livaja ruled out by back pain.

Match report

he match got under way in windy conditions at Poljud, and Hajduk threatened from the first attack. Martin played in Hrgović, whose shot was blocked, though the Spanish striker had already strayed offside. Bamba looked for Martin at the far post with a cross from the right in the 5th minute, but it was too high.

Sint-Truiden’s first real attack came in the 8th minute, when Baždar’s shot from 18 meters was blocked behind for a corner, to the delight of the small group of visiting fans in Hajduk’s VIP section. A minute later the visitors had the ball in the net. Pupe crossed from the right, Shinkawa headed it down, and Musliu escaped the Hajduk defenders to score from close range. After a VAR review lasting more than three minutes, the goal was ruled out for offside against Musliu.

Hajduk almost broke quickly in the 15th minute, but Pupe got to the ball before Martin. There had been a heavy foul on Bamba in the build-up, though the referee kept his cards in his pocket.

Hajduk’s first big chance came in the 19th minute. Hrgović sent a superb ball into the box, but Martin could not connect properly. Hrgović then found Šotiček with another pass into space, but it was cleared behind for a corner, and Šotiček could not head down a Fayad delivery for a teammate.

Sint-Truiden had more of the ball for a spell without creating anything clear. Hajduk responded in the 28th minute with a neat one-two between Hrgović and Šotiček, after which Šotiček went down in the box following a challenge. The referee was close by and waved at the winger to get up. The ball broke to Hrgović, whose shot flew over.

Silić comfortably claimed a Shinkawa free kick in the 32nd minute, and a minute later Hajduk had their best chance of the half. Fayad beat his man brilliantly and slipped the ball into space for Martin, who was through alone in the box, but Kokubo saved. Šotiček headed off target in the 36th minute.

In the 39th minute Hajduk were awarded an indirect free kick when Kokubo picked up a pass from Pupe. The Japanese goalkeeper protested that Martin had deflected the ball, and replays backed him up, but the referee was having none of it. Dalisson’s thunderous strike from the edge of the box was superbly saved by Kokubo.

Dalisson was booked in the 42nd minute for a foul in midfield. Two minutes later Hadžikadunić took a risk on the ball but won a foul from Shinkawa, though he appeared to pick up a knock in the process and needed treatment. Five minutes of stoppage time were added.

Sint-Truiden then took the lead in the first minute of added time. Bosnia and Herzegovina international Samed Baždar picked up the ball around 30 meters from goal, skipped past a sliding challenge from Hadžikadunić, made space for himself and beat Silić with a powerful strike from 20 meters to make it 0-1.

Hajduk went into the break 1-0 down.

Garcia then made a triple change, sending on Šego, Pajaziti and Dendoncker for Martin, Dalisson and Šotiček.

It did not help. In the 51st minute Dendoncker lost the ball around 20 meters from goal, Shinkawa pounced, cut inside slightly and fired a superb shot into the top right corner to make it 0-2.

Sint-Truiden could have caused more trouble in the 55th minute, but Vanwesemael’s cross went wide of the goal. The visitors brought on Matsuzawa for goalscorer Shinkawa four minutes later.

Hajduk tried to respond in the 62nd minute. Pajaziti won the ball in midfield and carried it 20 meters before finding Bamba, who cut in slightly from the right, but his shot struck the head of the defender.

Apart from the Japanese midfielder’s stunning goal, the second half offered little, and Hajduk did not look like a team capable of turning the match around.

Sint-Truiden should have scored a third in the 68th minute. Vanwesemael crossed from the right for Ishiwatari, who was unmarked at the left-hand post but headed wide. A minute later the visitors replaced Pupe with Muja.

Fayad tried his luck from distance in the 72nd minute, but Kokubo saved.

Sint-Truiden made a double change in the 79th minute, bringing on Diouf and Merlen for Sebaoui and goalscorer Baždar. Huram was booked for a foul two minutes later. In the 85th minute Šego shot from distance but missed the target, and Garcia sent on Šutalo for Bamba.

A minute later Merlen tried to catch Silić off his line with a long-range effort, but it went wide. Three minutes of stoppage time were added.

Hajduk could not find a way back, and Sint-Truidense held on to win 2-0, leaving Garcsa’s side on six points after four rounds. Two league-phase matches remain, both against Danish opposition: Hajduk hosts Nordsjælland at Poljud in the fifth round on December 10, then travels to Midtjylland on December 17.

Mistakes are part of football. We did not deserve the victory. We had a few chances in the first half; maybe we could have gone ahead even. I am not mad at the situation itself, but I am angry at the game.

“The players are doing a lot of good things. But the reality today was that we didn’t do what we needed to do. We have a lot of quality, but we need to play 100%,” said Garcia after the match. “It’s normal that after so many games, something like this happened.”

“We are a young team. I am very happy with the team, always. I am proud of the work, but my job is also to make sure they don’t fall asleep.”

World.title: Ivan Anušić’s New 24-Year-Old Adviser Earns More Than a Retired General
World.content:
November the 26th, 2026 – Ivan Anušić’s new 24-year-old adviser Nina Mikulandra will allegedly earn more than a retired general. She is otherwise the vice-president of the Šibenik-Knin County HDZ Youth.

Defence Minister Ivan Anušić has seven special advisers. Ilko Cimic reports for Index that the highest individual net earnings among them will go to the newest member of his team, 24-year-old Nina Mikulandra, a recently graduated political scientist and vice-president of the HDZ Youth of Šibenik-Knin County. Her net salary will amount to around €1,850, which is more than the fees received by retired generals, war commanders and Anušić’s other advisers. No previous work experience was required for the position she holds. According to official data from the Ministry of Defence (MORH) analysed by Index, the highest fee among the previous advisers, €1,700 net, is received by Ivan Hampovčan. Željko Živanović, Božo Kožul, Ivica Ušljebrka and Luka Bandalo each receive €1,100, while Zvonimir Gvozdanović advises the minister without compensation.

The form of engagement also differs. Mikulandra is employed in the minister’s cabinet for a fixed term, at the latest until the end of his mandate, while the other advisers, according to the MORH form, are engaged with an advisory fee and without an employment relationship. We looked at who Anušić’s advisers are, what experience they have, how much they’re paid and what they are actually responsible for.

from the university classroom to the minister’s cabinet

Mikulandra graduated in political science this year from the Faculty of Political Science in Zagreb. She is the vice-president of the county HDZ Youth and a member of the Youth Council of Šibenik-Knin County. She was appointed Anušić’s special adviser on the 20th of November, following a procedure in which nine candidates met the competition conditions. No previous work experience was required for that position. Experience in the defence system, state administration or security policy was not required either. The only condition was a completed appropriate master’s degree in the field of social sciences.

MORH explains her selection with her academic results and performance at the job interview. They state that she completed her studies with the highest praise, summa cum laude, and that she received the Dean’s Award twice, both times with a grade point average of 5.00. She is also attending a postgraduate specialist study in “Security Policy of the Republic of Croatia.” According to the Ministry’s response, she showed the best competences and motivation at the interview. The final decision on the appointment was made by Minister Anušić.

what will she actually do for the salary?

The basic gross salary of the new adviser is €2,794.50. With residence in Zagreb and without additional tax reliefs, that would mean around €1,850 net. The competition lists support tasks for the minister, advising, preparation for strategic planning and cooperation with the media. At the same time it is stated that the person in that position is not a civil servant and “does not perform tasks within the competence of the Ministry of Defence.” MORH replied to Index that her tasks will include “support to the minister and assistance in the implementation of the established policy of the Government of the Republic of Croatia.” They did not, however, specify concrete projects she will take on or the results expected of her.

The best-paid adviser from the previous list, Ivan Hampovčan, is a law graduate and former secretary of Osijek-Baranja County. He was appointed to that position back in 2017, when Anušić became county prefect. Earlier he worked at the RODA development agency in Antunovac, the municipality Anušić ran before moving to the county. Since May this year, Hampovčan has also been listed in the register of the Commission for Deciding on Conflict of Interest as the director of the county Pharmacies Srce. For advising the defence minister he receives €1,700. The MORH form states that he is engaged for “drawing up analyses and opinions and giving advice on individual issues within the competence of the defence sector.” Which issues those are is not explained in the document.

retired generals and commanders receive less than 24-year-old loyal hdz member mikulandra

Željko Živanović is a retired major general and Vukovar defender. He took part in the defence of Vukovar and after the war held positions in the military education system. MORH lists him in official announcements as a special adviser to the defence minister. For that work he receives €1,100. The same amount is received by Božo Kožul, the former commander of the 1st Guard Brigade “Tigers.” During the war he held command duties in that unit and was retired back in 2001. Ivica Ušljebrka, a retired colonel and wartime member of the 4th Guard Brigade “Spiders,” also receives €1,100. He was an adviser during the term of Minister Damir Krstičević and remained in that position under Anušić. For none of them does the official MORH form state a concrete area of work; descriptions of their duties are limited to drawing up analyses and giving opinions and advice on issues within the defence sector.

the director of a state-owned company is also among the advisers

Anušić is also advised by Luka Bandalo, whom the state agency ALAN, responsible for trade in arms and military equipment, presents as its operational director. For advice and opinions on issues within the defence sector he receives €1,100. The only one who, according to the official list, advises the minister without compensation is Zvonimir Gvozdanović, a doctor of dental medicine and director of the Vukovar Health Centre. He too is engaged for drawing up analyses and giving advice on individual issues within the competence of the defence sector. What those issues are cannot be determined from the MORH form.

there was also a former journalist among the ranks

It should certainly be noted that Mikulandra is not the first person Anušić employed as a special adviser in his cabinet. That position was also held after his arrival at MORH by former journalist Iva Puljić Šego. In January 2024 the Ministry confirmed to Index that she was appointed after a competition published on 22 November 2023, also for support tasks for the minister and at the latest until the end of his mandate.

Puljić Šego is no longer a special adviser but is listed by MORH as a civil servant employed within the Ministry of Defence system. As a reminder, Minister Anušić said in Parliament that it was he who had leaked information, not his associate and MORH spokesperson Iva Puljić Šego, who after an investigation by the Military Security and Intelligence Agency (VSOA) lost her NATO security clearance.

World.title: Fake Doctor Defrauds Zagreb Woman of 9,000 Euros
World.content:
November the 26th, 2026 – A fake doctor has defrauded a Zagreb woman of 9,000 euros, and it turns out the police are already well aware of the individual in question.

Zagreb police have been met with another case of fraud in which the perpetrators posed as no less than doctors. Index reports that they convinced a Zagreb woman that a member of her family needed urgent surgery, after which she handed them 9,000 euros. Police suspected a 42-year-old man for the fraud, who is already in investigative detention for allegedly committing fraud previously.

His currently unknown accomplice has not yet been located. According to police suspicions, the two men contacted the 70-year-old woman by phone and misled her into believing that a family member of hers needed urgent surgery that had to be paid for. The woman believed their story and handed the money over to the 42-year-old.

he was previously arrested at the croatian-serbian border

This is a man against whom the police have already filed criminal charges multiple times for various criminal offences. Back in October, together with a 70-year-old man, he was arrested at the Bajakovo border crossing while attempting to exit Croatia into Serbia. Police suspect them of defrauding a 69-year-old woman from Zagreb’s Susedgrad district, whom they convinced that her daughter had been injured in a traffic accident. Material damage in that case amounted to around 50,000 euros. During a search of his vehicle, police officers found a hidden pouch with money in a portable cooler, which they suspect came from the fraud.

police have issued a public warning

The police have repeatedly warned the general public about scams in which perpetrators pose as doctors and exploit their fear for family members. They therefore advise people to never hand over any money in the event of such a call, to verify the information with family members, and to notify the police immediately. A special report has been filed against the 42-year-old with the competent state attorney’s office, and the criminal investigation continues.

World.title: Mate Rimac Recalls His Argument With Volkswagen Over Bugatti
World.content:
November the 26th, 2026 – Croatian entrepreneur Mate Rimac recalled his intense argument with Volkswagen over Bugatti in a recent interview with the Classic Driver portal.

In an interview for the automotive portal Classic Driver, Mate Rimac revealed previously lesser-known details about the acquisition of Bugatti and fierce disagreements with the leaders of the Volkswagen Group regarding the future of the French car brand. Index reports that according to his recollection of events, the Germans initially wanted the successor to the Chiron to be an electric SUV with four seats, and later insisted on an all-electric hypercar. Rimac, who built his career precisely on the development of electric hypercars, opposed their plans. He also recounted how he went from being a potential manufacturer of the new Bugatti to acquiring the entire company, reports Motor1.

volkswagen allegedly wanted an electric suv

The story began back in 2020, at a time of great enthusiasm in the automotive industry for electric vehicles. The Volkswagen Group was then considering the possibility of Bugatti’s Chiron being succeeded by an all-electric SUV with four seats. Rimac’s company participated in the development of the electric powertrain for that car, which was supposed to use technology developed for the Nevera. However, it soon became apparent that the realization of the project would be extremely demanding and expensive. For such a car, it was not possible to use any of the existing platforms, so Volkswagen would have to invest billions in developing a completely new one. The project ultimately didn’t prove to be economically viable and as such did not get the green light from the German management.

“why don’t you just take over the entire company?

Since Bugatti did not have a viable plan for a successor to the Chiron, Rimac saw a business opportunity in this. He proposed to the leaders of the Volkswagen Group that his company take over the development and production of the entire car, while Volkswagen would be in charge of its sales. At one of the meetings, he received an answer he did not expect.

“Why don’t you just take over the whole company?” one of the Volkswagen Group leaders asked him.

Rimac initially thought it was a joke. Upon returning home, he didn’t even mention the offer to his associates. However, a few months later, the same man called him and asked why he hadn’t gotten back to him. Only then did Rimac realise that the offer was serious. Negotiations followed that lasted two and a half years.

“i had an extremely serious argument with them”

When the question of Bugatti’s future came up during the negotiations, the leaders of Volkswagen and Porsche told Rimac that the next Bugatti hypercar had to be all-electric. Considering that Rimac had by then developed the electric hypercars Concept One and Nevera and collaborated with major car manufacturers on the development of battery technology, such a choice seemed logical at first glance.

However, Rimac believed that this would be the wrong move for Bugatti. “I had an extremely serious argument with them because I thought it was the wrong move for Bugatti. I said: ‘No, I don’t want to make an electric Bugatti,'” he recounted.

The Volkswagen Group eventually agreed to the development of a car with a hybrid power-train, but in order to reduce costs, it wanted to keep the existing Chiron platform. Rimac opposed this proposal as well. He believed that adapting the existing structure of the car to batteries would require too many compromises. Even before the completion of the negotiations on the acquisition of Bugatti, his company financed the start of the development of a completely new gasoline engine with its own money in collaboration with the British engineering company Cosworth. To test the feasibility of the project, engineers first built a prototype engine with only four cylinders, or a quarter of the planned V16 engine. This allowed them to test performance and emissions and estimate the costs and time required for development. The results, it seems, were good enough for Rimac to convince the other participants in the project of his vision.

now, all the new bugatti units have been sold

The result of multi-year development was the Bugatti Tourbillon, unveiled back in 2024. Instead of an all-electric power-train, it got a new naturally aspirated 8.3-litre V16 engine combined with electric motors. Six years after the start of development, Rimac says his decision paid off. Bugatti has, according to his words, already sold all units of the Tourbillon it plans to produce. Motor1 also points out the irony of the whole story. The man who developed one of the fastest electric cars in the world ended up being the one who convinced the leaders of one of the world’s largest automotive conglomerates that their most prestigious brand should not switch to an all-electric power-train.
